// commandRunnable resolves the command's first word on PATH, expanding a
// leading environment variable so "$EDITOR ." checks the editor itself. The
// returned probe is run by a bounded Bubble Tea command, never by View.
func commandRunnable(run string, interactive bool) func(context.Context) bool {
	return func(ctx context.Context) bool { return checkCommandRunnable(ctx, run, interactive) }
}

func checkCommandRunnable(ctx context.Context, run string, interactive bool) bool {
	if ctx == nil {
		ctx = context.Background()
	}
	word := firstWord(run)
	if strings.HasPrefix(word, "$") {
		word = os.Getenv(strings.TrimPrefix(word, "$"))
		if word == "" {
			return false
		}
		word = firstWord(word)
	}
	if word == "" {
		return false
	}
	if interactive {
		// Ask the configured shell after it loads its rc files; LookPath
		// cannot see aliases or functions.
		probeCtx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, 3*time.Second)
		defer cancel()
		probe := exec.CommandContext(probeCtx, shellPath(), "-lic",
			`command -v "$1" >/dev/null 2>&1`, "dev-tool-probe", word)
		return probe.Run() == nil
	}
	if filepath.IsAbs(word) {
		_, err := os.Stat(word)
		return err == nil
	}
	_, err := exec.LookPath(word)
	return err == nil
}

func firstWord(s string) string {
	f := strings.Fields(s)
	if len(f) == 0 {
		return ""
	}
	return f[0]
}

# Changelog

All notable changes to this project are documented in this file.

The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/), and releases use [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).

## [Unreleased]

## [0.2.5] - 2026-09-01

### Added

- `dev repo context [repo]` now has an additive schema-v1 `--json` report and an
  explicit `--refresh` path. Local checkout, Git, task, worktree, and runtime facts
  stay live and network-free; optional forge and configured-fleet observations carry
  source, age, freshness, completeness, and collection errors. Remote endpoints are
  structurally sanitized before public output, and readiness remains split by scope
  instead of collapsing unknown evidence into a global safe value. `dev status`
  reuses the same cheap local readiness projection without network probes.
- `dev fleet machine-id <host>` exposes the remote host's non-secret durable machine
  UUID and compares it with the optional `machine_id` pin in `remotes.toml`.
  `dev fleet files [repo-or-path] --to <host>` plans a one-way transfer of explicitly
  allowlisted ignored files and mutates only with `--apply`; both hosts must prove
  every exact path is untracked, ignored, regular, portable, bounded, and bound to the
  same fetch identity, attached branch, and commit; apply additionally requires the
  pinned target machine. Differing target bytes require a separate `--replace`;
  `--yes` never implies replacement.

### Fixed

- Task writes now carry an in-memory revision from read to write, so existing
  lifecycle callers cannot silently overwrite a concurrent process's newer task
  record. Park holds the task transaction through runtime/worktree cleanup, and a
  DONE direct-task ID starts a new compare-and-swap generation. Catalog create,
  update, import, and experiment reconciliation share one
  cross-process transaction lock, while corrupt task records make repository-context
  inventory explicitly incomplete instead of disappearing behind a warning.
- Portable-file retries now recover an interrupted store both before and after the
  first journal write. Source branch/HEAD/fetch identity is revalidated around payload
  reads; target sync/apply and remote aliases share the canonical clone lease. Durable

	"bytes"
	"strings"

	tea "github.com/charmbracelet/bubbletea"

func TestLineEditorSupportsInlineNavigationAndDeletion(t *testing.T) {
	model := newLineEditorModel("? Value: ")
	for _, message := range []tea.KeyMsg{
		{Type: tea.KeyRunes, Runes: []rune("ac")},
		{Type: tea.KeyLeft},
		{Type: tea.KeyRunes, Runes: []rune("b")},
		{Type: tea.KeyHome},
		{Type: tea.KeyRunes, Runes: []rune("^")},
		{Type: tea.KeyEnd},
		{Type: tea.KeyRunes, Runes: []rune("$")},
		{Type: tea.KeyLeft},
		{Type: tea.KeyLeft},
		{Type: tea.KeyDelete},
		{Type: tea.KeyBackspace},
		{Type: tea.KeyRight},
		{Type: tea.KeyRunes, Runes: []rune("!")},
	} {
		updated, _ := model.Update(message)
		var ok bool
		model, ok = updated.(lineEditorModel)
		if !ok {
			t.Fatalf("Update returned %T", updated)
		}
	}

	if got := model.input.Value(); got != "^a$!" {
		t.Fatalf("edited value = %q, want %q", got, "^a$!")
	}
}

func TestLineEditorSubmitKeepsPromptAndFinalValue(t *testing.T) {
	model := newLineEditorModel("? Value: ")
	updated, _ := model.Update(tea.KeyMsg{Type: tea.KeyRunes, Runes: []rune("answer")})
	model = updated.(lineEditorModel)
	updated, command := model.Update(tea.KeyMsg{Type: tea.KeyEnter})
	model = updated.(lineEditorModel)

	if !model.done || model.canceled {
		t.Fatalf("submitted model state = done %v, canceled %v", model.done, model.canceled)
	}
	if got := model.View(); got != "? Value: answer\n" {
		t.Fatalf("final view = %q", got)
	}
	if command == nil {
		t.Fatal("submit did not return a quit command")
	}
}

func runDoctor(app *App) error {
	ctx := ctxOf()
	var checks []check

	// What am I running? A build several commits past its last release behaves
	// differently from that release, and `dev --version` alone does not say so.
	checks = append(checks, check{"dev", checkOK, versionSummary()})
	if install, err := runningInstall(); err == nil {
		detail := install.Method.label() + " — " + install.Path
		if install.Resolved != install.Path {
			detail += " → " + install.Resolved
		}
		checks = append(checks, check{"install", checkOK, detail})
		if others := otherDevInstalls(install, devInstallsOnPath()); len(others) > 0 {
			var copies []string
			for _, other := range others {
				copies = append(copies, other.Method.label()+" at "+other.Path)
			}
			checks = append(checks, check{"dev copies", checkWarn,
				"other executable(s) on PATH may shadow this install: " + strings.Join(copies, "; ")})
		}
	} else {

=== makefile
BINARY  := dev
PREFIX  ?= $(HOME)/.local
# Only vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH tags are version authority; any other tag in the
# repository (a backup or rescue marker, say) must never become --version.
VERSION ?= $(shell git describe --tags --match 'v[0-9]*' --always --dirty 2>/dev/null || echo dev)
LDFLAGS := -s -w -X github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/cli.Version=$(VERSION)

.PHONY: build install test lint fmt vet skill-sync skill-check e2e clean all

all: fmt vet test build

build:
	go build -ldflags '$(LDFLAGS)' -o $(BINARY) ./cmd/dev

# Install the binary and its agent skill together, so the documentation an
# agent reads always matches the binary that is on PATH.
install: build
	install -d $(PREFIX)/bin
	install -m 0755 $(BINARY) $(PREFIX)/bin/$(BINARY)
	$(PREFIX)/bin/$(BINARY) skill install
	@echo
	@echo 'Add to your shell rc:  eval "$$($(PREFIX)/bin/$(BINARY) shell-init zsh)"'

test:
	go test ./...

vet:
	go vet ./...

fmt:
	gofmt -w .

# Regenerate the skill's command reference from the live command tree.
skill-sync: build
	./$(BINARY) skill sync
	$(MAKE) build

# Fail if the checked-in command reference has drifted from the command tree.
# Wire this into CI and a pre-push hook.
skill-check: build
	./$(BINARY) skill sync --check

e2e: build
	./scripts/e2e.sh

clean:
	rm -f $(BINARY)
	go clean -testcache

=== shell.go
package cli

import (
	"fmt"
	"os"

	"github.com/spf13/cobra"
)

// posixInit and fishInit define the wrapper that makes `dev resume` able to
// leave the user *inside* the checkout. The binary keeps its real stdout so a
// terminal still opens the TUI and a pipe still receives plain output; a
// private file carries only the requested parent-directory change.
const posixInit = `# dev shell integration — add to your rc file:
#   eval "$(dev shell-init %[2]s)"
export DEV_SHELL_INIT=1
dev() {
  # Commands outside the navigation surface need no side channel. Besides
  # avoiding two subprocesses, this keeps them working when TMPDIR is stale.
  case "${1:-}" in
    __complete|__completeNoDesc|--help|-h|--version|--skill|completion|config|doctor|done|retire|prepare|artifact|git|edit|gitignore|ignore|help|list|ls|park|skill|shell-init|cache|stats|status|sweep|adopt|bootstrap)
      command %[1]s "$@" || return $?
      return 0
      ;;
  esac

  local __dev_cd_file __dev_dir __dev_status
  if ! __dev_cd_file="$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/dev-cd.XXXXXX" 2>/dev/null)"; then
    __dev_cd_file="$(mktemp "/tmp/dev-cd.XXXXXX" 2>/dev/null)" || {
      printf 'dev: cannot create the shell directory side channel\n' >&2
      return 1
    }
  fi

  __dev_status=0
  DEV_SHELL_CD_FD=3 command %[1]s "$@" 3>"$__dev_cd_file" || __dev_status=$?
  if [ $__dev_status -eq 0 ] && [ -s "$__dev_cd_file" ]; then
    if IFS= read -r -d '' __dev_dir < "$__dev_cd_file"; then
      if [ -n "$__dev_dir" ]; then
        builtin cd -- "$__dev_dir" || __dev_status=$?
      fi
    else
      __dev_status=1
    fi
  fi
  rm -f -- "$__dev_cd_file" || :
  return $__dev_status
}
`

const fishInit = `# dev shell integration — add to config.fish:
#   dev shell-init fish | source
set -gx DEV_SHELL_INIT 1
function dev
    set -l __dev_command ""
    if test (count $argv) -gt 0
        set __dev_command $argv[1]
    end
    if contains -- "$__dev_command" __complete __completeNoDesc --help -h --version --skill completion config doctor done retire prepare artifact git edit gitignore ignore help list ls park skill shell-init cache stats status sweep adopt bootstrap
        command %[1]s $argv
        return $status
    end

    set -l __dev_tmpdir /tmp
    set -q TMPDIR; and set __dev_tmpdir $TMPDIR
    set -l __dev_cd_file (mktemp "$__dev_tmpdir/dev-cd.XXXXXX" 2>/dev/null)
    if test $status -ne 0
        set __dev_cd_file (mktemp "/tmp/dev-cd.XXXXXX" 2>/dev/null)
    end
    if test -z "$__dev_cd_file"
        printf 'dev: cannot create the shell directory side channel\n' >&2
        return 1
    end

    set -lx DEV_SHELL_CD_FD 3
    command %[1]s $argv 3>"$__dev_cd_file"
    set -l __dev_status $status
    if test $__dev_status -eq 0; and test -s "$__dev_cd_file"
        if read -z -l __dev_dir < "$__dev_cd_file"
            if test -n "$__dev_dir"
                builtin cd -- "$__dev_dir"
                set __dev_status $status
            end
        else
            set __dev_status 1
        end
    end
    rm -f -- "$__dev_cd_file"
    return $__dev_status
end

// Cloned reports whether this remote already has a local checkout.
func (r RemoteRow) Cloned() bool { return r.LocalPath != "" }

func (r RemoteRow) searchText() string {
	return strings.ToLower(strings.Join([]string{
		string(r.Repo.Forge), r.Repo.Name, r.Repo.FullName, r.Repo.Description,
		r.Repo.Visibility, r.Repo.DefaultBranch, r.LocalName, string(r.LocalKind),
	}, " "))
}

func (r RemoteRow) matches(query string) bool {
	query = strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(query))
	for _, term := range strings.Fields(query) {
		key, value, structured := strings.Cut(term, ":")
		if structured && (key == "vis" || key == "visibility") {
			if strings.ToLower(r.Repo.Visibility) != value {
				return false
			}
			continue
		}
		if !strings.Contains(r.searchText(), term) {
			return false
		}
	}
	return true
}

```text
| `commit` | commits everything with `--message`/`-m` (prompted interactively if omitted) |
| `discard` | resets tracked changes and removes untracked files; destructive, requires `--yes` outside a TTY |

`--yes`/`-y` confirms the selected finish plan; it is mandatory for a non-interactive `--dirty discard` and otherwise skips the interactive confirmation step. `--keep-worktree` keeps the worktree after `--ff` integration (default: removed once merged), `--push` also pushes the resulting branch, and `--delete-branch` deletes the branch once its commits are contained in the base — never a branch with unpushed commits.

## Configuration

```bash
dev config init
dev config show
dev config path
dev config scaffolds init
dev config scaffolds show
dev config scaffolds path
dev config scaffolds edit
```

`config init` detects local roots and writes explicit defaults. A missing config file is allowed; the built-in defaults keep core Git behavior usable, but generated config is recommended because it makes machine policy reviewable.

Key sections:

| Section | Controls |
|---|---|
| `[paths]` | scan roots, project/tries/worktree roots, worktree template, state path |
| `[runtime]` | `auto`, Herdr, tmux, Zellij, or none plus metadata settings |
| `[worktree]` | local ignored-file provisioning, linked dirs, setup commands, strategies, timeout |
| `[local_files]` | host ceilings for portable files; project overlays provide the separate off-machine candidate allowlist |
| `[forge]` / `[[forge.azure_devops]]` | complete remote inventory cache TTL and opt-in Azure organization/project targets |
| `[bootstrap]` | recursion, symlink handling, index/layout policy |
| `[tui]` / `[[tui.tools]]` | columns, sorting, and external-tool bindings |
| `[stats]` | sampler and optional WakaTime import |
| `[update]` | `check` (default `true`) — allow the once-a-day "newer release available" hint and its background cache refresh; `DEV_NO_UPDATE_CHECK` overrides it |

`DEV_TUI_TRACE=/absolute/new-file.json` enables a one-run TUI startup/readiness
trace. The target must be absolute and must not exist; dev never overwrites it.
The private bounded document is written after TUI teardown and contains relative
categorical timings plus aggregate row counts rather than names, paths, or raw
payloads. It is not configuration,
cache, durable stats, stdout, or network telemetry. For TUI invocations, the
optional update-cache network refresh is also deferred until the initial view
has returned.

Repository quick-note Markdown is durable under configured `paths.state_dir/notes`, which defaults to `$XDG_DATA_HOME/dev/notes`. The full-text index at `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/dev/notes.db` is disposable and rebuilds from those files; changing `paths.state_dir` does not move the cache.

### Scaffold presets

Global repository recipes live at `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/dev/scaffolds.toml` (or
the root `--scaffolds` override). Every authored file declares `version = 1`.

func rejectNestedRepository(ctx context.Context, parent string) error {
	probe := parent
	for {
		if _, err := os.Stat(probe); err == nil {
			break
		} else if !errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
			return fmt.Errorf("inspect repository destination parent: %w", err)
		}
		next := filepath.Dir(probe)
		if next == probe {
			break
		}
		probe = next
	}
	if discovered, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, probe); err == nil && discovered.Root != "" {
		return fmt.Errorf("refusing to create a nested repository inside %s", discovered.Root)
	}
	return nil
}

// NormalizeCloneRef expands forge shorthand while leaving explicit URLs, SCP
// references and local paths unchanged.
func NormalizeCloneRef(ref string) string {
	ref = strings.TrimSpace(ref)
	if ref == "" {
		return ref
	}
	if filepath.IsAbs(ref) {
		return filepath.Clean(ref)
	}
	if ref == "~" || strings.HasPrefix(ref, "~/") {
		return config.Expand(ref)
	}
	if strings.HasPrefix(ref, "./") || strings.HasPrefix(ref, "../") {
		if absolute, err := filepath.Abs(ref); err == nil {
			return absolute
		}
	}
	if strings.HasPrefix(ref, "file://") || (!strings.Contains(ref, "://") && strings.ContainsAny(ref, "@:")) {
		return ref
	}
	if info, err := os.Stat(ref); err == nil && info.IsDir() {
		if absolute, err := filepath.Abs(ref); err == nil {
			return absolute
		}
	}
	if kind := forge.FromURL(ref); kind != forge.Unknown {
		if adapter, err := forge.For(kind); err == nil {
			return adapter.CloneURL(ref)
		}
		return ref
	}
	if !strings.Contains(ref, "://") && strings.Contains(ref, "/") {
		if adapter, err := forge.Preferred(); err == nil {
			return adapter.CloneURL(ref)
		}
	}
	return ref
}

7	## Toolchain and commands
8	
9	- Go 1.26.4 (from `go.mod`) builds the CLI. Python 3.11+ and `uv` are used only for the documentation site.

14	make build                         # build ./dev with git-derived version metadata
15	make test                          # go test ./...
16	go test -race ./...                # CI test command
17	go test ./internal/gitx -run '^TestAddWorktreeUsesExplicitBase$'  # one test
18	go test ./internal/cli -run '^TestName/Subtest$'                  # one subtest

32	uv run mkdocs build --strict

38	## Architecture
39	
40	The executable path is deliberately shallow:
41	
42	```text
43	cmd/dev/main.go
44	  -> cli.Execute()
45	  -> cli.NewRootCommandWithIO()
46	  -> App.Load()
47	  -> Cobra command handler
48	  -> domain package(s)
49	```
50	
51	`internal/cli` assembles commands, parses flags, invokes services, and renders output. Keep policy out of command handlers; it belongs in independently testable domain packages:
52	
53	- `config` owns defaults, TOML overlays, validation, and XDG paths.
54	- `gitx` is the Git porcelain boundary and canonicalizes repository identity through the shared Git common directory.
55	- `task` persists only human intent Git cannot derive: task mode/state, owner, next action, and runtime hints.
56	- `wt` owns managed linked-worktree creation, placement, provisioning plans, and safe removal. Runtimes never create or manage Git worktrees; they surface checkout or experiment paths selected and validated by the calling `dev` flow, including managed, external, or adopted worktrees and non-Git Try directories.
57	- `runtime` abstracts Herdr, tmux, Zellij, and the no-multiplexer backend. Handles are backend-qualified hints and must be checked against live checkout coverage before reuse.
58	- `repo` discovers and deduplicates repositories; `inventory` joins repositories, Git state, tasks, worktrees, and live runtime data. CLI listings and the TUI consume this joined view.
59	- `catalog` stores stable repository/Try identity and personal metadata. `experiment` owns Try creation, archive/restore, and graduation, including intent records and rollback/reconciliation around moves.
60	- `note` stores multiple repository thoughts as durable Markdown keyed by catalog ID and maintains a rebuildable SQLite FTS index. It is distinct from task context and the catalog's single metadata summary.
61	- `tui` owns Bubble Tea state/rendering only. `internal/cli/tui.go` injects callbacks to the same services used by non-interactive commands.
62	- `stats` is durable SQLite data; `diskusage`, note FTS, and forge/gitignore data are regenerable caches. Do not treat stats as cache.
63	- `forge` wraps optional `gh`, `glab`, and Azure CLI integrations and must degrade to local Git behavior when they are unavailable.
64	
65	The principal task flow spans `internal/cli/start.go`, `start_flow.go`, `gitx`/`wt`, `runtime`, and `task`: resolve the canonical repository and explicit base, create or select the checkout, provision/open it, then persist and annotate the task. Lifecycle behavior lives in `park.go`, `resume.go`, `done.go`, and `sweep.go`; preserve their report-before-apply and no-data-loss ordering.
66	
67	State is split intentionally:
68	
69	- Git remotes/branches are durable code truth.
70	- Worktrees are disposable local checkouts.
71	- Runtime sessions are per-host and re-derivable.
72	- Task TOML and catalog assets hold only intent/identity that Git cannot answer.
73	- Repository quick-note Markdown is durable sidecar data; `notes.db` is only its disposable search index.
74	- `stats.db` is durable observation data; `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/dev/*` is disposable.
75	
76	## Behavioral contracts
77	
78	- Task modes are `worktree`, `branch`, and `direct`; lifecycle states are `hot`, `warm`, `cold`, and `done`.
79	- Use an explicit base for branch/worktree creation. Do not infer a safe base from whichever branch happens to be checked out.
80	- Never nest a managed worktree inside a repository. Removing a worktree does not remove its branch, and dirty removal stays opt-in.
81	- Cold parking requires committed, pushed, reconstructible work before runtime/worktree cleanup.
82	- Reconciliation flows such as `sweep`, `adopt`, and bootstrap organization plans report before applying changes. Direct actions such as `wt rm`, `tries archive`, and `cache clear` mutate immediately after their own safety checks; do not treat them as previews.

26			input: app.In,
27			in:    bufio.NewReader(app.In),
28			out:   app.Out,
29			style: app.outStyle(),
30		}
31	}
32	
33	func (p *prompter) line(label, fallback string) (string, error) {
34		return p.lineWithDisplayFallback(label, fallback, fallback)
35	}
36	
37	func (p *prompter) lineWithDisplayFallback(label, fallback, displayFallback string) (string, error) {
38		prefix := fmt.Sprintf("%s %s: ", p.style.prompt("?"), p.style.prompt(label))
39		if displayFallback != "" {
40			prefix = fmt.Sprintf("%s %s %s: ", p.style.prompt("?"), p.style.prompt(label), p.style.dim("["+displayFallback+"]"))
41		}
42		value, err := p.readLine(prefix)
43		if err != nil {
44			return "", err
45		}
46		value = strings.TrimSpace(value)
47		if value == "" {
48			value = fallback
49		}
50		return value, nil
51	}
52	
53	func (p *prompter) dangerLine(label string) (string, error) {
54		prefix := fmt.Sprintf("%s %s: ", p.style.danger("?"), p.style.danger(label))
55		line, err := p.readLine(prefix)
56		if err != nil {
57			return "", err
58		}
59		return strings.TrimSpace(line), nil
60	}
61	
62	func (p *prompter) choice(label, fallback, hint string, choices map[string]string) (string, error) {
63		for {
64			value, err := p.line(label, fallback)
65			if err != nil {
66				return "", err
67			}
68			value = strings.ToLower(value)
69			if resolved, ok := choices[value]; ok {
70				return resolved, nil
71			}
72			fmt.Fprintf(p.out, "  %s\n", p.style.warning("enter one of: "+hint))
73		}
74	}
75	
76	func (p *prompter) confirm(label string, defaultYes bool) (bool, error) {
77		fallback := "y/N"
78		if defaultYes {
79			fallback = "Y/n"
80		}
81		for {
82			prefix := fmt.Sprintf("%s %s %s: ", p.style.prompt("?"), p.style.prompt(label), p.style.dim("["+fallback+"]"))
83			line, err := p.readLine(prefix)
84			if err != nil {
85				return false, err
86			}
87			value := strings.TrimSpace(line)
88			switch strings.ToLower(value) {
89			case "y", "yes":
90				return true, nil
91			case "n", "no":
92				return false, nil
93			case "":
94				return defaultYes, nil
95			default:
96				fmt.Fprintln(p.out, "  "+p.style.warning("enter y or n"))
97			}
98		}
99	}
100	
101	func (p *prompter) readLine(prefix string) (string, error) {
102		if terminalPair(p.input, p.out) {
103			return runLineEditor(p.input, p.out, prefix)
104		}
105	
106		fmt.Fprint(p.out, prefix)
107		line, err := p.in.ReadString('\n')
108		if err != nil {
109			return "", errPromptCanceled
110		}
111		return line, nil
112	}
113	
114	type fileDescriptor interface {
115		Fd() uintptr
116	}
117	
118	func terminalPair(input io.Reader, output io.Writer) bool {
119		in, inputOK := input.(fileDescriptor)
120		out, outputOK := output.(fileDescriptor)
121		return inputOK && outputOK && term.IsTerminal(in.Fd()) && term.IsTerminal(out.Fd())
122	}
123	
124	type lineEditorModel struct {
125		prefix   string
126		input    textinput.Model
127		done     bool
128		canceled bool
129	}
130	
131	func newLineEditorModel(prefix string) lineEditorModel {
132		input := textinput.New()
133		input.Prompt = prefix
134		input.Focus()
135		return lineEditorModel{prefix: prefix, input: input}
136	}
137	
138	func (m lineEditorModel) Init() tea.Cmd {
139		return textinput.Blink
140	}
141	
142	func (m lineEditorModel) Update(message tea.Msg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
143		if key, ok := message.(tea.KeyMsg); ok {
144			switch key.Type {
145			case tea.KeyEnter:
146				m.done = true
147				m.input.Blur()
148				return m, tea.Quit
149			case tea.KeyEsc, tea.KeyCtrlC:
150				m.done = true
151				m.canceled = true
152				m.input.Blur()
153				return m, tea.Quit
154			}
155		}
156	
157		var command tea.Cmd
158		m.input, command = m.input.Update(message)
159		return m, command
160	}
161	
162	func (m lineEditorModel) View() string {
163		if m.done {
164			// Leave the completed prompt in scrollback. Bubble Tea clears the line
165			// containing its cursor when the renderer stops, so the trailing newline
166			// moves that cursor below the submitted value first.
167			return m.prefix + m.input.Value() + "\n"
168		}
169		return m.input.View()
170	}
171	
172	func runLineEditor(input io.Reader, output io.Writer, prefix string) (string, error) {
173		final, err := tea.NewProgram(
174			newLineEditorModel(prefix),
175			tea.WithInput(input),
176			tea.WithOutput(output),
177		).Run()
178		if err != nil {
179			return "", fmt.Errorf("prompt editor: %w", err)
180		}
181		model, ok := final.(lineEditorModel)
182		if !ok {
183			return "", errors.New("prompt editor returned an unexpected model")
184		}
185		if model.canceled {
186			return "", errPromptCanceled
187		}
188		return model.input.Value(), nil
189	}

31			request, _, confirmed, err := promptRepoCloneWizard(app, p, flags, name, false)
32			return request, confirmed, err
33		}
34		flags.category, err = p.line("Category (optional)", flags.category)
35		if err != nil {
36			return repoWorkflowRequest{}, false, err
37		}
38		defaultDestination, err := repoDestination(app.Cfg.Paths.ProjectRoot, flags.category, name, flags.path)
39		if err != nil {
40			return repoWorkflowRequest{}, false, err
41		}
42		destination, err := p.line("Destination", config.Contract(defaultDestination))
43		if err != nil {
44			return repoWorkflowRequest{}, false, err
45		}
46		flags.path = config.Expand(destination)
47	
48		catalog, _, err := loadRepoScaffoldConfig(app, "", false)
49		if err != nil {
50			return repoWorkflowRequest{}, false, err
51		}
52		defaultPreset := interactiveDefaultPreset(catalog)
53		flags.preset, err = promptScaffoldPreset(p, catalog, defaultPreset)
54		if err != nil {
55			return repoWorkflowRequest{}, false, err
56		}
57		preset, err := catalog.ResolvePreset(flags.preset)
58		if err != nil {
59			return repoWorkflowRequest{}, false, err
60		}
61		flags.description, err = p.line("Description (optional)", flags.description)
62		if err != nil {
63			return repoWorkflowRequest{}, false, err
64		}
65		customize, err := p.confirm("Customize preset and template options?", repoWizardCustomizationSelected(flags) || presetRequiresWizardInput(preset))
66		if err != nil {
67			return repoWorkflowRequest{}, false, err
68		}
69		if customize {
70			templateDefault := preset.Template
71			if flags.template != "" {
72				templateDefault = flags.template
73			}
74			flags.template, err = p.lineWithDisplayFallback(
75				"Template source (optional; local path, Git URL, or owner/repo)",
76				templateDefault,
77				repo.RedactCloneRef(templateDefault),
78			)
79			if err != nil {
80				return repoWorkflowRequest{}, false, err
81			}
82			if strings.EqualFold(strings.TrimSpace(flags.template), "none") {
83				flags.templateRef, flags.templateSubdir = "", ""
84			} else if strings.TrimSpace(flags.template) != "" {
85				refDefault := preset.TemplateRef
86				if flags.templateRef != "" {
87					refDefault = flags.templateRef
88				}
89				flags.templateRef, err = p.line("Template ref (optional branch/tag/commit)", refDefault)
90				if err != nil {
91					return repoWorkflowRequest{}, false, err
92				}
93				subdirDefault := preset.TemplateSubdir
94				if flags.templateSubdir != "" {
95					subdirDefault = flags.templateSubdir
96				}
97				flags.templateSubdir, err = p.line("Template subdirectory (optional)", subdirDefault)
98				if err != nil {
99					return repoWorkflowRequest{}, false, err
100				}
101			}
102			if err := promptScaffoldOptions(p, catalog, flags.preset, &flags); err != nil {
103				return repoWorkflowRequest{}, false, err
104			}
105		}
106		if flags.remote || preset.Remote == "ask" {
107			if err := promptUpstream(app, p, name, &flags); err != nil {
108				return repoWorkflowRequest{}, false, err
109			}
110		}
111		checkInDefault := presetInitialCheckIn(preset)
112		if flags.checkIn != "" && flags.checkIn != string(repoCheckInAuto) {
113			checkInDefault = flags.checkIn
114		}
115		if flags.remote && (flags.checkIn == "" || flags.checkIn == string(repoCheckInAuto)) {
116			flags.checkIn = string(repoCheckInCommit)
117			fmt.Fprintln(p.out, "  check-in     commit (required before publishing)")
118		} else {
119			flags.checkIn, err = promptRepoCheckIn(p, checkInDefault)
120			if err != nil {
121				return repoWorkflowRequest{}, false, err
122			}
123		}
124		handoffDefault := defaultString(flags.handoff, defaultString(preset.Handoff, "cd"))
125		flags.handoff, err = promptRepoHandoff(p, handoffDefault)
126		if err != nil {
127			return repoWorkflowRequest{}, false, err
128		}
129		request, err := buildNewRepoRequest(app, name, flags)
130		if err != nil {
131			return repoWorkflowRequest{}, false, err
132		}
133		fmt.Fprintln(p.out)
134		renderPreparedRepoScaffold(app, request.Prepared)
135		renderRepoWorkflowSummary(app, request)
136		confirmed, err := p.confirm("Create this repository?", true)
137		return request, confirmed, err
138	}

150	func promptRepoCloneWizard(app *App, p *prompter, flags repoBootstrapFlags, ref string, offerSetup bool) (repoWorkflowRequest, bool, bool, error) {
151		name := repoNameFromRef(repo.RedactCloneRef(ref))
152		if name == "" {
153			return repoWorkflowRequest{}, false, false, fmt.Errorf("could not derive a repository name from %q", ref)
154		}
155		category, err := p.line("Category (optional)", flags.category)
156		if err != nil {
157			return repoWorkflowRequest{}, false, false, err
158		}
159		flags.category = category
160		defaultDestination, err := repoDestination(app.Cfg.Paths.ProjectRoot, flags.category, name, flags.path)
161		if err != nil {
162			return repoWorkflowRequest{}, false, false, err
163		}
164		destination, err := p.line("Destination", config.Contract(defaultDestination))
165		if err != nil {
166			return repoWorkflowRequest{}, false, false, err
167		}
168		flags.path = config.Expand(destination)
169		setup := flags.preset != ""
170		if offerSetup && !setup {
171			setup, err = p.confirm("Apply a repository setup preset after cloning?", false)
172			if err != nil {
173				return repoWorkflowRequest{}, false, false, err
174			}
175		}
176		flags.handoff, err = promptRepoHandoff(p, defaultString(flags.handoff, "cd"))
177		if err != nil {
178			return repoWorkflowRequest{}, false, false, err
179		}
180		request, err := buildCloneRepoRequest(app, ref, flags)
181		if err != nil {
182			return repoWorkflowRequest{}, false, false, err
183		}
184		fmt.Fprintln(p.out, "\n"+p.style.title("Summary"))
185		fmt.Fprintf(p.out, "  source       %s\n", repo.RedactCloneRef(ref))
186		fmt.Fprintf(p.out, "  destination  %s\n", config.Contract(request.Destination))
187		if request.Scaffold.Preset != "" {
188			fmt.Fprintf(p.out, "  setup        %s\n", request.Scaffold.Preset)
189		} else {
190			fmt.Fprintf(p.out, "  setup        %t\n", setup)
191		}
192		fmt.Fprintf(p.out, "  handoff      %s\n", request.Handoff)
193		confirmed, err := p.confirm("Clone this repository?", true)
194		return request, setup, confirmed, err
195	}

244		if flags.checkIn != "" && flags.checkIn != string(repoCheckInAuto) {

278	func promptScaffoldPreset(p *prompter, catalog scaffold.Config, fallback string) (string, error) {
279		names := scaffoldPresetNames(catalog)
280		fmt.Fprintln(p.out, p.style.title("Presets:"))
281		for _, name := range names {
282			preset, _ := catalog.ResolvePreset(name)
283			fmt.Fprintf(p.out, "  %-16s %s\n", name, preset.Description)
284		}
285		for {
286			value, err := p.line("Preset", fallback)
287			if err != nil {
288				return "", err
289			}
290			if _, ok := catalog.Presets[value]; ok {
291				return value, nil
292			}
293			fmt.Fprintf(p.out, "  %s\n", p.style.warning("choose one of: "+strings.Join(names, ", ")))
294		}
295	}

297	func promptScaffoldOptions(p *prompter, catalog scaffold.Config, presetName string, flags *repoBootstrapFlags) error {
298		preset, err := catalog.ResolvePreset(presetName)
299		if err != nil {
300			return err
301		}
302		for _, input := range preset.Inputs {
303			label := input.Label
304			if label == "" {
305				label = input.ID
306			}
307			fallback := parseInputDefault(input.Default)
308			switch input.Type {
309			case scaffold.InputBool:
310				value, _ := strconvParseBoolDefault(fallback)
311				chosen, err := p.confirm(label, value)
312				if err != nil {
313					return err
314				}
315				flags.set = replaceSetValue(flags.set, input.ID, fmt.Sprint(chosen))
316			case scaffold.InputChoice:
317				choices := map[string]string{}
318				for _, choice := range input.Choices {
319					choices[strings.ToLower(choice)] = choice
320				}
321				if fallback == "" && len(input.Choices) > 0 {
322					fallback = input.Choices[0]
323				}
324				value, err := p.choice(label+" ("+strings.Join(input.Choices, "/")+")", fallback,
325					strings.Join(input.Choices, ", "), choices)
326				if err != nil {
327					return err
328				}
329				flags.set = replaceSetValue(flags.set, input.ID, value)
330			default:
331				for {
332					value, err := p.line(label, fallback)
333					if err != nil {
334						return err
335					}
336					if input.IsRequired() && strings.TrimSpace(value) == "" {
337						fmt.Fprintln(p.out, "  "+p.style.warning(label+" is required"))
338						continue
339					}
340					flags.set = replaceSetValue(flags.set, input.ID, value)
341					break
342				}
343			}
344		}
345	
346		readme := preset.Readme != nil && *preset.Readme
347		readme, err = p.confirm("Create README.md?", readme)
348		if err != nil {
349			return err
350		}
351		if presetHasItem(preset, "readme") {
352			setSelection(flags, "readme", readme)
353		}
354	
355		gitignoreFallback := strings.Join(preset.Gitignore, ",")
356		gitignore, err := p.line("Gitignore templates (comma-separated, blank for common only)", gitignoreFallback)
357		if err != nil {
358			return err
359		}
360		flags.gitignore = splitCommaValues(gitignore)
361	
362		licenseFallback := preset.License
363		if licenseFallback == "ask" || licenseFallback == "" {
364			licenseFallback = "none"
365		}
366		flags.license, err = p.line("License (none/mit/apache-2.0/...)", licenseFallback)
367		if err != nil {
368			return err
369		}
370		if flags.license != "" && flags.license != "none" {
371			flags.licenseHolder, err = p.line("License holder", flags.licenseHolder)
372			if err != nil {
373				return err
374			}
375		}
376	
377		if preset.ClaudePlans != nil || presetHasItem(preset, "claude-settings") || presetHasItem(preset, "claude-plans-directory") {
378			claudePlans := preset.ClaudePlans != nil && *preset.ClaudePlans
379			claudePlans, err = p.confirm("Keep Claude plans in .claude/plans?", claudePlans)
380			if err != nil {
381				return err
382			}
383			if presetHasItem(preset, "claude-settings") {
384				setSelection(flags, "claude-settings", claudePlans)
385			}
386			if presetHasItem(preset, "claude-plans-directory") {
387				setSelection(flags, "claude-plans-directory", claudePlans)
388			}
389		}
390	
391		if preset.AgentContract != "" || presetHasItem(preset, "agent-contract") {
392			agentContract := preset.AgentContract != "" && preset.AgentContract != "none"
393			agentContract, err = p.confirm("Create AGENTS.md guidance?", agentContract)
394			if err != nil {
395				return err
396			}
397			if presetHasItem(preset, "agent-contract") {
398				setSelection(flags, "agent-contract", agentContract)
399			}
400		}
401	
402		for _, item := range preset.Catalog {
403			selected, err := p.confirm("Enable "+item.Label+"?", item.IsDefault())
404			if err != nil {
405				return err
406			}
407			setSelection(flags, item.ID, selected)
408		}
409		if len(preset.Skills) > 0 {
410			agentDefault := catalog.DefaultAgents
411			if flags.agents != nil {
412				agentDefault = flags.agents
413			}
414			agents, err := p.line("Skill agents (comma-separated)", strings.Join(agentDefault, ","))
415			if err != nil {
416				return err
417			}
418			flags.agents = splitCommaValues(agents)
419			if len(flags.agents) == 0 {
420				return fmt.Errorf("at least one skill agent is required")
421			}
422		}
423		flags.browseSkills, err = p.confirm("Browse additional skills in the upstream installer?", flags.browseSkills)
424		return err
425	}

427	func promptUpstream(app *App, p *prompter, name string, flags *repoBootstrapFlags) error {
428		create, err := p.confirm("Create a GitHub/GitLab upstream?", flags.remote)
429		if err != nil || !create {
430			flags.remote = false
431			return err
432		}
433		ready := forge.ProbeAll(ctxOf())
434		var available []forge.Readiness
435		for _, candidate := range ready {
436			if candidate.Ready() {
437				available = append(available, candidate)
438			} else {
439				fmt.Fprintf(p.out, "  %s: %s (%s)\n", candidate.Forge, candidate.Status, candidate.Action)
440			}
441		}
442		if len(available) == 0 {
443			fmt.Fprintln(p.out, "  "+p.style.warning("no authenticated GitHub or GitLab CLI is ready; creating locally only"))
444			flags.remote = false
445			return nil
446		}
447		selected := available[0].Forge
448		if len(available) > 1 {
449			choices := map[string]string{"github": "github", "gh": "github", "gitlab": "gitlab", "gl": "gitlab"}
450			choice, err := p.choice("Forge (github/gitlab)", string(selected), "github, gitlab", choices)
451			if err != nil {
452				return err
453			}
454			selected = forge.Kind(choice)
455		}
456		flags.remote = true
457		flags.forge = string(selected)
458		flags.namespace, err = p.line("Owner / organization / namespace (optional)", flags.namespace)
459		if err != nil {
460			return err
461		}
462		flags.visibility, err = p.choice("Visibility (private/public/internal)", "private",
463			"private, public, internal", map[string]string{
464				"private": "private", "public": "public", "internal": "internal",
465			})
466		if err != nil {
467			return err
468		}
469		flags.push, err = p.confirm("Push the initial branch?", true)
470		_ = name
471		return err
472	}

483			"commit": "commit", "c": "commit",
484			"stage": "stage", "s": "stage",
485			"none": "none", "n": "none",

490		if preset.InitialCheckIn != "" {
491			return preset.InitialCheckIn
492		}
493		if preset.InitialCommit == nil || *preset.InitialCommit {

499	func repoWizardCustomizationSelected(flags repoBootstrapFlags) bool {
500		return flags.template != "" || flags.templateRef != "" || flags.templateSubdir != "" ||
501			flags.gitignore != nil || flags.license != "" || flags.licenseHolder != "" ||
502			len(flags.set) > 0 || len(flags.enable) > 0 || len(flags.disable) > 0 ||
503			flags.agents != nil || flags.browseSkills || flags.importOrphans
504	}

506	func presetRequiresWizardInput(preset scaffold.Preset) bool {
507		for _, input := range preset.Inputs {
508			if input.IsRequired() && strings.TrimSpace(parseInputDefault(input.Default)) == "" {
509				return true
510			}
511		}
512		return false
513	}

515	func renderRepoWorkflowSummary(app *App, request repoWorkflowRequest) {
516		fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, app.outStyle().title("Repository workflow"))
517		if template := repoTemplateSummary(request.Template); template != nil {
518			selection := template.Source
519			if template.Ref != "" {
520				selection += "@" + template.Ref
521			}
522			if template.Subdir != "" {
523				selection += "//" + template.Subdir
524			}
525			fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "  template   %s (%d files)\n", selection, template.Files)
526			renderRepoTemplateFilePreview(app, request.Template)
527		}
528		checkIn, message := plannedRepoCheckIn(request)
529		if message == "" {
530			fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "  check-in   %s\n", checkIn)
531		} else {
532			fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "  check-in   %s (%s)\n", checkIn, message)
533		}
534		fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "  handoff    %s\n", request.Handoff)
535		if request.Publish == nil {
536			fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "  upstream   local only")
537		} else {
538			fullName := request.Publish.Name
539			if request.Publish.Namespace != "" {
540				fullName = request.Publish.Namespace + "/" + fullName
541			}
542			fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "  upstream   %s:%s (%s, push=%t)\n",
543				request.Publish.Forge, fullName, request.Publish.Visibility, request.Publish.Push)
544		}
545	}
546	
547	func setSelection(flags *repoBootstrapFlags, id string, enabled bool) {
548		flags.enable = removeString(flags.enable, id)
549		flags.disable = removeString(flags.disable, id)
550		if enabled {
551			flags.enable = append(flags.enable, id)
552		} else {
553			flags.disable = append(flags.disable, id)
554		}
555	}
556	
557	func replaceSetValue(values []string, key, value string) []string {
558		prefix := key + "="
559		result := values[:0]
560		for _, existing := range values {
561			if !strings.HasPrefix(existing, prefix) {
562				result = append(result, existing)
563			}
564		}
565		return append(result, prefix+value)
566	}
567	
568	func removeString(values []string, remove string) []string {
569		result := values[:0]
570		for _, value := range values {
571			if value != remove {
572				result = append(result, value)
573			}
574		}
575		return result
576	}
577	
578	func splitCommaValues(value string) []string {
579		var result []string
580		for _, part := range strings.Split(value, ",") {
581			if trimmed := strings.TrimSpace(part); trimmed != "" {
582				result = append(result, trimmed)
583			}
584		}
585		return result
586	}
587	
588	func defaultString(value, fallback string) string {
589		if value != "" {
590			return value
591		}
592		return fallback
593	}
594	
595	func interactiveDefaultPreset(catalog scaffold.Config) string {
596		if len(catalog.Sources) > 1 && catalog.DefaultPreset != "" {
597			return catalog.DefaultPreset
598		}
599		if _, ok := catalog.Presets["agent-ready"]; ok {
600			return "agent-ready"
601		}
602		return catalog.DefaultPreset
603	}
604	
605	func strconvParseBoolDefault(value string) (bool, bool) {

319	// Load reads config.toml over the defaults. A missing file is not an error —
320	// dev must be useful with zero setup. A malformed file is, because silently
321	// falling back to defaults would send worktrees to the wrong volume.
322	func Load(path string) (Config, error) {
323		cfg := Default()
324		if path == "" {
325			path = ConfigFile()
326		}
327		md, err := toml.DecodeFile(path, &cfg)
328		switch {
329		case errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist):
330			return cfg, nil
331		case err != nil:
332			return cfg, fmt.Errorf("read %s: %w", path, err)
333		}
334		if undecoded := md.Undecoded(); len(undecoded) > 0 {
335			// Unknown keys are usually typos ("worktree_dir" vs "worktree_root").
336			// Warn rather than fail so a newer config still works on an older dev.
337			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "dev: warning: unknown key(s) in %s: %v\n", path, undecoded)
338		}
339		cfg.Source = path
340		return cfg, cfg.Validate()
341	}

343	// Validate catches the settings that would otherwise fail deep inside a
344	// worktree create, when a directory has already been made.
345	func (c Config) Validate() error {
346		switch c.Runtime.Backend {
347		case "", "auto", "herdr", "tmux", "zellij", "none":
348		default:
349			return fmt.Errorf("runtime.backend %q: want auto, herdr, tmux, zellij or none", c.Runtime.Backend)
350		}
351		if c.Paths.WorktreePath == "" {
352			return errors.New("paths.worktree_path must not be empty")
353		}
354		if _, err := Render(c.Paths.WorktreePath, c.probeVars()); err != nil {
355			return fmt.Errorf("paths.worktree_path: %w", err)
356		}
357		if err := c.LocalFiles.Limits().Validate(); err != nil {
358			return fmt.Errorf("local_files: %w", err)
359		}
360		switch c.Bootstrap.Layout {
361		case "", "flat", "preserve":
362		default:
363			return fmt.Errorf("bootstrap.layout %q: want flat or preserve", c.Bootstrap.Layout)
364		}
365		if c.Bootstrap.MaxDepth < 0 {
366			return fmt.Errorf("bootstrap.max_depth must be zero (unlimited) or positive")
367		}
368		if c.Forge.RemoteLimit < 0 {
369			return fmt.Errorf("deprecated forge.remote_limit must be zero or positive")
370		}
371		seenAzureTargets := map[string]bool{}
372		for i, target := range c.Forge.AzureDevOps {
373			organization := strings.TrimSpace(target.Organization)
374			project := strings.TrimSpace(target.Project)
375			if !validAzureDevOpsOrganization(organization) {
376				return fmt.Errorf("forge.azure_devops[%d].organization %q: want an Azure DevOps Services URL like https://dev.azure.com/acme", i, target.Organization)
377			}
378			if project == "" {
379				return fmt.Errorf("forge.azure_devops[%d].project must not be empty", i)
380			}
381			key := strings.ToLower(strings.TrimRight(organization, "/") + "/" + project)
382			if seenAzureTargets[key] {
383				return fmt.Errorf("forge.azure_devops[%d] duplicates organization/project %s / %s", i, organization, project)
384			}
385			seenAzureTargets[key] = true
386		}
387		validStrategy := func(v string) bool {
388			switch v {
389			case "", "reinstall", "copy", "link", "skip":
390				return true
391			}
392			return false
393		}
394		if !validStrategy(c.Worktree.Strategy) {
395			return fmt.Errorf("worktree.strategy %q: want reinstall, copy, link or skip", c.Worktree.Strategy)
396		}
397		for ecosystem, strategy := range c.Worktree.Strategies {
398			if !validStrategy(strategy) {
399				return fmt.Errorf("worktree.strategies.%s %q: want reinstall, copy, link or skip",
400					ecosystem, strategy)
401			}
402		}
403		validColumns := map[string]bool{
404			"repo": true, "branch": true, "git": true, "remote": true, "size": true, "live": true,
405			"latest": true, "worktrees": true, "tasks": true, "notes": true,
406			"category": true, "path": true,
407		}
408		for i, column := range c.TUI.Repos.Columns {
409			if !validColumns[column] {
410				return fmt.Errorf("tui.repos.columns[%d] %q: unknown column", i, column)
411			}
412		}
413		switch c.EffectiveRepoSort() {
414		case "activity", "latest", "name", "git", "size", "tasks":
415		default:
416			return fmt.Errorf("tui.repos.sort %q: want activity, latest, name, git, size or tasks", c.TUI.Repos.Sort)
417		}
418		seen := map[string]string{}
419		for i, t := range c.TUI.Tools {
420			switch {
421			case t.Key == "":
422				return fmt.Errorf("tui.tools[%d]: key is required", i)
423			case t.Run == "":
424				return fmt.Errorf("tui.tools[%d] (%s): run is required", i, t.Key)
425			}
426			if binding, ok := ReservedKey(t.Key); ok {
427				return fmt.Errorf("tui.tools[%d]: key %q is the dashboard's %q binding; pick another",
428					i, t.Key, binding)
429			}
430			if prev, ok := seen[t.Key]; ok {
431				return fmt.Errorf("tui.tools[%d]: key %q is already bound to %q", i, t.Key, prev)
432			}
433			seen[t.Key] = t.Name
434		}
435		return nil
436	}

438	func validAzureDevOpsOrganization(raw string) bool {
439		u, err := url.Parse(raw)
440		if err != nil || !strings.EqualFold(u.Scheme, "https") || u.User != nil ||
441			u.RawQuery != "" || u.Fragment != "" || u.Port() != "" {
442			return false
443		}
444		host := strings.ToLower(u.Hostname())
445		segments := strings.FieldsFunc(u.Path, func(r rune) bool { return r == '/' })
446		switch {
447		case host == "dev.azure.com":
448			return len(segments) == 1
449		case strings.HasSuffix(host, ".visualstudio.com"):
450			organization := strings.TrimSuffix(host, ".visualstudio.com")
451			return organization != "" && organization != "vs-ssh" && len(segments) == 0
452		default:
453			return false
454		}
455	}

508	// DiscoveryRoots returns exact repositories first, followed by recursive scan
509	// roots. repo.Discover recognises when a supplied root is itself a repository.
510	func (c Config) DiscoveryRoots() []string {
511		seen := map[string]bool{}
512		out := make([]string, 0, len(c.Paths.RepoPaths)+len(c.Paths.ScanRoots))
513		for _, roots := range [][]string{c.RepoPaths(), c.ScanRoots()} {
514			for _, root := range roots {
515				clean := filepath.Clean(root)
516				if clean == "" || seen[clean] {
517					continue
518				}
519				seen[clean] = true
520				out = append(out, clean)
521			}
522		}
523		return out
524	}

43	// LoadCache returns only a fresh, complete cache. TUI callers that can label
44	// stale rows while refreshing use LoadCacheAny instead.
45	func LoadCache(path string, maxAge time.Duration) (Cache, bool) {
46		c, ok := LoadCacheAny(path)
47		if !ok || !c.Fresh(maxAge) {
48			return Cache{}, false

53	// LoadCacheAny returns a cache regardless of age or completeness. This powers
54	// stale-while-revalidate UI behavior; callers must inspect Fresh/Complete.
55	func LoadCacheAny(path string) (Cache, bool) {
56		info, err := os.Stat(path)
57		if err != nil || info.Size() < 0 || info.Size() > maxCacheBytes {
58			return Cache{}, false
59		}
60		b, err := os.ReadFile(path)
61		if err != nil {
62			return Cache{}, false

64		var c Cache

66			return Cache{}, false
67		}
68		if c.Version == 0 {
69			// Version 1 caches were valid snapshots but capped per provider, so they
70			// are useful for instant display and must immediately be refreshed.
71			c.Complete = false
72		}
73		return c, true
74	}

78			c.FetchedAt.After(now.Add(maxCacheClockSkew)) || len(c.Repos) > maxCachedRepos ||

119	func (c Cache) Fresh(maxAge time.Duration) bool {
120		if c.Version != CacheVersion || !c.Complete {
121			return false
122		}
123		if maxAge <= 0 {
124			return true
125		}
126		if len(c.Providers) == 0 {

128		}
129		for _, provider := range c.Providers {
130			if !provider.Complete || provider.Error != "" || provider.FetchedAt.IsZero() || time.Since(provider.FetchedAt) > maxAge {
131				return false
132			}
133		}
134		return true

137	// SaveCache atomically replaces the cache. A partial forge response may be
138	// cached — its FetchedAt still says exactly when it was observed.
139	func SaveCache(path string, repos []RemoteRepo) error {
140		now := time.Now().UTC()
141		providers := map[Kind]ProviderStatus{}
142		for _, repo := range repos {
143			providers[repo.Forge] = ProviderStatus{FetchedAt: now, Complete: true}
144		}
145		return SaveCacheState(path, Cache{Version: CacheVersion, FetchedAt: now, Complete: true, Providers: providers, Repos: repos})
146	}
147	
148	// SaveCacheState atomically replaces the versioned inventory cache.
149	func SaveCacheState(path string, cache Cache) error {
150		return SaveCacheStateContext(context.Background(), path, cache)
151	}
152	
153	// SaveCacheStateContext serializes one cache target and checks cancellation
154	// while holding that ordering boundary. A superseded generation therefore
155	// cannot rename after a newer generation has committed.
156	func SaveCacheStateContext(ctx context.Context, path string, cache Cache) error {
157		if path == "" {
158			return errors.New("empty cache path")
159		}
160		if ctx == nil {
161			ctx = context.Background()
162		}
163		lock := cacheWriteLock(path)
164		lock.Lock()
165		defer lock.Unlock()
166		if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
167			return err
168		}
169		if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(path), 0o755); err != nil {
170			return err
171		}
172		if cache.Version == 0 {
173			cache.Version = CacheVersion
174		}
175		if cache.FetchedAt.IsZero() {
176			cache.FetchedAt = time.Now().UTC()
177		}
178		b, err := json.MarshalIndent(cache, "", "  ")
179		if err != nil {
180			return err
181		}
182		b = append(b, '\n')
183		tmp, err := os.CreateTemp(filepath.Dir(path), ".remotes-*.tmp")
184		if err != nil {
185			return err
186		}
187		name := tmp.Name()
188		defer os.Remove(name)
189		if _, err := tmp.Write(b); err != nil {
190			tmp.Close()
191			return err
192		}
193		if err := tmp.Close(); err != nil {
194			return err
195		}
196		if err := os.Chmod(name, 0o600); err != nil {
197			return err
198		}
199		if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
200			return err
201		}
202		return os.Rename(name, path)
203	}
204	
205	func cacheWriteLock(path string) *sync.Mutex {
206		loaded, _ := cacheWriteLocks.LoadOrStore(filepath.Clean(path), &sync.Mutex{})
207		return loaded.(*sync.Mutex)
208	}

213		_, err := os.Stat(path)
214		return err == nil || !errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist)
215	}

600						string(r.Repo.Forge), r.Repo.FullName, r.Repo.Description,
601						r.Repo.Visibility, r.LocalName,

612					}
613				}
614				sort.SliceStable(filtered, func(i, j int) bool {

626					enc.SetIndent("", "  ")

628						return encodeErr

630				} else {

648					} else {

650					}
651				}
652				if err != nil {
653					app.warnf("partial remote results: %v", err)
654				}
655				return nil
656			},
657		}
658		f := cmd.Flags()

250		if !f.Available() {

265		defer cancel()
266		if _, err := probeRunner(probeCtx, f.Bin(), "", args...); err != nil {
267			if probeCtx.Err() != nil {

269				result.Detail = probeCtx.Err().Error()
270				result.Action = "run `" + f.Bin() + " auth status` to diagnose the provider CLI"
271				return result

274			result.Detail = err.Error()

339	func resolveRepoRequest(req RepoRequest) (repoTarget, error) {
340		fullName := strings.Trim(strings.TrimSpace(req.FullName), "/")
341		name := strings.Trim(strings.TrimSpace(req.Name), "/")
342		namespace := strings.Trim(strings.TrimSpace(req.Namespace), "/")
343		if fullName == "" {
344			fullName = name
345			if namespace != "" && !strings.Contains(name, "/") {
346				fullName = namespace + "/" + name
347			}
348		}
349		if fullName == "" {
350			return repoTarget{}, errors.New("repository name is required")
351		}
352		if strings.Contains(fullName, "://") || strings.HasPrefix(fullName, "git@") {
353			return repoTarget{}, fmt.Errorf("repository name %q must not be a URL", fullName)
354		}
355		parts := strings.Split(fullName, "/")
356		for _, part := range parts {
357			if part == "" || part == "." || part == ".." {
358				return repoTarget{}, fmt.Errorf("invalid repository name %q", fullName)
359			}
360		}
361		name = parts[len(parts)-1]
362		if len(parts) > 1 {
363			namespace = strings.Join(parts[:len(parts)-1], "/")
364		}
365	
366		visibility := req.Visibility
367		if visibility == "" {
368			if req.Private {
369				visibility = VisibilityPrivate
370			} else {
371				visibility = VisibilityPublic
372			}
373		}
374		switch visibility {
375		case VisibilityPublic, VisibilityPrivate, VisibilityInternal:
376		default:
377			return repoTarget{}, fmt.Errorf("unsupported repository visibility %q", visibility)
378		}
379		remoteName := strings.TrimSpace(req.RemoteName)
380		if remoteName == "" {
381			remoteName = "origin"
382		}
383		return repoTarget{
384			name: name, namespace: namespace, fullName: fullName,
385			visibility: visibility, remoteName: remoteName,
386		}, nil
387	}

400			host := defaultForgeHost(kind)
401			if host != "" {

403			}
404		}
405		webURL = strings.TrimSuffix(strings.TrimRight(webURL, "/"), ".git")
406		cloneURL := ""
407		sshURL := ""
408		if parsed, err := url.Parse(webURL); err == nil && parsed.Host != "" {
409			path := strings.Trim(strings.TrimSuffix(parsed.Path, ".git"), "/")
410			cloneURL = strings.TrimRight(webURL, "/") + ".git"
411			sshURL = "git@" + parsed.Host + ":" + path + ".git"
412		}
413		name := target.name

417		return CreateRepoResult{
418			Forge: kind, Name: name, FullName: fullName, URL: webURL,

420			RemoteName: target.remoteName,

441	type cliRunner func(context.Context, string, string, ...string) (string, error)
442	
443	// Separate hooks keep readiness and publishing tests platform-independent;
444	// production uses the same subprocess runner as the legacy adapter methods.
445	var (
446		probeRunner   cliRunner = run
447		publishRunner cliRunner = runCombined
448		lookupPath              = exec.LookPath
449	)
450	
451	// run executes a forge CLI, streaming stderr through so the user sees the
452	// CLI's own authentication prompts and error messages verbatim.
453	func run(ctx context.Context, bin, dir string, args ...string) (string, error) {
454		cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, bin, args...)
455		cmd.Dir = dir
456		var stdout, stderr bytes.Buffer
457		cmd.Stdout = &stdout
458		cmd.Stderr = &stderr
459		cmd.Stdin = os.Stdin
460		if err := cmd.Run(); err != nil {
461			detail := strings.TrimSpace(stderr.String())
462			if detail != "" {
463				return strings.TrimSpace(stdout.String()), fmt.Errorf("%s %s: %s: %w",
464					bin, strings.Join(args, " "), detail, err)
465			}
466			return strings.TrimSpace(stdout.String()), fmt.Errorf("%s %s: %w", bin, strings.Join(args, " "), err)
467		}
468		return strings.TrimSpace(stdout.String()), nil
469	}
470	
471	// runCombined is used for non-interactive publishing because gh/glab versions
472	// differ on whether the created repository URL is written to stdout or stderr.
473	// Stdin is deliberately left closed so a supposedly complete publish request
474	// cannot unexpectedly drop into a second provider-owned wizard.
475	func runCombined(ctx context.Context, bin, dir string, args ...string) (string, error) {
476		cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, bin, args...)
477		cmd.Dir = dir
478		var stdout, stderr bytes.Buffer
479		cmd.Stdout = &stdout
480		cmd.Stderr = &stderr
481		if err := cmd.Run(); err != nil {
482			detail := strings.TrimSpace(stderr.String())
483			if detail != "" {
484				return strings.TrimSpace(stdout.String()), fmt.Errorf("%s %s: %s: %w",
485					bin, strings.Join(args, " "), detail, err)
486			}
487			return strings.TrimSpace(stdout.String()), fmt.Errorf("%s %s: %w", bin, strings.Join(args, " "), err)
488		}
489		return strings.TrimSpace(strings.TrimSpace(stdout.String()) + "\n" + strings.TrimSpace(stderr.String())), nil
490	}

494		return err == nil
495	}

497	func lastHTTPURL(out string) string {
498		var found string
499		for _, field := range strings.Fields(out) {
500			candidate := strings.Trim(field, "<>()[]{}\"',;.")
501			if strings.HasPrefix(candidate, "http://") || strings.HasPrefix(candidate, "https://") {
502				found = candidate
503			}
504		}
505		return found
506	}

508	// IdentityFromURL returns a forge and decoded owner/name identity for a
509	// structurally valid HTTPS or SSH Git remote. Query, fragment, and userinfo are
510	// never part of the returned identity.
511	func IdentityFromURL(raw string) (Kind, string) {
512		if identity, _, ok := parseAzureDevOpsRemote(raw); ok {
513			return AzureDevOps, identity
514		}
515		endpoint, ok := parseForgeEndpoint(raw)
516		if !ok {
517			return Unknown, ""
518		}
519		kind := webHostPolicy(WebURLRequest{}).identityProvider(endpoint.host)
520		if kind == Unknown || !validRepositorySegments(kind, endpoint.segments) {
521			return Unknown, ""
522		}
523		segments := stripGitSuffix(endpoint.segments)
524		if segments == nil {
525			return Unknown, ""
526		}
527		return kind, strings.Join(segments, "/")
528	}

7	### P1 · L — Verified backup receipts and safe local eviction
8	Phase 1 intentionally stops at reversible archive. Before adding `dev reclaim`
9	or any action that deletes a local checkout, build a fresh preflight that checks
10	all local heads/tags/notes/stash against actual remote refs, plus dirty,
11	untracked, ignored, LFS, submodule/nested-repo, live-runtime, task, cwd and
12	linked-worktree state. `no remote` or any local-only ref must block safe

18	remote/shared-Git restore. Non-Git experiments need a real archive/export
19	format before they can be called recoverable. Do not infer safety merely from

23	The backward-compatible retirement MVP derives READY/MERGED/RETIRED while

25	separate execution disposition from integration phase, adopt strict versioned
26	decoding plus cross-process update locks, and explicitly migrate ambiguous
27	legacy done records. Old binaries currently ignore and later erase unknown TOML
28	fields, so this requires a deliberate minimum-version/downgrade policy.

31	Persist PR/MR identity and extend forge adapters to report open/draft/merged
32	state, merge commit and method. Until then `done --merged` proves ordinary
33	ancestry and squash completion requires explicit operator attestation; never
34	infer a squash solely because the source branch disappeared.

36	### P2 · M — Incremental local repo snapshot
37	The TUI now renders immediately and probes repositories in the background with
38	bounded concurrency, reducing perceived startup latency. A 56-repo refresh
39	still takes roughly three seconds because status + latest commit remain live Git
40	queries. If inventories grow into the hundreds, persist a short-lived snapshot
41	and stream changed rows into the model; keep `r` as the explicit live refresh.

44	Research and detect repo-local task stores without making either a core

48	- beads: <https://github.com/gastownhall/beads>

50	Both may create dot-folders inside a repo. An adapter should report which
51	backend is present, delegate through its CLI, and avoid copying its task data
52	into dev's own notes/tasks. Decide only after comparing lifecycle, multi-agent
53	locking, git noise, cross-machine sync, archival and uninstall behavior. Until
54	then, record the integration point rather than prematurely selecting a tool.

57	A `tv` channel over `dev ls --json` for fuzzy-picking a task, and an `fzf`
58	fallback. Navigation by metadata rather than by remembering a path is the point

61	### P3 · S — `dev stats` per-repo heatmap
62	`--repo X` currently filters the totals and the combined grid. A dedicated
63	per-repo grid, several stacked, would answer "which project did I move to in

70	## Deliberately not doing
71	
72	### Installing dependencies
73	`dev doctor` reports what is missing and what degrades; it will not install
74	anything. This is the one place where being glue matters most: git, herdr,
75	tmux, gh, glab, lazygit and yazi are all installed by a package manager the
76	user already has opinions about (brew, apt, mise, nix, chezmoi), and a tool
77	that shells out to one of them is guessing. `doctor` naming the missing binary
78	is enough — the user knows how they install things on that machine.

84	Anything derivable from git is derived live, every run. Durable stores hold

87	past verification, but apply must verify again. Live branches, remotes,

230	## Configuration
231	
232	```bash
233	dev config init
234	dev config show
235	dev config path
236	dev config scaffolds init
237	dev config scaffolds show
238	dev config scaffolds path
239	dev config scaffolds edit
240	```
241	
242	`config init` detects local roots and writes explicit defaults. A missing config file is allowed; the built-in defaults keep core Git behavior usable, but generated config is recommended because it makes machine policy reviewable.
243	
244	Key sections:
245	
246	| Section | Controls |
247	|---|---|
248	| `[paths]` | scan roots, project/tries/worktree roots, worktree template, state path |
249	| `[runtime]` | `auto`, Herdr, tmux, Zellij, or none plus metadata settings |
250	| `[worktree]` | local ignored-file provisioning, linked dirs, setup commands, strategies, timeout |
251	| `[local_files]` | host ceilings for portable files; project overlays provide the separate off-machine candidate allowlist |
252	| `[forge]` / `[[forge.azure_devops]]` | complete remote inventory cache TTL and opt-in Azure organization/project targets |
253	| `[bootstrap]` | recursion, symlink handling, index/layout policy |
254	| `[tui]` / `[[tui.tools]]` | columns, sorting, and external-tool bindings |
255	| `[stats]` | sampler and optional WakaTime import |
256	| `[update]` | `check` (default `true`) — allow the once-a-day "newer release available" hint and its background cache refresh; `DEV_NO_UPDATE_CHECK` overrides it |
257	
258	`DEV_TUI_TRACE=/absolute/new-file.json` enables a one-run TUI startup/readiness
259	trace. The target must be absolute and must not exist; dev never overwrites it.
260	The private bounded document is written after TUI teardown and contains relative
261	categorical timings plus aggregate row counts rather than names, paths, or raw
262	payloads. It is not configuration,
263	cache, durable stats, stdout, or network telemetry. For TUI invocations, the
264	optional update-cache network refresh is also deferred until the initial view
265	has returned.
266	
267	Repository quick-note Markdown is durable under configured `paths.state_dir/notes`, which defaults to `$XDG_DATA_HOME/dev/notes`. The full-text index at `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/dev/notes.db` is disposable and rebuilds from those files; changing `paths.state_dir` does not move the cache.
268	
269	### Scaffold presets
270	
271	Global repository recipes live at `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/dev/scaffolds.toml` (or
272	the root `--scaffolds` override). Every authored file declares `version = 1`.
273	A compact preset looks like:
274	
275	```toml
276	version = 1
277	default_preset = "team"
278	default_agents = ["claude-code", "codex"]
279	
280	[presets.team]
281	extends = "agent-ready"
282	handoff = "cd"
283	initial_check_in = "stage"
284	template = "acme/starter-catalog"
285	template_ref = "v2"
286	template_subdir = "services/go"
287	
288	[[presets.team.inputs]]
289	id = "deployment"
290	type = "choice"
291	choices = ["none", "docker"]
292	default = "none"
293	
294	[[presets.team.files]]
295	id = "service-readme"
296	source = "service/README.md" # templates/service/README.md beside this file
297	destination = "docs/service.md"
298	
299	[[presets.team.hooks]]
300	id = "verify"
301	phase = "before_commit"
302	command = ["make", "test"]
303	required = true
304	
305	[[presets.team.skills]]
306	id = "knowledge"
307	source = "daviddwlee84/agent-skills/skills"
308	name = "project-knowledge-harness"
309	agents = ["claude-code", "codex"]
310	default = true
311	
312	[presets.team.skills.setup]
313	phase = "before_commit"
314	interpreter = "bash"
315	script = "scripts/init.sh"
316	args = ["--target", "{{path}}", "--project-name", "{{name}}"]
317	required = true
318	```
319	
320	Skill setup normally names a project-local script inside the installed skill.
321	The shipped recommendations instead use `builtin = "agent-history-hygiene"` or
322	`builtin = "project-knowledge-harness"`; these fixed reviewed initializers do
323	not execute downloaded skill code.
324	
325	A preset may extend one parent. Scalars override; simple lists replace; files,
326	hooks, and skills merge by `id`, and an inherited item can be disabled with
327	`enabled = false`. A `[[presets.*.files]]` rendering source must remain in the
328	`templates/` tree next to its config source; that file-level mechanism is
329	separate from the repository snapshot `template` scalar above. Destinations
330	must remain inside the repository, and a skill setup script must remain inside
331	the installed skill directory. `initial_check_in` accepts `commit`, `stage`, or
332	`none`; the legacy `initial_commit` boolean remains readable, but a preset must
333	not set both.
334	
335	### Safe project overlays
336	
337	A repository may commit these fixed files:
338	
339	- `.dev-cli/config.toml`: allowlisted worktree provisioning, separately
340	  proposed portable local-file patterns, and repository setup wizard defaults.
341	- `.dev-cli/scaffolds.toml`: project presets, templates, hooks, and skill
342	  setup using the same versioned schema.
343	
344	```toml
345	# .dev-cli/config.toml
346	version = 1
347	
348	[worktree]
349	include = [".env.example"]
350	strategy = "reinstall"
351	
352	# Proposed candidates only; export still requires explicit fleet files --to.
353	[local_files]
354	include = [".env", ".mcp/**"]
355	
356	[repo.setup]
357	preset = "team"
358	handoff = "cd"
359	check_in = "stage"
360	```
361	
362	Effective precedence, lowest to highest, is built-ins, global config/scaffolds,
363	legacy `.dev.toml`, the target repository's `.dev-cli/*`, then explicit CLI or
364	wizard choices. `.dev.toml` remains readable for compatibility; new project
365	configuration should use `.dev-cli/config.toml`. Global `default_preset` and the
366	project `[repo.setup]` preset, handoff, and check-in fields seed interactive
367	wizard choices; they do not change scripted defaults, which are controlled by
368	the corresponding flags. The legacy `commit` boolean remains readable, but may
369	not be combined with `check_in` in the same layer.
370	
371	`[local_files].include` never inherits `[worktree].include`: provisioning a local checkout is not authorization to export a secret. Project overlays may propose only the portable include list; host-owned count/size/path ceilings come from global config and cannot be raised by a repository. The command remains report-only until an explicit `--apply`, target pin, and confirmation.
372	
373	Project files cannot override host paths, state location, runtime backend,
374	forge inventory or credentials, stats, update, bootstrap, or TUI policy. They
375	also cannot silently publish a repository. Before a post-create command from
376	`.dev-cli/config.toml`, or a hook or skill setup from project
377	`.dev-cli/scaffolds.toml`, executes, dev asks to trust the canonical repository
378	plus an execution-content hash. Changed executable content requires new
379	consent; non-interactive use without a matching trust record fails closed.
380	Legacy `.dev.toml` retains its compatibility behavior. Keep credentials and
381	host-specific paths in user config or ignored environment files, never in a
382	committed project overlay.
383	
384	Project-authored skill setup must use a local source so its bytes can be bound
385	to the trust hash. Remote project skills may still be installed, but cannot
386	declare executable setup; global presets remain host-owned policy.
387	
388	## Colored output
389	
390	Every human-readable surface applies semantic ANSI color through a small set of roles: `title`/`header`/`prompt` (bold cyan), `label`/`dim` (dim), `success` (green), `warning` (yellow), `danger` (bold red), `review` (magenta, for a PR/review handoff), and `strong`/`code` for Markdown. Values that carry their own meaning are colored by that meaning rather than by a fixed role:
391	
392	| Value | Green | Yellow | Red |
393	|---|---|---|---|
394	| Git status | `clean` | `dirty`, `ahead`, `behind`, `no checkout` | `conflict`, `error` |
395	| Task state | `hot`, `done` | `warm`, `cold`, `parked` | — |
396	| Fleet host | `ok` | `stale`, `no-dev` | `unreachable`, `timeout`, `incompatible` |
397	| Skill update | `current` | `update` | `missing`, `failed` |
398	| Artifact intent | `finalized` | `armed`, `finalizing` | `failed` |
399
