1	# Repository bootstrap
2	
3	`dev repo new`, `repo clone`, and `repo setup` share one scaffold pipeline. A
4	plain name creates a new repository. A clear Git URL, local Git path, or
5	`owner/name` passed to either `repo new` or its `create` alias routes to clone
6	automatically, preserving source history and its remote. Template and
7	upstream-creation flags conflict with that route; use explicit `repo clone`
8	whenever callers should state acquisition unambiguously.
9	
10	```bash
11	dev repo new                              # interactive
12	dev repo create api                       # minimal, script-friendly
13	dev repo new api --template owner/starter --check-in=stage
14	dev repo clone owner/api                  # optional setup after clone
15	dev repo setup . --preset agent-ready --check-in=stage
16	```
17	
18	The interactive default is `agent-ready`; explicit `repo new NAME` remains
19	`minimal`. Use `--dry-run` before a custom preset and `--json` for automation.
20	Dry-run does not mutate the target repository. JSON never prompts, changes
21	directory, or activates a runtime; automation supplies the required name/ref
22	and an explicit setup preset.
23	
24	`repo setup` repeat-safely merges native initializers and preset files. Custom
25	hooks and skill setup remain responsible for their own idempotency.
26	
27	The no-argument create/setup wizards keep the common path short. After preset
28	selection they ask `Customize preset ... options?` once. Answering no accepts
29	the resolved preset and skips its detailed template, typed-input,
30	README/gitignore/license, Claude plans, AGENTS, skill and catalog questions.
31	The gate defaults to yes when the command line already selected a customization
32	or a required typed input has no default. This changes prompt volume, not preset
33	resolution: supplied flags still participate in the final plan.
34	
35	On a real terminal, every shared wizard text field uses an inline editor.
36	Cursor keys, Home/End, Backspace and Delete edit the current text rather than
37	being decoded as literal `^[[C`/`^[[D` bytes. Esc and Ctrl-C cancel. Bracketed
38	defaults remain hints accepted by Enter rather than text silently inserted into
39	the field. Non-TTY and piped callers retain deterministic line-based input.
40	
41	## Template snapshots
42	
43	Only `repo new` accepts a starter tree:
44	
45	```bash
46	dev repo new api --template ./starters/service
47	dev repo new api --template owner/starter --template-ref v2 \
48	  --template-subdir services/go
49	```
50	
51	`--template` accepts a local directory, Git URL, or forge shorthand.
52	`--template-ref` selects an exact branch, tag, or commit;
53	`--template-subdir` promotes one relative directory to the new repository root.
54	A preset may provide `template`, `template_ref`, and `template_subdir`, and an
55	explicit `--template=none` disables that preset source.
56	
57	This is intentionally not clone semantics. dev takes a content snapshot and
58	then initializes a fresh repository, so source commits, remotes, branches and
59	all `.git` metadata stay behind. Source selection is:
60	
61	- A local Git worktree without `--template-ref` uses its current tracked files
62	  plus untracked files selected by Git's standard excludes. Ignored files are
63	  omitted, so build output and locally ignored secrets are not accidentally
64	  copied.
65	- A non-Git local directory uses its complete current regular-file tree.
66	- A local Git source with a ref, or a remote Git source, uses the tree at the
67	  resolved commit.
68	
69	Use `repo clone` when source history and its remote should survive. Credential
70	userinfo embedded in an HTTP(S) or similar URL is available to Git for the
71	fetch but is redacted anywhere dev renders, returns, or wraps that source.
72	
73	Preparation finishes before destination mutation. The snapshot owns stable
74	copies of file bytes, modes and empty directories; a local source changing
75	during the read fails closed. Parent traversal, absolute subdirectories,
76	symlinks, special files and reserved `.git` paths are rejected. Snapshot and
77	application traverse through held root, directory, and file handles rather
78	than re-resolving trusted string prefixes, so a directory-to-symlink or rename
79	race cannot redirect access outside the selected trees.
80	
81	Application requires a newly initialized repository containing only Git
82	metadata, uses exclusive file creation, and confines every target below its
83	held destination root. Template files are materialized before scaffold files,
84	so preset file generation skips collisions instead of overwriting the selected
85	starter; native merge initializers may still merge their specific safe
86	settings.
87	
88	`--dry-run` never creates the target, but preparing a remote template may still
89	fetch it into an isolated temporary checkout so the plan can report the exact
90	resolved commit and content counts. Human plans preview a bounded list of
91	quoted relative file paths plus a remaining count. A local snapshot with no
92	resolved commit is explicitly labelled as live current files and should be
93	reviewed before check-in or publication.
94	
95	## Check-in disposition
96	
97	Repository acquisition, generated content, and Git check-in are separate
98	decisions:
99	
100	```bash
101	dev repo new api --check-in=commit
102	dev repo new api --check-in=stage --message "chore: initial commit"
103	dev repo setup . --preset agent-ready --check-in=none
104	```
105	
106	`--check-in` accepts:
107	
108	- `auto`: for a new repository, use preset `initial_check_in`; legacy
109	  `initial_commit=true|false` maps to `commit|none`. Clone/setup preserve
110	  existing history and otherwise resolve `auto` to `none`.
111	- `commit`: run `git add -A`, create the commit, and then run `after_commit`
112	  skill/hook phases.
113	- `stage`: run `git add -A` after files, selected skills, built-in setup and
114	  `before_commit` hooks, but leave the commit for the user. `after_commit` does
115	  not run.
116	- `none`: leave generated changes unstaged.
117	
118	`repo setup --commit` remains a compatibility alias for
119	`--check-in=commit`; combining it with `stage` or `none` is an error. The
120	`--message` value applies to both committed and staged-for-review outcomes.
121	Project config can seed an existing-repository wizard with
122	`[repo.setup] check_in = "stage"`; it cannot set both `check_in` and the legacy
123	`commit` boolean.
124	
125	Stage mode seeds `<worktree-git-dir>/LAZYGIT_PENDING_COMMIT` with the suggested
126	message. Lazygit's lowercase `c` reads this private per-worktree draft and
127	clears it after a successful commit. It is deliberately best effort:
128	
129	- Git's `.git/COMMIT_EDITMSG` and `commit.template` are different mechanisms;
130	  lazygit's `c` does not use them.
131	- Lazygit's uppercase `C` editor path and other Git clients are not promised to
132	  read the draft. From lowercase `c`, switching to the editor preserves the
133	  already loaded text.
134	- A pre-existing different draft is user state, so dev leaves it untouched and
135	  warns instead of replacing it.
136	- Failure to create or sync this optional draft is also only a warning. The
137	  successfully staged index remains the result; enter the displayed message
138	  manually rather than rerunning setup.
139	
140	Creating an upstream from `repo setup` requires `commit`. A newly created
141	upstream can only be pushed after `commit`, while `stage` cannot be combined
142	with new-upstream creation at all. An existing clone remote does not prevent
143	local stage-for-review. `start` also requires a clean committed setup; use
144	`cd` or `open` while reviewing staged changes.
145	
146	## Configuration and trust
147	
148	Global presets live in `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/dev/scaffolds.toml`. A target repo may
149	override portable setup behavior with `.dev-cli/config.toml` and
150	`.dev-cli/scaffolds.toml`. It cannot change host paths, runtime, state, forge
151	inventory, stats, update or TUI policy.
152	
153	Project-owned hooks and skill setup entrypoints from `.dev-cli/scaffolds.toml`,
154	plus worktree post-create commands from `.dev-cli/config.toml`, are keyed by
155	canonical Git identity plus a SHA-256 of executable configuration. Legacy
156	`.dev.toml` retains its compatibility behavior. Review the plan and approve the
157	exact hash:
158	
159	```bash
160	dev config show --project
161	dev config trust . --yes
162	```
163	
164	A changed hash must be reviewed again. Pre-commit and gitleaks protect committed
165	bytes; they do not authorize command execution.
166	
167	## Skills and publication
168	
169	Selecting a setup-capable skill installs it in project scope. Custom global or
170	local presets can run a declared script below the installed skill directory in
171	the declared phase; project-authored executable setup is restricted to local,
172	content-hashed sources. For `agent-history-hygiene` and
173	`project-knowledge-harness`, dev uses reviewed built-in initializers for the
174	pre-commit/gitleaks and TODO/backlog/pitfalls surfaces instead of executing newly
175	downloaded skill code.
176	
177	The built-in `agent-history-hygiene` setup creates these files when absent:
178	
179	```text
180	.pre-commit-config.yaml
181	.gitleaks.toml
182	.specstory/.gitignore
183	```
184	
185	The nested SpecStory ignore is intentionally narrow: it ignores only
186	`.specstory/.project.json` (machine-local project identity) and
187	`.specstory/statistics.json` (generated session statistics). It does not ignore
188	`.specstory/history/*.md`; transcripts remain durable review artifacts that
189	belong beside the changes they produced. When `.specstory/.gitignore` already
190	exists, dev preserves its custom lines and permission mode and idempotently
191	appends only missing required rules. Symlink or special-file replacements are
192	rejected. A top-level rule that ignores all of `.specstory/` still wins, so
193	remove or correct that broader rule when transcript history is intended to be
194	committed.
195	
196	The wizard only offers GitHub/GitLab publication when the matching CLI is
197	installed and authenticated. Publication uses the local repository name and
198	configured description, follows required local commit steps, and optionally
199	pushes the initial/current branch. A create, remote-add, or push failure leaves
200	local work intact.
201	
202	Handoff is explicit: `stay`, `cd`, `open`, or `start`. `start` enters the normal
203	task wizard. None of these choices launches a coding agent.
204

132		if rt := a.runtimesByName[name]; rt != nil {
133			return rt
134		}

136			return a.runtimeInstance

156	// cdDirective asks the shell wrapper to move its parent process. The wrapper
157	// gives dev a child-only file descriptor so normal output stays connected to
158	// the terminal and an inherited environment variable can never name a file to
159	// overwrite. NUL terminates the path because filesystem paths may contain
160	// newlines. Without the wrapper, retain the printable directive used by older
161	// integrations.
162	func (a *App) cdDirective(dir string) error {
163		// Windows shells do not inherit an extra descriptor the way the POSIX
164		// wrapper's `3>file` redirection does, so the PowerShell wrapper names a
165		// temp file instead and reads it back after dev exits.
166		if path := os.Getenv("DEV_SHELL_CD_FILE"); path != "" {
167			return os.WriteFile(path, append([]byte(dir), 0), 0o600)
168		}
169		if rawFD := os.Getenv("DEV_SHELL_CD_FD"); rawFD != "" {
170			fd, err := strconv.Atoi(rawFD)
171			if err != nil || fd < 3 {
172				return fmt.Errorf("invalid DEV_SHELL_CD_FD %q", rawFD)
173			}
174			file := os.NewFile(uintptr(fd), "dev-shell-cd")
175			if file == nil {
176				return fmt.Errorf("invalid shell directory descriptor %d", fd)
177			}
178			if _, err := file.Write(append([]byte(dir), 0)); err != nil {
179				return fmt.Errorf("write shell directory directive: %w", err)
180			}
181			if err := file.Close(); err != nil {
182				return fmt.Errorf("close shell directory directive: %w", err)
183			}
184			return nil
185		}
186		_, err := fmt.Fprintf(a.Out, "cd %s\n", shellQuote(dir))
187		return err
188	}

190			fmt.Fprint(previous, renderCobraHelp(buf.String(), app.outStyle()))
191		})
192		enforceUsageErrors(root)
193		annotateHelp(root)
194		return root
195	}
196	
197	// Execute runs the CLI and maps errors to exit codes. SilenceErrors and
198	// SilenceUsage are set on the root, so nothing reaches the terminal unless it
199	// is printed here; ExecuteC hands back the command that failed so a usage
200	// mistake can be answered with that command's usage rather than the root's.
201	func Execute() int {
202		trace, tracePath, traceErr := traceFromEnvironment()
203		app := &App{
204			In: os.Stdin, Out: os.Stdout, Err: os.Stderr,
205			trace: trace, tracePath: tracePath, traceOnce: &sync.Once{},
206		}
207		if traceErr != nil {
208			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "dev: warning: performance trace disabled: %v\n", traceErr)
209		}
210		app.trace.Mark(perftrace.CLIExecuteBegin, perftrace.Fields{})
211		defer app.finishTrace()
212	
213		sweepStaleUpgradeArtifacts()
214		finishRoot := app.trace.Start(perftrace.CLIRootBuild, perftrace.Fields{})
215		root := newRootCommand(app)
216		finishRoot(perftrace.OutcomeSuccess)
217		cmd, err := root.ExecuteC()
218		if err == nil {
219			return 0
220		}
221		style := styleForWriter(os.Stderr, colorModeFromArgs(os.Args[1:]))
222		fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, style.danger("dev:")+" "+err.Error())
223		if cmd != nil && wantsUsage(err) {
224			fmt.Fprint(os.Stderr, renderCobraHelp(cmd.UsageString(), style))
225		}
226		return 1
227	}
228

120	func renderStarterConfig(l config.Layout) string {
121		roots := make([]string, len(l.ScanRoots))
122		for i, r := range l.ScanRoots {
123			roots[i] = strconv.Quote(filepath.ToSlash(r))
124		}
125		r := strings.NewReplacer(
126			"@@SCAN_ROOTS@@", strings.Join(roots, ", "),
127			"@@REPO_PATHS@@", quotedStrings(l.RepoPaths),
128			"@@TRIES_ROOT@@", filepath.ToSlash(l.TriesRoot),
129			"@@PROJECT_ROOT@@", filepath.ToSlash(l.ProjectRoot),
130			"@@WORKTREE_ROOT@@", filepath.ToSlash(l.WorktreeRoot),
131		)
132		return r.Replace(starterConfig)
133	}
134	
135	func quotedStrings(values []string) string {
136		quoted := make([]string, len(values))
137		for index, value := range values {
138			quoted[index] = strconv.Quote(filepath.ToSlash(value))
139		}
140		return strings.Join(quoted, ", ")
141	}

```text
1	---
2	description: Inventory repositories over SSH, pin remote machine identity, safely fast-forward branches, and explicitly transfer bounded ignored files with dev fleet.
3	authority: project
4	status: stable
5	verified_on: 2026-08-31

7	
8	# Remote repository fleet
9	
10	`dev fleet` fans out over SSH to other machines running their own `dev`, so you can see and open their repositories and safely propagate a branch, without merging their independent configuration into this machine's view.
11	
12	## What a fleet is
13	
14	A remote fleet is a list of other hosts, each running its own `dev` binary against its own `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, its own scan roots, its own task registry, and its own runtime. Inventory stays decentralized: each host's `dev` produces its own read-only snapshot over SSH, and one unreachable host never blocks the remaining rows. Mutation is confined to separately named commands such as `fleet sync` and `fleet files --apply`; neither makes this machine authoritative for the target's paths, task registry, or runtime.
15	
16	This is a different concept from the REMOTE TUI view and publishing/PR flows,
17	which use `gh` or `glab` for GitHub/GitLab repository publication and PRs, plus
18	the Azure CLI for Azure DevOps inventory and PRs. Fleet talks to *your own
19	machines* about *your own local checkouts* on those machines.
20	
21	## Configure hosts
22	
23	```bash
24	dev fleet config init
25	dev fleet config edit
26	dev fleet config show
27	dev fleet config path
28	```
29	
30	Hosts live in `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/dev/remotes.toml` (override the path with the global `--remotes <path>` flag). `config init` writes a starter file (`--force` to overwrite, `--stdout` to print without writing); `config edit` opens it in `$VISUAL`/`$EDITOR` (`--editor` overrides); `config show` prints the effective configuration with any plaintext password redacted; `config path` prints the resolved path.
31	
32	```toml
33	schema_version = 1
34	
35	[defaults]
36	connect_timeout = "15s"
37	command_timeout = "5m"
38	cache_ttl = "15m"
39	max_parallel = 4
40	dev_path = "auto"
41	
42	[[hosts]]
43	name = "lab"
44	ssh_alias = "lab"
45	# Add only after `dev fleet machine-id lab` and independent verification.
46	machine_id = "00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000000"
47	
48	[[hosts]]
49	name = "vps"
50	hostname = "203.0.113.10"
51	user = "dev"
52	port = 22
53	identity_file = "~/.ssh/id_ed25519"
54	ssh_login_password_source = { type = "bitwarden", item = "ssh-vps-login" }
55	```
56	
57	`schema_version = 1` is required. `[defaults]` supplies `connect_timeout`, `command_timeout`, `cache_ttl`, `max_parallel` (fan-out concurrency), and `dev_path` (`"auto"` searches `PATH`); each `[[hosts]]` entry inherits any of these it does not set explicitly. A host needs `name` plus either `ssh_alias` (preferred — it reuses `~/.ssh/config`'s `ProxyJump`, `IdentityAgent`, and host-key policy exactly like a plain `ssh` invocation) or `hostname` (optionally with `user`, `port`, `identity_file`). The optional `machine_id` is a durable UUID pin: read-only inventory can warn or proceed without it, but mutating portable-file apply requires an exact match. `ssh_login_password_source.type` is one of `none` (default), `prompt`, `plain` (inline `value`), or `bitwarden` (`item` looked up with the `bw` CLI). A config file with a `plain` password must be mode `0600`, or `dev fleet` refuses to load it.
58	
59	Discover a target UUID with `dev fleet machine-id <host>`, verify it through an independent channel on that machine, then copy it into `remotes.toml`. The command is read-only and reports `unpinned`, `match`, or `mismatch`; it never edits configuration on your behalf.
60	
61	## `dev fleet` commands
62	
63	| Command | Flags | Purpose |
64	|---|---|---|
65	| `dev fleet list` | `--host <name>` (repeatable), `--repo <query>`, `--json`, `--cached`, `--strict` | List repositories and activity across this machine and configured hosts |
66	| `dev fleet status` | `--json`, `--strict` | Probe configured hosts and report snapshot health |
67	| `dev fleet machine-id <host>` | `--json` | Show the observed durable UUID and compare the configured pin |
68	| `dev fleet sync <repo>` | `--push`, `--remote <name>`, `--host <name>` (repeatable), `--json` | Push optionally, then safely fast-forward clean matching checkouts |
69	| `dev fleet files [repo-or-path]` | `--to <host>`, `--file <pattern>` (repeatable), `--apply`, `--replace`, `--yes`, `--json` | Plan or apply one-way transfer of explicit ignored files |
70	| `dev fleet open <host> <repo>` | — | Open a remote repository through Herdr or an SSH login shell |
71	| `dev fleet config init` | `-f`/`--force`, `--stdout` | Write a starter `remotes.toml` |
72	| `dev fleet config edit` | `--editor <cmd>` | Open `remotes.toml` in `$VISUAL`/`$EDITOR` |
73	| `dev fleet config show` | — | Print the effective configuration (passwords redacted) |
74	| `dev fleet config path` | — | Print the resolved `remotes.toml` path |
75	
76	`--repo` on `list` filters by name, remote identity, branch, or path; `--cached` answers entirely from the last saved snapshot with no network activity; `--strict` turns an unreachable/timeout/incompatible/invalid host into a non-zero exit for both `list` and `status`. `sync <repo>` resolves `<repo>` locally like any other repository reference; without `--push` its `HEAD` must already equal the fetched upstream, and `--remote` picks which Git remote identifies the repository across hosts (default: the branch's upstream remote, then `origin`).
77	
78	## Explicit portable local files
79	
80	A repository may propose export candidates separately from worktree provisioning:
81	
82	```toml
83	# .dev-cli/config.toml
84	version = 1
85	
86	[local_files]
87	include = [".env", ".mcp/**"]
88	```
89	
90	`[worktree].include` is local provisioning policy and is never inherited here.
91	`[local_files].include` also grants no standing permission: an explicit invocation
92	must select exactly one target, and repeatable `--file` adds ad-hoc patterns for
93	that invocation only. Patterns expand on the source into sorted exact paths;
94	no glob crosses the wire.
95	
96	```bash
97	dev fleet files api --to lab                    # report only
98	dev fleet files api --to lab --apply --yes      # create absent target files
99	dev fleet files api --to lab --replace --apply  # authorize differing bytes separately
100	```
101	
102	The source and target must already resolve to one clone with the same normalized
103	**fetch** identity, attached branch, and exact commit. A push-only URL match is
104	insufficient. Both hosts independently prove every exact path is untracked and
105	ignored under their own Git configuration. Only regular files pass: no
106	symlinks/reparse points, directories, sockets, devices, FIFOs, `.git`, nested
107	repositories, or submodule boundaries. Compiled ceilings are 128 files,
108	8 MiB per file, 32 MiB total, with bounded path length/depth; host policy may
109	lower but never raise them. The source branch, HEAD, and fetch identity are
110	revalidated both before and after payload reads; target apply shares the
111	canonical Git-common-directory lease used by `fleet sync`.
112	
113	Plan is the default and sends no file body. Apply additionally requires the
114	configured `machine_id` to match the content-free capability probe. Missing files
115	are atomically created owner-only; identical files are no-ops; differing bytes
116	block unless `--replace` was present in the displayed plan. Replacement binds the
117	observed target digest/mode, retains a private rollback copy, revalidates both
118	roots, and rolls back file changes on failure. `--yes` only answers confirmation
119	and never implies replacement. Public human/JSON output contains path, size,
120	mode, and state—never content or hashes.
121	
122	The transaction journal is durable before manifest/payload staging, so an
123	interrupted request ID can resume or reconcile. Rollback intentionally leaves an
124	empty parent directory when its post-crash identity cannot be proven; deleting
125	another process's replacement would be worse. Native Windows payload transfer is
126	capability-blocked before content is sent.
127	
128	This command is not repository/task ownership transfer, clone acquisition,
129	provisioning, backup, restore, or eviction. It never switches a branch, copies
130	task/catalog/note state, watches for changes, propagates deletions, or removes the
131	source.
132	
133	`dev fleet` also registers bounded hidden capability/file commands in addition to
134	`_snapshot`, `_sync`, `_open-herdr`, and `_shell`. They exist only for the two
135	`dev` processes to invoke over SSH; they are wire protocols, not user-facing
136	surfaces.
137	
138	## Transport and authentication
139	
140	Every fleet command reaches a host by shelling out to the system `ssh` binary with `ConnectTimeout`, `ServerAliveInterval=15`, and `ServerAliveCountMax=2`, and first attempts `BatchMode=yes` — key or agent authentication only, exactly like a script-friendly `ssh` call. Fixed protocols use non-PTY `-T` and disable agent, X11, local-command, and all port forwarding while retaining the user's normal host-key policy. `dev fleet open` separately allocates a PTY (`-t`) for its interactive login shell.
141	
142	If that attempt is rejected with "permission denied" and the host defines a `ssh_login_password_source`, `dev` retries once with password authentication. The password itself never touches argv or the environment: `dev` re-executes itself as a one-shot `SSH_ASKPASS` helper, and the secret is handed to that helper over an inherited file descriptor. `prompt` reads a hidden password from `/dev/tty` at run time; `plain` and `bitwarden` resolve it from the config file or from `bw get password <item>` respectively.
143	
144	On the remote side, `dev_path = "auto"` (the default) searches common install locations (`~/.local/bin`, `~/go/bin`, mise shims, Homebrew/Linuxbrew, `/usr/local/bin`, `/snap/bin`) and then `PATH`, exiting `127` if no `dev` is found; an explicit absolute `dev_path` skips that search and execs it directly.
145	
146	## What's cached vs. durable
147	
148	`$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/dev/remotes.toml` is durable, user-authored configuration, on the same footing as `config.toml` — `dev fleet config init`/`edit` manage it, and nothing regenerates it automatically.
149	
150	Each successful probe writes a per-host JSON snapshot under `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/dev/fleet/v1/<host-name-slug>.json`. That cache is a disposable accelerator, not durable data: it is fingerprinted with an "endpoint ID" derived from the host's connection fields and timeouts, so editing a host's `machine_id`, `ssh_alias`, `hostname`, `user`, `port`, `identity_file`, `dev_path`, or timeouts automatically invalidates its old cache the next time `dev` reads it. Oversized snapshots, future timestamps, invalid counts, and oversized/NUL-containing identity or path fields are ignored rather than displayed. `dev cache list` shows its path, size, and age; `dev cache clear fleet` (or `dev cache clear all`) removes it outright. There is nothing to "rebuild" explicitly — the next `dev fleet list`, `dev fleet status`, or TUI FLEET reload regenerates it from a fresh probe.
151	
152	The cache exists so an unreachable, timed-out, incompatible, or invalid-response host can still report its last known state (marked `stale`, with `FromCache` set) instead of vanishing from the listing; `--cached` uses only this cache and never touches the network. Each remote host's own `config.toml`, task registry, and repository paths remain authoritative on that host — the cache only ever holds a read-only snapshot of them.
153	
154	## Fleet in the TUI
155	
156	FLEET is one of the TUI's six views (`TASKS`, `REPOS`, `FLEET`, `TRY`, `REMOTE`, `SKILLS`, switched with `tab`/`h`/`l`). Like REMOTE, it loads lazily — no live probe starts until the view is first opened — but its cache is decoded in the background after the initial TASKS view so a valid snapshot still within `defaults.cache_ttl` can seed the table. The TUI hides this machine by default because REPOS already provides its richer local inventory; `a` includes/hides local rows. The local-host snapshot reuses the current accepted REPOS generation instead of running repository/task/runtime discovery again; if that generation is still loading, FLEET keeps cached rows visible and says it is waiting. `r` supersedes an older request and forces a live reload of every configured host. The non-interactive `dev fleet list` output remains local plus remote.
157	
158	Its table shows `HOST`, `STATE`, `REPO`, `BRANCH`, `GIT`, `LIVE`, `TASKS`, and `PATH`. `enter` opens the selected repository: an explicitly revealed local host row uses an ordinary local open; for a remote row `dev` prefers native Herdr remoting when that host's snapshot reports the `herdr` runtime and the host connects through `ssh_alias` with no password step, and otherwise falls back to an interactive SSH login shell in the repository's directory. Git changes are read-only in this view — FLEET is for inspecting and opening work, not editing it in place.
159	
160	`e` opens `remotes.toml` in `$VISUAL`/`$EDITOR` — the file this view is about, rather than dev's own `config.toml`, which `e` opens everywhere else. On leaving the editor `dev` reparses the file before using it. A parse failure, an unknown field, or a permissions problem on a file holding a plaintext password is reported and the previous rows are kept, so a typo cannot silently drop a host from the fleet. A file that parses triggers an immediate live reload of every configured host.
161	
162	## Degrading gracefully
163	
164	Every host is probed independently, so one bad host never fails the fleet as a whole. Per-host states are `ok`, `stale` (cache reused, optionally with an error explaining why), `no-dev` (the remote has no `dev` on its `PATH` — reported, not an error), `unreachable` (SSH itself failed), `timeout`, `incompatible` (an old or unrecognized remote `dev`), and `invalid-response` (malformed snapshot JSON). `ok` and a clean `no-dev` never fail `--strict`; every other state does, including a `stale` result that carries an error.
165	
166	Separately, forge integration is optional: `gh` and `glab` enable GitHub/GitLab
167	inventory, publication, and pull/merge requests, while `az` enables Azure
168	DevOps inventory and pull requests. `dev doctor` reports missing CLIs as
169	warnings. Local Git workflows remain available, but an explicit non-interactive
170	publication request fails with login/install guidance instead of silently
171	changing its meaning. Azure DevOps inventory is additionally opt-in and stays
172	disabled until `forge.azure_devops` targets are configured.
173

1	---
2	name: dev-cli
3	description: 'Manage repositories and work-in-progress with the dev CLI: create/clone/setup agent-ready repos, bootstrap and organise them safely, own worktree/task lifecycle, safely prepare/finalize/retire agent sessions, run guarded Git transactions, capture sidecar repo notes, track HOT/WARM/COLD tasks, navigate via TUI, and bridge gh/glab/Azure DevOps/herdr/tmux/zellij. 5	
6	# dev-cli
7	
8	The `dev` command is a thin glue layer over git, worktrees, forges and agent
9	runtimes. It exists to stop four different things collapsing into one:
10	
11	```
12	git remote      durable code state, the source of truth
13	git worktree    a disposable local checkout
14	herdr / tmux / zellij
15	                a per-host live runtime
16	dev             human intent: what am I working on, and what is next
17	```
18	
19	Everything derivable from git or the runtime is derived live. `dev` persists
20	human/task facts such as identity, checkout mode, **state**, **owner** and **next
21	action** in one TOML file per task under configured `paths.state_dir/tasks`
22	(default `$XDG_DATA_HOME/dev/tasks`); transient pane data is not persisted.
23	
24	**The problem it solves:** when a terminal multiplexer's sidebar is the only
25	record of what you are working on, nothing can ever be closed. `dev` gives that
26	record a home outside the runtime, so closing a session stops meaning
27	abandoning a task.
28	
29	## Check it is there first
30	
31	`dev` is not installed everywhere. Before using it:
32	
33	```bash
34	command -v dev || echo "not installed"
35	dev doctor          # version/install owner/path, PATH collisions, and capabilities
36	```
37	
38	Only **git** is required. `herdr`, `tmux`, `zellij`, `gh`, `glab` and Azure CLI
39	each enable more and degrade cleanly when absent — never make a step
40	hard-depend on one.
41	
42	## Worktree ownership — read this before creating any worktree
43	
44	There are three mechanisms that create git worktrees, and picking the wrong one
45	is the most common source of confusion. The rule:
46	
47	| Kind of worktree | Owner | Where | Lifetime |
48	|---|---|---|---|
49	| Feature, fix, experiment, cross-machine handoff — anything you might return to | **`dev`** | `paths.worktree_path`, default `~/Worktrees/<repo>/<branch-slug>` | until `dev done` or `dev sweep` |
50	| Harness-owned turn-scoped isolation (`isolation: worktree`, `/batch`, `EnterWorktree`) | **Claude Code** | `.claude/worktrees/` (keep gitignored) | owned by that harness; not a transcript-relocation guarantee |
51	| `herdr worktree create` | **not used** — `dev` runs `git worktree add` itself, then `herdr worktree open --path …` | — | — |
52	
53	**Rule of thumb: if code/history/plan must remain reviewable or a human may
54	return tomorrow, use `dev`. Use native isolation only when the harness owns the
55	entire turn-scoped lifecycle.**
56	
57	Why `dev` does not delegate to `herdr worktree create`: the path policy has to
58	hold on machines where herdr is not installed. `dev` creates the checkout with
59	plain git and asks herdr only to *open* it — which still makes it appear in the
60	sidebar grouped under its parent repo with its own branch and ahead/behind row.
61	
62	Never nest a `dev` worktree inside a repository. A checkout inside another
63	checkout makes every indexer, file watcher and `rg` run see a second copy of
64	the tree. `dev` refuses to do it.
65	
66	Full detail: `references/worktree-ownership.md`.
67	
68	## The task lifecycle
69	
70	| State | Git | Runtime | Meaning |
71	|---|---|---|---|
72	| 🔥 `hot` | worktree + branch | session open | working on it now |
73	| 🌤 `warm` | worktree + branch kept | normally closed | back within days |
74	| ❄️ `cold` | committed and pushed; worktree removed | nothing | paused, reconstructible anywhere |
75	| ✅ `done` | merged | may remain open | MERGED; external retirement pending |
76	
77	```bash
78	dev repo open api                                  # ad hoc; no task/worktree
79	dev start api --task "typo" --direct                # track current/main directly
80	dev start api --task "small" --branch-only --base main
81	dev start api --task "token refresh" --base main   # isolated worktree → hot
82	dev park --next "add the regression test" --wip    # → warm, session closed
83	dev park --cold --push                             # → cold, worktree removed
84	dev resume "token refresh"                         # → hot, rebuilt if needed
85	dev prepare --session claude:<uuid>                # arm final transcript handoff
86	dev done                                           # TTY wizard: inspect dirty state, then FF/PR/merged
87	dev done --ff                                      # → done/MERGED; resources kept
88	dev retire "token refresh"                         # external-only cleanup → RETIRED
89	```
90	
91	**Parking is the move that matters.** `dev park --next "…"` is what makes it
92	safe to close a session, and the `--next` text is what makes resuming cheap.
93	Always suggest a `--next` when parking.
94	
95	Full detail: `references/task-lifecycle.md`. Before integrating or deleting an
96	agent-owned checkout, read `references/agent-retirement.md`.
97	
98	## Pick the task's checkout mode
99	
100	A task does not imply a worktree. Use the lightest explicit boundary:
101	
102	- `dev repo open <repo>` / REPOS Enter — ad-hoc open, no task at all.
103	- `dev start … --direct` / REPOS `d` — track current branch (usually main),
104	  create no branch/worktree. HOT ↔ WARM only; `dev done` needs no merge mode.
105	- `dev start … --branch-only` — create and switch a branch in the canonical
106	  checkout. No concurrent branch there.
107	- `dev start …` / REPOS `s` — default isolated branch + worktree. Use once work
108	  may be interrupted, experimental, or parallel.
109	
110	Do not create isolation before it has a job, but do not carry dirty main changes
111	into a parallel task implicitly either: a worktree starts from committed HEAD.
112	Checkpoint first when the new task depends on that work.
113	
114	## Parallel background work
115	
116	Read `references/parallel-agents.md` before spawning an independent agent while
117	another remains live. The fail-closed workflow uses `dev start --json`, requires
118	a newly created first-class Herdr worktree and its exact returned root pane,
119	then launches an explicit SpecStory/profile command there. Reused, fallback,
120	non-Herdr, missing or unverified panes are never launch targets.
121	
122	For a human one-liner, `dev start --run '<shell command>'` uses the same exact
123	new-worktree/root-pane proof and `--focus` independently switches afterward.
124	It does not choose a launcher profile, permission mode, agent name, or wait
125	policy; use the full JSON workflow when those require separate validation.
126	
127	`dev` guards writer-claiming direct/branch starts and resume when another
128	recognized Herdr agent occupies the same canonical Git worktree. Every state,
129	including `idle`, `done`, and `unknown`, is occupied; Herdr resolves the current
130	pane before excluding it. Pure repo/worktree/TUI open is navigation to the live
131	owner, not writer authorization. Never add `--allow-shared-checkout` unless
132	agents already have coordinated disjoint file ownership.
133	
134	A new external agent does not inherit the parent permission mode, and a resumed
135	Claude fork does not restore bypass. Inspect the effective SpecStory/provider
136	command: local wrappers may already be elevated, so never claim they are safe or
137	append a conflicting mode. Herdr `done` is turn-settled—not cleanup done.
138

211	## Bootstrapping and adopting an existing machine
212	
213	Read `references/bootstrap.md` before recursively scanning paths, creating a
214	symlink index, moving physical repositories, or generating layout config. Move
215	is destructive and must follow its report → review → apply procedure.
216	
217	There is nothing to migrate for ordinary use. `dev` discovers repositories through
218	`paths.scan_roots` plus exact `paths.repo_paths` and never moves, renames or deletes anything.
219	
220	```bash
221	dev config init     # detects this machine's roots; every value stays editable
222	dev adopt           # report existing worktrees, sessions and unmerged branches
223	dev adopt --apply   # record them as tasks (nothing on disk changes)
224	```
225	
226	Do not assume the user's layout is `~/Documents/Program`. Run `dev config show`
227	or `dev repo list` to see what this machine is actually configured for.
228	
229	## Creating and setting up repositories
230	
231	Read `references/repository-bootstrap.md` before creating a published repo,
232	running project-owned hooks, or installing setup-capable skills. A bare
233	`dev repo new` is interactive; `dev repo new NAME` deliberately retains the
234	minimal README + initial-commit contract. A clear Git URL, local Git path, or
235	`owner/name` argument to `new` or `create` automatically clones and preserves
236	its remote; template and upstream-creation flags cannot accompany that route.
237	Explicit `repo clone` remains available when scripts should state acquisition
238	directly.
239	`repo new --template` snapshots a local directory or Git tree into a fresh
240	history; it is not a clone. `--template-ref` and `--template-subdir` select the
241	exact source tree.
242	
243	Use `--check-in=commit|stage|none` to choose whether generated changes are
244	committed, staged for human review, or left unstaged (`auto` follows a new
245	repository's preset and otherwise defaults to none). `repo setup --commit`
246	remains the compatibility spelling for commit.
247	Stage mode cannot create an upstream and cannot hand dirty setup directly to
248	`start`.
249	
250	On a TTY, wizard fields are real inline editors: arrows, Home/End,
251	Backspace and Delete edit typed text rather than inserting escape sequences.
252	Esc or Ctrl-C cancels; piped input remains line-oriented.
253	
254	The create/setup wizard asks one customization-gate question after preset
255	selection. Declining uses resolved defaults and skips detailed template,
256	README/gitignore/license/agent/skill questions; explicit customization flags or
257	a required input without a default make yes the suggested answer.
258	
259	Global recipes live in `scaffolds.toml`. Repositories may commit the allowlisted
260	`.dev-cli/config.toml` and `.dev-cli/scaffolds.toml`, but executable project
261	configuration in those files must be trusted by its exact content hash before
262	it runs. Legacy `.dev.toml` retains its compatibility behavior.
263	
264	## Dashboard and forge inventory
265	
266	The TUI has TASKS, REPOS, FLEET, TRY, REMOTE and SKILLS views, switched with tab
267	or vim-style h/l. TRY `n` creates an experiment; `space` opens metadata/lifecycle actions;
268	`a` includes retained history. Archive is a reversible same-filesystem move,
269	not deletion or disk reclamation. `?` opens the full key map.
270	
271	The initial view never waits for runtime/project-root resolution, cache decoding,
272	or shell tool probes. TASKS/REPOS/TRY publish independently from one shared local
273	cycle; optional tabs remain lazy. Refreshes are generation-scoped: late results
274	are ignored, failed refreshes keep usable rows, and valid empty results clear
275	obsolete rows. For a one-run diagnostic, set `DEV_TUI_TRACE` to an absolute new
276	file. The private bounded trace is written after TUI teardown with relative
277	startup/view timings and aggregate row counts only; it excludes names, paths,
278	commands, key values, URLs, handles and raw errors, and never enters `stats.db`
279	or a network sink. In SKILLS, `c` waits for the initial local snapshot before it
280	can run the explicit source check; it never cancels that inventory with an empty
281	check.
282	
283	REMOTE queries authenticated `gh` and `glab` plus configured Azure DevOps
284	organization/project targets lazily and fully paginates every repository the
285	account can access. A private cache is decoded after the first view; stale rows
286	stay searchable while refresh runs. Malformed/oversized payloads and caches
287	fingerprinted for another configured GH/GL host or Azure target are ignored.
288	GitLab uses explicit `GITLAB_HOST`/`GLAB_HOST` (default `gitlab.com`) instead of
289	cwd inference; a successful empty refresh clears obsolete rows. `/` filters provider,
290	owner/name, visibility and description, with `vis:private` for an exact visibility match. Enter opens a local clone; `c`
291	confirms before cloning an absent remote. Use `dev repo remote [query] --json`
292	for the non-interactive form; `--cached` avoids a network query and `--refresh`
293	forces a complete synchronization.
294	
295	`dev journal` derives calendar-day reports from Git rather than storing a
296	second history database. The default current-user report adds existing
297	session/WakaTime observations, matching task intent and recent dirty-worktree
298	snapshots, clearly separated from committed history. `auto` expands at most 100
299	commit details while retaining complete aggregates; `--max-commits 0` is
300	unlimited. Use `--author <email>` or `--all-authors` for commit-only team views,
301	and `--json` for a stable structured report. dev generates the context only; it
302	does not launch the receiving agent.
303	
304	`dev summary` is the complementary current-state view across this machine. It
305	combines durable repositories and present active/deprecated Tries with live Git,
306	worktree, task, runtime, recovery and catalog facts. The default `auto` Markdown
307	expands active work and leaves quiet projects in a compact index; `--attention`
308	selects both active work and recovery hazards, while `--json` always emits the
309	complete selected snapshot. Use journal for time ranges and `repo context` for
310	one repository.
311	
312	Azure DevOps inventory is opt-in and cloud-only:
313	
314	```toml
315	[[forge.azure_devops]]
316	organization = "https://dev.azure.com/acme"
317	project = "Platform"
318	```
319	
320	Install Azure CLI's `azure-devops` extension separately. `dev` never installs
321	the extension, logs in, changes Azure defaults, or stores a PAT.
322	
323	FLEET reuses the accepted REPOS snapshot for the local host, then calls each
324	configured host's own `dev` over SSH, preserving its XDG paths. If the current
325	REPOS generation is still loading, FLEET waits while keeping usable cached rows
326	visible rather than rescanning local repositories. The TUI hides this machine
327	by default because REPOS already shows its richer local state; `a` includes
328	local rows. Host cache identity includes the SSH port. `dev fleet list` remains
329	local plus remote. Enter prefers Herdr remote navigation and falls back to an
330	SSH login shell.
331	`dev fleet sync` is explicit and strict: it only fast-forwards a clean checkout
332	of the same behind-only branch; dirty/ahead/diverged clones are never rewritten.
333	
334	`dev fleet files [repo-or-path] --to <host>` is a separate one-shot channel for
335	explicitly exported ignored files. It is report-only unless `--apply` is passed;
336	`--yes` never implies `--replace`. Both clones must already match by fetch
337	identity, attached branch and exact commit, and each exact path must be untracked
338	and ignored on both sides. Only bounded regular files are accepted. Apply also
339	requires a `machine_id` pin obtained with the read-only `dev fleet machine-id
340	<host>` command and verified independently. The operation never clones, switches
341	branches, runs provisioning, transfers task/catalog/note state, deletes source
342	files, or evicts a repository; native Windows payloads are disabled.
343	
344	REPOS has LIVE, LATEST and asynchronous SIZE. SIZE is logical
345	checkout+private-Git bytes; shared Git is separate and marked `+S`. Detail also
346	shows no-remote/local-only/multi-upstream recovery topology. Press space to
347	expand linked worktrees; children
348	show their own Git/session/task state and mark harness-owned or untracked
349	checkouts `(ephemeral)` / `(external)`. Press `y` followed by `y/p/b/s/w` to
350	copy contextual Markdown, path, branch, runtime/agent sessions, or every
351	worktree path. `dev repo context [repo]` prints the full Markdown without a TUI.
352	`[tui.repos]` chooses columns and default sort; `O` cycles sort and `R` reverses
353	it.
354	
355	`H` opens the selected repo's heatmap. On an empty panel, `b` backfills only
356	that repo and redraws; `r` rereads existing stats. Stats live in
357	`$XDG_DATA_HOME/dev/stats.db` and are durable observations, not cache — use
358	`dev stats clear` with an explicit scope. `dev cache clear` only removes
359	regenerable forge/size/gitignore/note-FTS data under `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/dev`.
360	
361	`e` edits config and returning live-reloads data/tool bindings; `r` reloads
362	explicitly. Runtime
363	backend changes require restarting the TUI.
364	
365	External tools are explicit `[[tui.tools]]` config. Run `dev tui tools` before
366	recommending a binding; it shows the exact command and whether it is available.
367	Commands run through `$SHELL` in the selected checkout. For an alias/function
368	that exists only in shell rc, set `interactive = true`; dev uses `$SHELL -lic`
369	and evaluates the command after rc loading. Prefer an executable on PATH when
370	the binding should be portable across machines.
371	
372	## Repository quick notes
373	
374	Read `references/notes.md` before adding/searching/editing/deleting notes or
375	when deciding whether content belongs in dev vs td/beads.
376	
377	Quick notes are multiple timestamped Markdown files under configured
378	`paths.state_dir/notes/<catalog-id>/` (default `$XDG_DATA_HOME/dev/notes`); the
379	catalog ID attaches them to the canonical clone across worktrees, symlinks and
380	moves. `dev` does not synchronize notes or catalog state, so cross-host
381	attachment requires syncing both. SQLite FTS at `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/dev/notes.db`
382	is disposable: clearing it removes no thoughts and the next search rebuilds it.
383	
384	TUI context keys: `n` quick-adds on TASKS/REPOS; `N` browses with `/` search,
385	Enter expand, `a` add, `e` editor, and confirmed `d` delete. In TRY, `n` remains
386	“new Try.” REMOTE needs a local clone.
387	
388	## Editing configuration
389	
390	Use `dev edit` (or `dev config edit`) rather than guessing the XDG path. It
391	opens the file selected by `--config`, generating the machine-detected starter
392	when absent, and resolves `--editor` → `$VISUAL` → `$EDITOR` → nvim/vim/vi.
393	
394	## Rules for agents
395	
396	1. **Do not equate task with worktree.** Ad-hoc opening needs no task; `--direct`
397	   tracks current/main; `--branch-only` is lightweight isolation; default
398	   worktree is for interruption/experimentation/parallelism.
399	
400	2. **Always pass `--base` for branch/worktree tasks.** Without it a new branch starts from the current
401	   HEAD, so starting a task while standing on `feature/A` silently builds on
402	   `feature/A`. This is the single most common way to produce a confusing
403	   history unattended.
404	
405	3. **Never `--force` a worktree removal on your own.** `dev wt rm` refuses a
406	   checkout with uncommitted changes; that refusal is the feature. Ask the
407	   user before overriding it.
408	
409	4. **Report drift, do not fix it silently.** `dev sweep` without `--apply`
410	   changes nothing. Show the user its output rather than running `--apply --yes`
411	   for them. For merged worktree cleanup, run `dev sweep --merged-worktrees`
412	   from the canonical main checkout, present every candidate and blocker as a
413	   QA question, and use `--apply --yes` only after the user explicitly approves
414	   that exact set. Branch deletion remains a separate `--delete-branches` opt-in.
415	
416	5. **Prefer a checkpoint commit over `git stash`.** A stash is invisible in the
417	   log, easy to forget, and cannot be pushed — so it can never reach another
418	   machine. `dev park --wip` makes a `wip:` commit instead.
419	
420	6. **One writer per branch at a time.** `dev resume` refuses a task owned by
421	   another host without `--force`. Before overriding, confirm that machine has
422	   pushed.
423	
424	7. **Check `dev wt plan` before blaming a worktree.** A worktree that comes up
425	   broken is nearly always a provisioning gap, not a git problem. The plan
426	   shows the detected project types, which tools are missing, and exactly what
427	   would be copied or run. Dependencies arrive by a per-ecosystem strategy —
428	   `reinstall` (default), `copy`, `link` or `skip` — and dev refuses an unsound
429	   one rather than producing a broken checkout: a virtualenv cannot be copied,
430	   because it bakes its own absolute path into `pyvenv.cfg`.
431	
432	8. **Do not create a worktree per agent.** Worktrees isolate *change streams*;
433	   panes isolate *agents*. A writer claim in one checkout needs explicit
434	   disjoint ownership; pure open/focus may navigate to the existing owner.
435	
436	9. **Parallel launch is exact-pane and fail-closed.** Accept only a new
437	   first-class Herdr worktree/root pane from `dev start --json` or the same
438	   internal proof used by explicit `dev start --run`. Never infer from
439	   focus/sidebar order, relocate SpecStory with mid-session `EnterWorktree`, or
440	   treat any recognized agent state as a free pane. Never add
441	   `--allow-shared-checkout` without coordinated ownership.
442	
443	10. **Launcher profile and effective permissions are explicit.** Standard
444	    Claude/Codex put the complete native command inside SpecStory `-c`; verified
445	    `*-copilot-once` wrappers already wrap SpecStory but inherit effective
446	    provider permissions, which may be dangerous. Never append a conflicting
447	    safer mode to an elevated command. Read `parallel-agents.md`.
448	
449	11. **Cleanup is external, never self-triggered by agent state.** Herdr `done`
450	    means a turn settled. Arm and finalize exact artifacts first; `dev done`
451	    integrates only, and `dev retire` must run outside the target workspace.
452	    Never run raw `git worktree remove --force` against the caller's checkout.
453	
454	12. **Prefer `dev bootstrap --index` over `--move`.** If the problem is
455	   navigation, a symlink catalog solves it without changing the authoritative
456	   paths. For a physical move, never add `--apply --yes` on the user's behalf;
457	   blocked rows are preconditions to resolve, not checks to bypass.
458	
459	13. **`dev adopt` without `--apply` changes nothing.** Show the user its report
460	   rather than applying it for them — which branches count as work in flight is
461	   their judgement, not yours.
462	
463	14. **Treat Markdown notes as durable and notes.db as cache.** Never delete
464	   configured `paths.state_dir/notes` to fix search; use `dev cache clear notes`
465	   and reindex. Note deletion itself requires explicit confirmation, and `dev`
466	   does not synchronize note/catalog state between hosts.
467	
468	15. **Do not call stats.db a cache.** Session/WakaTime observations may not be
469	   reconstructible. Use `dev stats clear --repo/--source/--all`; use
470	   `dev cache clear` only for regenerable remote/fleet/size/gitignore/license/note-FTS caches.
471	
472	16. **Archive is not eviction.** `dev tries archive` is a reversible hidden move
473	   on the same filesystem; it does not free space. Phase 1 has no project-data
474	   delete command. Never substitute `rm -rf` merely because a remote exists —
475	   no-remote, local-only refs, ignored files and stash are independent risks.
476	
477	17. **Read Git state as counts, not a dirty boolean.** `⇡`/`⇣` are upstream
478	   divergence; `=` conflicts, `+` staged, `!` unstaged, `?` untracked. Use
479	   `dev status` or JSON for the unique-path and type breakdown before cleanup.
480	
481	18. **Portable export is separately authorized.** Never treat `[worktree].include`
482	   as permission to send a file off-machine. Use only `[local_files].include` or
483	   explicit `--file`, show the report first, independently verify and pin the
484	   target UUID before apply, and never infer `--replace` from `--yes`.
485	
486	19. **Commit messages stay English** and follow Conventional Commits, even when
487	   the conversation is in another language — see the companion `git-workflow`
488	   skill, which owns commit conventions, SemVer and branch naming. This skill
489	   does not duplicate them.
490	
491	20. **Never bypass `.dev-cli` project-config trust.** Inspect the rendered hooks
492	    and skill entrypoints, then use `dev config trust <repo> --yes`. A changed
493	    executable hash is a new decision. Pre-commit/gitleaks inspect generated
494	    content; they do not make an untrusted command safe to execute. Legacy
495	    `.dev.toml` remains a compatibility surface rather than acquiring this trust
496	    contract retroactively.
497	
498	## When to use this skill
499	
500	- "What am I working on?" / "我在做什麼" / too many terminal workspaces open.
501	- Starting, parking or resuming a piece of work.
502	- Spawning independent background agents without disturbing a live checkout.
503	- "Where should this worktree go?" / "should I use `claude --worktree` or herdr?"
504	- A new worktree is missing `node_modules`, `.venv` or `.env`.
505	- Cleaning up stale branches, worktrees and sessions.
506	- Cloning, creating or auditing repositories across a machine.
507	- Promoting an experiment into a real project.
508	- "Which repo do I spend my time in?"
509	- Setting up a `.gitignore`, or a harness worktree showing as untracked.
510	- Adopting a machine that already has repos, worktrees and sessions.
511	- Recursively scanning, indexing, or physically reorganising existing repos.
512	- Configuring a flat repo/worktree layout or generating config for one.
513	
514	## When NOT to use it
515	
516	- **Commit messages, SemVer, branch naming, PR-vs-main tiering** — that is the
517	  `git-workflow` skill. This one links to it rather than restating it.
518	- **Standalone Herdr pane/agent control** — that is the `herdr` skill. The
519	  `dev start --json` and explicit `--run` cross-tool launch paths remain here.
520	- A single `git add` + `git commit` needs no tooling at all.
521	
522	## Reference files
523	
524	- `references/notes.md` — read before repository quick-note operations or
525	  choosing the boundary with td/beads.
526	- `references/bootstrap.md` — read before scanning or organising an existing
527	  machine; includes the non-destructive index default and move safety gates.
528	- `references/worktree-ownership.md` — who owns which worktree, and how a
529	  worktree gets a working environment. Read before creating one.
530	- `references/task-lifecycle.md` — HOT/WARM/COLD/DONE, when to park, and how
531	  work moves between machines.
532	- `references/agent-retirement.md` — prepare/finalize/integrate/retire, caller
533	  safety, exact transcript handling and orphaned-runtime recovery.
534	- `references/runtime-herdr.md` — how `dev` and herdr divide responsibility,
535	  including native worktree grouping, collisions and cleanup semantics.
536	- `references/parallel-agents.md` — read before launching parallel background
537	  work; exact JSON/pane validation, SpecStory profiles and permissions.
538	- `references/commands.md` — the full command reference, generated from the
539	  binary by `dev skill sync` so it cannot drift.
540	- `references/repository-bootstrap.md` — new/clone/setup presets, project
541	  overrides, skill initialization, upstream publishing, trust and handoff.
542	
543	## Gotchas
544	
545	- **`dev` may be a shell wrapper around the binary.** The trusted `shell-init`
546	  output defines a wrapper that gives navigation commands a private side channel
547	  (a child-only file descriptor for POSIX shells, a `DEV_SHELL_CD_FILE` temp
548	  file for `shell-init powershell`), reads one NUL-terminated path and calls
549	  `builtin cd` / `Set-Location` without evaluating command output. Without the
550	  wrapper, the binary's printable legacy directive cannot change the parent
551	  shell — that is not a bug.
552	- **Windows runs without a multiplexer.** There is no tmux, Zellij or Herdr on
553	  Windows, so the runtime backend is always `none`; `dev fleet open` starts a
554	  child shell instead of replacing the process. `dev upgrade` self-replaces only
555	  a standalone install and otherwise delegates to the detected Homebrew/Scoop/
556	  `go install` command. Stable releases advance the Homebrew tap; never overwrite its Cellar
557	  binary manually.
558	- **A worktree is a clean checkout.** It has no `node_modules`, no `.venv` and
559	  none of the gitignored env files. `dev` provisions it; `--no-provision`
560	  skips that and leaves you to it.
561	- **Only explicitly included, gitignored stable regular files are copied.**
562	  Source swaps and symlinked destination parents are refused; existing targets
563	  are reported skipped, not copied. Do not universally include
564	  `.claude/settings.local.json`: only sticky/plain-Claude profiles opt in.
565	- **Worktree provisioning and fleet export use different allowlists.**
566	  `[worktree].include` is local-only. `fleet files` reads `[local_files].include`
567	  plus explicit `--file`, expands patterns before transport, and defaults to a
568	  content-free plan. It is not task transfer, backup, restore, or eviction.
569	- **A repository template is a snapshot, not a clone.** Source Git metadata,
570	  remotes and history are excluded. A local Git worktree without a ref includes
571	  tracked plus nonignored untracked files; a non-Git directory includes its
572	  complete current tree. Human plans preview paths and warn about live unpinned
573	  sources. URL userinfo is redacted, while held root/directory/file handles
574	  confine traversal. Symlinks, special files, traversal and source changes fail
575	  closed, and the snapshot applies only to an otherwise-empty new repo.
576	- **Lazygit commit drafts are a best-effort adapter.** `--check-in=stage` writes
577	  `LAZYGIT_PENDING_COMMIT` in that worktree's Git directory so lowercase `c`
578	  can preload the proposed message. This is not `commit.template` or
579	  `COMMIT_EDITMSG`, uppercase `C` and other clients need not read it, and an
580	  existing different draft is preserved. Draft write/sync failure is a warning,
581	  not rollback: the successfully staged index remains ready for manual commit.
582	- **Agent history remains reviewable.** Built-in `agent-history-hygiene` seeds
583	  `.specstory/.gitignore` only for machine-local `.project.json` and generated
584	  `statistics.json`; it does not ignore `.specstory/history/*.md`. An existing
585	  nested ignore keeps its custom content and mode while missing required rules
586	  are appended. Correct any broader parent `.specstory/` rule explicitly.
587	- **Removing a worktree never deletes the branch.** Those are separate
588	  decisions; conflating them is how work gets lost.
589	- **Bare `dev done` is interactive only on a TTY.** It reports branch relation
590	  and dirty-content equivalence, then offers commit/discard and FF/PR/cleanup.
591	  Non-interactive use remains report-only without `--ff`/`--pr`. Unique discard
592	  requires `DROP` or explicit `--dirty=discard --yes`.
593	- **The stats sampler must be scheduled.** `dev stats` is empty until
594	  `dev stats backfill` runs once and `dev stats sample` runs periodically.
595

136	// NormalizeCloneRef expands forge shorthand while leaving explicit URLs, SCP
137	// references and local paths unchanged.
138	func NormalizeCloneRef(ref string) string {
139		ref = strings.TrimSpace(ref)
140		if ref == "" {
141			return ref
142		}
143		if filepath.IsAbs(ref) {
144			return filepath.Clean(ref)
145		}
146		if ref == "~" || strings.HasPrefix(ref, "~/") {
147			return config.Expand(ref)
148		}
149		if strings.HasPrefix(ref, "./") || strings.HasPrefix(ref, "../") {
150			if absolute, err := filepath.Abs(ref); err == nil {
151				return absolute
152			}
153		}
154		if strings.HasPrefix(ref, "file://") || (!strings.Contains(ref, "://") && strings.ContainsAny(ref, "@:")) {
155			return ref
156		}
157		if info, err := os.Stat(ref); err == nil && info.IsDir() {
158			if absolute, err := filepath.Abs(ref); err == nil {
159				return absolute
160			}
161		}
162		if kind := forge.FromURL(ref); kind != forge.Unknown {
163			if adapter, err := forge.For(kind); err == nil {
164				return adapter.CloneURL(ref)
165			}
166			return ref
167		}
168		if !strings.Contains(ref, "://") && strings.Contains(ref, "/") {
169			if adapter, err := forge.Preferred(); err == nil {
170				return adapter.CloneURL(ref)
171			}
172		}
173		return ref
174	}
175	
176	// NameFromRef derives the checkout directory name from a clone reference.
177	func NameFromRef(ref string) string {
178		ref = strings.TrimSpace(ref)
179		ref = strings.TrimSuffix(strings.TrimSuffix(ref, "/"), ".git")
180		if index := strings.LastIndexAny(ref, "/:\\"); index >= 0 {
181			return ref[index+1:]
182		}
183		return ref
184	}
185

1377	func matchRemoteLocals(ctx context.Context, app *App, remoteRepos []forge.RemoteRepo) []tui.RemoteRow {
1378		locals, _ := repo.Discover(ctx, app.Cfg.DiscoveryRoots(), repo.DefaultOptions())
1379		assets, _, assetErr := joinRepoAssets(app, locals)
1380		if assetErr != nil {
1381			app.warnf("could not join catalog metadata to remote locals: %v", assetErr)
1382			assets = make([]*catalog.Entry, len(locals))
1383		}
1384		type localMatch struct {
1385			repository repo.Repo
1386			asset      *catalog.Entry
1387		}
1388		localByRemote := map[string]localMatch{}
1389		ambiguous := map[string]bool{}
1390		for index, r := range locals {
1391			if r.Bare {
1392				continue
1393			}
1394			kind, name := forge.IdentityFromURL(gitx.RemoteFromConfig(r.CommonDir, "origin"))
1395			if kind == forge.Unknown || name == "" {
1396				continue
1397			}
1398			key := string(kind) + "/" + strings.ToLower(name)
1399			if ambiguous[key] {
1400				continue
1401			}
1402			if _, exists := localByRemote[key]; exists {
1403				delete(localByRemote, key)
1404				ambiguous[key] = true
1405				continue
1406			}
1407			localByRemote[key] = localMatch{repository: r, asset: assets[index]}
1408		}
1409		out := make([]tui.RemoteRow, 0, len(remoteRepos))
1410		for _, rr := range remoteRepos {
1411			row := tui.RemoteRow{Repo: rr}
1412			if local, ok := localByRemote[string(rr.Forge)+"/"+strings.ToLower(rr.FullName)]; ok {
1413				row.LocalPath, row.LocalName = local.repository.Path, local.repository.Display()
1414				row.LocalKind = catalog.KindRepository
1415				if local.asset != nil {
1416					row.LocalKind = local.asset.Kind
1417				}
1418			}
1419			out = append(out, row)
1420		}
1421		// Linked-worktree Tries are intentionally absent from repo.Discover's project
1422		// inventory, so use their explicit catalog identity as a second safe source.
1423		applyCatalogRemoteMatches(app, out)
1424		return out
1425	}
1426	
1427	func applyCatalogRemoteMatches(app *App, rows []tui.RemoteRow) {
1428		if app == nil || app.Catalog == nil || len(rows) == 0 {
1429			return
1430		}
1431		entries, diagnostics, err := app.Catalog.ListWithDiagnostics()
1432		if err != nil {
1433			app.warnf("could not read catalog for remote matching: %v", err)
1434			return
1435		}
1436		for _, diagnostic := range diagnostics {
1437			app.warnf("%s", diagnostic.Error())
1438		}
1439		if len(diagnostics) > 0 {
1440			return
1441		}
1442		host := config.Hostname()
1443		byIdentity := make(map[string][]*catalog.Entry)
1444		for _, entry := range entries {
1445			location, ok := entry.LocationFor(host)
1446			if !ok || location.State != catalog.LocationPresent || entry.RemoteIdentity == "" ||
1447				liveCatalogLocationPath(location) == "" {
1448				continue
1449			}

149	
150	Only **git** is required at runtime. `herdr`, `tmux`, `zellij`, `gh`, `glab` and
151	Azure CLI each enable more and degrade cleanly when absent.
152	
153	## Create, clone, or set up a repository
154	
155	Repository bootstrap works from any directory. Bare `dev repo new` opens an
156	interactive flow that chooses the destination under the configured
157	`project_root`, previews the setup, and confirms before writing anything:
158	
159	```bash
160	dev repo new                                  # interactive new-repository flow
161	dev repo create api --preset agent-ready      # `create` is an alias for `new`
162	dev repo new owner/api                        # clear clone reference: preserve history/origin
163	dev repo new api --template owner/starters --template-subdir go/service
164	dev repo new api --check-in stage -m "chore: initialize api"
165	dev repo clone owner/api                      # owner/name or a Git URL
166	dev repo setup . --preset agent-ready         # add the same setup to an existing repo
167	```
168	
169	`repo new NAME` keeps the small scripted default: `main`, README, and an
170	initial commit. When the argument is clearly a Git URL, local Git path, or
171	owner/name, however, `new`/`create` routes to the clone flow and preserves the
172	source history and configured remote; `repo clone` remains the explicit spelling.
173	Clone can optionally apply a preset after the checkout exists, while `repo setup` repeat-safely merges native
174	initializers and preset files into a repository you already have. Custom hooks
175	and skill setup remain responsible for their own idempotency. Use `--dry-run`
176	to inspect the available plan without mutating the target repository.
177	
178	`repo new` can also start from a content snapshot rather than an empty tree.
179	`--template` accepts a local directory/repository, Git URL, or owner/name;
180	`--template-ref` selects a branch, tag, or commit, and `--template-subdir`
181	selects a confined folder within the source. The snapshot becomes a fresh Git
182	history: source `.git` metadata is never copied, template files win scaffold
183	conflicts, regular-file modes are preserved, and traversal, symlinks, and
184	special files fail before the destination is created. A local Git working tree
185	without `--template-ref` includes existing tracked files plus untracked,
186	non-ignored files; Git-ignored files are omitted. A non-Git directory snapshots
187	its complete current tree. The same `template`, `template_ref`, and
188	`template_subdir` keys can live in a preset, which makes one starter catalog
189	repository with a preset per subfolder practical.
190	
191	Human confirmation and dry-run plans preview the selected file paths (with a
192	bounded list) and warn when the source is a live local snapshot rather than a
193	commit. URL userinfo is removed from rendered summaries and errors. Filesystem
194	walking and writes are confined relative to held `os.Root` handles, and source
195	file content is read from the handle that was validated instead of reopening a
196	mutable path.
197

519	private XDG cache is decoded after the first view and contains the complete

551	REPOS has an explicit LIVE column (`herdr:working`, `herdr:idle`, …). Multiple
552	repo sessions collapse to `herdr:N live`; expanding the repo reveals each
553	checkout and whether its session is live or closed. External and turn-scoped
554	agent worktrees remain visible with `(external)` / `(ephemeral)` labels, so the
555	tree always reconciles with WT. `H` opens the selected repo's
556	one-year activity heatmap and `e` edits config. Returning from the editor, or

558	the TUI; a runtime-backend change is reported as requiring restart.

```text
175	
176	### Upstream publishing
177	
178	Before offering publication, dev probes `gh` and `glab` without changing
179	state. A provider is offered only when its CLI is installed and authenticated;
180	otherwise the wizard gives the relevant installation or login guidance.
181	Local-only is the default, and a newly published repository defaults private.
182	
183	Publishing uses the local repository name and configured description, then asks
184	for the provider namespace/owner, visibility, and whether to push the
185	initial/current branch. Dev creates the empty GitHub or GitLab repository after
186	required local setup and commit steps succeed, then adds/verifies `origin` and
187	optionally pushes with upstream tracking. A
188	provider, name-conflict, or push failure never deletes the local checkout or
189	an upstream that was already created.
190	
191	Publishing from `repo setup` requires `--check-in=commit` (or the compatible
192	`--commit` flag), so the newly created upstream cannot omit the generated setup
193	changes. `--check-in=stage` is incompatible with any new upstream; for a new
194	repository, `none` may create an intentionally empty upstream only with
195	`--push=false`.
196	
197	### Handoff
198	
199	`stay` prints the result only. `cd` uses the trusted `shell-init` wrapper to
200	change the parent shell. `open` opens the configured Herdr/tmux/Zellij runtime
201	and falls back to `cd` when runtime is `none`. `start` continues into the
202	existing task wizard with the repository fixed, and is unavailable when setup
203	leaves uncommitted files that a new worktree would omit. Neither repository
204	bootstrap nor a default `dev start` launches a coding agent. Explicit
205	worktree-mode `dev start --run '<shell command>'` dispatches one command only
206	when a newly created first-class Herdr worktree returns its exact root pane;
207	`--focus` independently controls navigation afterward.
208	
209	All shared TTY text fields in the repository, task-start, and finish wizards
210	use an inline editor: Left/Right, Home/End, Delete/Backspace, insertion at the
211	cursor, and Esc/Ctrl-C cancellation work as terminal actions rather than being
212	inserted as raw escape bytes. Buffered and piped non-TTY input retains its
213	line-oriented behavior.
214	
215	## `dev done` finish flags
216	
217	`dev done` for branch/worktree tasks integrates through exactly one of `--ff` (rebase onto the base, then fast-forward it) or `--pr` (push and open a pull/merge request). Omitting both opens the interactive finish wizard on a TTY — see [Change-stream workflow](../guides/change-stream-workflow.md) for the prompts.
218	
219	A dirty checkout is handled by `--dirty <auto|fail|commit|discard>` (default `auto`):
220	
221	| Value | Behavior |
222	|---|---|
223	| `auto` | interactive: prompts to commit or discard; non-interactive: fails, same as `fail` |
224	| `fail` | refuses to finish with a dirty checkout |
225	| `commit` | commits everything with `--message`/`-m` (prompted interactively if omitted) |
226	| `discard` | resets tracked changes and removes untracked files; destructive, requires `--yes` outside a TTY |
227	
228	`--yes`/`-y` confirms the selected finish plan; it is mandatory for a non-interactive `--dirty discard` and otherwise skips the interactive confirmation step. `--keep-worktree` keeps the worktree after `--ff` integration (default: removed once merged), `--push` also pushes the resulting branch, and `--delete-branch` deletes the branch once its commits are contained in the base — never a branch with unpushed commits.
229	
230	## Configuration
231	
232	```bash
233	dev config init
234	dev config show
235	dev config path
236	dev config scaffolds init
237	dev config scaffolds show
238	dev config scaffolds path
239	dev config scaffolds edit
240	```
241	
242	`config init` detects local roots and writes explicit defaults. A missing config file is allowed; the built-in defaults keep core Git behavior usable, but generated config is recommended because it makes machine policy reviewable.
243	
244	Key sections:
245	
246	| Section | Controls |
247	|---|---|
248	| `[paths]` | scan roots, project/tries/worktree roots, worktree template, state path |
249	| `[runtime]` | `auto`, Herdr, tmux, Zellij, or none plus metadata settings |
250	| `[worktree]` | local ignored-file provisioning, linked dirs, setup commands, strategies, timeout |
251	| `[local_files]` | host ceilings for portable files; project overlays provide the separate off-machine candidate allowlist |
252	| `[forge]` / `[[forge.azure_devops]]` | complete remote inventory cache TTL and opt-in Azure organization/project targets |
253	| `[bootstrap]` | recursion, symlink handling, index/layout policy |
254	| `[tui]` / `[[tui.tools]]` | columns, sorting, and external-tool bindings |
255	| `[stats]` | sampler and optional WakaTime import |
256	| `[update]` | `check` (default `true`) — allow the once-a-day "newer release available" hint and its background cache refresh; `DEV_NO_UPDATE_CHECK` overrides it |
257	
258	`DEV_TUI_TRACE=/absolute/new-file.json` enables a one-run TUI startup/readiness
259	trace. The target must be absolute and must not exist; dev never overwrites it.
260	The private bounded document is written after TUI teardown and contains relative
261	categorical timings plus aggregate row counts rather than names, paths, or raw
262	payloads. It is not configuration,
263	cache, durable stats, stdout, or network telemetry. For TUI invocations, the
264	optional update-cache network refresh is also deferred until the initial view
265	has returned.
266	
267	Repository quick-note Markdown is durable under configured `paths.state_dir/notes`, which defaults to `$XDG_DATA_HOME/dev/notes`. The full-text index at `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/dev/notes.db` is disposable and rebuilds from those files; changing `paths.state_dir` does not move the cache.
268	
269	### Scaffold presets
270	
271	Global repository recipes live at `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/dev/scaffolds.toml` (or
272	the root `--scaffolds` override). Every authored file declares `version = 1`.
273	A compact preset looks like:

1	// Package repo discovers the repositories a user actually owns by walking the
2	// configured scan roots. It answers "what projects do I have?", which is a
3	// different question from "what am I working on?" — that one belongs to
4	// package task.
5	package repo
6	
7	import (
8		"context"
9		"io/fs"
10		"os"
11		"path/filepath"
12		"sort"
13		"strings"
14	
15		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/gitx"
16	)
17	
18	// Repo is one discovered repository.
19	type Repo struct {
20		// Name is the directory basename, which is how users refer to it.
21		Name string
22		// Path is the absolute path reached through the scan root. It may be a
23		// symlink from a bootstrap index; commands intentionally keep that human
24		// navigation path rather than replacing it with the physical one.
25		Path string
26		// RealPath is the physical checkout path.
27		RealPath string
28		// Symlink reports that Path is an alias to RealPath.
29		Symlink bool
30		// Root is the scan root it was found under.
31		Root string
32		// Category is the path between the scan root and the repo ("Quant",
33		// "Web/Frontend"), empty for a repo sitting directly in the root. It is
34		// human organisation metadata, preserved for `dev graduate` to place new
35		// projects consistently.
36		Category string
37		// GitDir is this checkout's administrative directory; CommonDir is shared
38		// by every linked worktree of the clone.
39		GitDir    string
40		CommonDir string
41		MainRoot  string
42		// Bare reports a bare repository (a worktree hub).
43		Bare bool
44		// HasGit distinguishes a real repo from a plain directory that was found
45		// in a scan root; non-repos are reported so `dev repo list` can offer to
46		// initialise them.
47		HasGit bool
48	}
49	
50	// Display renders "Category/Name" or just "Name".
51	func (r Repo) Display() string {
52		if r.Category == "" {
53			return r.Name
54		}
55		return r.Category + "/" + r.Name
56	}
57	
58	// Options tunes discovery.
59	type Options struct {

```text
## Television channel TOML schema

**Version:** No Television software version is stated. The page is marked copyright 2026.

### `[metadata]`

| Field | Type | Required |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | Yes |
| `description` | string | No |
| `requirements` | string array | No |

Minimal example:

```toml
[metadata]
name = "files"
description = "Browse files"
requirements = ["fd"]
```

### `[source]`

| Field | Type | Required |
|---|---|---|
| `command` | string, string array, `{ name, run }`, or array of those | Yes |
| `ansi` | boolean | No; defaults to `false` |
| `display` | string | No; incompatible with `ansi = true` |
| `output` | string | No |
| `watch` | float | No |
| `entry_delimiter` | string | No; defaults to newline |
| `no_sort` | boolean | No; defaults to `false` |
| `frecency` | boolean | No; defaults to `true` |

Minimal source example:

```toml
[source]
command = "fd -t f"
```

Named or multiple source commands:

```toml
[source]
command = [
  { name = "Default", run = "fd -t f" },
  { name = "Hidden", run = "fd -t f -H" },
]
```

Display and output templates:

```toml
[source]
command = "docker ps --format '{{.ID}}\t{{.Names}}'"
display = "{split:\t:1}"
output = "{split:\t:0}"
```

`display` controls how an entry appears; `output` controls its final output. Templates use `string-pipeline` syntax, including `{}`, `{0}`, `{split:DELIM:INDEX}`, `{trim}`, `{upper}`, and `{lower}`.

### `[preview]`

| Field | Type | Required |
|---|---|---|
| `command` | string or string array | No |
| `env` | table | No |
| `offset` | string | No |
| `header` | string | No |
| `footer` | string | No |

Minimal example:

```toml
[preview]
command = "bat -n --color=always '{}'"
```

### `[keybindings]`

`shortcut` is a channel-switching shortcut. Other keys override default bindings or invoke actions.

```toml
[keybindings]
shortcut = "f1"
ctrl-e = "actions:edit"
```

### `[actions.NAME]`

| Field | Type | Required | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `description` | string | No | — |
| `command` | string | Yes | — |
| `mode` | string | No | `"fork"` |
| `separator` | string | No | space |

`mode` may be `"fork"` or `"execute"`.

```toml
[actions.edit]
description = "Edit file"
command = "nvim '{}'"
mode = "execute"
```

The documentation does not state whether command strings are executed through a shell. It only documents command templates and gives examples containing shell-style constructs such as pipes and command substitution.
```
