```text
```toml
[metadata]
name = "git-repos"
requirements = ["fd", "git"]
description = """
A channel to select from git repositories on your local machine.

This channel uses `fd` to find directories that contain a `.git` subdirectory, and then allows you to preview the git log of the selected repository.
"""

[source]
# this is a macos version of the command. While perfectly usable on linux, you may want to tweak it a bit.
command = "fd -g .git -HL -t d -d 10 --prune ~ -E 'Library' -E 'Application Support' --exec dirname '{}'"
display = "{split:/:-1}"

[preview]
command = "cd '{}'; git log -n 200 --pretty=medium --all --graph --color"

[keybindings]
enter = "actions:cd"
ctrl-e = "actions:edit"

[actions.cd]
description = "Open a new shell in the selected repository"
command = "cd {} && $SHELL"
mode = "execute"

[actions.edit]
description = "Open the repository in editor"
command = "${EDITOR:-vim} {}"
shell = "bash"
mode = "execute"
```

- **Source/output:** Uses `fd` to search under the home directory for `.git` directories, following links, limiting depth, pruning results, and excluding two macOS library paths. It outputs each repository’s parent directory through `dirname`.
- **Display:** Splits paths on `/` and selects the final component, showing the repository directory name.
- **Preview:** Changes into the selected repository and displays up to 200 commits across all refs, using medium formatting, a graph, and terminal colors.
- **Keybindings:** Enter runs the shell-opening action; Ctrl-E runs the editor action.
- **Actions:** The first opens a new shell in the chosen repository. The second launches the configured editor, falling back to Vim.
- **Shell assumptions:** `fd` and `git` must be installed. The source command targets macOS-style home-directory exclusions but may work on Linux with adjustments. The editor action explicitly uses Bash; the shell-opening action relies on the user’s `SHELL` environment variable.
```
</details></tool-use>

- **Installation location:**  
  Unix-like systems: `~/.config/television/cable/`  
  Windows: `%LocalAppData%\television\config\cable\`

- **Invocation:**  
  Name the file `tldr.toml`, then run:
  ```sh
  tv tldr
  ```

- **Minimal TOML:**
  ```toml
  [metadata]
  name = "tldr"
  description = "Browse and preview TLDR help pages"
  requirements = ["tldr"]

  [source]
  command = "tldr --list"
  ```

- **Selected output and actions:**  
  The source command generates the searchable entries. The selected entry replaces `{}` in preview or action commands, such as `tldr '{}'`. A `fork` action runs the command and returns to Television; `execute` replaces Television with the command.
```
</details></tool-use>

18	#   Ctrl+Y     Copy the repo URL to clipboard            (overrides TV's full-line copy)
19	#   Alt+C      Clone into tv's launch cwd                (execute — shows progress)
20	#   Ctrl+R     Reload from cache                         (TV global reload_source)
21	#   Alt+R      Force a live refresh from the API, then reload

29	#   2. primaryLanguage
30	#   3. visibility

```text
1	# Custom fleet-hosts channel for television (tv).
2	# Sourced from ~/.config/fleet/machines.toml — the same inventory used by
3	# `fleet chezmoi apply` / `fleet tmux` / `fleet info` / `fleet pueue` /
4	# `fleet exec`. Mirrors the `ssh-config` cable's UX but reads fleet's TOML
5	# inventory instead of ~/.ssh/config, so hosts with explicit
6	# hostname/user/port/identity_file (no ssh_alias) are reachable too.
7	#
8	# The actual TOML parsing lives in Python — this cable shells out to:
9	#   fleet hosts --list-tsv      (source — `name<TAB>target<TAB>kind` lines)
10	#   fleet hosts --describe N    (preview pane content)
11	#   fleet hosts N               (Enter action — os.execvp("ssh", ...))
12	# So this file stays small and the picker tracks any inventory changes
13	# automatically (no parallel TOML parser to keep in sync).
14	#
15	# Enter lands you in an attach-or-create tmux session (`fleet`) on the remote,
16	# so a dropped connection resumes instead of losing the shell. That lives in
17	# `fleet hosts` itself, NOT here — do not inline an `ssh` invocation into this
18	# cable or the two will drift. See docs/tools/fleet-hosts.md.
19	#
20	# Usage:
21	#   tv fleet-hosts
22	#   fleet hosts          # same picker via the fleet umbrella
23	#   fleet hosts lab-box  # skip the picker, SSH directly
24	#
25	# Keybindings (Alt+ namespace to avoid TV/tmux conflicts):
26	#   Enter      SSH into the selected host
27	#   Alt+T      BatchMode SSH probe (does passwordless login actually work?)
28	#   Alt+S      fleet chezmoi status scoped to this host
29	#   Alt+I      fleet info scoped to this host
30	#   Alt+P      fleet pueue scoped to this host
31	#   Ctrl+/     Toggle preview panel
32	#
33	# `local = true` hosts are intentionally hidden — they live on the
34	# orchestrator and have no SSH endpoint. Run `fleet hosts --list-tsv
35	# --include-local` to confirm one is in the inventory.
36	
37	[metadata]
38	name = "fleet-hosts"
39	description = "Fleet hosts (from ~/.config/fleet/machines.toml)"
40	requirements = ["fleet", "ssh"]
41	
42	[source]
43	command = "fleet hosts --list-tsv"
44	# Lines look like:   name<TAB>target<TAB>kind
45	# e.g.   lab-box <TAB> lab-box <TAB> alias:lab-box
46	#        vps-tokyo <TAB> 203.0.113.42 <TAB> explicit:dwlee@203.0.113.42
47	display = "{split:\\t:0}  ({split:\\t:2})"
48	output = "{split:\\t:0}"
49	
50	[preview]
51	command = "fleet hosts --describe '{split:\\t:0}'"
52	
53	[keybindings]
54	enter = "actions:connect"
55	alt-t = "actions:probe"
56	alt-s = "actions:status"
57	alt-i = "actions:info"
58	alt-p = "actions:pueue"
59	
60	[actions.connect]
61	description = "SSH into the selected fleet host"
62	command = "fleet hosts '{split:\\t:0}'"
63	mode = "execute"
64	
65	[actions.probe]
66	description = "BatchMode SSH probe (passwordless login check)"
67	command = "fleet hosts --probe '{split:\\t:0}'; echo; echo '[Press Enter to exit]'; read -r _"
68	mode = "execute"
69	
70	[actions.status]
71	description = "fleet chezmoi status for this host"
72	command = "fleet chezmoi status --hosts '{split:\\t:0}'; echo; echo '[Press Enter to exit]'; read -r _"
73	mode = "execute"
74	
75	[actions.info]
76	description = "fleet info for this host"
77	command = "fleet info --hosts '{split:\\t:0}'; echo; echo '[Press Enter to exit]'; read -r _"
78	mode = "execute"
79	
80	[actions.pueue]
81	description = "fleet pueue for this host"
82	command = "fleet pueue --hosts '{split:\\t:0}'; echo; echo '[Press Enter to exit]'; read -r _"
83	mode = "execute"
84
```
</details></tool-use>

`/opt/homebrew/bin/tv --help`

```text
A very fast, portable and hackable fuzzy finder for the terminal

Usage: tv [OPTIONS] [CHANNEL] [PATH] [COMMAND]

Commands:
  list-channels    Lists the available channels
  init             Initializes shell completion ("tv init zsh")
  completions      Generates standard shell tab-completion scripts for tv's various subcommands
  update-channels  Downloads the latest collection of channel prototypes from github and saves them to the local configuration directory
  help             Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Arguments:
  [CHANNEL]
          Which channel shall we watch?
          
          Channels provide predefined configurations including source commands,
          preview commands, UI settings, and more.
          
          To list available channels, use the `list-channels` subcommand.
          
          To pull the latest collection of channels from github, use the
          `update-channels` subcommand.

  [PATH]
          The working directory to start the application in.
          
          Defaults to the current directory.

Options:
  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

  -V, --version
          Print version

Source:
  -s, --source-command <STRING>
          Source command to use for the current channel.
          
          When a channel is specified: This overrides the command defined in the channel prototype.
          When no channel is specified: This creates an ad-hoc channel with the given command.
          
          Example: `find . -name '*.rs'`

      --ansi
          Whether tv should extract and parse ANSI style codes from the source command output.
          
          This is useful when the source command outputs colored text or other ANSI styles and you
          want `tv` to preserve them in the UI. It does come with a slight performance cost but
          which should go mostly unnoticed for typical human interaction workloads.
          
          Example: `tv --source-command="echo -e 'Red'" --ansi`

      --no-sort
          Disable automatic sorting of entries based on match quality.
          
          This is useful when you want to preserve the original order of entries
          as provided by the source command.

      --source-display <STRING>
          Source display template to use for the current channel.
          
          When a channel is specified: This overrides the display template defined in the channel prototype.
          When no channel is specified: This flag requires --source-command to be set.
          
          The template is used to format each entry in the results list.
          Example: `{split:/:-1}` (show only the last path segment)

      --source-output <STRING>
          Source output template to use for the current channel.
          
          When a channel is specified: This overrides the output template defined in the channel prototype.
          When no channel is specified: This flag requires --source-command to be set.
          
          The template is used to format the final output when an entry is selected.
          Example: "{}" (output the full entry)

      --source-entry-delimiter <STRING>
          The delimiter byte to use for splitting the source's command output into entries.
          
          This can be useful when the source command outputs multiline entries and you want to
          rely on another delimiter to split the entries such a null byte or a custom character.

Preview:
  -p, --preview-command <STRING>
          Preview command to use for the current channel.
          
          When a channel is specified: This overrides the preview command defined in the channel prototype.
          When no channel is specified: This enables preview functionality for the ad-hoc channel.
          
          Example: "cat {}" (where {} will be replaced with the entry)
          
          Parts of the entry can be extracted positionally using the `delimiter`
          option.
          Example: "echo {0} {1}" will split the entry by the delimiter and pass
          the first two fields to the command.

      --preview-header <STRING>
          Preview header template
          
          When a channel is specified: This overrides the header defined in the channel prototype.
          When no channel is specified: This flag requires --preview-command to be set.
          
          The given value is parsed as a `MultiTemplate`. It is evaluated for every
          entry and its result is displayed above the preview panel.

      --preview-footer <STRING>
          Preview footer template
          
          When a channel is specified: This overrides the footer defined in the channel prototype.
          When no channel is specified: This flag requires --preview-command to be set.
          
          The given value is parsed as a `MultiTemplate`. It is evaluated for every
          entry and its result is displayed below the preview panel.

      --cache-preview
          Whether to cache the preview command output for each entry.
          
          This can be useful when the preview command is expensive to run
          and you want to avoid running it multiple times for the same entry.
          
          This is enabled by default since most channels will benefit from it.
          
          This can be disabled for special cases e.g. where the preview command output changes
          frequently and/or you want live udpates.

      --preview-offset <STRING>
          A preview line number offset template to use to scroll the preview to for each
          entry.
          
          When a channel is specified: This overrides the offset defined in the channel prototype.
          When no channel is specified: This flag requires --preview-command to be set.
          
          This template uses the same syntax as the `preview` option and will be formatted
          using the currently selected entry.

      --no-preview
          Disable the preview panel entirely on startup.
          
          This flag works identically in both channel mode and ad-hoc mode.
          When set, no preview panel will be shown regardless of channel configuration
          or preview-related flags.

1	name: Release
2	
3	on:
4	  push:
5	    tags: ["v*"]
6	
7	permissions:
8	  contents: write
9	
10	jobs:
11	  validate:
12	    uses: ./.github/workflows/ci.yml
13	
14	  release:
15	    needs: validate
16	    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
17	    env:
18	      VERSION: ${{ github.ref_name }}
19	    steps:
20	      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
21	        with:
22	          fetch-depth: 0
23	      - uses: actions/setup-go@v5
24	        with:
25	          go-version-file: go.mod
26	          cache: true
27	
28	      - name: Validate stable release tag
29	        shell: bash
30	        run: |
31	          [[ "$VERSION" =~ ^v(0|[1-9][0-9]*)\.(0|[1-9][0-9]*)\.(0|[1-9][0-9]*)$ ]]
32	          git fetch origin main
33	          git merge-base --is-ancestor "$GITHUB_SHA" origin/main
34	
35	      - name: Build tagged version
36	        run: |
37	          make build
38	          test "$(./dev --version)" = "dev version $VERSION"
39	
40	      # modernc.org/sqlite is pure Go, so every target cross-compiles from one
41	      # runner with CGO disabled and ships as a static binary. Windows ships a
42	      # .zip with dev.exe; every other platform a .tar.gz with dev.
43	      - name: Build release archives
44	        run: |
45	          mkdir -p dist
46	          ldflags="-s -w -X github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/cli.Version=$VERSION"
47	          for target in darwin/arm64 darwin/amd64 linux/amd64 linux/arm64 windows/amd64 windows/arm64; do
48	            os="${target%/*}"; arch="${target#*/}"
49	            bin=dev; [ "$os" = windows ] && bin=dev.exe
50	            CGO_ENABLED=0 GOOS="$os" GOARCH="$arch" \
51	              go build -ldflags "$ldflags" -o "dist/$bin" ./cmd/dev
52	            if [ "$os" = windows ]; then
53	              ( cd dist && zip -q "dev-cli_${VERSION}_${os}_${arch}.zip" "$bin" )
54	            else
55	              tar -czf "dist/dev-cli_${VERSION}_${os}_${arch}.tar.gz" -C dist "$bin"
56	            fi
57	            rm "dist/$bin"
58	          done
59	          ( cd dist && sha256sum -- *.tar.gz *.zip > SHA256SUMS )
60	          ls -l dist
61	
62	      # The changelog is the account a human wrote; generated notes are the
63	      # fallback for a tag whose section is missing.
64	      - name: Extract release notes
65	        run: |
66	          awk -v ver="${VERSION#v}" '
67	            $0 ~ "^## \\[" ver "\\]" { found = 1; next }
68	            found && /^## \[/ { exit }
69	            found { print }
70	          ' CHANGELOG.md > notes.md
71	          if [ ! -s notes.md ]; then
72	            echo "no CHANGELOG section for $VERSION; falling back to generated notes"
73	            rm -f notes.md
74	          fi
75	
76	      - name: Create GitHub release
77	        env:
78	          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
79	        run: |
80	          if gh release view "$VERSION" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
81	            echo "release $VERSION already exists"
82	            exit 0
83	          fi
84	          if [ -s notes.md ]; then
85	            gh release create "$VERSION" --verify-tag --notes-file notes.md --title "$VERSION"
86	          else
87	            gh release create "$VERSION" --verify-tag --generate-notes --title "$VERSION"
88	          fi
89	          gh release upload "$VERSION" dist/*.tar.gz dist/*.zip dist/SHA256SUMS
90	
91	      # Homebrew owns its Cellar binary, so releases advance the tap rather
92	      # than asking `dev upgrade` to overwrite a package-managed file. This is
93	      # a required distribution path: a configured token failure fails the job
94	      # and a rerun can safely retry an already-created GitHub release.
95	      - name: Update Homebrew formula
96	        env:
97	          HOMEBREW_TAP_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.HOMEBREW_TAP_TOKEN }}
98	        run: ./scripts/update-homebrew-formula.sh "$VERSION"
99	
100	      # Refresh the in-repo Scoop manifest from the built checksums and, when a
101	      # bucket token is configured, push it to the bucket repo. Never fail the
102	      # release over a packaging problem.
103	      - name: Update Scoop manifest
104	        continue-on-error: true
105	        env:
106	          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
107	          SCOOP_BUCKET_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SCOOP_BUCKET_TOKEN }}
108	        run: ./scripts/update-scoop-manifest.sh "$VERSION" dist/SHA256SUMS

1	# Changelog
2	
3	All notable changes to this project are documented in this file.
4	
5	The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/), and releases use [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).
6	
7	## [Unreleased]
8	
9	## [0.2.5] - 2026-09-01
10	
11	### Added
12	
13	- `dev repo context [repo]` now has an additive schema-v1 `--json` report and an
14	  explicit `--refresh` path. Local checkout, Git, task, worktree, and runtime facts
15	  stay live and network-free; optional forge and configured-fleet observations carry
16	  source, age, freshness, completeness, and collection errors. Remote endpoints are
17	  structurally sanitized before public output, and readiness remains split by scope
18	  instead of collapsing unknown evidence into a global safe value. `dev status`
19	  reuses the same cheap local readiness projection without network probes.
20	- `dev fleet machine-id <host>` exposes the remote host's non-secret durable machine
21	  UUID and compares it with the optional `machine_id` pin in `remotes.toml`.
22	  `dev fleet files [repo-or-path] --to <host>` plans a one-way transfer of explicitly
23	  allowlisted ignored files and mutates only with `--apply`; both hosts must prove
24	  every exact path is untracked, ignored, regular, portable, bounded, and bound to the
25	  same fetch identity, attached branch, and commit; apply additionally requires the
26	  pinned target machine. Differing target bytes require a separate `--replace`;
27	  `--yes` never implies replacement.
28	
29	### Fixed
30	
31	- Task writes now carry an in-memory revision from read to write, so existing
32	  lifecycle callers cannot silently overwrite a concurrent process's newer task
33	  record. Park holds the task transaction through runtime/worktree cleanup, and a
34	  DONE direct-task ID starts a new compare-and-swap generation. Catalog create,
35	  update, import, and experiment reconciliation share one
36	  cross-process transaction lock, while corrupt task records make repository-context
37	  inventory explicitly incomplete instead of disappearing behind a warning.
38	- Portable-file retries now recover an interrupted store both before and after the
39	  first journal write. Source branch/HEAD/fetch identity is revalidated around payload
40	  reads; target sync/apply and remote aliases share the canonical clone lease. Durable
41	  publication provenance plus exact digest/mode prevents rollback from deleting a
42	  foreign identical file or retaining changed permissions. Target discovery errors fail
43	  closed, nested bare repositories are excluded, post-publication filesystem errors
44	  remove their own destination, and credential-bearing SCP-like tokens cannot enter
45	  catalog keys, protocol journals, or repository-context output.
46	
47	## [0.2.4] - 2026-09-01
48	
49	### Added
50	
51	- Stable releases now render and publish `Formula/dev-cli.rb` to
52	  `daviddwlee84/homebrew-tap`. The release job requires a fine-grained
53	  `HOMEBREW_TAP_TOKEN`, fails visibly when the distribution update cannot be
54	  published, and has a manual workflow for retrying or backfilling an existing
55	  stable release without creating another tag. Homebrew installs remain
56	  package-manager-owned rather than letting `dev upgrade` overwrite a Cellar
57	  binary.
58	
59	### Changed
60	
61	- `dev upgrade` now delegates directly to the detected Homebrew, Scoop, or

# Context

`dev` already has robust domain-owned caches (forge remotes, fleet snapshots, disk sizes, note FTS, templates), but it has no generic cache of selectable CLI values and no picker integration. Repository discovery/inventory remains deliberately live. The first useful integration is therefore narrow: reuse the existing forge cache to choose a remote for `dev repo clone`, use fast live discovery to choose a local repository in the `dev start` wizard, and expose the existing `dev repo remote --json` contract to Television/fzf recipes. This removes repetitive path/name typing without making fzf mandatory, changing scripted behavior, or adding a second inventory/cache.

The user selected an internal configurable picker plus composable external recipes, with a built-in Bubble Tea fallback. This slice intentionally does not add pickers to `dev done` (which already has task completion) or to every finite-choice command.

## 1. Add a reusable, safe selector primitive

- Add `internal/textmatch` with an exported term matcher equivalent to the current `internal/tui/rows.go:matches`: trim/lowercase, split whitespace, require every term as a substring. Have the TUI delegate to it so the built-in picker and `/` keep one tested matching contract; do not introduce a fuzzy-scoring dependency.
- Add `internal/picker` with small caller-neutral types such as:
  - `Item { Value, Label, Description string }`
  - `Request { Prompt, InitialQuery string; Items []Item }`
  - `Result { Item Item; Selected, Canceled bool }`
  - a selector object constructed with input/output/error streams and configured external argv, exposing `Select(context.Context, Request) (Result, error)`.
- Keep backend selection internal: use the configured external executable when `exec.LookPath` succeeds, otherwise use the built-in Bubble Tea backend. An explicitly empty argv forces the built-in backend. A configured executable that starts and then fails is an error rather than silently replaying the interaction in a second UI.
- Execute external argv directly with `exec.CommandContext`, never via a shell. Feed normalized, uniquely rendered candidate lines on child stdin, capture only the selected line from stdout, and leave stderr attached to the caller terminal for fzf-style UI. Map the exact returned line back to the source `Item`; decorate otherwise-identical rendered lines with a deterministic ordinal so duplicate labels/descriptions cannot select the wrong value. Reject unexpected/multiple output instead of guessing. Treat exit codes 1 and 130 as cancellation, propagate context cancellation, and report other exits.
- Support a literal `{prompt}` substitution in argv elements so the per-call label can reach fzf without shell interpolation. Newlines/NULs in item display fields are normalized before rendering; the opaque `Value` is never rendered or trusted back from the child.
- Implement the fallback as a compact Bubble Tea list with `bubbles/textinput`: live term filtering, up/down plus Ctrl-N/Ctrl-P, Enter to select, Esc/Ctrl-C to cancel, and a bounded viewport. Test the model directly rather than requiring a real terminal.
- Add an `App` adapter/test seam in `internal/cli` that passes `App.In/Out/Err` and `App.Cfg.Picker` into `internal/picker`. It should only open a picker when input and output are a terminal pair; non-TTY readers keep the existing deterministic line prompts.

Critical files: `internal/picker/*.go`, `internal/textmatch/*.go`, `internal/tui/rows.go`, `internal/cli/app.go`, and a small `internal/cli/picker.go` adapter.

## 2. Add minimal global picker configuration

- Extend `internal/config/config.go` with `Config.Picker` and a global-only `[picker]` section containing one `command []string` argv vector. Default it to fzf with conservative presentation args and `{prompt}` (for example `fzf`, reverse layout, bounded height/border, and a prompt). `command = []` is the documented way to force the built-in picker.
- Keeping executable and arguments in one replacement-valued slice avoids a partial TOML overlay accidentally retaining fzf arguments when the executable is changed to `tv`, `sk`, or `gum`.
- Validation permits an empty vector, but rejects an empty first element and NUL/newline-bearing argv elements. It does not require the binary to be installed: absence is a supported fallback state.
- Add the annotated section to `internal/cli/config.go`'s starter config. `dev config show` will include it automatically. Keep picker policy out of repo-owned `.dev-cli/config.toml`.
- Extend `dev doctor` to identify the configured external selector as optional and state that the built-in picker will be used when it is unavailable; do not install anything.

Critical files: `internal/config/config.go`, `internal/config/config_test.go`, `internal/cli/config.go`, `internal/cli/doctor.go` and focused CLI tests.

## 3. Wire only the two approved interactive entry points

### `dev repo clone`

- In `internal/cli/repo_create_wizard.go:runRepoCloneWizard`, before the existing free-form source prompt, read the raw forge cache through `cachedRemoteRows(app)` / `forge.LoadCacheAny`. This is disk-only and must not trigger provider network calls or the expensive `matchRemoteLocals` repository scan.
- Build candidates from cache rows with non-empty `CloneURL`, displaying forge-qualified full name plus visibility/archived/description metadata. Preserve cache ordering (or the existing deterministic updated/name ordering). Use `RemoteRepo.CloneURL` as `Item.Value`, not `FullName`, so GitHub, GitLab (including self-hosted), and Azure DevOps keep the exact provider URL.
- Append a synthetic “Enter a URL, path, or owner/name…” item. Selecting it, having no usable cache/candidates, or running through non-TTY input goes through the current `prompter.line` path unchanged. A stale but source-compatible cache remains useful and is visibly warned as stale; a missing/source-mismatched cache simply falls back to manual entry. Never refresh the network merely to open the picker.
- Picker cancellation returns `errPromptCanceled`, preserving the command’s existing “Canceled; nothing was cloned” behavior. Explicit positional refs and non-interactive/`--json` behavior bypass the picker exactly as today.
- Do not add a costly local scan merely to badge/exclude already-cloned remotes. Existing destination/nested-repository checks remain authoritative and prevent unsafe duplicate acquisition.

### `dev start`

- Replace `internal/cli/start_wizard.go:promptStartRepository`’s numbered listing with the shared picker.
- Obtain candidates with `repo.Discover(..., repo.CompletionOptions())`, filter to non-bare Git repositories, and render `Repo.Display()` plus `config.Contract(Repo.Path)`. Put the current repository first when it resolves, while retaining a synthetic manual/name/path item for values not discovered under configured roots.
- Return the selected repo directly; the manual path continues through `repo.Resolve`. Preserve explicit `dev start <repo>`, non-TTY prompts, empty-inventory errors, and cancellation before any mutation.

Tests should inject selector results through the `App` seam, so command/wizard tests do not depend on fzf, PTYs, or a developer’s PATH.

## 4. Ship composable Television/fzf usage without another command

- Do not add `dev pick`: `dev repo remote --cached --json` already supplies the cache-backed, pipe-friendly candidate contract, while `--refresh` explicitly populates it. Reusing this command avoids duplicate filtering, freshness, JSON, and cache semantics.
- Add `contrib/television/dev-remote-repos.toml`. Its source invokes `dev repo remote --cached --json` and `jq` to emit TSV containing exact `repo.clone_url`, display/full name, forge, visibility, local path, and description. Enter outputs the exact clone URL; an action can run `dev repo clone` on it. Metadata declares `dev` and `jq` requirements. The repository only ships the file; it does not modify the user’s Television/chezmoi configuration.
- Document both compositions near repository bootstrap:
  - initialize/refresh once with `dev repo remote --refresh`;
  - copy or symlink the channel and use `dev repo clone "$(tv dev-remote-repos)"`;
  - provide an fzf shell function that transforms the same JSON with `jq`, displays descriptive columns, extracts the exact clone URL, handles cancellation/empty output, and invokes `dev repo clone`.
- Explain that the internal no-argument clone picker needs neither `tv` nor `jq`, uses no network, and falls back to the built-in UI when its configured external command is absent.

## 5. Record intentionally deferred picker surfaces

Replace the completed `TODO.md` “Television / fzf channel” item with a scoped backlog item for extending the shared selector only where it improves over completion. List:

- `tries *`, `graduate`, note show/edit/delete, fleet open/host, artifact discard, and skill update;
- interactive disambiguation for structured repo/experiment/catalog ambiguity errors;
- branch/base selection after adding one canonical `gitx` branch enumerator;
- larger enum sets currently handled by `prompter.choice`.

Explicitly note that task lifecycle commands such as `dev done` already expose shell completion and should not automatically gain a picker merely because the primitive exists.

## 6. Keep product surfaces synchronized

## Approved Plan:
# Context

`dev` already has robust domain-owned caches (forge remotes, fleet snapshots, disk sizes, note FTS, templates), but it has no generic cache of selectable CLI values and no picker integration. Repository discovery/inventory remains deliberately live. The first useful integration is therefore narrow: reuse the existing forge cache to choose a remote for `dev repo clone`, use fast live discovery to choose a local repository in the `dev start` wizard, and expose the existing `dev repo remote --json` contract to Television/fzf recipes. This removes repetitive path/name typing without making fzf mandatory, changing scripted behavior, or adding a second inventory/cache.

The user selected an internal configurable picker plus composable external recipes, with a built-in Bubble Tea fallback. This slice intentionally does not add pickers to `dev done` (which already has task completion) or to every finite-choice command.

## 1. Add a reusable, safe selector primitive

- Add `internal/textmatch` with an exported term matcher equivalent to the current `internal/tui/rows.go:matches`: trim/lowercase, split whitespace, require every term as a substring. Have the TUI delegate to it so the built-in picker and `/` keep one tested matching contract; do not introduce a fuzzy-scoring dependency.
- Add `internal/picker` with small caller-neutral types such as:
  - `Item { Value, Label, Description string }`
  - `Request { Prompt, InitialQuery string; Items []Item }`
  - `Result { Item Item; Selected, Canceled bool }`
  - a selector object constructed with input/output/error streams and configured external argv, exposing `Select(context.Context, Request) (Result, error)`.
- Keep backend selection internal: use the configured external executable when `exec.LookPath` succeeds, otherwise use the built-in Bubble Tea backend. An explicitly empty argv forces the built-in backend. A configured executable that starts and then fails is an error rather than silently replaying the interaction in a second UI.
- Execute external argv directly with `exec.CommandContext`, never via a shell. Feed normalized, uniquely rendered candidate lines on child stdin, capture only the selected line from stdout, and leave stderr attached to the caller terminal for fzf-style UI. Map the exact returned line back to the source `Item`; decorate otherwise-identical rendered lines with a deterministic ordinal so duplicate labels/descriptions cannot select the wrong value. Reject unexpected/multiple output instead of guessing. Treat exit codes 1 and 130 as cancellation, propagate context cancellation, and report other exits.
- Support a literal `{prompt}` substitution in argv elements so the per-call label can reach fzf without shell interpolation. Newlines/NULs in item display fields are normalized before rendering; the opaque `Value` is never rendered or trusted back from the child.
- Implement the fallback as a compact Bubble Tea list with `bubbles/textinput`: live term filtering, up/down plus Ctrl-N/Ctrl-P, Enter to select, Esc/Ctrl-C to cancel, and a bounded viewport. Test the model directly rather than requiring a real terminal.
- Add an `App` adapter/test seam in `internal/cli` that passes `App.In/Out/Err` and `App.Cfg.Picker` into `internal/picker`. It should only open a picker when input and output are a terminal pair; non-TTY readers keep the existing deterministic line prompts.

Critical files: `internal/picker/*.go`, `internal/textmatch/*.go`, `internal/tui/rows.go`, `internal/cli/app.go`, and a small `internal/cli/picker.go` adapter.

## 2. Add minimal global picker configuration

- Extend `internal/config/config.go` with `Config.Picker` and a global-only `[picker]` section containing one `command []string` argv vector. Default it to fzf with conservative presentation args and `{prompt}` (for example `fzf`, reverse layout, bounded height/border, and a prompt). `command = []` is the documented way to force the built-in picker.

```text
1	# Repository bootstrap
2	
3	Create, clone, or initialize a repository from any directory.
4	
5	```bash
6	dev repo new                         # interactive wizard
7	dev repo create api                  # minimal scripted creation
8	dev repo new api --template owner/starter --check-in=stage
9	dev repo clone owner/api             # clone, optionally set up
10	dev repo setup . --preset agent-ready --check-in=stage
11	```
12	
13	`repo new NAME` preserves the minimal contract: create the configured
14	`project_root[/category]/NAME`, initialize `main`, write README, and make an
15	initial commit. A bare `repo new` opens the richer wizard. `create` is an alias.
16	When the argument is clearly a Git URL, local Git path, or `owner/name`, both
17	`new` and `create` route to clone automatically and preserve source history and
18	its remote. Template and upstream-creation flags are rejected on this route;
19	use explicit `repo clone` when the operation should be unmistakable.
20	`repo setup` repeat-safely merges native initializers and preset files; custom
21	hooks and skill setup must provide their own idempotency. `--dry-run` does not
22	mutate the target repository.
23	
24	After choosing a preset, the wizard asks once whether to customize its template
25	and detailed options. Declining accepts the preset defaults and skips the
26	README/gitignore/license/Claude/AGENTS/skill questionnaire. The gate defaults
27	to yes when customization flags were supplied or a preset has a required input
28	without a default. Existing-repository setup uses the same condensed gate.
29	
30	When both stdin and stdout are terminals, wizard text fields use an inline
31	editor: left/right, Home/End, Backspace and Delete edit the current value
32	instead of inserting terminal escape bytes such as `^[[C`. Esc or Ctrl-C
33	cancels the prompt. Piped input retains the line-oriented interface used by
34	scripts and tests; a bracketed default remains a hint accepted with Enter.
35	
36	## Templates and check-in
37	
38	`repo new` can seed the otherwise-empty repository from `--template`, using a
39	local directory, Git URL, or forge shorthand. `--template-ref` selects a
40	branch, tag, or commit and `--template-subdir` selects the directory that
41	becomes the new repository root. Presets expose the same settings as
42	`template`, `template_ref`, and `template_subdir`; `--template=none` disables a
43	preset template.
44	
45	A template is a filesystem snapshot, not a clone: source history, remotes and
46	Git metadata are not copied. A local Git worktree without a ref uses its current
47	tracked files plus untracked files that are not ignored; ignored build outputs
48	and secrets stay out. A non-Git local directory snapshots its complete current
49	tree. A Git source with a ref, or a remote Git source, snapshots the resolved
50	commit. The confirmation/dry-run plan previews relative paths and warns when a
51	local source is live rather than pinned to a commit.
52	
53	dev validates and reads the complete snapshot before changing the destination,
54	rejects traversal, symlinks and special files, excludes `.git`, and preserves
55	regular-file modes and empty directories. Held root, directory, and file
56	handles confine reads and writes if a path is swapped while the operation is in
57	progress. URL userinfo such as embedded credentials is redacted from plans,
58	results, and errors. Templates apply only to a new repository; use `repo clone`
59	when history should be retained.
60	
61	`--check-in=auto|commit|stage|none` controls the generated changes:
62	
63	- `auto` follows a new repository's preset (`initial_check_in`, or legacy
64	  `initial_commit`); clone/setup otherwise preserve history and default to no
65	  automatic check-in.
66	- `commit` stages and commits with the preset or `--message` text.
67	- `stage` runs `git add -A` and leaves the index ready for human review.
68	- `none` leaves generated changes unstaged.
69	
70	`repo setup --commit` remains a compatibility alias for
71	`--check-in=commit`. Creating an upstream from `repo setup`, pushing a newly
72	created upstream, and handing changed setup directly to `start` require
73	`commit`. `stage` cannot create a new upstream; review and commit locally
74	first.
75	
76	Stage mode also writes the suggested message to the worktree Git directory as
77	`LAZYGIT_PENDING_COMMIT`, so lazygit's lowercase `c` dialog opens with that
78	message. This is a best-effort lazygit implementation detail, not a Git commit
79	template: `.git/COMMIT_EDITMSG`, `commit.template`, uppercase `C`, and other Git
80	clients are not promised to consume it. An existing different lazygit draft is
81	preserved and reported rather than overwritten. Staging is the primary
82	operation: if the optional draft cannot be written, setup still succeeds with
83	the index staged and emits a warning telling the user to enter the message
84	manually.
85	
86	## Presets
87	
88	The built-in `minimal` preset matches scripted creation. `agent-ready` adds a
89	managed `.gitignore`, `AGENTS.md`, and repository-local Claude plans. Optional
90	skills may declare a setup entrypoint. For `agent-history-hygiene` and
91	`project-knowledge-harness`, dev installs the skill but uses reviewed built-in
92	initializers before the first commit instead of executing newly downloaded code.
93	
94	The built-in `agent-history-hygiene` initializer seeds
95	`.pre-commit-config.yaml`, `.gitleaks.toml`, and, when absent,
96	`.specstory/.gitignore`. That nested ignore contains only `/.project.json` and
97	`/statistics.json`; `.specstory/history/*.md` remains part of the review trail
98	and must not be ignored. If the nested file already exists, dev preserves its
99	custom rules and mode and appends only whichever required entries are missing.
100	If a parent `.gitignore` already ignores the entire `.specstory/` directory,
101	review and remove that broader rule yourself.
102	
103	Global presets live in `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/dev/scaffolds.toml` and are managed
104	with `dev config scaffolds init|show|path|edit`. A repository may commit
105	`.dev-cli/config.toml` and `.dev-cli/scaffolds.toml`; only portable setup and
106	worktree policy is allowed there. Paths, state, runtime and credentials remain
107	host-owned global configuration.
108	
109	Executable hooks and skill setup from `.dev-cli/scaffolds.toml`, plus
110	`post_create` from `.dev-cli/config.toml`, are trusted by repository identity
111	and content hash. Legacy `.dev.toml` retains its compatibility behavior:
112	
113	```bash
114	dev config show --project
115	dev config trust . --yes
116	dev config trust . --revoke
117	```
118	
119	Changing executable configuration invalidates the prior approval. Trust data
120	is private host state and is never committed.
121	
122	## Publishing and handoff
123	
124	The wizard offers GitHub or GitLab only when its CLI is installed and
125	authenticated. Local-only and private visibility are the defaults. Publication
126	uses the local repository name and configured description, follows required
127	local commit steps, and optionally pushes the initial/current branch. A remote
128	or push failure never deletes the checkout.
129	
130	Final handoffs are explicit:
131	
132	- `stay` prints the result.
133	- `cd` enters it through `dev shell-init`.
134	- `open` opens the configured runtime, falling back to `cd` with no runtime.
135	- `start` continues into the normal tracked-task wizard.
136	
137	Neither repository bootstrap nor `dev start` launches a coding agent.
138
```

74		}

90		if r.Bare {
91			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%s is a bare repository and cannot host a task checkout", r.Display())
92		}
93	
94		name := strings.TrimSpace(req.Name)
95		if name == "" && req.Branch != "" && req.Mode != task.ModeDirect {
96			name = req.Branch
97		}
98		if name == "" {
99			return nil, errors.New("give the work a name: dev start <repo> --task <name>")
100		}
101	
102		branch, base := strings.TrimSpace(req.Branch), strings.TrimSpace(req.Base)
103		mode := req.Mode
104		if mode == "" {
105			mode = task.ModeWorktree
106		}
107		switch mode {
108		case task.ModeDirect:
109			st, err := gitx.StatusOf(ctx, r.Path)
110			if err != nil {
111				return nil, err
112			}
113			if st.Detached || st.Branch == "" {
114				return nil, errors.New("--direct needs a named branch; this checkout has detached HEAD")
115			}
116			if branch != "" && branch != st.Branch {
117				return nil, fmt.Errorf("--direct tracks the branch already checked out (%s), not --branch %s; "+
118					"omit --branch or use --branch-only", st.Branch, branch)
119			}
120			branch, base = st.Branch, st.Branch
121	
122		case task.ModeBranch, task.ModeWorktree:
123			if branch == "" {

125			}
126			if base == "" {

128			}
129			if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, r.Path, "check-ref-format", "--branch", branch); err != nil {
130				return nil, fmt.Errorf("invalid branch %q: %w", branch, err)
131			}
132			if !gitx.BranchExists(ctx, r.Path, branch) {
133				if base == "" {
134					return nil, errors.New("cannot determine a base ref; enter one explicitly")
135				}
136				if !gitx.RefExists(ctx, r.Path, base) {
137					return nil, fmt.Errorf("base ref %q does not exist in %s", base, r.Path)
138				}
139			}
140	
141		default:
142			return nil, fmt.Errorf("unknown start mode %q", mode)
143		}
144		if req.Run != "" && mode != task.ModeWorktree {
145			return nil, errors.New("--run requires the default worktree mode; it cannot be used with --direct or --branch-only")
146		}

149		existing, err := existingTaskForStart(app.Tasks, id)
150		if err != nil {
151			return nil, err
152		}
153		if existing != nil && existing.State != task.Done {
154			return nil, fmt.Errorf("task %s already exists (state %s) — use `dev resume %s`",
155				existing.ID, existing.State, existing.ID)
156		}
157	
158		spec := &startSpec{
159			RepoPath: r.Path, RepoName: r.Name, Category: r.Category,
160			Name: name, Branch: branch, Base: base, Next: req.Next, Run: req.Run, Mode: mode,
161			NoProvision: req.NoProvision, Focus: req.Focus,
162		}

168			}

2	
3	## Context
4	
5	The user wants quick thoughts attached to a repository and triggerable directly
6	from the TASKS/REPOS TUI. Notes must live in dev's sidecar state rather than

9	`internal/catalog` with stable asset IDs, path/symlink/common-dir matching and
10	cross-host locations. Notes should wait for that work to land and use its stable
11	repository ID rather than invent a competing identity.
12	
13	Chosen interaction:
14	
15	- multiple append-only notes, not one overwritable scratchpad;
16	- `n` adds a quick one-line note to the selected local repo;
17	- `N` opens a notes overlay for browse/search/edit/delete;
18	- Markdown files are durable truth; SQLite FTS is a disposable index;
19	- `td` and `beads` stay optional future adapters, not core dependencies.

21	## Dependency / sequencing
22	
23	1. Wait until the catalog agent's changes are committed and available on the
24	   current branch.
25	2. Verify the final `catalog.Registry` API and storage location before writing
26	   notes code. Reuse `EnsureRepository`, `Match`, stable `Entry.ID`, and
27	   host-local location matching.
28	3. Do not modify or stage the other agent's currently untracked
29	   `internal/catalog/`, `internal/pathx/`, or App/config integration while it is
30	   active.
31	
32	## Storage design
33	
34	### Durable source of truth
35	
36	```
37	$XDG_DATA_HOME/dev/notes/
38	└── <catalog-repository-id>/
39	    ├── <uuid>.md
40	    └── <uuid>.md
41	```
42	
43	One file per thought minimizes cross-machine merge conflicts and keeps every
44	note readable/exportable without dev. Each file uses YAML/TOML-style frontmatter
45	plus Markdown body:
46	
47	```markdown
48	---
49	schema_version: 1
50	id: <uuid>
51	repository_id: <catalog-id>
52	created: 2026-08-27T10:30:00Z
53	updated: 2026-08-27T10:30:00Z
54	tags: [idea, follow-up]
55	---
56	
57	Try replacing the polling loop with an event subscription.
58	```
59	
60	The filename ID and frontmatter ID must agree. Writes are temp-file + atomic
61	rename. Editing preserves ID/created/repository ID. Deleting requires explicit
62	confirmation (`--yes` escape hatch).
63	
64	### Search index (disposable)
65	
66	```
67	$XDG_CACHE_HOME/dev/notes.db
68	```
69	
70	Use the existing pure-Go `modernc.org/sqlite` dependency with FTS5. Index note
71	body, tags, repo display name and catalog ID. The Markdown files remain
72	authoritative; if the database is absent/stale/corrupt, rebuild it.
73	
74	- `dev note reindex` performs an explicit rebuild.
75	- add/edit/delete update the index incrementally.
76	- search detects a missing index and builds it.
77	- `dev cache list` reports `notes`; `dev cache clear notes` deletes only the
78	  FTS database and never the Markdown source.
79	- `stats.db` remains activity-only. Do not add note tables to it.
80	
81	## CLI surface
82	
83	Add `internal/note/` for the file store and FTS index, then wire:
84	
85	```bash
86	dev note add [repo] "thought" [--tag TAG...]
87	dev note add [repo] --editor
88	dev note list [repo] [--tag TAG] [--json]
89	dev note show <note-id>
90	dev note search <query> [--repo REPO] [--json]
91	dev note edit <note-id> [--editor CMD]
92	dev note delete <note-id> [--yes]
93	dev note path [repo]
94	dev note reindex
95	```

97	Repo inference follows existing command conventions: explicit repo argument,
98	otherwise task/repository containing cwd. Resolve/ensure repository identity

100	Git common dir and normalised remote identity.

111	
112	- TASKS / REPOS: `n` opens a one-line prompt for the selected repo.
113	- REMOTE: only enabled when a local clone exists.
114	- Enter atomically creates one note and refreshes note counts/latest preview.
115	- Esc cancels without writing.

118	
119	Default scope is the selected repository:
120	
121	```text
122	NOTES · dev-cli                                     4 notes
123	
124	  WHEN   TAGS              THOUGHT
125	▸ 2m     idea,git          distinguish staged vs unstaged counts
126	  3d     follow-up         test glab member endpoint on newer CLI
127	
128	j/k move · / search · Enter expand · a add · e edit · d delete · Esc back

138	- The global `e = edit config` remains unchanged outside the notes overlay.

145	
146	Create a small adapter from live `repo.Repo` / task checkout facts to

284		return Config{

287				TriesRoot:    "~/src/tries",

303			},

305			Bootstrap: Bootstrap{

307				FollowSymlinks: true,
308				Layout:         "flat",
309			},

314			},

316		}

319	// Load reads config.toml over the defaults. A missing file is not an error —
320	// dev must be useful with zero setup. A malformed file is, because silently
321	// falling back to defaults would send worktrees to the wrong volume.
322	func Load(path string) (Config, error) {
323		cfg := Default()
324		if path == "" {
325			path = ConfigFile()
326		}
327		md, err := toml.DecodeFile(path, &cfg)
328		switch {
329		case errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist):
330			return cfg, nil
331		case err != nil:
332			return cfg, fmt.Errorf("read %s: %w", path, err)
333		}
334		if undecoded := md.Undecoded(); len(undecoded) > 0 {
335			// Unknown keys are usually typos ("worktree_dir" vs "worktree_root").
336			// Warn rather than fail so a newer config still works on an older dev.
337			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "dev: warning: unknown key(s) in %s: %v\n", path, undecoded)
338		}
339		cfg.Source = path
340		return cfg, cfg.Validate()
341	}
342	
343	// Validate catches the settings that would otherwise fail deep inside a
344	// worktree create, when a directory has already been made.
345	func (c Config) Validate() error {
346		switch c.Runtime.Backend {
347		case "", "auto", "herdr", "tmux", "zellij", "none":
348		default:
349			return fmt.Errorf("runtime.backend %q: want auto, herdr, tmux, zellij or none", c.Runtime.Backend)
350		}
351		if c.Paths.WorktreePath == "" {
352			return errors.New("paths.worktree_path must not be empty")
353		}
354		if _, err := Render(c.Paths.WorktreePath, c.probeVars()); err != nil {
355			return fmt.Errorf("paths.worktree_path: %w", err)
356		}
357		if err := c.LocalFiles.Limits().Validate(); err != nil {
358			return fmt.Errorf("local_files: %w", err)
359		}
360		switch c.Bootstrap.Layout {
361		case "", "flat", "preserve":
362		default:
363			return fmt.Errorf("bootstrap.layout %q: want flat or preserve", c.Bootstrap.Layout)
364		}
365		if c.Bootstrap.MaxDepth < 0 {
366			return fmt.Errorf("bootstrap.max_depth must be zero (unlimited) or positive")
367		}
368		if c.Forge.RemoteLimit < 0 {
369			return fmt.Errorf("deprecated forge.remote_limit must be zero or positive")
370		}
371		seenAzureTargets := map[string]bool{}
372		for i, target := range c.Forge.AzureDevOps {
373			organization := strings.TrimSpace(target.Organization)
374			project := strings.TrimSpace(target.Project)
375			if !validAzureDevOpsOrganization(organization) {
376				return fmt.Errorf("forge.azure_devops[%d].organization %q: want an Azure DevOps Services URL like https://dev.azure.com/acme", i, target.Organization)
377			}
378			if project == "" {
379				return fmt.Errorf("forge.azure_devops[%d].project must not be empty", i)
380			}
381			key := strings.ToLower(strings.TrimRight(organization, "/") + "/" + project)
382			if seenAzureTargets[key] {
383				return fmt.Errorf("forge.azure_devops[%d] duplicates organization/project %s / %s", i, organization, project)
384			}
385			seenAzureTargets[key] = true
386		}
387		validStrategy := func(v string) bool {
388			switch v {
389			case "", "reinstall", "copy", "link", "skip":
390				return true
391			}
392			return false
393		}
394		if !validStrategy(c.Worktree.Strategy) {
395			return fmt.Errorf("worktree.strategy %q: want reinstall, copy, link or skip", c.Worktree.Strategy)
396		}
397		for ecosystem, strategy := range c.Worktree.Strategies {
398			if !validStrategy(strategy) {
399				return fmt.Errorf("worktree.strategies.%s %q: want reinstall, copy, link or skip",

```go
// Package textmatch provides the small query language shared by interactive
// lists. It deliberately matches terms rather than assigning fuzzy scores so
// filtering stays predictable across dev's built-in interfaces.
package textmatch

import "strings"

// Terms reports whether every whitespace-separated query term appears in the
// haystack, case-insensitively and in any order. An empty query matches all.
func Terms(haystack, query string) bool {
	haystack = strings.ToLower(haystack)
	query = strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(query))
	for _, term := range strings.Fields(query) {
		if !strings.Contains(haystack, term) {
			return false
		}
	}
	return true
}

// Package picker selects one value from a caller-provided list. It can hand
// the terminal to a line-oriented external picker such as fzf, and otherwise
// falls back to dev's built-in Bubble Tea interface.
package picker

import (
	"bytes"
	"context"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"io"
	"os/exec"
	"strings"
)

// Item is one selectable value. Value is opaque caller data and is never sent
// to an external picker; Label and Description are display-only.
type Item struct {
	Value       string
	Label       string
	Description string
}

// Request describes one selection interaction.
type Request struct {
	Prompt       string
	InitialQuery string
	Items        []Item
}

// Result distinguishes a selection from an explicit cancellation.
type Result struct {
	Item     Item
	Selected bool
	Canceled bool
}

// Selector owns the streams and optional external command for one application.
type Selector struct {
	in      io.Reader
	out     io.Writer
	errOut  io.Writer
	command []string
	lookPath func(string) (string, error)
}

// New constructs a selector. command is an argv vector, not a shell command;
// an empty vector always selects the built-in backend.
func New(in io.Reader, out, errOut io.Writer, command []string) *Selector {
	return &Selector{
		in:       in,
		out:      out,
		errOut:   errOut,
		command:  append([]string(nil), command...),
		lookPath: exec.LookPath,
	}
}

// Select uses the configured external picker when it is installed and the
// built-in picker otherwise.
func (s *Selector) Select(ctx context.Context, request Request) (Result, error) {
	if len(request.Items) == 0 {
		return Result{}, nil
	}
	if len(s.command) == 0 {
		return s.selectBuiltin(ctx, request)
	}
	path, err := s.lookPath(s.command[0])
	if err != nil {
		return s.selectBuiltin(ctx, request)
	}
	return s.selectExternal(ctx, path, request)
}

func (s *Selector) selectExternal(ctx context.Context, path string, request Request) (Result, error) {
	lines, items := renderCandidates(request.Items)
	args := make([]string, len(s.command)-1)
	for index, arg := range s.command[1:] {
		args[index] = strings.ReplaceAll(arg, "{prompt}", request.Prompt)
	}
	cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, path, args...)
	cmd.Stdin = strings.NewReader(strings.Join(lines, "\n") + "\n")
	if s.errOut == nil {
		cmd.Stderr = io.Discard
	} else {
		cmd.Stderr = s.errOut
	}
	var stdout bytes.Buffer
	cmd.Stdout = &stdout

	err := cmd.Run()
	if ctxErr := ctx.Err(); ctxErr != nil {
		return Result{}, ctxErr
	}
	if err != nil {
		var exitErr *exec.ExitError
		if errors.As(err, &exitErr) && (exitErr.ExitCode() == 1 || exitErr.ExitCode() == 130) {
			return Result{Canceled: true}, nil
		}
		return Result{}, fmt.Errorf("external picker: %w", err)
	}

	selected, err := selectedLine(stdout.String())
	if err != nil {
		return Result{}, err
	}
	item, ok := items[selected]
	if !ok {
		return Result{}, fmt.Errorf("external picker returned an unknown selection")
	}
	return Result{Item: item, Selected: true}, nil
}

func selectedLine(output string) (string, error) {
	output = strings.TrimSuffix(output, "\n")
	output = strings.TrimSuffix(output, "\r")
	if output == "" || strings.ContainsAny(output, "\r\n\x00") {
		return "", errors.New("external picker returned malformed output")
	}
	return output, nil
}

func renderCandidates(items []Item) ([]string, map[string]Item) {
	lines := make([]string, 0, len(items))
	byLine := make(map[string]Item, len(items))
	for _, item := range items {
		label := cleanDisplay(item.Label)
		if label == "" {
			label = cleanDisplay(item.Value)
		}
		base := label
		if description := cleanDisplay(item.Description); description != "" {
			base += "\t" + description
		}
		line := base
		for ordinal := 2; ; ordinal++ {
			if _, exists := byLine[line]; !exists {
				break
			}
			line = fmt.Sprintf("%s\t[%d]", base, ordinal)
		}
		lines = append(lines, line)
		byLine[line] = item
	}
	return lines, byLine
}

func cleanDisplay(value string) string {
	return strings.Join(strings.FieldsFunc(value, func(r rune) bool {
		return r == '\r' || r == '\n' || r == '\t' || r == 0
	}), " ")
}

```go
package picker

import (
	"context"
	"fmt"
	"strings"

	"github.com/charmbracelet/bubbles/textinput"
	tea "github.com/charmbracelet/bubbletea"
	"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/textmatch"
)

const defaultVisibleRows = 10

type builtinModel struct {
	prompt   string
	input    textinput.Model
	items    []Item
	visible  []int
	cursor   int
	offset   int
	rows     int
	width    int
	done     bool
	canceled bool
	selected Item
}

func newBuiltinModel(request Request) builtinModel {
	input := textinput.New()
	input.Prompt = fmt.Sprintf("? %s: ", request.Prompt)
	input.SetValue(request.InitialQuery)
	input.Focus()
	model := builtinModel{
		prompt: request.Prompt,
		input:  input,
		items:  append([]Item(nil), request.Items...),
		rows:   defaultVisibleRows,
	}
	model.refilter()
	return model
}

func (m builtinModel) Init() tea.Cmd {
	return textinput.Blink
}

func (m builtinModel) Update(message tea.Msg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
	switch msg := message.(type) {
	case tea.WindowSizeMsg:
		m.width = msg.Width
		if available := msg.Height - 3; available > 0 && available < defaultVisibleRows {
			m.rows = available
		} else {
			m.rows = defaultVisibleRows
		}
		m.keepVisible()
		return m, nil
	case tea.KeyMsg:
		switch msg.Type {
		case tea.KeyEsc, tea.KeyCtrlC:
			m.done = true
			m.canceled = true
			m.input.Blur()
			return m, tea.Quit
		case tea.KeyEnter:
			if len(m.visible) == 0 {
				return m, nil
			}
			m.done = true
			m.selected = m.items[m.visible[m.cursor]]
			m.input.Blur()
			return m, tea.Quit
		case tea.KeyUp, tea.KeyCtrlP:
			m.move(-1)
			return m, nil
		case tea.KeyDown, tea.KeyCtrlN:
			m.move(1)
			return m, nil
		}
	}

	var command tea.Cmd
	m.input, command = m.input.Update(message)
	m.refilter()
	return m, command
}

func (m builtinModel) View() string {
	if m.done {
		return "\n"
	}
	var out strings.Builder
	out.WriteString(m.input.View())
	out.WriteByte('\n')
	if len(m.visible) == 0 {
		out.WriteString("  No matches\n")
		return out.String()
	}
	end := m.offset + m.rows
	if end > len(m.visible) {
		end = len(m.visible)
	}
	for position := m.offset; position < end; position++ {
		item := m.items[m.visible[position]]
		marker := "  "
		if position == m.cursor {
			marker = "> "
		}
		line := marker + item.Label
		if item.Description != "" {
			line += "  " + item.Description
		}
		out.WriteString(clipRunes(line, m.width))
		out.WriteByte('\n')
	}
	return out.String()
}

func (m *builtinModel) refilter() {
	m.visible = m.visible[:0]
	for index, item := range m.items {
		if textmatch.Terms(item.Label+" "+item.Description, m.input.Value()) {
			m.visible = append(m.visible, index)
		}
	}
	m.cursor = 0
	m.offset = 0
}

func (m *builtinModel) move(delta int) {
	if len(m.visible) == 0 {
		return
	}
	m.cursor += delta
	if m.cursor < 0 {
		m.cursor = len(m.visible) - 1
	}
	if m.cursor >= len(m.visible) {
		m.cursor = 0
	}
	m.keepVisible()
}

func (m *builtinModel) keepVisible() {
	if m.rows <= 0 {
		m.rows = 1
	}
	if m.cursor < m.offset {
		m.offset = m.cursor
	}
	if m.cursor >= m.offset+m.rows {
		m.offset = m.cursor - m.rows + 1
	}
}

func clipRunes(value string, width int) string {
	if width <= 0 {
		return value
	}
	runes := []rune(value)
	if len(runes) <= width {
		return value
	}
	if width == 1 {
		return "…"
	}
	return string(runes[:width-1]) + "…"
}

func (s *Selector) selectBuiltin(ctx context.Context, request Request) (Result, error) {
	program := tea.NewProgram(
		newBuiltinModel(request),
		tea.WithInput(s.in),
		tea.WithOutput(s.out),
		tea.WithContext(ctx),
	)
	final, err := program.Run()
	if ctxErr := ctx.Err(); ctxErr != nil {
		return Result{}, ctxErr
	}
	if err != nil {
		return Result{}, fmt.Errorf("built-in picker: %w", err)
	}
	model, ok := final.(builtinModel)
	if !ok {
		return Result{}, fmt.Errorf("built-in picker returned an unexpected model")
	}
	if model.canceled {
		return Result{Canceled: true}, nil
	}
	if !model.done {
		return Result{}, nil
	}
	return Result{Item: model.selected, Selected: true}, nil
}

71	// Sessions returns every runtime session attached to any checkout in this
72	// repository.
73	func (r RepoRow) Sessions() []runtime.Session { return r.Context.Sessions() }
74	
75	// HotTasks counts the repository's tasks that are currently hot.
76	// IsTry reports an ungraduated Try that should live in the dedicated TRY view,
77	// while remaining in the model's local snapshot for REMOTE matching.
78	func (r RepoRow) IsTry() bool {
79		return r.Asset != nil && r.Asset.Kind == catalog.KindTry && r.Asset.Experiment != nil &&
80			(r.Asset.Experiment.Phase == catalog.PhaseActive || r.Asset.Experiment.Phase == catalog.PhaseDeprecated)
81	}
82	
83	func (r RepoRow) HotTasks() int {
84		n := 0
85		for _, t := range r.Tasks {
86			if t.State == task.Hot {
87				n++
88			}
89		}
90		return n
91	}
92	
93	// StateSummary renders the repository's tasks as a compact per-state tally,
94	// which is what makes the list scannable at forty repositories.
95	func (r RepoRow) StateSummary() string {
96		if len(r.Tasks) == 0 {
97			return ""
98		}
99		counts := map[task.State]int{}
100		for _, t := range r.Tasks {
101			counts[t.State]++
102		}
103		var parts []string
104		for _, s := range task.States {
105			if counts[s] > 0 {
106				parts = append(parts, s.Icon()+strconv.Itoa(counts[s]))
107			}
108		}
109		return strings.Join(parts, " ")
110	}
111	
112	// searchText is what a filter query matches against.
113	func (r RepoRow) searchText() string {
114		var b strings.Builder
115		b.WriteString(r.Repo.Display())
116		b.WriteString(" ")
117		b.WriteString(r.Status.Branch)
118		b.WriteString(" ")
119		b.WriteString(r.Topology.Summary())
120		for _, branch := range r.Topology.Branches {
121			b.WriteString(" ")
122			b.WriteString(branch.Branch)
123			b.WriteString(" ")
124			b.WriteString(branch.Upstream)
125		}
126		if r.Asset != nil {
127			b.WriteString(" ")
128			b.WriteString(string(r.Asset.Kind))
129			b.WriteString(" ")
130			b.WriteString(r.Asset.Note)
131			b.WriteString(" ")
132			b.WriteString(strings.Join(r.Asset.Tags, " "))
133		}
134		for _, t := range r.Tasks {
135			b.WriteString(" ")
136			b.WriteString(t.Title())
137			b.WriteString(" ")
138			b.WriteString(t.Branch)
139		}
140		for _, checkout := range r.Context.Checkouts {
141			b.WriteString(" ")
142			b.WriteString(checkout.Worktree.Path)
143			b.WriteString(" ")
144			b.WriteString(checkout.Branch())
145			b.WriteString(" ")
146			b.WriteString(string(checkout.Ownership))
147		}
148		return strings.ToLower(b.String())
149	}
150	
151	func (r RepoRow) matches(query string) bool {
152		query = strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(query))
153		for _, term := range strings.Fields(query) {
154			key, value, structured := strings.Cut(term, ":")
155			if structured {
156				switch key {
157				case "tag":
158					if r.Asset == nil || !r.Asset.HasTag(value) {
159						return false
160					}
161					continue
162				case "remote":
163					if !strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(r.Topology.Summary()), value) {
164						return false
165					}
166					continue
167				case "size":
168					if !matchesSize(r.Usage, value) {
169						return false
170					}
171					continue
172				case "kind":
173					kind := catalog.KindRepository
174					if r.Asset != nil {
175						kind = r.Asset.Kind
176					}
177					if string(kind) != value {
178						return false
179					}
180					continue
181				}
182			}
183			if !strings.Contains(r.searchText(), term) {
184				return false
185			}
186		}
187		return true
188	}
189	
190	// taskSearchText is what a filter query matches a task row against.
191	func taskSearchText(r inventory.Row) string {
192		t := r.Task
193		return strings.ToLower(strings.Join([]string{
194			t.Title(), t.Repo, t.Branch, t.Next, t.Note, string(t.State),
195		}, " "))
196	}
197	
198	// matches reports whether every whitespace-separated term of the query appears
199	// in the haystack.
200	//
201	// Term-wise rather than substring so "auth api" finds a task named "api token
202	// auth" — the order words come to mind in is rarely the order they appear in.
203	func matches(haystack, query string) bool {
204		query = strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(query))
205		if query == "" {
206			return true
207		}
208		for _, term := range strings.Fields(query) {
209			if !strings.Contains(haystack, term) {
210				return false
211			}
212		}
213		return true
214	}

217	// a local checkout. The REMOTE view is the bridge between "what exists on the
218	// forge" and "what is already on this machine".
219	type RemoteRow struct {
220		Repo forge.RemoteRepo `json:"repo"`

1	// Package picker selects one value from a caller-provided list. It can hand
2	// the terminal to a line-oriented external picker such as fzf, and otherwise
3	// falls back to dev's built-in Bubble Tea interface.
4	package picker
5	
6	import (
7		"bytes"
8		"context"
9		"errors"
10		"fmt"
11		"io"
12		"os/exec"
13		"strings"
14	)
15	
16	// Item is one selectable value. Value is opaque caller data and is never sent
17	// to an external picker; Label and Description are display-only.
18	type Item struct {
19		Value       string
20		Label       string
21		Description string
22	}
23	
24	// Request describes one selection interaction.
25	type Request struct {
26		Prompt       string
27		InitialQuery string
28		Items        []Item
29	}
30	
31	// Result distinguishes a selection from an explicit cancellation.
32	type Result struct {
33		Item     Item
34		Selected bool
35		Canceled bool
36	}
37	
38	// Selector owns the streams and optional external command for one application.
39	type Selector struct {
40		in      io.Reader
41		out     io.Writer
42		errOut  io.Writer
43		command []string
44		lookPath func(string) (string, error)
45	}
46	
47	// New constructs a selector. command is an argv vector, not a shell command;
48	// an empty vector always selects the built-in backend.
49	func New(in io.Reader, out, errOut io.Writer, command []string) *Selector {
50		return &Selector{
51			in:       in,
52			out:      out,
53			errOut:   errOut,
54			command:  append([]string(nil), command...),
55			lookPath: exec.LookPath,
56		}
57	}
58	
59	// Select uses the configured external picker when it is installed and the
60	// built-in picker otherwise.
61	func (s *Selector) Select(ctx context.Context, request Request) (Result, error) {
62		if len(request.Items) == 0 {
63			return Result{}, nil
64		}
65		if len(s.command) == 0 {
66			return s.selectBuiltin(ctx, request)
67		}
68		path, err := s.lookPath(s.command[0])
69		if err != nil {
70			return s.selectBuiltin(ctx, request)
71		}
72		return s.selectExternal(ctx, path, request)
73	}
74	
75	func (s *Selector) selectExternal(ctx context.Context, path string, request Request) (Result, error) {
76		lines, items := renderCandidates(request.Items)
77		args := make([]string, len(s.command)-1)
78		for index, arg := range s.command[1:] {
79			args[index] = strings.ReplaceAll(arg, "{prompt}", request.Prompt)
80		}
81		cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, path, args...)
82		cmd.Stdin = strings.NewReader(strings.Join(lines, "\n") + "\n")
83		if s.errOut == nil {
84			cmd.Stderr = io.Discard
85		} else {
86			cmd.Stderr = s.errOut
87		}
88		var stdout bytes.Buffer
89		cmd.Stdout = &stdout
90	
91		err := cmd.Run()
92		if ctxErr := ctx.Err(); ctxErr != nil {
93			return Result{}, ctxErr
94		}
95		if err != nil {
96			var exitErr *exec.ExitError
97			if errors.As(err, &exitErr) && (exitErr.ExitCode() == 1 || exitErr.ExitCode() == 130) {
98				return Result{Canceled: true}, nil
99			}
100			return Result{}, fmt.Errorf("external picker: %w", err)
101		}
102	
103		selected, err := selectedLine(stdout.String())
104		if err != nil {
105			return Result{}, err
106		}
107		item, ok := items[selected]
108		if !ok {
109			return Result{}, fmt.Errorf("external picker returned an unknown selection")
110		}
111		return Result{Item: item, Selected: true}, nil
112	}
113	
114	func selectedLine(output string) (string, error) {
115		output = strings.TrimSuffix(output, "\n")
116		output = strings.TrimSuffix(output, "\r")
117		if output == "" || strings.ContainsAny(output, "\r\n\x00") {
118			return "", errors.New("external picker returned malformed output")
119		}
120		return output, nil
121	}
122	
123	func renderCandidates(items []Item) ([]string, map[string]Item) {
124		lines := make([]string, 0, len(items))
125		byLine := make(map[string]Item, len(items))
126		for _, item := range items {
127			label := cleanDisplay(item.Label)
128			if label == "" {
129				label = cleanDisplay(item.Value)
130			}
131			base := label
132			if description := cleanDisplay(item.Description); description != "" {
133				base += "\t" + description
134			}
135			line := base
136			for ordinal := 2; ; ordinal++ {
137				if _, exists := byLine[line]; !exists {
138					break
139				}
140				line = fmt.Sprintf("%s\t[%d]", base, ordinal)
141			}
142			lines = append(lines, line)
143			byLine[line] = item
144		}
145		return lines, byLine
146	}
147	
148	func cleanDisplay(value string) string {
149		return strings.Join(strings.FieldsFunc(value, func(r rune) bool {
150			return r == '\r' || r == '\n' || r == '\t' || r == 0
151		}), " ")
152	}
153

1	package picker
2	
3	import (
4		"context"
5		"fmt"
6		"strings"
7	
8		"github.com/charmbracelet/bubbles/textinput"
9		tea "github.com/charmbracelet/bubbletea"
10		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/textmatch"
11	)
12	
13	const defaultVisibleRows = 10
14	
15	type builtinModel struct {
16		prompt   string
17		input    textinput.Model
18		items    []Item
19		visible  []int
20		cursor   int
21		offset   int
22		rows     int
23		width    int
24		done     bool
25		canceled bool
26		selected Item
27	}
28	
29	func newBuiltinModel(request Request) builtinModel {
30		input := textinput.New()
31		input.Prompt = fmt.Sprintf("? %s: ", request.Prompt)
32		input.SetValue(request.InitialQuery)
33		input.Focus()
34		model := builtinModel{
35			prompt: request.Prompt,
36			input:  input,
37			items:  append([]Item(nil), request.Items...),
38			rows:   defaultVisibleRows,
39		}
40		model.refilter()
41		return model
42	}
43	
44	func (m builtinModel) Init() tea.Cmd {
45		return textinput.Blink
46	}
47	
48	func (m builtinModel) Update(message tea.Msg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
49		switch msg := message.(type) {
50		case tea.WindowSizeMsg:
51			m.width = msg.Width
52			if available := msg.Height - 3; available > 0 && available < defaultVisibleRows {
53				m.rows = available
54			} else {
55				m.rows = defaultVisibleRows
56			}
57			m.keepVisible()
58			return m, nil
59		case tea.KeyMsg:
60			switch msg.Type {
61			case tea.KeyEsc, tea.KeyCtrlC:
62				m.done = true
63				m.canceled = true
64				m.input.Blur()
65				return m, tea.Quit
66			case tea.KeyEnter:
67				if len(m.visible) == 0 {
68					return m, nil
69				}
70				m.done = true
71				m.selected = m.items[m.visible[m.cursor]]
72				m.input.Blur()
73				return m, tea.Quit
74			case tea.KeyUp, tea.KeyCtrlP:
75				m.move(-1)
76				return m, nil
77			case tea.KeyDown, tea.KeyCtrlN:
78				m.move(1)
79				return m, nil
80			}
81		}
82	
83		var command tea.Cmd
84		m.input, command = m.input.Update(message)
85		m.refilter()
86		return m, command
87	}
88	
89	func (m builtinModel) View() string {
90		if m.done {
91			return "\n"
92		}
93		var out strings.Builder
94		out.WriteString(m.input.View())
95		out.WriteByte('\n')
96		if len(m.visible) == 0 {
97			out.WriteString("  No matches\n")
98			return out.String()
99		}
100		end := m.offset + m.rows
101		if end > len(m.visible) {
102			end = len(m.visible)
103		}
104		for position := m.offset; position < end; position++ {
105			item := m.items[m.visible[position]]
106			marker := "  "
107			if position == m.cursor {
108				marker = "> "
109			}
110			line := marker + item.Label
111			if item.Description != "" {
112				line += "  " + item.Description
113			}
114			out.WriteString(clipRunes(line, m.width))
115			out.WriteByte('\n')
116		}
117		return out.String()
118	}
119	
120	func (m *builtinModel) refilter() {
121		m.visible = m.visible[:0]
122		for index, item := range m.items {
123			if textmatch.Terms(item.Label+" "+item.Description, m.input.Value()) {
124				m.visible = append(m.visible, index)
125			}
126		}
127		m.cursor = 0
128		m.offset = 0
129	}
130	
131	func (m *builtinModel) move(delta int) {
132		if len(m.visible) == 0 {
133			return
134		}
135		m.cursor += delta
136		if m.cursor < 0 {
137			m.cursor = len(m.visible) - 1
138		}
139		if m.cursor >= len(m.visible) {
140			m.cursor = 0
141		}
142		m.keepVisible()
143	}
144	
145	func (m *builtinModel) keepVisible() {
146		if m.rows <= 0 {
147			m.rows = 1
148		}
149		if m.cursor < m.offset {
150			m.offset = m.cursor
151		}
152		if m.cursor >= m.offset+m.rows {
153			m.offset = m.cursor - m.rows + 1
154		}
155	}
156	
157	func clipRunes(value string, width int) string {
158		if width <= 0 {
159			return value
160		}
161		runes := []rune(value)
162		if len(runes) <= width {
163			return value
164		}
165		if width == 1 {
166			return "…"
167		}
168		return string(runes[:width-1]) + "…"
169	}
170	
171	func (s *Selector) selectBuiltin(ctx context.Context, request Request) (Result, error) {
172		program := tea.NewProgram(
173			newBuiltinModel(request),
174			tea.WithInput(s.in),
175			tea.WithOutput(s.out),
176			tea.WithContext(ctx),
177		)
178		final, err := program.Run()
179		if ctxErr := ctx.Err(); ctxErr != nil {
180			return Result{}, ctxErr
181		}
182		if err != nil {
183			return Result{}, fmt.Errorf("built-in picker: %w", err)
184		}
185		model, ok := final.(builtinModel)
186		if !ok {
187			return Result{}, fmt.Errorf("built-in picker returned an unexpected model")
188		}
189		if model.canceled {
190			return Result{Canceled: true}, nil
191		}
192		if !model.done {
193			return Result{}, nil
194		}
195		return Result{Item: model.selected, Selected: true}, nil
196	}
197

func TestTerms(t *testing.T) {

package picker

import (

	tea "github.com/charmbracelet/bubbletea"

func TestRenderCandidatesKeepsDuplicateItemsDistinct(t *testing.T) {
	items := []Item{
		{Value: "first", Label: "same", Description: "description"},
		{Value: "second", Label: "same", Description: "description"},
		{Value: "third", Label: "line\nwith\ttabs", Description: "clean\x00me"},
	}
	lines, byLine := renderCandidates(items)
	if len(lines) != len(items) || lines[0] == lines[1] {
		t.Fatalf("rendered lines = %q", lines)
	}
	for index, line := range lines {
		if got := byLine[line].Value; got != items[index].Value {
			t.Fatalf("line %d maps to %q, want %q", index, got, items[index].Value)
		}
		if strings.ContainsAny(line, "\r\n\x00") {
			t.Fatalf("unsafe rendered line %q", line)
		}
	}
}

func TestBuiltinModelFiltersNavigatesAndCancels(t *testing.T) {
	request := Request{Prompt: "Repository", Items: []Item{
		{Value: "one", Label: "alpha", Description: "service"},
		{Value: "two", Label: "beta", Description: "service"},
		{Value: "three", Label: "gamma", Description: "docs"},
	}}
	model := newBuiltinModel(request)
	updated, _ := model.Update(tea.KeyMsg{Type: tea.KeyRunes, Runes: []rune("service")})
	model = updated.(builtinModel)
	if len(model.visible) != 2 {
		t.Fatalf("visible = %v", model.visible)
	}
	updated, _ = model.Update(tea.KeyMsg{Type: tea.KeyDown})
	model = updated.(builtinModel)
	updated, command := model.Update(tea.KeyMsg{Type: tea.KeyEnter})
	model = updated.(builtinModel)
	if command == nil || !model.done || model.canceled || model.selected.Value != "two" {
		t.Fatalf("selected model = %+v, command nil = %t", model, command == nil)
	}

	model = newBuiltinModel(request)
	updated, command = model.Update(tea.KeyMsg{Type: tea.KeyEsc})
	model = updated.(builtinModel)
	if command == nil || !model.done || !model.canceled {
		t.Fatalf("canceled model = %+v, command nil = %t", model, command == nil)
	}
}

func TestExternalPickerReturnsExactItem(t *testing.T) {
	t.Setenv("DEV_PICKER_HELPER", "select-second")
	selector := helperSelector()
	request := Request{Prompt: "Repo", Items: []Item{
		{Value: "first-value", Label: "same"},
		{Value: "second-value", Label: "same"},
	}}
	result, err := selector.Select(t.Context(), request)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if !result.Selected || result.Canceled || result.Item.Value != "second-value" {
		t.Fatalf("result = %+v", result)
	}
}

func TestExternalPickerCancellationCodes(t *testing.T) {
	for _, mode := range []string{"exit-1", "exit-130"} {
		t.Run(mode, func(t *testing.T) {
			t.Setenv("DEV_PICKER_HELPER", mode)
			result, err := helperSelector().Select(t.Context(), Request{Items: []Item{{Value: "v", Label: "item"}}})
			if err != nil || !result.Canceled || result.Selected {
				t.Fatalf("result = %+v, err = %v", result, err)
			}
		})
	}
}

func TestExternalPickerRejectsUnknownOutput(t *testing.T) {
	t.Setenv("DEV_PICKER_HELPER", "unknown")
	_, err := helperSelector().Select(t.Context(), Request{Items: []Item{{Value: "v", Label: "item"}}})
	if err == nil || !strings.Contains(err.Error(), "unknown selection") {
		t.Fatalf("err = %v", err)
	}
}

func TestExternalPickerHonorsContext(t *testing.T) {
	t.Setenv("DEV_PICKER_HELPER", "wait")
	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 50*time.Millisecond)
	defer cancel()
	_, err := helperSelector().Select(ctx, Request{Items: []Item{{Value: "v", Label: "item"}}})
	if !errors.Is(err, context.DeadlineExceeded) {
		t.Fatalf("err = %v", err)
	}
}

func helperSelector() *Selector {
	return New(nil, io.Discard, io.Discard, []string{
		os.Args[0], "-test.run=^TestPickerHelperProcess$", "--", "{prompt}",
	})
}

func TestPickerHelperProcess(t *testing.T) {
	mode := os.Getenv("DEV_PICKER_HELPER")
	if mode == "" {
		return
	}
	body, _ := io.ReadAll(os.Stdin)
	lines := strings.Split(strings.TrimSuffix(string(body), "\n"), "\n")
	switch mode {
	case "select-second":
		fmt.Fprintln(os.Stdout, lines[1])
	case "exit-1":
		os.Exit(1)
	case "exit-130":
		os.Exit(130)
	case "unknown":
		fmt.Fprintln(os.Stdout, "not one of the candidates")
	case "wait":
		time.Sleep(5 * time.Second)
	default:
		os.Exit(2)
	}
}
