```text
1	# Cached remote repositories known to dev.
2	#
3	# Populate or refresh the private cache first:
4	#   dev repo remote --refresh
5	#
6	# Usage:
7	#   tv dev-remote-repos
8	#   dev repo clone "$(tv dev-remote-repos)"
9	#
10	# Enter prints the exact provider clone URL. The source never refreshes the
11	# network; stale cache is still useful and dev reports that it should be updated.
12	
13	[metadata]
14	name = "dev-remote-repos"
15	description = "Select a cached forge repository known to dev"
16	requirements = ["dev", "jq"]
17	
18	[source]
19	command = '''dev repo remote --cached --json | jq -r '.[] | select(.repo.clone_url != null and .repo.clone_url != "") | select((.repo.clone_url | test("[\\t\\r\\n]")) | not) | [.repo.clone_url, (.repo.forge + ":" + .repo.full_name), (.repo.visibility // ""), (.local_path // ""), ((.repo.description // "") | gsub("[\\t\\r\\n]+"; " "))] | @tsv' '''
20	display = "{split:\\t:1}  {split:\\t:2}  {split:\\t:3}  │  {split:\\t:4}"
21	output = "{split:\\t:0}"
22	
23	[ui]
24	layout = "portrait"
25
```

```text
1	# Context
2	
3	`dev` already has robust domain-owned caches (forge remotes, fleet snapshots, disk sizes, note FTS, templates), but it has no generic cache of selectable CLI values and no picker integration. Repository discovery/inventory remains deliberately live. The first useful integration is therefore narrow: reuse the existing forge cache to choose a remote for `dev repo clone`, use fast live discovery to choose a local repository in the `dev start` wizard, and expose the existing `dev repo remote --json` contract to Television/fzf recipes. This removes repetitive path/name typing without making fzf mandatory, changing scripted behavior, or adding a second inventory/cache.
4	
5	The user selected an internal configurable picker plus composable external recipes, with a built-in Bubble Tea fallback. This slice intentionally does not add pickers to `dev done` (which already has task completion) or to every finite-choice command.
6	
7	## 1. Add a reusable, safe selector primitive
8	
9	- Add `internal/textmatch` with an exported term matcher equivalent to the current `internal/tui/rows.go:matches`: trim/lowercase, split whitespace, require every term as a substring. Have the TUI delegate to it so the built-in picker and `/` keep one tested matching contract; do not introduce a fuzzy-scoring dependency.
10	- Add `internal/picker` with small caller-neutral types such as:
11	  - `Item { Value, Label, Description string }`
12	  - `Request { Prompt, InitialQuery string; Items []Item }`
13	  - `Result { Item Item; Selected, Canceled bool }`
14	  - a selector object constructed with input/output/error streams and configured external argv, exposing `Select(context.Context, Request) (Result, error)`.
15	- Keep backend selection internal: use the configured external executable when `exec.LookPath` succeeds, otherwise use the built-in Bubble Tea backend. An explicitly empty argv forces the built-in backend. A configured executable that starts and then fails is an error rather than silently replaying the interaction in a second UI.
16	- Execute external argv directly with `exec.CommandContext`, never via a shell. Feed normalized, uniquely rendered candidate lines on child stdin, capture only the selected line from stdout, and leave stderr attached to the caller terminal for fzf-style UI. Map the exact returned line back to the source `Item`; decorate otherwise-identical rendered lines with a deterministic ordinal so duplicate labels/descriptions cannot select the wrong value. Reject unexpected/multiple output instead of guessing. Treat exit codes 1 and 130 as cancellation, propagate context cancellation, and report other exits.
17	- Support a literal `{prompt}` substitution in argv elements so the per-call label can reach fzf without shell interpolation. Newlines/NULs in item display fields are normalized before rendering; the opaque `Value` is never rendered or trusted back from the child.
18	- Implement the fallback as a compact Bubble Tea list with `bubbles/textinput`: live term filtering, up/down plus Ctrl-N/Ctrl-P, Enter to select, Esc/Ctrl-C to cancel, and a bounded viewport. Test the model directly rather than requiring a real terminal.
19	- Add an `App` adapter/test seam in `internal/cli` that passes `App.In/Out/Err` and `App.Cfg.Picker` into `internal/picker`. It should only open a picker when input and output are a terminal pair; non-TTY readers keep the existing deterministic line prompts.
20	
21	Critical files: `internal/picker/*.go`, `internal/textmatch/*.go`, `internal/tui/rows.go`, `internal/cli/app.go`, and a small `internal/cli/picker.go` adapter.
22	
23	## 2. Add minimal global picker configuration
24	
25	- Extend `internal/config/config.go` with `Config.Picker` and a global-only `[picker]` section containing one `command []string` argv vector. Default it to fzf with conservative presentation args and `{prompt}` (for example `fzf`, reverse layout, bounded height/border, and a prompt). `command = []` is the documented way to force the built-in picker.
26	- Keeping executable and arguments in one replacement-valued slice avoids a partial TOML overlay accidentally retaining fzf arguments when the executable is changed to `tv`, `sk`, or `gum`.
27	- Validation permits an empty vector, but rejects an empty first element and NUL/newline-bearing argv elements. It does not require the binary to be installed: absence is a supported fallback state.
28	- Add the annotated section to `internal/cli/config.go`'s starter config. `dev config show` will include it automatically. Keep picker policy out of repo-owned `.dev-cli/config.toml`.
29	- Extend `dev doctor` to identify the configured external selector as optional and state that the built-in picker will be used when it is unavailable; do not install anything.
30	
31	Critical files: `internal/config/config.go`, `internal/config/config_test.go`, `internal/cli/config.go`, `internal/cli/doctor.go` and focused CLI tests.
32	
33	## 3. Wire only the two approved interactive entry points
34	
35	### `dev repo clone`
36	
37	- In `internal/cli/repo_create_wizard.go:runRepoCloneWizard`, before the existing free-form source prompt, read the raw forge cache through `cachedRemoteRows(app)` / `forge.LoadCacheAny`. This is disk-only and must not trigger provider network calls or the expensive `matchRemoteLocals` repository scan.
38	- Build candidates from cache rows with non-empty `CloneURL`, displaying forge-qualified full name plus visibility/archived/description metadata. Preserve cache ordering (or the existing deterministic updated/name ordering). Use `RemoteRepo.CloneURL` as `Item.Value`, not `FullName`, so GitHub, GitLab (including self-hosted), and Azure DevOps keep the exact provider URL.
39	- Append a synthetic “Enter a URL, path, or owner/name…” item. Selecting it, having no usable cache/candidates, or running through non-TTY input goes through the current `prompter.line` path unchanged. A stale but source-compatible cache remains useful and is visibly warned as stale; a missing/source-mismatched cache simply falls back to manual entry. Never refresh the network merely to open the picker.
40	- Picker cancellation returns `errPromptCanceled`, preserving the command’s existing “Canceled; nothing was cloned” behavior. Explicit positional refs and non-interactive/`--json` behavior bypass the picker exactly as today.
41	- Do not add a costly local scan merely to badge/exclude already-cloned remotes. Existing destination/nested-repository checks remain authoritative and prevent unsafe duplicate acquisition.
42	
43	### `dev start`
44	
45	- Replace `internal/cli/start_wizard.go:promptStartRepository`’s numbered listing with the shared picker.
46	- Obtain candidates with `repo.Discover(..., repo.CompletionOptions())`, filter to non-bare Git repositories, and render `Repo.Display()` plus `config.Contract(Repo.Path)`. Put the current repository first when it resolves, while retaining a synthetic manual/name/path item for values not discovered under configured roots.
47	- Return the selected repo directly; the manual path continues through `repo.Resolve`. Preserve explicit `dev start <repo>`, non-TTY prompts, empty-inventory errors, and cancellation before any mutation.
48	
49	Tests should inject selector results through the `App` seam, so command/wizard tests do not depend on fzf, PTYs, or a developer’s PATH.
50	
51	## 4. Ship composable Television/fzf usage without another command
52	
53	- Do not add `dev pick`: `dev repo remote --cached --json` already supplies the cache-backed, pipe-friendly candidate contract, while `--refresh` explicitly populates it. Reusing this command avoids duplicate filtering, freshness, JSON, and cache semantics.
54	- Add `contrib/television/dev-remote-repos.toml`. Its source invokes `dev repo remote --cached --json` and `jq` to emit TSV containing exact `repo.clone_url`, display/full name, forge, visibility, local path, and description. Enter outputs the exact clone URL; an action can run `dev repo clone` on it. Metadata declares `dev` and `jq` requirements. The repository only ships the file; it does not modify the user’s Television/chezmoi configuration.
55	- Document both compositions near repository bootstrap:
56	  - initialize/refresh once with `dev repo remote --refresh`;
57	  - copy or symlink the channel and use `dev repo clone "$(tv dev-remote-repos)"`;
58	  - provide an fzf shell function that transforms the same JSON with `jq`, displays descriptive columns, extracts the exact clone URL, handles cancellation/empty output, and invokes `dev repo clone`.
59	- Explain that the internal no-argument clone picker needs neither `tv` nor `jq`, uses no network, and falls back to the built-in UI when its configured external command is absent.
60	
61	## 5. Record intentionally deferred picker surfaces
62	
63	Replace the completed `TODO.md` “Television / fzf channel” item with a scoped backlog item for extending the shared selector only where it improves over completion. List:
64	
65	- `tries *`, `graduate`, note show/edit/delete, fleet open/host, artifact discard, and skill update;
66	- interactive disambiguation for structured repo/experiment/catalog ambiguity errors;
67	- branch/base selection after adding one canonical `gitx` branch enumerator;
68	- larger enum sets currently handled by `prompter.choice`.
69	
70	Explicitly note that task lifecycle commands such as `dev done` already expose shell completion and should not automatically gain a picker merely because the primitive exists.
71	
72	## 6. Keep product surfaces synchronized
73	
74	- Add the user-visible feature to `[Unreleased]` in `CHANGELOG.md`.
```

```text
+func promptRepoCloneReference(app *App, p *prompter) (string, error) {
+	manual := func() (string, error) {
+		return p.line("Git URL, path, or owner/name", "")
+	}
+	if !app.canPick() {
+		return manual()
+	}
+
+	cache, ok := forge.LoadCacheAny(remoteCachePath())
+	sourceID := remoteCacheSourceID(app)
+	if !ok || (cache.SourceID != "" && cache.SourceID != sourceID) {
+		return manual()
+	}
+	items := make([]picker.Item, 0, len(cache.Repos)+1)
+	for _, remote := range cache.Repos {
+		if strings.TrimSpace(remote.CloneURL) == "" {
+			continue
+		}
+		var details []string
+		if remote.Visibility != "" {
+			details = append(details, strings.ToLower(remote.Visibility))
+		}
+		if remote.Archived {
+			details = append(details, "archived")
+		}
+		if remote.Description != "" {
+			details = append(details, truncate(remote.Description, 72))
+		}
+		items = append(items, picker.Item{
+			Value:       remote.CloneURL,
+			Label:       remote.Label(),
+			Description: strings.Join(details, " · "),
+		})
+	}
+	if len(items) == 0 {
+		return manual()
+	}
+	items = append(items, picker.Item{
+		Value:       manualCloneReference,
+		Label:       "Enter a URL, path, or owner/name manually…",
+		Description: "use a source not present in the cached forge inventory",
+	})
+	if !cache.FreshFor(app.Cfg.Forge.CacheTTL.Duration, sourceID) {
+		app.warnf("remote cache is stale or incomplete; run `dev repo remote --refresh` to update picker candidates")
+	}
+	result, used, err := app.pick(ctxOf(), picker.Request{Prompt: "Repository to clone", Items: items})
+	if err != nil {
+		return "", err
+	}
+	if !used || !result.Selected || result.Item.Value == manualCloneReference {
+		if result.Canceled {
+			return "", errPromptCanceled
+		}
+		return manual()
+	}
+	return result.Item.Value, nil
+}

 func promptRepoCloneWizard(app *App, p *prompter, flags repoBootstrapFlags, ref string, offerSetup bool) (repoWorkflowRequest, bool, bool, error) {
 	name := repoNameFromRef(repo.RedactCloneRef(ref))
 	if name == "" {
 		return repoWorkflowRequest{}, false, false, fmt.Errorf("could not derive a repository name from %q", ref)
 	}
 	category, err := p.line("Category (optional)", flags.category)
 	if err != nil {
 		return repoWorkflowRequest{}, false, false, err
 	}
 	flags.category = category
 	defaultDestination, err := repoDestination(app.Cfg.Paths.ProjectRoot, flags.category, name, flags.path)
 	if err != nil {
 		return repoWorkflowRequest{}, false, false, err
 	}
 	destination, err := p.line("Destination", config.Contract(defaultDestination))
 	if err != nil {
 		return repoWorkflowRequest{}, false, false, err
 	}
 	flags.path = config.Expand(destination)
 	setup := flags.preset != ""
 	if offerSetup && !setup {
 		setup, err = p.confirm("Apply a repository setup preset after cloning?", false)
 		if err != nil {
 			return repoWorkflowRequest{}, false, false, err
 		}
 	}
 	flags.handoff, err = promptRepoHandoff(p, defaultString(flags.handoff, "cd"))
 	if err != nil {
 		return repoWorkflowRequest{}, false, false, err
 	}
 	request, err := buildCloneRepoRequest(app, ref, flags)
 	if err != nil {
 		return repoWorkflowRequest{}, false, false, err
 	}
 	fmt.Fprintln(p.out, "\n"+p.style.title("Summary"))
 	fmt.Fprintf(p.out, "  source       %s\n", repo.RedactCloneRef(ref))
 	fmt.Fprintf(p.out, "  destination  %s\n", config.Contract(request.Destination))
 	if request.Scaffold.Preset != "" {
 		fmt.Fprintf(p.out, "  setup        %s\n", request.Scaffold.Preset)
 	} else {
 		fmt.Fprintf(p.out, "  setup        %t\n", setup)
 	}
 	fmt.Fprintf(p.out, "  handoff      %s\n", request.Handoff)
 	confirmed, err := p.confirm("Clone this repository?", true)
 	return request, setup, confirmed, err
 }

+const manualStartRepository = "\x00manual-start-repository"
+
+func pickStartRepository(ctx context.Context, app *App, current repo.Repo) (repo.Repo, bool, error) {
+	discovered, err := repo.Discover(ctx, app.Cfg.DiscoveryRoots(), repo.CompletionOptions())
+	if err != nil && current.Path == "" {
+		return repo.Repo{}, false, err
+	}
+
+	items := make([]picker.Item, 0, len(discovered)+2)
+	byPath := make(map[string]repo.Repo, len(discovered)+1)
+	seen := make(map[string]bool, len(discovered)+1)
+	add := func(repository repo.Repo) {
+		if repository.Path == "" || !repository.HasGit || repository.Bare {
+			return
+		}
+		identity := repository.RealPath
+		if identity == "" {
+			identity = repository.Path
+		}
+		identity = filepath.Clean(identity)
+		if seen[identity] {
+			return
+		}
+		seen[identity] = true
+		byPath[repository.Path] = repository
+		items = append(items, picker.Item{
+			Value:       repository.Path,
+			Label:       repository.Display(),
+			Description: config.Contract(repository.Path),
+		})
+	}
+	add(current)
+	for _, repository := range discovered {
+		add(repository)
+	}
+	if len(items) == 0 {
+		return repo.Repo{}, false, nil
+	}
+	items = append(items, picker.Item{
+		Value:       manualStartRepository,
+		Label:       "Enter a repository name or path manually…",
+		Description: "resolve a repository not present in the discovered list",
+	})
+
+	result, used, err := app.pick(ctx, picker.Request{Prompt: "Repository", Items: items})
+	if err != nil {
+		return repo.Repo{}, false, err
+	}
+	if result.Canceled {
+		return repo.Repo{}, false, errPromptCanceled
+	}
+	if !used || !result.Selected || result.Item.Value == manualStartRepository {
+		return repo.Repo{}, false, nil
+	}
+	selected, ok := byPath[result.Item.Value]
+	if !ok {
+		return repo.Repo{}, false, fmt.Errorf("picker returned an unknown repository")
+	}
+	resolved, err := resolveStartRepository(ctx, app, selected.Path)
+	if err != nil {
+		return repo.Repo{}, false, err
+	}
+	return resolved, true, nil
+}
```

```text
 // Load reads configuration and prepares the shared stores.
 func (a *App) Load() error {
 	cfg, err := config.Load(a.configPath)
 	if err != nil {
 		return err
 	}
 	a.Cfg = cfg
 	if a.In == nil {
 		a.In = os.Stdin
 	}
 	if a.Out == nil {
 		a.Out = os.Stdout
 	}
 	if a.Err == nil {
 		a.Err = os.Stderr
 	}
 	a.Tasks = task.NewStore(cfg.TasksDir())
 	a.Catalog = catalog.NewStore(cfg.AssetsDir(), catalog.WithDiagnosticSink(func(diagnostic catalog.Diagnostic) {
 		fmt.Fprintf(a.Err, "%s %s\n", a.errStyle().warning("dev: warning:"), diagnostic.Error())
 	}))
 	a.Registry = catalog.NewRegistry(a.Catalog)
 	noteStore := note.NewStore(cfg.NotesDir(), note.WithDiagnosticSink(func(path string, err error) {
 		fmt.Fprintf(a.Err, "dev: warning: skipping note %s: %v\n", filepath.Base(path), err)
 	}))
 	a.Notes = note.NewService(noteStore, cfg.NotesIndexFile())
 	a.Notes.IndexDiagnostic = func(err error) {
 		fmt.Fprintf(a.Err, "dev: warning: note search index: %v\n", err)
 	}
 	if a.Sizes == nil {
 		cache := diskusage.NewCache(filepath.Join(config.CacheHome(), "dev", "sizes-v1.json"), 10*time.Minute)
 		a.Sizes = diskusage.NewManager(cache, 2)
 	}
 	return nil
 }

 				BaseExplicit:   cmd.Flags().Changed("base"),
 				NextExplicit:   cmd.Flags().Changed("next"),
 				NoProvision:    noProvision, Focus: focus,
 			}
 			if len(args) == 1 {
 				req.RepoRef, req.RepoExplicit = args[0], true
 			}
 			if req.Name == "" && req.Branch != "" && req.Mode != task.ModeDirect {
 				req.Name = req.Branch
 			}
 
 			var spec *startSpec
 			var err error
 			if req.Name == "" {
 				if jsonOut || !app.interactive() {
 					return errors.New("give the work a name: dev start <repo> --task <name>")
 				}
 				var confirmed bool
 				spec, confirmed, err = runStartWizard(ctx, app, req)
 				if errors.Is(err, errPromptCanceled) {
 					fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "Canceled; nothing was created.")
 					return nil
 				}
 				if err != nil {
 					return err
 				}
 				if !confirmed {
 					fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "Canceled; nothing was created.")
 					return nil
 				}
 			} else {
 				spec, err = buildStartSpec(ctx, app, req)
 				if err != nil {
 					return decorateStartError(err)
 				}
 			}

 // RepoRow is one repository as the dashboard shows it: what it is, plus how
 // much of it is currently in flight.
 //
 // The repository view exists because the task list alone answers only half the
 // question. On a machine with forty repositories and no tasks recorded yet,
 // a task-only dashboard is empty — and the honest answer to "what do I have
 // here?" has to come before "what am I working on?"
 // RepoActions groups catalog metadata mutations for ordinary repositories.
 type RepoActions struct {
 	Patch func(ctx context.Context, row RepoRow, tags []string, note string) (string, error)
 }
 
 type RepoRow struct {
 	Repo        repo.Repo
 	Status      gitx.Status
 	Topology    gitx.RecoveryTopology
 	TopologyErr error
 	SizeTarget  diskusage.Target
 	Usage       *diskusage.Usage
 	SizeError   error
 	// Asset is catalog metadata joined without persisting an otherwise
 	// unobserved repository. A Try asset lets callers suppress or label it.
 	Asset *catalog.Entry
 	// Context is the canonical checkout plus every linked worktree, enriched
 	// with task and runtime state. It is shared by the tree, copy actions and
 	// `dev repo context`, so those surfaces cannot disagree.
 	Context inventory.RepoContext
 	// LastActivity is the newest commit time in this checkout. It is a durable,
 	// cheap approximation of "when was this repo last touched" and is sortable.
 	LastActivity time.Time
 	// Worktrees is the number of linked worktrees, excluding the main checkout.
 	Worktrees int
 	// Tasks are the recorded tasks belonging to this repository.
 	Tasks []*task.Task
 	// NoteCount/LatestNote are joined from the durable sidecar store when this
 	// repo already has a catalog identity.
 	NoteCount  int
 	LatestNote *note.Note
 	// Live reports a runtime session sitting in this repository.
 	Live          bool
 	Runtime       string
 	RuntimeHandle string
 	RuntimeStatus string
 	// RemoteForge / RemoteName identify origin for matching the REMOTE view to
 	// this local checkout without rescanning every repo when a cache opens.
 	RemoteForge forge.Kind
 	RemoteName  string
 }
 
 // Sessions returns every runtime session attached to any checkout in this
 // repository.
 func (r RepoRow) Sessions() []runtime.Session { return r.Context.Sessions() }
 
 // HotTasks counts the repository's tasks that are currently hot.
 // IsTry reports an ungraduated Try that should live in the dedicated TRY view,
 // while remaining in the model's local snapshot for REMOTE matching.
 func (r RepoRow) IsTry() bool {
 	return r.Asset != nil && r.Asset.Kind == catalog.KindTry && r.Asset.Experiment != nil &&
 		(r.Asset.Experiment.Phase == catalog.PhaseActive || r.Asset.Experiment.Phase == catalog.PhaseDeprecated)
 }
 
 func (r RepoRow) HotTasks() int {
 	n := 0
 	for _, t := range r.Tasks {
 		if t.State == task.Hot {
 			n++
 		}
 	}
 	return n
 }
 
 // StateSummary renders the repository's tasks as a compact per-state tally,
 // which is what makes the list scannable at forty repositories.
 func (r RepoRow) StateSummary() string {
 	if len(r.Tasks) == 0 {
 		return ""
 	}
 	counts := map[task.State]int{}

 }
 
 func (r RepoRow) matches(query string) bool {
 	query = strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(query))
 	for _, term := range strings.Fields(query) {
 		key, value, structured := strings.Cut(term, ":")
 		if structured {
 			switch key {
 			case "tag":
 				if r.Asset == nil || !r.Asset.HasTag(value) {
 					return false
 				}
 				continue
 			case "remote":
 				if !strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(r.Topology.Summary()), value) {
 					return false
 				}
 				continue
 			case "size":
 				if !matchesSize(r.Usage, value) {
 					return false
 				}
 				continue
 			case "kind":
 				kind := catalog.KindRepository
 				if r.Asset != nil {
 					kind = r.Asset.Kind
 				}
 				if string(kind) != value {
 					return false
 				}
 				continue
 			}
 		}
 		if !strings.Contains(r.searchText(), term) {
 			return false
 		}
 	}
 	return true
 }
 
 // taskSearchText is what a filter query matches a task row against.
 func taskSearchText(r inventory.Row) string {
 	t := r.Task
 	return strings.ToLower(strings.Join([]string{
 		t.Title(), t.Repo, t.Branch, t.Next, t.Note, string(t.State),
 	}, " "))
 }

-			return false
-		}
-	}

 }
 
 // RemoteRow is one repository known to a configured forge, optionally matched to
 // a local checkout. The REMOTE view is the bridge between "what exists on the
 // forge" and "what is already on this machine".
 type RemoteRow struct {
 	Repo forge.RemoteRepo `json:"repo"`
 	// LocalPath is the checkout under the configured scan roots, empty when the
 	// remote has not been cloned here.
 	LocalPath string `json:"local_path,omitempty"`
 	// LocalName is the discovered repo's display name.
 	LocalName string `json:"local_name,omitempty"`
 	// LocalKind distinguishes a cataloged Try from an ordinary repository.
 	LocalKind catalog.Kind `json:"local_kind,omitempty"`
 }
 
 // FleetRow is one host/repository observation. Repository is nil for a host
 // health row such as unreachable or no-dev.
 type FleetRow struct {
 	Host       string
 	Local      bool
 	State      fleet.HostState
 	Repository *fleet.RepoSnapshot
 	Error      string
 	FromCache  bool
 }
 
 func (r FleetRow) searchText() string {
 	parts := []string{r.Host, string(r.State), r.Error}
 	if r.Repository != nil {
 		parts = append(parts, r.Repository.Name, r.Repository.Display, r.Repository.Path,
 			r.Repository.Branch, r.Repository.Status.Summary(), strings.Join(r.Repository.RemoteIdentities, " "))
 	}
 	return strings.ToLower(strings.Join(parts, " "))
 }
 
 // Cloned reports whether this remote already has a local checkout.
 func (r RemoteRow) Cloned() bool { return r.LocalPath != "" }
 
 func (r RemoteRow) searchText() string {
 	return strings.ToLower(strings.Join([]string{
 		string(r.Repo.Forge), r.Repo.Name, r.Repo.FullName, r.Repo.Description,
 		r.Repo.Visibility, r.Repo.DefaultBranch, r.LocalName, string(r.LocalKind),
 	}, " "))
 }
 
 func (r RemoteRow) matches(query string) bool {
 	query = strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(query))
 	for _, term := range strings.Fields(query) {
 		key, value, structured := strings.Cut(term, ":")
 		if structured && (key == "vis" || key == "visibility") {
 			if strings.ToLower(r.Repo.Visibility) != value {
 				return false
 			}
 			continue
 		}
 		if !strings.Contains(r.searchText(), term) {
 			return false
 		}
 	}
 	return true
 }
 
 // StatsPanel is the repo activity overlay opened by H.
 type StatsPanel struct {
 	Repo       string
 	Heatmap    string
 	Seconds    int
 	ActiveDays int
 	Since      time.Time
 	Until      time.Time
 }
 
 // NoteTarget identifies the selected local repository. CatalogID may be empty
 // until the first note action persists the repository observation.
 type NoteTarget struct {
 	CatalogID string
 	Repo      repo.Repo
 }
```

```text
1	// Package picker selects one value from a caller-provided list. It can hand
2	// the terminal to a line-oriented external picker such as fzf, and otherwise
3	// falls back to dev's built-in Bubble Tea interface.
4	package picker
5	
6	import (
7		"bytes"
8		"context"
9		"errors"
10		"fmt"
11		"io"
12		"os/exec"
13		"strings"
14	)
15	
16	// Item is one selectable value. Value is opaque caller data and is never sent
17	// to an external picker; Label and Description are display-only.
18	type Item struct {
19		Value       string
20		Label       string
21		Description string
22	}
23	
24	// Request describes one selection interaction.
25	type Request struct {
26		Prompt       string
27		InitialQuery string
28		Items        []Item
29	}
30	
31	// Result distinguishes a selection from an explicit cancellation.
32	type Result struct {
33		Item     Item
34		Selected bool
35		Canceled bool
36	}
37	
38	// Selector owns the streams and optional external command for one application.
39	type Selector struct {
40		in       io.Reader
41		out      io.Writer
42		errOut   io.Writer
43		command  []string
44		lookPath func(string) (string, error)
45	}
46	
47	// New constructs a selector. command is an argv vector, not a shell command;
48	// an empty vector always selects the built-in backend.
49	func New(in io.Reader, out, errOut io.Writer, command []string) *Selector {
50		return &Selector{
51			in:       in,
52			out:      out,
53			errOut:   errOut,
54			command:  append([]string(nil), command...),
55			lookPath: exec.LookPath,
56		}
57	}
58	
59	// Select uses the configured external picker when it is installed and the
60	// built-in picker otherwise.
61	func (s *Selector) Select(ctx context.Context, request Request) (Result, error) {
62		if len(request.Items) == 0 {
63			return Result{}, nil
64		}
65		if len(s.command) == 0 {
66			return s.selectBuiltin(ctx, request)
67		}
68		path, err := s.lookPath(s.command[0])
69		if err != nil {
70			return s.selectBuiltin(ctx, request)
71		}
72		return s.selectExternal(ctx, path, request)
73	}
74	
75	func (s *Selector) selectExternal(ctx context.Context, path string, request Request) (Result, error) {
76		lines, items := renderCandidates(request.Items)
77		args := make([]string, len(s.command)-1)
78		for index, arg := range s.command[1:] {
79			args[index] = strings.ReplaceAll(arg, "{prompt}", request.Prompt)
80		}
81		cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, path, args...)
82		cmd.Stdin = strings.NewReader(strings.Join(lines, "\n") + "\n")
83		if s.errOut == nil {
84			cmd.Stderr = io.Discard
85		} else {
86			cmd.Stderr = s.errOut
87		}
88		var stdout bytes.Buffer
89		cmd.Stdout = &stdout
90	
91		err := cmd.Run()
92		if ctxErr := ctx.Err(); ctxErr != nil {
93			return Result{}, ctxErr
94		}
95		if err != nil {
96			var exitErr *exec.ExitError
97			if errors.As(err, &exitErr) && (exitErr.ExitCode() == 1 || exitErr.ExitCode() == 130) {
98				return Result{Canceled: true}, nil
99			}
100			return Result{}, fmt.Errorf("external picker: %w", err)
101		}
102	
103		selected, err := selectedLine(stdout.String())
104		if err != nil {
105			return Result{}, err
106		}
107		item, ok := items[selected]
108		if !ok {
109			return Result{}, fmt.Errorf("external picker returned an unknown selection")
110		}
111		return Result{Item: item, Selected: true}, nil
112	}
113	
114	func selectedLine(output string) (string, error) {
115		output = strings.TrimSuffix(output, "\n")
116		output = strings.TrimSuffix(output, "\r")
117		if output == "" || strings.ContainsAny(output, "\r\n\x00") {
118			return "", errors.New("external picker returned malformed output")
119		}
120		return output, nil
121	}
122	
123	func renderCandidates(items []Item) ([]string, map[string]Item) {
124		lines := make([]string, 0, len(items))
125		byLine := make(map[string]Item, len(items))
126		for _, item := range items {
127			label := cleanDisplay(item.Label)
128			if label == "" {
129				label = "(unnamed)"
130			}
131			base := label
132			if description := cleanDisplay(item.Description); description != "" {
133				base += "\t" + description
134			}
135			line := base
136			for ordinal := 2; ; ordinal++ {
137				if _, exists := byLine[line]; !exists {
138					break
139				}
140				line = fmt.Sprintf("%s\t[%d]", base, ordinal)
141			}
142			lines = append(lines, line)
143			byLine[line] = item
144		}
145		return lines, byLine
146	}
147	
148	func cleanDisplay(value string) string {
149		return strings.Join(strings.FieldsFunc(value, func(r rune) bool {
150			return r == '\r' || r == '\n' || r == '\t' || r == 0
151		}), " ")
152	}
153
```

```text
1	package picker
2	
3	import (
4		"context"
5		"fmt"
6		"strings"
7	
8		"github.com/charmbracelet/bubbles/textinput"
9		tea "github.com/charmbracelet/bubbletea"
10		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/textmatch"
11	)
12	
13	const defaultVisibleRows = 10
14	
15	type builtinModel struct {
16		prompt   string
17		input    textinput.Model
18		items    []Item
19		visible  []int
20		cursor   int
21		offset   int
22		rows     int
23		width    int
24		done     bool
25		canceled bool
26		selected Item
27	}
28	
29	func newBuiltinModel(request Request) builtinModel {
30		input := textinput.New()
31		input.Prompt = fmt.Sprintf("? %s: ", request.Prompt)
32		input.SetValue(request.InitialQuery)
33		input.Focus()
34		model := builtinModel{
35			prompt: request.Prompt,
36			input:  input,
37			items:  append([]Item(nil), request.Items...),
38			rows:   defaultVisibleRows,
39		}
40		model.refilter()
41		return model
42	}
43	
44	func (m builtinModel) Init() tea.Cmd {
45		return textinput.Blink
46	}
47	
48	func (m builtinModel) Update(message tea.Msg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
49		switch msg := message.(type) {
50		case tea.WindowSizeMsg:
51			m.width = msg.Width
52			if available := msg.Height - 3; available > 0 && available < defaultVisibleRows {
53				m.rows = available
54			} else {
55				m.rows = defaultVisibleRows
56			}
57			m.keepVisible()
58			return m, nil
59		case tea.KeyMsg:
60			switch msg.Type {
61			case tea.KeyEsc, tea.KeyCtrlC:
62				m.done = true
63				m.canceled = true
64				m.input.Blur()
65				return m, tea.Quit
66			case tea.KeyEnter:
67				if len(m.visible) == 0 {
68					return m, nil
69				}
70				m.done = true
71				m.selected = m.items[m.visible[m.cursor]]
72				m.input.Blur()
73				return m, tea.Quit
74			case tea.KeyUp, tea.KeyCtrlP:
75				m.move(-1)
76				return m, nil
77			case tea.KeyDown, tea.KeyCtrlN:
78				m.move(1)
79				return m, nil
80			}
81		}
82	
83		var command tea.Cmd
84		m.input, command = m.input.Update(message)
85		m.refilter()
86		return m, command
87	}
88	
89	func (m builtinModel) View() string {
90		if m.done {
91			return "\n"
92		}
93		var out strings.Builder
94		out.WriteString(m.input.View())
95		out.WriteByte('\n')
96		if len(m.visible) == 0 {
97			out.WriteString("  No matches\n")
98			return out.String()
99		}
100		end := m.offset + m.rows
101		if end > len(m.visible) {
102			end = len(m.visible)
103		}
104		for position := m.offset; position < end; position++ {
105			item := m.items[m.visible[position]]
106			marker := "  "
107			if position == m.cursor {
108				marker = "> "
109			}
110			line := marker + item.Label
111			if item.Description != "" {
112				line += "  " + item.Description
113			}
114			out.WriteString(clipRunes(line, m.width))
115			out.WriteByte('\n')
116		}
117		return out.String()
118	}
119	
120	func (m *builtinModel) refilter() {
121		m.visible = m.visible[:0]
122		for index, item := range m.items {
123			if textmatch.Terms(item.Label+" "+item.Description, m.input.Value()) {
124				m.visible = append(m.visible, index)
125			}
126		}
127		m.cursor = 0
128		m.offset = 0
129	}
130	
131	func (m *builtinModel) move(delta int) {
132		if len(m.visible) == 0 {
133			return
134		}
135		m.cursor += delta
136		if m.cursor < 0 {
137			m.cursor = len(m.visible) - 1
138		}
139		if m.cursor >= len(m.visible) {
140			m.cursor = 0
141		}
142		m.keepVisible()
143	}
144	
145	func (m *builtinModel) keepVisible() {
146		if m.rows <= 0 {
147			m.rows = 1
148		}
149		if m.cursor < m.offset {
150			m.offset = m.cursor
151		}
152		if m.cursor >= m.offset+m.rows {
153			m.offset = m.cursor - m.rows + 1
154		}
155	}
156	
157	func clipRunes(value string, width int) string {
158		if width <= 0 {
159			return value
160		}
161		runes := []rune(value)
162		if len(runes) <= width {
163			return value
164		}
165		if width == 1 {
166			return "…"
167		}
168		return string(runes[:width-1]) + "…"
169	}
170	
171	func (s *Selector) selectBuiltin(ctx context.Context, request Request) (Result, error) {
172		program := tea.NewProgram(
173			newBuiltinModel(request),
174			tea.WithInput(s.in),
175			tea.WithOutput(s.out),
176			tea.WithContext(ctx),
177		)
178		final, err := program.Run()
179		if ctxErr := ctx.Err(); ctxErr != nil {
180			return Result{}, ctxErr
181		}
182		if err != nil {
183			return Result{}, fmt.Errorf("built-in picker: %w", err)
184		}
185		model, ok := final.(builtinModel)
186		if !ok {
187			return Result{}, fmt.Errorf("built-in picker returned an unexpected model")
188		}
189		if model.canceled {
190			return Result{Canceled: true}, nil
191		}
192		if !model.done {
193			return Result{}, nil
194		}
195		return Result{Item: model.selected, Selected: true}, nil
196	}
197
```

```text
1	// Package textmatch provides the small query language shared by interactive
2	// lists. It deliberately matches terms rather than assigning fuzzy scores so
3	// filtering stays predictable across dev's built-in interfaces.
4	package textmatch
5	
6	import "strings"
7	
8	// Terms reports whether every whitespace-separated query term appears in the
9	// haystack, case-insensitively and in any order. An empty query matches all.
10	func Terms(haystack, query string) bool {
11		haystack = strings.ToLower(haystack)
12		query = strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(query))
13		for term := range strings.FieldsSeq(query) {
14			if !strings.Contains(haystack, term) {
15				return false
16			}
17		}
18		return true
19	}
```

```text
153	func promptRepoCloneReference(app *App, p *prompter) (string, error) {
154		manual := func() (string, error) {
155			return p.line("Git URL, path, or owner/name", "")
156		}
157		if !app.canPick() {
158			return manual()
159		}
160	
161		cache, ok := forge.LoadCacheAny(remoteCachePath())
162		sourceID := remoteCacheSourceID(app)
163		if !ok || (cache.SourceID != "" && cache.SourceID != sourceID) {
164			return manual()
165		}
166		items := make([]picker.Item, 0, len(cache.Repos)+1)
167		for _, remote := range cache.Repos {
168			if strings.TrimSpace(remote.CloneURL) == "" {
169				continue
170			}
171			var details []string
172			if remote.Visibility != "" {
173				details = append(details, strings.ToLower(remote.Visibility))
174			}
175			if remote.Archived {
176				details = append(details, "archived")
177			}
178			if remote.Description != "" {
179				details = append(details, truncate(remote.Description, 72))
180			}
181			items = append(items, picker.Item{
182				Value:       remote.CloneURL,
183				Label:       remote.Label(),
184				Description: strings.Join(details, " · "),
185			})
186		}
187		if len(items) == 0 {
188			return manual()
189		}
190		items = append(items, picker.Item{
191			Value:       manualCloneReference,
192			Label:       "Enter a URL, path, or owner/name manually…",
193			Description: "use a source not present in the cached forge inventory",
194		})
195		if !cache.FreshFor(app.Cfg.Forge.CacheTTL.Duration, sourceID) {
196			app.warnf("remote cache is stale or incomplete; run `dev repo remote --refresh` to update picker candidates")
197		}
198		result, used, err := app.pick(ctxOf(), picker.Request{Prompt: "Repository to clone", Items: items})
199		if err != nil {
200			return "", err
201		}
202		if !used || !result.Selected || result.Item.Value == manualCloneReference {
203			if result.Canceled {
204				return "", errPromptCanceled
205			}
206			return manual()
207		}
208		return result.Item.Value, nil
209	}

488	func promptUpstream(app *App, p *prompter, name string, flags *repoBootstrapFlags) error {
489		create, err := p.confirm("Create a GitHub/GitLab upstream?", flags.remote)
490		if err != nil || !create {
491			flags.remote = false
492			return err
493		}
494		ready := forge.ProbeAll(ctxOf())
495		var available []forge.Readiness
496		for _, candidate := range ready {
497			if candidate.Ready() {
498				available = append(available, candidate)
499			} else {
500				fmt.Fprintf(p.out, "  %s: %s (%s)\n", candidate.Forge, candidate.Status, candidate.Action)
501			}
502		}
503		if len(available) == 0 {
504			fmt.Fprintln(p.out, "  "+p.style.warning("no authenticated GitHub or GitLab CLI is ready; creating locally only"))
505			flags.remote = false
506			return nil
507		}
508		selected := available[0].Forge
509		if len(available) > 1 {
510			choices := map[string]string{"github": "github", "gh": "github", "gitlab": "gitlab", "gl": "gitlab"}
511			choice, err := p.choice("Forge (github/gitlab)", string(selected), "github, gitlab", choices)
512			if err != nil {
513				return err
514			}
515			selected = forge.Kind(choice)
516		}

618	func replaceSetValue(values []string, key, value string) []string {
619		prefix := key + "="
620		result := values[:0]
621		for _, existing := range values {
622			if !strings.HasPrefix(existing, prefix) {
623				result = append(result, existing)
624			}
625		}
626		return append(result, prefix+value)
627	}

630		result := values[:0]
631		for _, value := range values {
632			if value != remove {
633				result = append(result, value)
634			}
635		}
636		return result
637	}

640		var result []string
641		for _, part := range strings.Split(value, ",") {
642			if trimmed := strings.TrimSpace(part); trimmed != "" {
643				result = append(result, trimmed)
644			}
645		}
646		return result
647	}

652		}
```

```text
17	func promptStartRepository(ctx context.Context, app *App, p *prompter, req startRequest) (repo.Repo, error) {
18		if req.RepoExplicit {
19			return resolveStartRepository(ctx, app, req.RepoRef)
20		}

33			}
34		}
35		if current.Path == "" {
36			all, err := repo.Discover(ctx, app.Cfg.DiscoveryRoots(), repo.DefaultOptions())

42				if r.HasGit && !r.Bare {

53			}

61					return repo.Repo{}, err
62				}

65					continue

70				}

97	func pickStartRepository(ctx context.Context, app *App, current repo.Repo) (repo.Repo, bool, error) {
98		discovered, err := repo.Discover(ctx, app.Cfg.DiscoveryRoots(), repo.CompletionOptions())
99		if err != nil && current.Path == "" {
100			return repo.Repo{}, false, err
101		}
102	
103		items := make([]picker.Item, 0, len(discovered)+2)
104		byPath := make(map[string]repo.Repo, len(discovered)+1)
105		seen := make(map[string]bool, len(discovered)+1)
106		add := func(repository repo.Repo) {
107			if repository.Path == "" || !repository.HasGit || repository.Bare {
108				return
109			}
110			identity := repository.RealPath
111			if identity == "" {
112				identity = repository.Path
113			}
114			identity = filepath.Clean(identity)
115			if seen[identity] {
116				return
117			}
118			seen[identity] = true
119			byPath[repository.Path] = repository
120			items = append(items, picker.Item{
121				Value:       repository.Path,
122				Label:       repository.Display(),
123				Description: config.Contract(repository.Path),
124			})
125		}
126		add(current)
127		for _, repository := range discovered {
128			add(repository)
129		}
130		if len(items) == 0 {
131			return repo.Repo{}, false, nil
132		}
133		items = append(items, picker.Item{
134			Value:       manualStartRepository,
135			Label:       "Enter a repository name or path manually…",
136			Description: "resolve a repository not present in the discovered list",
137		})
138	
139		result, used, err := app.pick(ctx, picker.Request{Prompt: "Repository", Items: items})
140		if err != nil {
141			return repo.Repo{}, false, err
142		}
143		if result.Canceled {
144			return repo.Repo{}, false, errPromptCanceled
145		}
146		if !used || !result.Selected || result.Item.Value == manualStartRepository {
147			return repo.Repo{}, false, nil
148		}
149		selected, ok := byPath[result.Item.Value]
150		if !ok {
151			return repo.Repo{}, false, fmt.Errorf("picker returned an unknown repository")
152		}
153		resolved, err := resolveStartRepository(ctx, app, selected.Path)
154		if err != nil {
155			return repo.Repo{}, false, err
156		}
157		return resolved, true, nil
158	}

160	func runStartWizard(ctx context.Context, app *App, req startRequest) (*startSpec, bool, error) {
161		p := newPrompter(app)
162		fmt.Fprintln(p.out, p.style.title("Start a tracked change stream"))
163	
164		r, err := promptStartRepository(ctx, app, p, req)
165		if err != nil {
166			return nil, false, err
167		}
168		if r.Bare {
169			return nil, false, fmt.Errorf("%s is a bare repository and cannot host a task checkout", r.Display())
170		}
171		req.RepoRef, req.RepoExplicit = r.Path, true
172	
173		for strings.TrimSpace(req.Name) == "" {
174			req.Name, err = p.line("Task name", "")
175			if err != nil {
176				return nil, false, err
177			}
178			if strings.TrimSpace(req.Name) == "" {
179				fmt.Fprintln(p.out, "  "+p.style.warning("task name is required"))
180			}
181		}
182	
183		for {
184			if !req.ModeExplicit {
185				fallback := "worktree"
186				switch req.Mode {
187				case task.ModeBranch:
188					fallback = "branch-only"
189				case task.ModeDirect:
190					fallback = "direct"
191				}
192				selected, err := p.choice("Mode (w=worktree, b=branch-only, d=direct)", fallback,
193					"worktree (w), branch-only (b), direct (d)", map[string]string{
194						"w": "worktree", "worktree": "worktree",
195						"b": "branch-only", "branch": "branch-only", "branch-only": "branch-only",
196						"d": "direct", "direct": "direct",
197					})
198				if err != nil {
199					return nil, false, err
200				}
201				switch selected {
202				case "direct":
203					req.Mode = task.ModeDirect
204				case "branch-only":
205					req.Mode = task.ModeBranch
206				default:
207					req.Mode = task.ModeWorktree
208				}
209			}
210	
211			if req.Mode == task.ModeDirect {
212				st, statusErr := gitx.StatusOf(ctx, r.Path)
213				if statusErr != nil {
214					return nil, false, statusErr
215				}
216				req.Branch, req.Base = st.Branch, st.Branch
217			} else {
218				if !req.BranchExplicit {
219					fallback := req.Branch
220					if fallback == "" {
221						fallback = "feat/" + config.Slug(req.Name)
222					}
223					req.Branch, err = p.line("Branch", fallback)
224					if err != nil {
225						return nil, false, err
226					}
227				}
228				if !req.BaseExplicit {
229					fallback := req.Base
230					if fallback == "" {
231						fallback = gitx.DefaultBranch(ctx, r.Path)
232					}
233					req.Base, err = p.line("Base", fallback)
234					if err != nil {
235						return nil, false, err
236					}
237				}
238			}
239			if !req.NextExplicit {
240				req.Next, err = p.line("Next action (optional)", req.Next)
241				if err != nil {
242					return nil, false, err
243				}
244			}
245	
246			spec, buildErr := buildStartSpec(ctx, app, req)
247			if buildErr != nil {
248				fmt.Fprintf(p.out, "  %s\n", p.style.warning(buildErr.Error()))
249				if req.BranchExplicit || req.BaseExplicit || req.ModeExplicit {
250					return nil, false, buildErr
251				}
252				req.Branch, req.Base = "", ""
253				continue
254			}
255	
256			rt := app.Runtime()
257			checkout := spec.RepoPath
258			if spec.WorktreePath != "" {
259				checkout = spec.WorktreePath
260			}
261			fmt.Fprintln(p.out, "\n"+p.style.title("Summary"))
262			fmt.Fprintf(p.out, "  %s  %s (%s)\n", p.style.label("repository"), spec.RepoName, config.Contract(spec.RepoPath))
263			fmt.Fprintf(p.out, "  %s        %s\n", p.style.label("task"), spec.Name)

265			fmt.Fprintf(p.out, "  %s      %s\n", p.style.label("branch"), spec.Branch)
266			fmt.Fprintf(p.out, "  %s        %s\n", p.style.label("base"), spec.Base)
267			fmt.Fprintf(p.out, "  %s    %s\n", p.style.label("checkout"), config.Contract(checkout))
268			fmt.Fprintf(p.out, "  %s   %s\n", p.style.label("provision"), p.style.success(fmt.Sprint(!spec.NoProvision)))
269			fmt.Fprintf(p.out, "  %s     %s\n", p.style.label("runtime"), p.style.success(rt.Name()))
270			fmt.Fprintf(p.out, "  %s       %s\n", p.style.label("focus"), fmt.Sprint(spec.Focus))
```

```text
17	// Config is the whole of dev's configuration. Zero values are never used
18	// directly — Default() supplies the baseline and Load() overlays the user's
19	// config.toml on top of it.
20	type Config struct {
21		Paths      Paths      `toml:"paths"`
22		Runtime    Runtime    `toml:"runtime"`
23		Worktree   Worktree   `toml:"worktree"`
24		LocalFiles LocalFiles `toml:"local_files"`
25		Stats      Stats      `toml:"stats"`
26		TUI        TUI        `toml:"tui"`
27		Bootstrap  Bootstrap  `toml:"bootstrap"`
28		Forge      Forge      `toml:"forge"`
29		Picker     Picker     `toml:"picker"`
30		Update     Update     `toml:"update"`
31	
32		// Source records where the config was loaded from; "" means defaults only.
33		Source string `toml:"-"`
34	}
35	
36	// Update controls the release-freshness check.
37	type Update struct {
38		// Check lets `dev` note when a newer release is available. It only ever
39		// reads a day-old cache on the command path; the network fetch that fills
40		// that cache is opportunistic and best-effort. Set to false (or export
41		// DEV_NO_UPDATE_CHECK) on CI and air-gapped machines.
42		Check bool `toml:"check"`
43	}
44	
45	// Picker configures the optional external selector used by interactive
46	// commands. Command is an argv vector rather than shell source; an empty vector
47	// forces dev's built-in selector.
48	type Picker struct {
49		Command []string `toml:"command"`
50	}
51	
52	// Paths tells dev where repos live and where derived state goes. Every entry
53	// is a template-or-path expanded through Expand, so "~", "$VAR" and absolute
54	// paths on another volume (e.g. /mnt/fast/worktrees) all work.
55	type Paths struct {
56		ScanRoots []string `toml:"scan_roots"`
57		// RepoPaths names repositories which do not live below a useful scan root,
58		// such as chezmoi's XDG data checkout. Exact repositories are considered
59		// before recursive roots, so an intentional navigation alias wins deduplication.
60		RepoPaths    []string `toml:"repo_paths"`
61		TriesRoot    string   `toml:"tries_root"`
62		WorktreeRoot string   `toml:"worktree_root"`
63		WorktreePath string   `toml:"worktree_path"`
64		StateDir     string   `toml:"state_dir"`
65		// ProjectRoot is where `dev graduate` promotes a try to, joined with the
66		// chosen category.
67		ProjectRoot string `toml:"project_root"`
68	}
69	
70	// Runtime selects the terminal-multiplexer backend used to open a checkout.
71	type Runtime struct {
72		// Backend is "auto" (herdr, then tmux, then zellij, then none), or one of
73		// those names.
74		Backend string `toml:"backend"`
75		// MetadataSource is the --source id used for herdr workspace metadata.
76		MetadataSource string `toml:"metadata_source"`
77	}
78	
79	// Worktree controls where linked worktrees land and how they get provisioned
80	// into a usable state (deps installed, gitignored env files carried over).
81	type Worktree struct {
82		// Include lists .gitignore-syntax patterns; matching files are copied into
83		// a new worktree only when they are actually gitignored in the source
84		// checkout. Tracked files are already in the checkout.
85		Include []string `toml:"include"`
86		// Link names directories symlinked rather than copied (opt-in: sharing
87		// node_modules across checkouts breaks native builds often enough that it
88		// must never be a default).
89		Link []string `toml:"link"`
90		// PostCreate is either the string "auto" (detect from lockfiles) or an
91		// explicit list of shell commands run in a new worktree.
92		PostCreate PostCreate `toml:"post_create"`
93		// Strategy is how a new worktree gets its installed dependencies:
94		// "reinstall" (correct, the default), "copy", "link" or "skip". dev
95		// narrows an unsound choice back to reinstall and says why — copying a
96		// virtualenv, for instance, cannot work, because it bakes its own
97		// absolute path into pyvenv.cfg.
98		Strategy string `toml:"strategy"`
99		// Strategies overrides Strategy per ecosystem ("python", "node", "go",
100		// "rust", "ruby", "elixir").
101		Strategies map[string]string `toml:"strategies"`
102		// ProvisionTimeout caps a single post-create command.
103		ProvisionTimeout Duration `toml:"provision_timeout"`
104	}

106	// LocalFiles is host policy for portable ignored-file operations. It contains

135	// Forge configures the combined remote inventory.
136	type Forge struct {

330	// Load reads config.toml over the defaults. A missing file is not an error —
331	// dev must be useful with zero setup. A malformed file is, because silently
332	// falling back to defaults would send worktrees to the wrong volume.
333	func Load(path string) (Config, error) {
334		cfg := Default()
335		if path == "" {
336			path = ConfigFile()
337		}
338		md, err := toml.DecodeFile(path, &cfg)
339		switch {
340		case errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist):
341			return cfg, nil
342		case err != nil:
343			return cfg, fmt.Errorf("read %s: %w", path, err)
344		}
345		if undecoded := md.Undecoded(); len(undecoded) > 0 {
346			// Unknown keys are usually typos ("worktree_dir" vs "worktree_root").
347			// Warn rather than fail so a newer config still works on an older dev.
348			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "dev: warning: unknown key(s) in %s: %v\n", path, undecoded)
349		}
350		cfg.Source = path
351		return cfg, cfg.Validate()
352	}

354	// Validate catches the settings that would otherwise fail deep inside a
355	// worktree create, when a directory has already been made.
356	func (c Config) Validate() error {
357		switch c.Runtime.Backend {
358		case "", "auto", "herdr", "tmux", "zellij", "none":
359		default:
360			return fmt.Errorf("runtime.backend %q: want auto, herdr, tmux, zellij or none", c.Runtime.Backend)
361		}
362		if c.Paths.WorktreePath == "" {
363			return errors.New("paths.worktree_path must not be empty")
364		}
365		if _, err := Render(c.Paths.WorktreePath, c.probeVars()); err != nil {
366			return fmt.Errorf("paths.worktree_path: %w", err)
367		}
368		if err := c.LocalFiles.Limits().Validate(); err != nil {
369			return fmt.Errorf("local_files: %w", err)
370		}
371		switch c.Bootstrap.Layout {
372		case "", "flat", "preserve":
373		default:
374			return fmt.Errorf("bootstrap.layout %q: want flat or preserve", c.Bootstrap.Layout)
375		}
376		if c.Bootstrap.MaxDepth < 0 {
377			return fmt.Errorf("bootstrap.max_depth must be zero (unlimited) or positive")
378		}
379		if c.Forge.RemoteLimit < 0 {
380			return fmt.Errorf("deprecated forge.remote_limit must be zero or positive")
381		}
382		for index, arg := range c.Picker.Command {
383			if strings.ContainsAny(arg, "\x00\r\n") {
384				return fmt.Errorf("picker.command[%d] must not contain NUL or a newline", index)
385			}
386			if index == 0 && strings.TrimSpace(arg) == "" {
387				return errors.New("picker.command[0] must name an executable; use an empty command array for the built-in picker")
388			}
389		}
390		seenAzureTargets := map[string]bool{}
391		for i, target := range c.Forge.AzureDevOps {
392			organization := strings.TrimSpace(target.Organization)
393			project := strings.TrimSpace(target.Project)
394			if !validAzureDevOpsOrganization(organization) {
395				return fmt.Errorf("forge.azure_devops[%d].organization %q: want an Azure DevOps Services URL like https://dev.azure.com/acme", i, target.Organization)
396			}
397			if project == "" {
398				return fmt.Errorf("forge.azure_devops[%d].project must not be empty", i)
399			}
400			key := strings.ToLower(strings.TrimRight(organization, "/") + "/" + project)
401			if seenAzureTargets[key] {
402				return fmt.Errorf("forge.azure_devops[%d] duplicates organization/project %s / %s", i, organization, project)
403			}
404			seenAzureTargets[key] = true
405		}
406		validStrategy := func(v string) bool {
407			switch v {
408			case "", "reinstall", "copy", "link", "skip":
409				return true
410			}
411			return false
412		}
413		if !validStrategy(c.Worktree.Strategy) {
414			return fmt.Errorf("worktree.strategy %q: want reinstall, copy, link or skip", c.Worktree.Strategy)
415		}
416		for ecosystem, strategy := range c.Worktree.Strategies {
417			if !validStrategy(strategy) {
418				return fmt.Errorf("worktree.strategies.%s %q: want reinstall, copy, link or skip",
419					ecosystem, strategy)
420			}
421		}
422		validColumns := map[string]bool{
423			"repo": true, "branch": true, "git": true, "remote": true, "size": true, "live": true,
424			"latest": true, "worktrees": true, "tasks": true, "notes": true,
425			"category": true, "path": true,
426		}
427		for i, column := range c.TUI.Repos.Columns {
428			if !validColumns[column] {
429				return fmt.Errorf("tui.repos.columns[%d] %q: unknown column", i, column)
430			}
431		}
432		switch c.EffectiveRepoSort() {
433		case "activity", "latest", "name", "git", "size", "tasks":
434		default:
435			return fmt.Errorf("tui.repos.sort %q: want activity, latest, name, git, size or tasks", c.TUI.Repos.Sort)
436		}
437		seen := map[string]string{}
438		for i, t := range c.TUI.Tools {
439			switch {
440			case t.Key == "":
441				return fmt.Errorf("tui.tools[%d]: key is required", i)
442			case t.Run == "":
443				return fmt.Errorf("tui.tools[%d] (%s): run is required", i, t.Key)
444			}
445			if binding, ok := ReservedKey(t.Key); ok {
446				return fmt.Errorf("tui.tools[%d]: key %q is the dashboard's %q binding; pick another",
447					i, t.Key, binding)
448			}
449			if prev, ok := seen[t.Key]; ok {
450				return fmt.Errorf("tui.tools[%d]: key %q is already bound to %q", i, t.Key, prev)
451			}
452			seen[t.Key] = t.Name
453		}
454		return nil
455	}
456	
457	func validAzureDevOpsOrganization(raw string) bool {
458		u, err := url.Parse(raw)
459		if err != nil || !strings.EqualFold(u.Scheme, "https") || u.User != nil ||
460			u.RawQuery != "" || u.Fragment != "" || u.Port() != "" {
461			return false
462		}
463		host := strings.ToLower(u.Hostname())
464		segments := strings.FieldsFunc(u.Path, func(r rune) bool { return r == '/' })
465		switch {
466		case host == "dev.azure.com":
467			return len(segments) == 1
468		case strings.HasSuffix(host, ".visualstudio.com"):
469			organization := strings.TrimSuffix(host, ".visualstudio.com")
470			return organization != "" && organization != "vs-ssh" && len(segments) == 0
471		default:
472			return false
473		}
474	}

518		out := make([]string, 0, len(c.Paths.RepoPaths))
519		for _, path := range c.Paths.RepoPaths {
520			if expanded := Expand(path); expanded != "" {
521				out = append(out, expanded)
522			}
523		}
524		return out

527	// DiscoveryRoots returns exact repositories first, followed by recursive scan
528	// roots. repo.Discover recognises when a supplied root is itself a repository.
529	func (c Config) DiscoveryRoots() []string {
530		seen := map[string]bool{}
531		out := make([]string, 0, len(c.Paths.RepoPaths)+len(c.Paths.ScanRoots))
532		for _, roots := range [][]string{c.RepoPaths(), c.ScanRoots()} {
533			for _, root := range roots {
534				clean := filepath.Clean(root)
535				if clean == "" || seen[clean] {
536					continue
537				}
538				seen[clean] = true
539				out = append(out, clean)
540			}
541		}
542		return out
543	}

547		v := Vars{
548			"worktree_root": Expand(c.Paths.WorktreeRoot),
549			"repo":          repoName,
550			"repo_path":     repoPath,
551			"branch":        branch,
552			"category":      category,
553			"host":          Hostname(),
554			"date":          time.Now().Format("2006-01-02"),
555		}
556		rendered, err := Render(c.Paths.WorktreePath, v)
557		if err != nil {
558			return "", err
559		}
560		return Expand(rendered), nil
561	}
```

```text
78	// while remaining in the model's local snapshot for REMOTE matching.

89			}

94	// StateSummary renders the repository's tasks as a compact per-state tally,
95	// which is what makes the list scannable at forty repositories.
96	func (r RepoRow) StateSummary() string {
97		if len(r.Tasks) == 0 {
98			return ""
99		}
100		counts := map[task.State]int{}
101		for _, t := range r.Tasks {
102			counts[t.State]++
103		}
104		var parts []string
105		for _, s := range task.States {
106			if counts[s] > 0 {
107				parts = append(parts, s.Icon()+strconv.Itoa(counts[s]))
108			}
109		}
110		return strings.Join(parts, " ")
111	}

130			b.WriteString(" ")
131			b.WriteString(r.Asset.Note)
132			b.WriteString(" ")
133			b.WriteString(strings.Join(r.Asset.Tags, " "))
134		}
135		for _, t := range r.Tasks {
136			b.WriteString(" ")
137			b.WriteString(t.Title())
138			b.WriteString(" ")
139			b.WriteString(t.Branch)
140		}
141		for _, checkout := range r.Context.Checkouts {
142			b.WriteString(" ")
143			b.WriteString(checkout.Worktree.Path)
144			b.WriteString(" ")
145			b.WriteString(checkout.Branch())
146			b.WriteString(" ")
147			b.WriteString(string(checkout.Ownership))
148		}
149		return strings.ToLower(b.String())
150	}
151	
152	func (r RepoRow) matches(query string) bool {
153		query = strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(query))
154		for _, term := range strings.Fields(query) {
155			key, value, structured := strings.Cut(term, ":")
156			if structured {
157				switch key {
158				case "tag":
159					if r.Asset == nil || !r.Asset.HasTag(value) {
160						return false
161					}
162					continue
163				case "remote":
164					if !strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(r.Topology.Summary()), value) {
165						return false
166					}
167					continue
168				case "size":
169					if !matchesSize(r.Usage, value) {
170						return false
171					}
172					continue
173				case "kind":
174					kind := catalog.KindRepository
175					if r.Asset != nil {
176						kind = r.Asset.Kind
177					}
178					if string(kind) != value {
179						return false
180					}
181					continue
182				}
183			}
184			if !strings.Contains(r.searchText(), term) {
185				return false
186			}
187		}
188		return true
189	}
190	
191	// taskSearchText is what a filter query matches a task row against.
192	func taskSearchText(r inventory.Row) string {
193		t := r.Task
194		return strings.ToLower(strings.Join([]string{
195			t.Title(), t.Repo, t.Branch, t.Next, t.Note, string(t.State),
196		}, " "))
197	}
198	
199	// matches reports whether every whitespace-separated term of the query appears
200	// in the haystack.
201	//
202	// Term-wise rather than substring so "auth api" finds a task named "api token
203	// auth" — the order words come to mind in is rarely the order they appear in.
204	func matches(haystack, query string) bool {
205		return textmatch.Terms(haystack, query)
206	}
207	
208	// RemoteRow is one repository known to a configured forge, optionally matched to
209	// a local checkout. The REMOTE view is the bridge between "what exists on the
210	// forge" and "what is already on this machine".
211	type RemoteRow struct {
212		Repo forge.RemoteRepo `json:"repo"`
213		// LocalPath is the checkout under the configured scan roots, empty when the
214		// remote has not been cloned here.
215		LocalPath string `json:"local_path,omitempty"`
216		// LocalName is the discovered repo's display name.
217		LocalName string `json:"local_name,omitempty"`
218		// LocalKind distinguishes a cataloged Try from an ordinary repository.
219		LocalKind catalog.Kind `json:"local_kind,omitempty"`
220	}
221	
222	// FleetRow is one host/repository observation. Repository is nil for a host
223	// health row such as unreachable or no-dev.
224	type FleetRow struct {
225		Host       string
226		Local      bool
227		State      fleet.HostState
228		Repository *fleet.RepoSnapshot
229		Error      string
230		FromCache  bool
231	}
232	
233	func (r FleetRow) searchText() string {
234		parts := []string{r.Host, string(r.State), r.Error}
235		if r.Repository != nil {
236			parts = append(parts, r.Repository.Name, r.Repository.Display, r.Repository.Path,
237				r.Repository.Branch, r.Repository.Status.Summary(), strings.Join(r.Repository.RemoteIdentities, " "))
238		}
239		return strings.ToLower(strings.Join(parts, " "))
240	}
241	
242	// Cloned reports whether this remote already has a local checkout.
243	func (r RemoteRow) Cloned() bool { return r.LocalPath != "" }
244	
245	func (r RemoteRow) searchText() string {
246		return strings.ToLower(strings.Join([]string{
247			string(r.Repo.Forge), r.Repo.Name, r.Repo.FullName, r.Repo.Description,
248			r.Repo.Visibility, r.Repo.DefaultBranch, r.LocalName, string(r.LocalKind),
249		}, " "))
250	}
251	
252	func (r RemoteRow) matches(query string) bool {
253		query = strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(query))
254		for _, term := range strings.Fields(query) {
255			key, value, structured := strings.Cut(term, ":")
256			if structured && (key == "vis" || key == "visibility") {
257				if strings.ToLower(r.Repo.Visibility) != value {
258					return false
259				}
260				continue
261			}
262			if !strings.Contains(r.searchText(), term) {
263				return false
264			}
265		}
266		return true
267	}

284	}

292			if value != "" {

294			}
295		}
296		return t.Repo.Name
297	}

304		// cleaned. It may replace runErr with validation/index errors.
305		Complete func(runErr error) error
```

```text
106			}

109			err = filepath.WalkDir(rootClean, func(path string, d fs.DirEntry, err error) error {
110				if err != nil {

112				}
113				if ctx.Err() != nil {
```

```text
97	func pickStartRepository(ctx context.Context, app *App, current repo.Repo) (repo.Repo, bool, error) {

124			})
125		}

132		}

136			Description: "resolve a repository not present in the discovered list",
137		})
```

```text
286		}

288			project.Phase, project.Note, strings.Join(project.Tags, " ")}

294		}

300				strings.Join(project.Recovery.LocalOnlyBranches, " "))
301		}
302		haystack := strings.ToLower(strings.Join(values, " "))
303		for _, term := range strings.Fields(query) {
304			if !strings.Contains(haystack, term) {
305				return false
306			}
307		}
308		return true
309	}
```

```text
1	// Package repo discovers the repositories a user actually owns by walking the
2	// configured scan roots. It answers "what projects do I have?", which is a
3	// different question from "what am I working on?" — that one belongs to
4	// package task.
5	package repo
6	
7	import (
8		"context"
9		"io/fs"
10		"os"
11		"path/filepath"
12		"sort"
13		"strings"
14	
15		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/gitx"
16	)
17	
18	// Repo is one discovered repository.
19	type Repo struct {
20		// Name is the directory basename, which is how users refer to it.
21		Name string
22		// Path is the absolute path reached through the scan root. It may be a
23		// symlink from a bootstrap index; commands intentionally keep that human
24		// navigation path rather than replacing it with the physical one.
25		Path string
26		// RealPath is the physical checkout path.
27		RealPath string
28		// Symlink reports that Path is an alias to RealPath.
29		Symlink bool
30		// Root is the scan root it was found under.
31		Root string
32		// Category is the path between the scan root and the repo ("Quant",
33		// "Web/Frontend"), empty for a repo sitting directly in the root. It is
34		// human organisation metadata, preserved for `dev graduate` to place new
35		// projects consistently.
36		Category string
37		// GitDir is this checkout's administrative directory; CommonDir is shared
38		// by every linked worktree of the clone.
39		GitDir    string
40		CommonDir string
41		MainRoot  string
42		// Bare reports a bare repository (a worktree hub).
43		Bare bool
44		// HasGit distinguishes a real repo from a plain directory that was found
45		// in a scan root; non-repos are reported so `dev repo list` can offer to
46		// initialise them.
47		HasGit bool
48	}
49	
50	// Display renders "Category/Name" or just "Name".
51	func (r Repo) Display() string {
52		if r.Category == "" {
53			return r.Name
54		}
55		return r.Category + "/" + r.Name
56	}
57	
58	// Options tunes discovery.
59	type Options struct {
60		// MaxDepth limits how deep below a scan root a repo may be found. The
61		// default layout is <root>/<Category>/<Repo>, so 2 suffices; 3 leaves room
62		// for a nested grouping without walking an entire home directory.
63		MaxDepth int
64		// IncludeNonRepos reports plain directories alongside repositories.
65		IncludeNonRepos bool
66		// Fast avoids per-repository git subprocesses. It is intended for shell
67		// completion: direct .git-file checkouts are skipped as linked worktrees and
68		// symlink aliases are deduplicated by their physical path.
69		Fast bool
70	}
71	
72	// DefaultOptions is the discovery configuration used by dev's commands.
73	func DefaultOptions() Options { return Options{MaxDepth: 3} }
74	
75	// CompletionOptions trades full Git metadata for interactive latency.
76	func CompletionOptions() Options { return Options{MaxDepth: 3, Fast: true} }
77	
78	// skipDirs are never descended into. These are large, never contain a project
79	// the user organises by hand, and walking them dominates scan time.
80	var skipDirs = map[string]bool{
81		"node_modules": true, ".venv": true, "venv": true, "target": true,
82		"vendor": true, "__pycache__": true, ".tox": true, "dist": true,
83		"build": true, ".next": true, ".cache": true, ".terraform": true,
84		"Library": true, ".Trash": true,
85	}
86	
87	// Discover walks every root and returns the repositories found, sorted by
88	// display name. Unreadable directories are skipped rather than fatal — a scan
89	// root that has been unmounted must not break `dev ls`.
90	func Discover(ctx context.Context, roots []string, opts Options) ([]Repo, error) {
91		if opts.MaxDepth <= 0 {
92			opts.MaxDepth = DefaultOptions().MaxDepth
93		}
94		seen := map[string]bool{}
95		// clone identities stop a physical path and a symlink index from showing
96		// the same repository twice. The first scan root wins, which lets users
97		// choose whether the curated index or the physical hierarchy is their UI
98		// simply by ordering scan_roots.
99		identities := map[string]bool{}
100		var out []Repo
101	
102		for _, root := range roots {
103			info, err := os.Stat(root)
104			if err != nil || !info.IsDir() {
105				continue // a missing scan root is normal on a fresh machine
106			}
107			rootClean := filepath.Clean(root)
108	
109			err = filepath.WalkDir(rootClean, func(path string, d fs.DirEntry, err error) error {
110				if err != nil {
111					return nil // unreadable entry: skip, keep walking
112				}
113				if ctx.Err() != nil {
114					return ctx.Err()
115				}
116				isRoot := path == rootClean
117				name := d.Name()
118				isLink := d.Type()&os.ModeSymlink != 0
119				isDir := d.IsDir()
120				if isLink {
121					// WalkDir does not follow symlinks. Inspect a direct symlink to
122					// a repository, but do not recurse through arbitrary symlinked
123					// containers — bootstrap does that with cycle detection.
124					if info, err := os.Stat(path); err == nil {
125						isDir = info.IsDir()
126					}
127				}
128				if !isDir {
129					return nil
130				}
131				if !isRoot && (skipDirs[name] || (strings.HasPrefix(name, ".") && name != ".bare")) {
132					return filepath.SkipDir
133				}
134	
135				rel := "."
136				depth := 0
137				if !isRoot {
138					rel, _ = filepath.Rel(rootClean, path)
139					depth = len(strings.Split(rel, string(filepath.Separator)))
140				}
141	
142				if isRepoDir(path) {
143					real, _ := filepath.EvalSymlinks(path)
144					if real == "" {
145						real = path
146					}
147					bare := isBareDir(path)
148					identity, gitDir, commonDir, mainRoot := real, real, real, real
149					if !bare && opts.Fast && gitEntryIsFile(path) {
150						// A direct .git file at a discovered root is a linked
151						// worktree. Submodules are already hidden below their parent
152						// repository because discovery never descends into one.
153						return filepath.SkipDir
154					}
155					if !bare && !opts.Fast {
156						if g, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, path); err == nil {
157							// A linked worktree is execution state, not another
158							// project in the repo inventory.
159							if g.IsLinkedWorktree {
160								return filepath.SkipDir
161							}
162							identity, gitDir, commonDir, mainRoot = g.GitCommonDir, g.GitDir, g.GitCommonDir, g.MainRoot
163							real = g.MainRoot
164						}
165					}
166					if !seen[path] && !identities[identity] {
167						seen[path], identities[identity] = true, true
168						out = append(out, Repo{
169							Name:      name,
170							Path:      path,
171							RealPath:  real,
172							Symlink:   isLink,
173							Root:      rootClean,
174							Category:  filepath.ToSlash(filepath.Dir(rel)),
175							GitDir:    gitDir,
176							CommonDir: commonDir,
177							MainRoot:  mainRoot,
178							Bare:      bare,
179							HasGit:    true,
180						})
181					}
182					// Never descend into a repo: its subdirectories are source
183					// code, and any nested .git is a submodule or a worktree that
184					// belongs to this repo, not a project of its own.
185					return filepath.SkipDir
186				}
187				if depth >= opts.MaxDepth {
188					return filepath.SkipDir
189				}
190				if opts.IncludeNonRepos && depth == 1 {
191					if !seen[path] {
192						seen[path] = true
193						out = append(out, Repo{Name: name, Path: path, Root: rootClean, Category: ""})
194					}
195				}
196				return nil
197			})
198			if err != nil && ctx.Err() != nil {
199				return out, ctx.Err()
200			}
201		}
202	
203		for i := range out {
204			if out[i].Category == "." {
205				out[i].Category = ""
206			}
207		}
208		sort.Slice(out, func(i, j int) bool {
209			if out[i].Name != out[j].Name {
210				return strings.ToLower(out[i].Name) < strings.ToLower(out[j].Name)
211			}
212			return out[i].Path < out[j].Path
213		})
214		return out, nil
215	}
216	
217	// isRepoDir reports whether path is a repository root: it holds a .git entry
218	// (directory for a normal clone, file for a linked worktree or submodule).
219	func isRepoDir(path string) bool {
220		if _, err := os.Lstat(filepath.Join(path, ".git")); err == nil {
221			return true
222		}
223		return isBareDir(path)
224	}
225	
226	func gitEntryIsFile(path string) bool {
227		info, err := os.Lstat(filepath.Join(path, ".git"))
228		return err == nil && info.Mode().IsRegular()
229	}
230	
231	// isBareDir recognises a bare repository by its skeleton, without shelling out.
232	func isBareDir(path string) bool {
233		for _, marker := range []string{"HEAD", "objects", "refs"} {
234			if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(path, marker)); err != nil {
235				return false
236			}
237		}
238		return true
239	}
240	
241	// Resolve finds a repo by name, display name, or path.
242	//
243	// Matching is deliberately layered: an exact name or path wins outright, and
244	// only then does a substring search run — so a repo literally named "web"
245	// is never shadowed by "web-frontend".
246	func Resolve(ctx context.Context, roots []string, ref string) (Repo, []Repo, error) {
247		return resolve(ctx, roots, ref, DefaultOptions())
248	}
249	
250	// ResolveCompletion resolves the same references without launching one Git
251	// process per repository in the scan roots.
252	func ResolveCompletion(ctx context.Context, roots []string, ref string) (Repo, []Repo, error) {
253		return resolve(ctx, roots, ref, CompletionOptions())
254	}
255	
256	func resolve(ctx context.Context, roots []string, ref string, opts Options) (Repo, []Repo, error) {
257		all, err := Discover(ctx, roots, opts)
258		if err != nil {
259			return Repo{}, nil, err
260		}
261		if abs, err := filepath.Abs(ref); err == nil {
262			if g, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, abs); err == nil {
263				real, _ := filepath.EvalSymlinks(abs)
264				if real == "" {
265					real = g.MainRoot
266				}
267				// Preserve an explicit navigation alias. The caller named this
268				// path on purpose; resolving it to the physical checkout would
269				// defeat a bootstrap symlink catalog.
270				return Repo{
271					Name: filepath.Base(abs), Path: abs, RealPath: real,
272					Symlink: real != abs, CommonDir: g.GitCommonDir, HasGit: true, Bare: g.Bare,
273				}, nil, nil
274			}
275		}
276		for _, r := range all {
277			if r.Name == ref || r.Display() == ref || r.Path == ref {
278				return r, nil, nil
279			}
280		}
281		needle := strings.ToLower(ref)
282		var hits []Repo
283		for _, r := range all {
284			if strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(r.Display()), needle) {
285				hits = append(hits, r)
286			}
287		}
288		switch len(hits) {
289		case 1:
290			return hits[0], nil, nil
291		case 0:
292			return Repo{}, nil, &NotFoundError{Ref: ref}
293		default:
294			return Repo{}, hits, &AmbiguousError{Ref: ref, Candidates: hits}
295		}
296	}
297	
298	// NotFoundError reports a repo reference that matched nothing.
299	type NotFoundError struct{ Ref string }
300	
301	func (e *NotFoundError) Error() string { return "no repository matching " + e.Ref }
302	
303	// AmbiguousError reports a repo reference that matched several repos.
304	type AmbiguousError struct {
305		Ref        string
306		Candidates []Repo
307	}
308	
309	func (e *AmbiguousError) Error() string {
310		names := make([]string, len(e.Candidates))
311		for i, c := range e.Candidates {
312			names[i] = c.Display()
313		}
314		return e.Ref + " is ambiguous: " + strings.Join(names, ", ")
315	}
316
```

```text
1	package cli
```
