```text
3	import (
4		"fmt"
5		"io"
6		"strings"
7		"time"
8		"unicode/utf8"
9	)
10	
11	// Table renders aligned columns. It measures width in runes rather than bytes
12	// so the CJK repo and branch names in a real inventory line up.
13	type Table struct {
14		head  []string
15		rows  [][]string
16		style cliStyle
17	}
18	
19	// Add appends a row. Short rows are padded, long ones are truncated to the
20	// header width so a stray field can never shift the whole table.
21	func (t *Table) Add(cells ...string) {
22		row := make([]string, len(t.head))
23		copy(row, cells)
24		t.rows = append(t.rows, row)
25	}
26	
27	// Len reports the number of data rows.
28	func (t *Table) Len() int { return len(t.rows) }
29	
30	// Render writes the table, sizing every column to its widest cell.
31	func (t *Table) Render(w io.Writer) {
32		if len(t.rows) == 0 {
33			return
34		}
35		widths := make([]int, len(t.head))
36		for i, h := range t.head {
37			widths[i] = width(h)
38		}
39		for _, r := range t.rows {
40			for i, c := range r {
41				if n := width(c); n > widths[i] {
42					widths[i] = n
43				}
44			}
45		}
46		head := make([]string, len(t.head))
47		for i, cell := range t.head {
48			head[i] = t.style.header(cell)
49		}
50		writeRow(w, head, widths)
51		for _, r := range t.rows {
52			writeRow(w, r, widths)
53		}
54	}
55	
56	func writeRow(w io.Writer, cells []string, widths []int) {
57		var b strings.Builder
58		for i, c := range cells {
59			if i == len(cells)-1 {
60				b.WriteString(c) // never pad the last column
61				break
62			}
63			b.WriteString(c)
64			b.WriteString(strings.Repeat(" ", widths[i]-width(c)+2))
65		}
66		fmt.Fprintln(w, strings.TrimRight(b.String(), " "))
67	}
68	
69	// width counts display columns, treating wide CJK runes as two.
70	func width(s string) int {
71		n := 0
72		for i := 0; i < len(s); {
73			if end := ansiEnd(s, i); end > i {
74				i = end
75				continue
76			}
77			r, size := utf8.DecodeRuneInString(s[i:])
78			if isWide(r) {
79				n += 2
80			} else {
81				n++
82			}
83			i += size
84		}
85		return n
86	}
87	
88	func ansiEnd(s string, start int) int {
89		if start+2 > len(s) || s[start] != '\x1b' || s[start+1] != '[' {
90			return start
91		}
92		for i := start + 2; i < len(s); i++ {
93			if s[i] >= 0x40 && s[i] <= 0x7e {
94				return i + 1
95			}
96		}
97		return start
98	}
99	
100	func stripANSI(s string) string {
101		var b strings.Builder
102		for i := 0; i < len(s); {
103			if end := ansiEnd(s, i); end > i {
104				i = end
105				continue
106			}
107			r, size := utf8.DecodeRuneInString(s[i:])
108			b.WriteRune(r)
109			i += size
110		}
111		return b.String()
112	}
113	
114	func isWide(r rune) bool {
115		switch {
116		case r >= 0x1100 && r <= 0x115F, // Hangul Jamo
117			r >= 0x2E80 && r <= 0xA4CF, // CJK radicals through Yi
118			r >= 0xAC00 && r <= 0xD7A3, // Hangul syllables
119			r >= 0xF900 && r <= 0xFAFF, // CJK compatibility ideographs
120			r >= 0xFE30 && r <= 0xFE6F, // CJK compatibility forms
121			r >= 0xFF00 && r <= 0xFF60, // fullwidth forms
122			r >= 0xFFE0 && r <= 0xFFE6,
123			r >= 0x20000 && r <= 0x3FFFD: // CJK extension planes
124			return true
125		}
126		return false
127	}
128	
129	// truncate shortens s to at most n display columns, marking the cut with "…".
130	func truncate(s string, n int) string {
131		if n <= 0 || width(s) <= n {
132			return s
133		}
134		var b strings.Builder
135		used := 0
136		hasANSI := false
137		for i := 0; i < len(s); {
138			if end := ansiEnd(s, i); end > i {
139				hasANSI = true
140				b.WriteString(s[i:end])
141				i = end
142				continue
143			}
144			r, size := utf8.DecodeRuneInString(s[i:])
145			rw := 1
146			if isWide(r) {
147				rw = 2
148			}
149			if used+rw > n-1 {
150				break
151			}
152			b.WriteRune(r)
153			used += rw
154			i += size
155		}
156		b.WriteString("…")
157		if hasANSI {
158			b.WriteString(ansiReset)
159		}
160		return b.String()
161	}
162	
163	// dash renders an empty value as a visible placeholder, so a blank column is
164	// never mistaken for a rendering bug.
165	func dash(s string) string {
166		if strings.TrimSpace(s) == "" {
167			return "—"
168		}
169		return s
170	}
171	
172	// humanAge renders a duration the way a changelog would: "3d", "2w", "5mo".
173	func humanAge(d time.Duration) string {
174		switch {
175		case d <= 0:
176			return "—"
177		case d < time.Hour:
178			return fmt.Sprintf("%dm", int(d.Minutes()))
179		case d < 24*time.Hour:
180			return fmt.Sprintf("%dh", int(d.Hours()))
181		case d < 14*24*time.Hour:
182			return fmt.Sprintf("%dd", int(d.Hours()/24))
183		case d < 60*24*time.Hour:
184			return fmt.Sprintf("%dw", int(d.Hours()/24/7))
185		default:
186			return fmt.Sprintf("%dmo", int(d.Hours()/24/30))
187		}
188	}
189	
190	// powershellQuote wraps s as a PowerShell single-quoted string literal, in
191	// which the only metacharacter is the single quote itself, escaped by doubling.
192	func powershellQuote(s string) string {
193		return "'" + strings.ReplaceAll(s, "'", "''") + "'"
194	}
195	
196	// shellQuote makes a path safe to paste into a POSIX shell command.
197	func shellQuote(s string) string {
198		if s == "" {
199			return "''"
200		}
201		safe := true
202		for _, r := range s {
203			if !(r == '/' || r == '.' || r == '-' || r == '_' || r == '~' ||
204				(r >= 'a' && r <= 'z') || (r >= 'A' && r <= 'Z') || (r >= '0' && r <= '9')) {
205				safe = false
206				break
207			}
208		}
209		if safe && utf8.ValidString(s) {
210			return s
211		}
212		return "'" + strings.ReplaceAll(s, "'", `'\''`) + "'"
213	}
```

```text
1	// Package repo discovers the repositories a user actually owns by walking the
2	// configured scan roots. It answers "what projects do I have?", which is a
3	// different question from "what am I working on?" — that one belongs to
4	// package task.
5	package repo
6	
7	import (
8		"context"
9		"io/fs"
10		"os"
11		"path/filepath"
12		"sort"
13		"strings"
14	
15		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/gitx"
16	)
17	
18	// Repo is one discovered repository.
19	type Repo struct {
20		// Name is the directory basename, which is how users refer to it.
21		Name string
22		// Path is the absolute path reached through the scan root. It may be a
23		// symlink from a bootstrap index; commands intentionally keep that human
24		// navigation path rather than replacing it with the physical one.
25		Path string
26		// RealPath is the physical checkout path.
27		RealPath string
28		// Symlink reports that Path is an alias to RealPath.
29		Symlink bool
30		// Root is the scan root it was found under.
31		Root string
32		// Category is the path between the scan root and the repo ("Quant",
33		// "Web/Frontend"), empty for a repo sitting directly in the root. It is
34		// human organisation metadata, preserved for `dev graduate` to place new
35		// projects consistently.
36		Category string
37		// GitDir is this checkout's administrative directory; CommonDir is shared
38		// by every linked worktree of the clone.
39		GitDir    string
40		CommonDir string
41		MainRoot  string
42		// Bare reports a bare repository (a worktree hub).
43		Bare bool
44		// HasGit distinguishes a real repo from a plain directory that was found
45		// in a scan root; non-repos are reported so `dev repo list` can offer to
46		// initialise them.
47		HasGit bool
48	}
49	
50	// Display renders "Category/Name" or just "Name".
51	func (r Repo) Display() string {
52		if r.Category == "" {
53			return r.Name
54		}
55		return r.Category + "/" + r.Name
56	}
57	
58	// Options tunes discovery.
59	type Options struct {
60		// MaxDepth limits how deep below a scan root a repo may be found. The
61		// default layout is <root>/<Category>/<Repo>, so 2 suffices; 3 leaves room
62		// for a nested grouping without walking an entire home directory.
63		MaxDepth int
64		// IncludeNonRepos reports plain directories alongside repositories.
65		IncludeNonRepos bool
66		// Fast avoids per-repository git subprocesses. It is intended for shell
67		// completion: direct .git-file checkouts are skipped as linked worktrees and
68		// symlink aliases are deduplicated by their physical path.
69		Fast bool
70	}
71	
72	// DefaultOptions is the discovery configuration used by dev's commands.
73	func DefaultOptions() Options { return Options{MaxDepth: 3} }
74	
75	// CompletionOptions trades full Git metadata for interactive latency.
76	func CompletionOptions() Options { return Options{MaxDepth: 3, Fast: true} }
77	
78	// skipDirs are never descended into. These are large, never contain a project
79	// the user organises by hand, and walking them dominates scan time.
80	var skipDirs = map[string]bool{
81		"node_modules": true, ".venv": true, "venv": true, "target": true,
82		"vendor": true, "__pycache__": true, ".tox": true, "dist": true,
83		"build": true, ".next": true, ".cache": true, ".terraform": true,
84		"Library": true, ".Trash": true,
85	}
86	
87	// Discover walks every root and returns the repositories found, sorted by
88	// display name. Unreadable directories are skipped rather than fatal — a scan
89	// root that has been unmounted must not break `dev ls`.
90	func Discover(ctx context.Context, roots []string, opts Options) ([]Repo, error) {
91		if opts.MaxDepth <= 0 {
92			opts.MaxDepth = DefaultOptions().MaxDepth
93		}
94		seen := map[string]bool{}
95		// clone identities stop a physical path and a symlink index from showing
96		// the same repository twice. The first scan root wins, which lets users
97		// choose whether the curated index or the physical hierarchy is their UI
98		// simply by ordering scan_roots.
99		identities := map[string]bool{}
100		var out []Repo
101	
102		for _, root := range roots {
103			info, err := os.Stat(root)
104			if err != nil || !info.IsDir() {
105				continue // a missing scan root is normal on a fresh machine
106			}
107			rootClean := filepath.Clean(root)
108	
109			err = filepath.WalkDir(rootClean, func(path string, d fs.DirEntry, err error) error {
110				if err != nil {
111					return nil // unreadable entry: skip, keep walking
112				}
113				if ctx.Err() != nil {
114					return ctx.Err()
115				}
116				isRoot := path == rootClean
117				name := d.Name()
118				isLink := d.Type()&os.ModeSymlink != 0
119				isDir := d.IsDir()
120				if isLink {
121					// WalkDir does not follow symlinks. Inspect a direct symlink to
122					// a repository, but do not recurse through arbitrary symlinked
123					// containers — bootstrap does that with cycle detection.
124					if info, err := os.Stat(path); err == nil {
125						isDir = info.IsDir()
126					}
127				}
128				if !isDir {
129					return nil
130				}
131				if !isRoot && (skipDirs[name] || (strings.HasPrefix(name, ".") && name != ".bare")) {
132					return filepath.SkipDir
133				}
134	
135				rel := "."
136				depth := 0
137				if !isRoot {
138					rel, _ = filepath.Rel(rootClean, path)
139					depth = len(strings.Split(rel, string(filepath.Separator)))
140				}
141	
142				if isRepoDir(path) {
143					real, _ := filepath.EvalSymlinks(path)
144					if real == "" {
145						real = path
146					}
147					bare := isBareDir(path)
148					identity, gitDir, commonDir, mainRoot := real, real, real, real
149					if !bare && opts.Fast && gitEntryIsFile(path) {
150						// A direct .git file at a discovered root is a linked
151						// worktree. Submodules are already hidden below their parent
152						// repository because discovery never descends into one.
153						return filepath.SkipDir
154					}
155					if !bare && !opts.Fast {
156						if g, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, path); err == nil {
157							// A linked worktree is execution state, not another
158							// project in the repo inventory.
159							if g.IsLinkedWorktree {
160								return filepath.SkipDir
161							}
162							identity, gitDir, commonDir, mainRoot = g.GitCommonDir, g.GitDir, g.GitCommonDir, g.MainRoot
163							real = g.MainRoot
164						}
165					}
166					if !seen[path] && !identities[identity] {
167						seen[path], identities[identity] = true, true
168						out = append(out, Repo{
169							Name:      name,
170							Path:      path,
171							RealPath:  real,
172							Symlink:   isLink,
173							Root:      rootClean,
174							Category:  filepath.ToSlash(filepath.Dir(rel)),
175							GitDir:    gitDir,
176							CommonDir: commonDir,
177							MainRoot:  mainRoot,
178							Bare:      bare,
179							HasGit:    true,
180						})
181					}
182					// Never descend into a repo: its subdirectories are source
183					// code, and any nested .git is a submodule or a worktree that
184					// belongs to this repo, not a project of its own.
185					return filepath.SkipDir
186				}
187				if depth >= opts.MaxDepth {
188					return filepath.SkipDir
189				}
190				if opts.IncludeNonRepos && depth == 1 {
191					if !seen[path] {
192						seen[path] = true
193						out = append(out, Repo{Name: name, Path: path, Root: rootClean, Category: ""})
194					}
195				}
196				return nil
197			})
198			if err != nil && ctx.Err() != nil {
199				return out, ctx.Err()
200			}
201		}
202	
203		for i := range out {
204			if out[i].Category == "." {
205				out[i].Category = ""
206			}
207		}
208		sort.Slice(out, func(i, j int) bool {
209			if out[i].Name != out[j].Name {
210				return strings.ToLower(out[i].Name) < strings.ToLower(out[j].Name)
211			}
212			return out[i].Path < out[j].Path
213		})
214		return out, nil
215	}
216	
217	// isRepoDir reports whether path is a repository root: it holds a .git entry
218	// (directory for a normal clone, file for a linked worktree or submodule).
219	func isRepoDir(path string) bool {
220		if _, err := os.Lstat(filepath.Join(path, ".git")); err == nil {
221			return true
222		}
223		return isBareDir(path)
224	}
225	
226	func gitEntryIsFile(path string) bool {
227		info, err := os.Lstat(filepath.Join(path, ".git"))
228		return err == nil && info.Mode().IsRegular()
229	}
230	
231	// isBareDir recognises a bare repository by its skeleton, without shelling out.
232	func isBareDir(path string) bool {
233		for _, marker := range []string{"HEAD", "objects", "refs"} {
234			if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(path, marker)); err != nil {
235				return false
236			}
237		}
238		return true
239	}
240	
241	// Resolve finds a repo by name, display name, or path.
242	//
243	// Matching is deliberately layered: an exact name or path wins outright, and
244	// only then does a substring search run — so a repo literally named "web"
245	// is never shadowed by "web-frontend".
246	func Resolve(ctx context.Context, roots []string, ref string) (Repo, []Repo, error) {
247		return resolve(ctx, roots, ref, DefaultOptions())
248	}
249	
250	// ResolveCompletion resolves the same references without launching one Git
251	// process per repository in the scan roots.
252	func ResolveCompletion(ctx context.Context, roots []string, ref string) (Repo, []Repo, error) {
253		return resolve(ctx, roots, ref, CompletionOptions())
254	}
255	
256	func resolve(ctx context.Context, roots []string, ref string, opts Options) (Repo, []Repo, error) {
257		all, err := Discover(ctx, roots, opts)
258		if err != nil {
259			return Repo{}, nil, err
260		}
261		if abs, err := filepath.Abs(ref); err == nil {
262			if g, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, abs); err == nil {
263				real, _ := filepath.EvalSymlinks(abs)
264				if real == "" {
265					real = g.MainRoot
266				}
267				// Preserve an explicit navigation alias. The caller named this
268				// path on purpose; resolving it to the physical checkout would
269				// defeat a bootstrap symlink catalog.
270				return Repo{
271					Name: filepath.Base(abs), Path: abs, RealPath: real,
272					Symlink: real != abs, CommonDir: g.GitCommonDir, HasGit: true, Bare: g.Bare,
273				}, nil, nil
274			}
275		}
276		for _, r := range all {
277			if r.Name == ref || r.Display() == ref || r.Path == ref {
278				return r, nil, nil
279			}
280		}
281		needle := strings.ToLower(ref)
282		var hits []Repo
283		for _, r := range all {
284			if strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(r.Display()), needle) {
285				hits = append(hits, r)
286			}
287		}
288		switch len(hits) {
289		case 1:
290			return hits[0], nil, nil
291		case 0:
292			return Repo{}, nil, &NotFoundError{Ref: ref}
293		default:
294			return Repo{}, hits, &AmbiguousError{Ref: ref, Candidates: hits}
295		}
296	}
297	
298	// NotFoundError reports a repo reference that matched nothing.
299	type NotFoundError struct{ Ref string }
300	
301	func (e *NotFoundError) Error() string { return "no repository matching " + e.Ref }
302	
303	// AmbiguousError reports a repo reference that matched several repos.
304	type AmbiguousError struct {
305		Ref        string
306		Candidates []Repo
307	}
308	
309	func (e *AmbiguousError) Error() string {
310		names := make([]string, len(e.Candidates))
311		for i, c := range e.Candidates {
312			names[i] = c.Display()
313		}
314		return e.Ref + " is ambiguous: " + strings.Join(names, ", ")
315	}
316
```

```text
16	
17	// Cache is the on-disk forge inventory. It exists for UI latency, not as a
18	// source of truth: the REMOTE tab should open instantly, and r refreshes it.
19	type Cache struct {
20		Version   int                     `json:"version,omitempty"`
21		SourceID  string                  `json:"source_id,omitempty"`
22		FetchedAt time.Time               `json:"fetched_at"`
23		Complete  bool                    `json:"complete,omitempty"`
24		Providers map[Kind]ProviderStatus `json:"providers,omitempty"`
25		Repos     []RemoteRepo            `json:"repos"`
26	}
27	
28	const (
29		CacheVersion      = 2
30		maxCacheBytes     = 32 << 20
31		maxCachedRepos    = 100_000
32		maxCacheClockSkew = 5 * time.Minute
33	)
34	
35	var cacheWriteLocks sync.Map
36	
37	type ProviderStatus struct {
38		FetchedAt time.Time `json:"fetched_at,omitempty"`
39		Complete  bool      `json:"complete"`
40		Error     string    `json:"error,omitempty"`
41	}
42	
43	// LoadCache returns only a fresh, complete cache. TUI callers that can label
44	// stale rows while refreshing use LoadCacheAny instead.
45	func LoadCache(path string, maxAge time.Duration) (Cache, bool) {
46		c, ok := LoadCacheAny(path)
47		if !ok || !c.Fresh(maxAge) {
48			return Cache{}, false
49		}
50		return c, true
51	}
52	
53	// LoadCacheAny returns a cache regardless of age or completeness. This powers
54	// stale-while-revalidate UI behavior; callers must inspect Fresh/Complete.
55	func LoadCacheAny(path string) (Cache, bool) {
56		info, err := os.Stat(path)
57		if err != nil || info.Size() < 0 || info.Size() > maxCacheBytes {
58			return Cache{}, false
59		}
60		b, err := os.ReadFile(path)
61		if err != nil {
62			return Cache{}, false
63		}
64		var c Cache
65		if json.Unmarshal(b, &c) != nil || !validCache(c, time.Now().UTC()) {
66			return Cache{}, false
67		}
68		if c.Version == 0 {
69			// Version 1 caches were valid snapshots but capped per provider, so they
70			// are useful for instant display and must immediately be refreshed.
71			c.Complete = false
72		}
73		return c, true
74	}
75	
76	func validCache(c Cache, now time.Time) bool {
77		if (c.Version != 0 && c.Version != CacheVersion) || c.FetchedAt.IsZero() ||
78			c.FetchedAt.After(now.Add(maxCacheClockSkew)) || len(c.Repos) > maxCachedRepos ||
79			!validCacheString(c.SourceID, 128, false) {
80			return false
81		}
82		for kind, status := range c.Providers {
83			if !validForgeKind(kind) || len(status.Error) > 16<<10 || strings.ContainsRune(status.Error, '\x00') ||
84				status.FetchedAt.After(now.Add(maxCacheClockSkew)) {
85				return false
86			}
87		}
88		for _, repository := range c.Repos {
89			if !validForgeKind(repository.Forge) || pathx.ValidateComponent(repository.Name) != nil ||
90				!validCacheString(repository.FullName, 2048, true) ||
91				!validCacheString(repository.Description, 64<<10, false) ||
92				!validCacheString(repository.URL, 8<<10, false) ||
93				!validCacheString(repository.CloneURL, 8<<10, false) ||
94				!validCacheString(repository.SSHURL, 8<<10, false) ||
95				!validCacheString(repository.Visibility, 128, false) ||
96				!validCacheString(repository.DefaultBranch, 1024, false) ||
97				repository.UpdatedAt.After(now.Add(maxCacheClockSkew)) {
98				return false
99			}
100		}
101		return true
102	}
103	
104	func validForgeKind(kind Kind) bool {
105		return kind == GitHub || kind == GitLab || kind == AzureDevOps
106	}
107	
108	func validCacheString(value string, limit int, required bool) bool {
109		return (!required || strings.TrimSpace(value) != "") && len(value) <= limit && !strings.ContainsRune(value, '\x00')
110	}
111	
112	// FreshFor additionally requires the cache to describe the same configured
113	// provider endpoints/targets. Caches without a source ID remain displayable but
114	// are immediately revalidated.
115	func (c Cache) FreshFor(maxAge time.Duration, sourceID string) bool {
116		return sourceID != "" && c.SourceID == sourceID && c.Fresh(maxAge)
117	}
118	
119	func (c Cache) Fresh(maxAge time.Duration) bool {
120		if c.Version != CacheVersion || !c.Complete {
121			return false
122		}
123		if maxAge <= 0 {
124			return true
125		}
126		if len(c.Providers) == 0 {
127			return time.Since(c.FetchedAt) <= maxAge
128		}
129		for _, provider := range c.Providers {
130			if !provider.Complete || provider.Error != "" || provider.FetchedAt.IsZero() || time.Since(provider.FetchedAt) > maxAge {
131				return false
132			}
133		}
134		return true
135	}
136	
137	// SaveCache atomically replaces the cache. A partial forge response may be
138	// cached — its FetchedAt still says exactly when it was observed.
139	func SaveCache(path string, repos []RemoteRepo) error {
140		now := time.Now().UTC()
141		providers := map[Kind]ProviderStatus{}
142		for _, repo := range repos {
143			providers[repo.Forge] = ProviderStatus{FetchedAt: now, Complete: true}
144		}
145		return SaveCacheState(path, Cache{Version: CacheVersion, FetchedAt: now, Complete: true, Providers: providers, Repos: repos})
146	}
147	
148	// SaveCacheState atomically replaces the versioned inventory cache.
149	func SaveCacheState(path string, cache Cache) error {
150		return SaveCacheStateContext(context.Background(), path, cache)
151	}
152	
153	// SaveCacheStateContext serializes one cache target and checks cancellation
154	// while holding that ordering boundary. A superseded generation therefore
155	// cannot rename after a newer generation has committed.
156	func SaveCacheStateContext(ctx context.Context, path string, cache Cache) error {
157		if path == "" {
158			return errors.New("empty cache path")
159		}
160		if ctx == nil {
161			ctx = context.Background()
162		}
163		lock := cacheWriteLock(path)
164		lock.Lock()
165		defer lock.Unlock()
166		if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
167			return err
168		}
169		if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(path), 0o755); err != nil {
170			return err
171		}
172		if cache.Version == 0 {
173			cache.Version = CacheVersion
174		}
175		if cache.FetchedAt.IsZero() {
176			cache.FetchedAt = time.Now().UTC()
177		}
178		b, err := json.MarshalIndent(cache, "", "  ")
179		if err != nil {
180			return err
181		}
182		b = append(b, '\n')
183		tmp, err := os.CreateTemp(filepath.Dir(path), ".remotes-*.tmp")
184		if err != nil {
185			return err
186		}
187		name := tmp.Name()
188		defer os.Remove(name)
189		if _, err := tmp.Write(b); err != nil {
190			tmp.Close()
191			return err
192		}
193		if err := tmp.Close(); err != nil {
194			return err
195		}
196		if err := os.Chmod(name, 0o600); err != nil {
197			return err
198		}
199		if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
200			return err
201		}
202		return os.Rename(name, path)
203	}
204	
205	func cacheWriteLock(path string) *sync.Mutex {
206		loaded, _ := cacheWriteLocks.LoadOrStore(filepath.Clean(path), &sync.Mutex{})
207		return loaded.(*sync.Mutex)
208	}
209	
210	// CacheExists reports whether any cache file exists, even stale. Used only for
211	// diagnostics.
212	func CacheExists(path string) bool {
213		_, err := os.Stat(path)
214		return err == nil || !errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist)
215	}
```

```text
1	# Source this file from Bash or Zsh after installing dev, jq, and fzf.
2	# Populate the private candidate cache once with: dev repo remote --refresh
3	
4	dev-repo-clone-fzf() {
5	  local selected status ref
6	  selected="$({
7	    dev repo remote --cached --json |
8	      jq -r '.[] | select(.repo.clone_url != null and .repo.clone_url != "") | select((.repo.clone_url | test("[\\t\\r\\n]")) | not) | [.repo.clone_url, (.repo.forge + ":" + .repo.full_name), (.repo.visibility // ""), (.local_path // ""), ((.repo.description // "") | gsub("[\\t\\r\\n]+"; " "))] | @tsv' |
9	      fzf --delimiter=$'\t' --with-nth=2.. --prompt='Repository to clone> '
10	  })"
11	  status=$?
12	  if [ "$status" -ne 0 ]; then
13	    return "$status"
14	  fi
15	  [ -n "$selected" ] || return 0
16	
17	  ref=${selected%%$'\t'*}
18	  [ -n "$ref" ] || return 1
19	  dev repo clone "$ref"
20	}
21
```

16	
17	```bash
18	dev repo clone "$(tv dev-remote-repos)"
19	```
20	
21	The channel requires `dev` and `jq`. It reads only
22	`dev repo remote --cached --json`; opening the channel never contacts a forge.
23	
24	## fzf shell helper
25	
26	Source `fzf/dev-repo-clone.bash`, then run:
27	
28	```bash
29	dev-repo-clone-fzf
30	```
31	
32	The helper requires `dev`, `jq`, and `fzf`. It does not use `eval` or `xargs`:
33	the selected canonical clone URL is passed to `dev repo clone` as one quoted
34	argument. Canceling fzf performs no clone.
35	
36	Both integrations retain already-cloned rows because a second destination may

```text
+func TestRepoClonePickerUsesStaleCacheAndCanCancel(t *testing.T) {

 func TestRepoNewWizardRoutesCloneReference(t *testing.T) {
 	app, out := newRepoWizardApp(t, "")
 	source := filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "source")
 	if err := os.Mkdir(source, 0o755); err != nil {
 		t.Fatal(err)
 	}
 	if _, err := gitx.Run(t.Context(), source, "init", "-b", "main"); err != nil {
 		t.Fatal(err)
 	}
 	if err := os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(source, "source.txt"), []byte("from clone\n"), 0o644); err != nil {
 		t.Fatal(err)
 	}
 	if _, err := gitx.Run(t.Context(), source, "add", "source.txt"); err != nil {
 		t.Fatal(err)
 	}
 	if _, err := gitx.Run(t.Context(), source, "commit", "-m", "test: source"); err != nil {
 		t.Fatal(err)
 	}
 	app.In = strings.NewReader(strings.Join([]string{source, "", "", "", ""}, "\n") + "\n")
 
 	cmd := newRepoNewCmd(app)
 	cmd.SetArgs([]string{"--preset", "minimal"})
 	if err := cmd.Execute(); err != nil {
 		t.Fatal(err)
 	}
 	destination := filepath.Join(config.Expand(app.Cfg.Paths.ProjectRoot), "source")
 	if body, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(destination, "source.txt")); err != nil || string(body) != "from clone\n" {
 		t.Fatalf("cloned file = %q, %v\n%s", body, err, out.String())
 	}
 	if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(destination, "README.md")); err != nil {
 		t.Fatalf("explicit clone preset was not applied: %v\n%s", err, out.String())
 	}
 	if !strings.Contains(out.String(), "detected a clone reference") || !strings.Contains(out.String(), "setup        minimal") || !strings.Contains(out.String(), "cloned") {
 		t.Fatalf("wizard output:\n%s", out.String())
 	}
 }
```

```text
 # Changelog
 
 All notable changes to this project are documented in this file.
 
 The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/), and releases use [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).
 
 ## [Unreleased]
 
+### Added
+
+- Bare `dev repo clone` and the interactive `dev start` repository step now
+  offer a configurable line picker. Clone candidates come from the existing
+  private forge cache without an implicit network refresh; start candidates use
+  fast live discovery and are fully resolved after selection. `fzf` is the
+  default when installed, a built-in Bubble Tea selector is the automatic
+  fallback, manual entry and non-TTY behavior remain available, and optional
+  Television/fzf compositions over `dev repo remote --cached --json` ship under
+  `contrib/`.
+
 ## [0.2.5] - 2026-09-01
 
 ### Added
 
 - `dev repo context [repo]` now has an additive schema-v1 `--json` report and an
   explicit `--refresh` path. Local checkout, Git, task, worktree, and runtime facts
   stay live and network-free; optional forge and configured-fleet observations carry
   source, age, freshness, completeness, and collection errors. Remote endpoints are
   structurally sanitized before public output, and readiness remains split by scope
   instead of collapsing unknown evidence into a global safe value. `dev status`
   reuses the same cheap local readiness projection without network probes.
 - `dev fleet machine-id <host>` exposes the remote host's non-secret durable machine
   UUID and compares it with the optional `machine_id` pin in `remotes.toml`.
   `dev fleet files [repo-or-path] --to <host>` plans a one-way transfer of explicitly
   allowlisted ignored files and mutates only with `--apply`; both hosts must prove
```

```text
109			err = filepath.WalkDir(rootClean, func(path string, d fs.DirEntry, err error) error {

112				}
113				if ctx.Err() != nil {
114					return ctx.Err()
115				}
116				isRoot := path == rootClean
117				name := d.Name()
118				isLink := d.Type()&os.ModeSymlink != 0
119				isDir := d.IsDir()
```

```text
101	func (p *prompter) readLine(prefix string) (string, error) {
102		if terminalPair(p.input, p.out) {
103			return runLineEditor(p.input, p.out, prefix)
104		}
105	
106		fmt.Fprint(p.out, prefix)
107		line, err := p.in.ReadString('\n')

110		}

112	}

114	type fileDescriptor interface {
115		Fd() uintptr
116	}
117	
118	func terminalPair(input io.Reader, output io.Writer) bool {
119		in, inputOK := input.(fileDescriptor)
120		out, outputOK := output.(fileDescriptor)
121		return inputOK && outputOK && term.IsTerminal(in.Fd()) && term.IsTerminal(out.Fd())
122	}
123	
124	type lineEditorModel struct {
125		prefix   string
126		input    textinput.Model
127		done     bool
128		canceled bool
129	}
130	
131	func newLineEditorModel(prefix string) lineEditorModel {
132		input := textinput.New()
133		input.Prompt = prefix
134		input.Focus()
135		return lineEditorModel{prefix: prefix, input: input}
136	}
137	
138	func (m lineEditorModel) Init() tea.Cmd {
139		return textinput.Blink
140	}
141	
142	func (m lineEditorModel) Update(message tea.Msg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
143		if key, ok := message.(tea.KeyMsg); ok {
144			switch key.Type {
145			case tea.KeyEnter:
146				m.done = true
147				m.input.Blur()
148				return m, tea.Quit
149			case tea.KeyEsc, tea.KeyCtrlC:
150				m.done = true
151				m.canceled = true
152				m.input.Blur()
153				return m, tea.Quit
154			}
155		}
156	
157		var command tea.Cmd
158		m.input, command = m.input.Update(message)
159		return m, command
160	}
161	
162	func (m lineEditorModel) View() string {
163		if m.done {
164			// Leave the completed prompt in scrollback. Bubble Tea clears the line
165			// containing its cursor when the renderer stops, so the trailing newline
166			// moves that cursor below the submitted value first.
167			return m.prefix + m.input.Value() + "\n"
168		}
169		return m.input.View()
170	}
171	
172	func runLineEditor(input io.Reader, output io.Writer, prefix string) (string, error) {
173		final, err := tea.NewProgram(
174			newLineEditorModel(prefix),
175			tea.WithInput(input),
176			tea.WithOutput(output),
177		).Run()
178		if err != nil {
179			return "", fmt.Errorf("prompt editor: %w", err)
180		}
181		model, ok := final.(lineEditorModel)
182		if !ok {
183			return "", errors.New("prompt editor returned an unexpected model")
184		}
185		if model.canceled {
186			return "", errPromptCanceled
187		}
188		return model.input.Value(), nil
189	}
```

```text
74				}

81			if err != nil {

83			}
84			if value == current.Display() || value == current.Name || value == current.Path {
85				return current, nil

88			if err == nil {

90			}

92		}

97	func pickStartRepository(ctx context.Context, app *App, current repo.Repo) (repo.Repo, bool, error) {
98		discovered, err := repo.Discover(ctx, app.Cfg.DiscoveryRoots(), repo.CompletionOptions())
99		if err != nil && current.Path == "" {
100			return repo.Repo{}, false, err
101		}
102	
103		items := make([]picker.Item, 0, len(discovered)+2)
104		byPath := make(map[string]repo.Repo, len(discovered)+1)
105		seen := make(map[string]bool, len(discovered)+1)
106		add := func(repository repo.Repo) {
107			if repository.Path == "" || !repository.HasGit || repository.Bare {
108				return
109			}
110			identity := repository.RealPath
111			if identity == "" {
112				identity = repository.Path
113			}
114			identity = filepath.Clean(identity)
115			if seen[identity] {
116				return
117			}
118			seen[identity] = true
119			byPath[repository.Path] = repository
120			items = append(items, picker.Item{
121				Value:       repository.Path,
122				Label:       repository.Display(),
123				Description: config.Contract(repository.Path),
124			})
125		}
126		add(current)
127		for _, repository := range discovered {
128			add(repository)
129		}
130		if len(items) == 0 {
131			return repo.Repo{}, false, nil
132		}
133		items = append(items, picker.Item{
134			Value:       manualStartRepository,
135			Label:       "Enter a repository name or path manually…",
136			Description: "resolve a repository not present in the discovered list",
137		})
138	
139		result, used, err := app.pick(ctx, picker.Request{Prompt: "Repository", Items: items})
140		if err != nil {
141			return repo.Repo{}, false, err
142		}
143		if result.Canceled {
144			return repo.Repo{}, false, errPromptCanceled
145		}
146		if !used || !result.Selected || result.Item.Value == manualStartRepository {
147			return repo.Repo{}, false, nil
148		}
149		selected, ok := byPath[result.Item.Value]
150		if !ok {
151			return repo.Repo{}, false, fmt.Errorf("picker returned an unknown repository")
152		}
153		resolved, err := resolveStartRepository(ctx, app, selected.Path)
154		if err != nil {
155			return repo.Repo{}, false, err
156		}
157		return resolved, true, nil
158	}
```

```text
1	// Package repo discovers the repositories a user actually owns by walking the
2	// configured scan roots. It answers "what projects do I have?", which is a
3	// different question from "what am I working on?" — that one belongs to
4	// package task.
5	package repo
6	
7	import (
8		"context"
9		"io/fs"
10		"os"
11		"path/filepath"
12		"sort"
13		"strings"
14	
15		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/gitx"
16	)
17	
18	// Repo is one discovered repository.
19	type Repo struct {
20		// Name is the directory basename, which is how users refer to it.
21		Name string
22		// Path is the absolute path reached through the scan root. It may be a
23		// symlink from a bootstrap index; commands intentionally keep that human
24		// navigation path rather than replacing it with the physical one.
25		Path string
26		// RealPath is the physical checkout path.
27		RealPath string
28		// Symlink reports that Path is an alias to RealPath.
29		Symlink bool
30		// Root is the scan root it was found under.
31		Root string
32		// Category is the path between the scan root and the repo ("Quant",
33		// "Web/Frontend"), empty for a repo sitting directly in the root. It is
34		// human organisation metadata, preserved for `dev graduate` to place new
35		// projects consistently.
36		Category string
37		// GitDir is this checkout's administrative directory; CommonDir is shared
38		// by every linked worktree of the clone.
39		GitDir    string
40		CommonDir string
41		MainRoot  string
42		// Bare reports a bare repository (a worktree hub).
43		Bare bool
44		// HasGit distinguishes a real repo from a plain directory that was found
45		// in a scan root; non-repos are reported so `dev repo list` can offer to
46		// initialise them.
47		HasGit bool
48	}
49	
50	// Display renders "Category/Name" or just "Name".
51	func (r Repo) Display() string {
52		if r.Category == "" {
53			return r.Name
54		}
55		return r.Category + "/" + r.Name
56	}
57	
58	// Options tunes discovery.
59	type Options struct {
60		// MaxDepth limits how deep below a scan root a repo may be found. The
61		// default layout is <root>/<Category>/<Repo>, so 2 suffices; 3 leaves room
62		// for a nested grouping without walking an entire home directory.
63		MaxDepth int
64		// IncludeNonRepos reports plain directories alongside repositories.
65		IncludeNonRepos bool
66		// Fast avoids per-repository git subprocesses. It is intended for shell
67		// completion: direct .git-file checkouts are skipped as linked worktrees and
68		// symlink aliases are deduplicated by their physical path.
69		Fast bool
70	}
71	
72	// DefaultOptions is the discovery configuration used by dev's commands.
73	func DefaultOptions() Options { return Options{MaxDepth: 3} }
74	
75	// CompletionOptions trades full Git metadata for interactive latency.
76	func CompletionOptions() Options { return Options{MaxDepth: 3, Fast: true} }
77	
78	// skipDirs are never descended into. These are large, never contain a project
79	// the user organises by hand, and walking them dominates scan time.
80	var skipDirs = map[string]bool{
81		"node_modules": true, ".venv": true, "venv": true, "target": true,
82		"vendor": true, "__pycache__": true, ".tox": true, "dist": true,
83		"build": true, ".next": true, ".cache": true, ".terraform": true,
84		"Library": true, ".Trash": true,
85	}
86	
87	// Discover walks every root and returns the repositories found, sorted by
88	// display name. Unreadable directories are skipped rather than fatal — a scan
89	// root that has been unmounted must not break `dev ls`.
90	func Discover(ctx context.Context, roots []string, opts Options) ([]Repo, error) {
91		if opts.MaxDepth <= 0 {
92			opts.MaxDepth = DefaultOptions().MaxDepth
93		}
94		seen := map[string]bool{}
95		// clone identities stop a physical path and a symlink index from showing
96		// the same repository twice. The first scan root wins, which lets users
97		// choose whether the curated index or the physical hierarchy is their UI
98		// simply by ordering scan_roots.
99		identities := map[string]bool{}
100		var out []Repo
101	
102		for _, root := range roots {
103			info, err := os.Stat(root)
104			if err != nil || !info.IsDir() {
105				continue // a missing scan root is normal on a fresh machine
106			}
107			rootClean := filepath.Clean(root)
108	
109			err = filepath.WalkDir(rootClean, func(path string, d fs.DirEntry, err error) error {
110				if err != nil {
111					return nil // unreadable entry: skip, keep walking
112				}
113				if ctx.Err() != nil {
114					return ctx.Err()
115				}
116				isRoot := path == rootClean
117				name := d.Name()
118				isLink := d.Type()&os.ModeSymlink != 0
119				isDir := d.IsDir()
120				if isLink {
121					// WalkDir does not follow symlinks. Inspect a direct symlink to
122					// a repository, but do not recurse through arbitrary symlinked
123					// containers — bootstrap does that with cycle detection.
124					if info, err := os.Stat(path); err == nil {
125						isDir = info.IsDir()
126					}
127				}
128				if !isDir {
129					return nil
130				}
131				if !isRoot && (skipDirs[name] || (strings.HasPrefix(name, ".") && name != ".bare")) {
132					return filepath.SkipDir
133				}
134	
135				rel := "."
136				depth := 0
137				if !isRoot {
138					rel, _ = filepath.Rel(rootClean, path)
139					depth = len(strings.Split(rel, string(filepath.Separator)))
140				}
141	
142				if isRepoDir(path) {
143					real, _ := filepath.EvalSymlinks(path)
144					if real == "" {
145						real = path
146					}
147					bare := isBareDir(path)
148					identity, gitDir, commonDir, mainRoot := real, real, real, real
149					if !bare && opts.Fast && gitEntryIsFile(path) {
150						// A direct .git file at a discovered root is a linked
151						// worktree. Submodules are already hidden below their parent
152						// repository because discovery never descends into one.
153						return filepath.SkipDir
154					}
155					if !bare && !opts.Fast {
156						if g, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, path); err == nil {
157							// A linked worktree is execution state, not another
158							// project in the repo inventory.
159							if g.IsLinkedWorktree {
160								return filepath.SkipDir
161							}
162							identity, gitDir, commonDir, mainRoot = g.GitCommonDir, g.GitDir, g.GitCommonDir, g.MainRoot
163							real = g.MainRoot
164						}
165					}
166					if !seen[path] && !identities[identity] {
167						seen[path], identities[identity] = true, true
168						out = append(out, Repo{
169							Name:      name,
170							Path:      path,
171							RealPath:  real,
172							Symlink:   isLink,
173							Root:      rootClean,
174							Category:  filepath.ToSlash(filepath.Dir(rel)),
175							GitDir:    gitDir,
176							CommonDir: commonDir,
177							MainRoot:  mainRoot,
178							Bare:      bare,
179							HasGit:    true,
180						})
181					}
182					// Never descend into a repo: its subdirectories are source
183					// code, and any nested .git is a submodule or a worktree that
184					// belongs to this repo, not a project of its own.
185					return filepath.SkipDir
186				}
187				if depth >= opts.MaxDepth {
188					return filepath.SkipDir
189				}
190				if opts.IncludeNonRepos && depth == 1 {
191					if !seen[path] {
192						seen[path] = true
193						out = append(out, Repo{Name: name, Path: path, Root: rootClean, Category: ""})
194					}
195				}
196				return nil
197			})
198			if err != nil && ctx.Err() != nil {
199				return out, ctx.Err()
200			}
201		}
202	
203		for i := range out {
204			if out[i].Category == "." {
205				out[i].Category = ""
206			}
207		}
208		sort.Slice(out, func(i, j int) bool {
209			if out[i].Name != out[j].Name {
210				return strings.ToLower(out[i].Name) < strings.ToLower(out[j].Name)
211			}
212			return out[i].Path < out[j].Path
213		})
214		return out, nil
215	}
216	
217	// isRepoDir reports whether path is a repository root: it holds a .git entry
218	// (directory for a normal clone, file for a linked worktree or submodule).
219	func isRepoDir(path string) bool {
220		if _, err := os.Lstat(filepath.Join(path, ".git")); err == nil {
221			return true
222		}
223		return isBareDir(path)
224	}
225	
226	func gitEntryIsFile(path string) bool {
227		info, err := os.Lstat(filepath.Join(path, ".git"))
228		return err == nil && info.Mode().IsRegular()
229	}
230	
231	// isBareDir recognises a bare repository by its skeleton, without shelling out.
232	func isBareDir(path string) bool {
233		for _, marker := range []string{"HEAD", "objects", "refs"} {
234			if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(path, marker)); err != nil {
235				return false
236			}
237		}
238		return true
239	}
240	
241	// Resolve finds a repo by name, display name, or path.
242	//
243	// Matching is deliberately layered: an exact name or path wins outright, and
244	// only then does a substring search run — so a repo literally named "web"
245	// is never shadowed by "web-frontend".
246	func Resolve(ctx context.Context, roots []string, ref string) (Repo, []Repo, error) {
247		return resolve(ctx, roots, ref, DefaultOptions())
248	}
249	
250	// ResolveCompletion resolves the same references without launching one Git
251	// process per repository in the scan roots.
252	func ResolveCompletion(ctx context.Context, roots []string, ref string) (Repo, []Repo, error) {
253		return resolve(ctx, roots, ref, CompletionOptions())
254	}
255	
256	func resolve(ctx context.Context, roots []string, ref string, opts Options) (Repo, []Repo, error) {
257		all, err := Discover(ctx, roots, opts)
258		if err != nil {
259			return Repo{}, nil, err
260		}
261		if abs, err := filepath.Abs(ref); err == nil {
262			if g, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, abs); err == nil {
263				real, _ := filepath.EvalSymlinks(abs)
264				if real == "" {
265					real = g.MainRoot
266				}
267				// Preserve an explicit navigation alias. The caller named this
268				// path on purpose; resolving it to the physical checkout would
269				// defeat a bootstrap symlink catalog.
270				return Repo{
271					Name: filepath.Base(abs), Path: abs, RealPath: real,
272					Symlink: real != abs, CommonDir: g.GitCommonDir, HasGit: true, Bare: g.Bare,
273				}, nil, nil
274			}
275		}
276		for _, r := range all {
277			if r.Name == ref || r.Display() == ref || r.Path == ref {
278				return r, nil, nil
279			}
280		}
281		needle := strings.ToLower(ref)
282		var hits []Repo
283		for _, r := range all {
284			if strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(r.Display()), needle) {
285				hits = append(hits, r)
286			}
287		}
288		switch len(hits) {
289		case 1:
290			return hits[0], nil, nil
291		case 0:
292			return Repo{}, nil, &NotFoundError{Ref: ref}
293		default:
294			return Repo{}, hits, &AmbiguousError{Ref: ref, Candidates: hits}
295		}
296	}
297	
298	// NotFoundError reports a repo reference that matched nothing.
299	type NotFoundError struct{ Ref string }
300	
301	func (e *NotFoundError) Error() string { return "no repository matching " + e.Ref }
302	
303	// AmbiguousError reports a repo reference that matched several repos.
304	type AmbiguousError struct {
305		Ref        string
306		Candidates []Repo
307	}
308	
309	func (e *AmbiguousError) Error() string {
310		names := make([]string, len(e.Candidates))
311		for i, c := range e.Candidates {
312			names[i] = c.Display()
313		}
314		return e.Ref + " is ambiguous: " + strings.Join(names, ", ")
315	}
316
```

```text
17	// Cache is the on-disk forge inventory. It exists for UI latency, not as a
18	// source of truth: the REMOTE tab should open instantly, and r refreshes it.
19	type Cache struct {
20		Version   int                     `json:"version,omitempty"`
21		SourceID  string                  `json:"source_id,omitempty"`
22		FetchedAt time.Time               `json:"fetched_at"`
23		Complete  bool                    `json:"complete,omitempty"`
24		Providers map[Kind]ProviderStatus `json:"providers,omitempty"`
25		Repos     []RemoteRepo            `json:"repos"`
26	}
27	
28	const (
29		CacheVersion      = 2
30		maxCacheBytes     = 32 << 20
31		maxCachedRepos    = 100_000
32		maxCacheClockSkew = 5 * time.Minute
33	)
34	
35	var cacheWriteLocks sync.Map
36	
37	type ProviderStatus struct {
38		FetchedAt time.Time `json:"fetched_at,omitempty"`
39		Complete  bool      `json:"complete"`
40		Error     string    `json:"error,omitempty"`
41	}
42	
43	// LoadCache returns only a fresh, complete cache. TUI callers that can label
44	// stale rows while refreshing use LoadCacheAny instead.
45	func LoadCache(path string, maxAge time.Duration) (Cache, bool) {
46		c, ok := LoadCacheAny(path)
47		if !ok || !c.Fresh(maxAge) {
48			return Cache{}, false
49		}
50		return c, true
51	}
52	
53	// LoadCacheAny returns a cache regardless of age or completeness. This powers
54	// stale-while-revalidate UI behavior; callers must inspect Fresh/Complete.
55	func LoadCacheAny(path string) (Cache, bool) {
56		info, err := os.Stat(path)
57		if err != nil || info.Size() < 0 || info.Size() > maxCacheBytes {
58			return Cache{}, false
59		}
60		b, err := os.ReadFile(path)
61		if err != nil {
62			return Cache{}, false
63		}
64		var c Cache
65		if json.Unmarshal(b, &c) != nil || !validCache(c, time.Now().UTC()) {
66			return Cache{}, false
67		}
68		if c.Version == 0 {
69			// Version 1 caches were valid snapshots but capped per provider, so they
70			// are useful for instant display and must immediately be refreshed.
71			c.Complete = false
72		}
73		return c, true
74	}
75	
76	func validCache(c Cache, now time.Time) bool {
77		if (c.Version != 0 && c.Version != CacheVersion) || c.FetchedAt.IsZero() ||
78			c.FetchedAt.After(now.Add(maxCacheClockSkew)) || len(c.Repos) > maxCachedRepos ||
79			!validCacheString(c.SourceID, 128, false) {
80			return false
81		}
82		for kind, status := range c.Providers {
83			if !validForgeKind(kind) || len(status.Error) > 16<<10 || strings.ContainsRune(status.Error, '\x00') ||
84				status.FetchedAt.After(now.Add(maxCacheClockSkew)) {
85				return false
86			}
87		}
88		for _, repository := range c.Repos {
89			if !validForgeKind(repository.Forge) || pathx.ValidateComponent(repository.Name) != nil ||
90				!validCacheString(repository.FullName, 2048, true) ||
91				!validCacheString(repository.Description, 64<<10, false) ||
92				!validCacheString(repository.URL, 8<<10, false) ||
93				!validCacheString(repository.CloneURL, 8<<10, false) ||
94				!validCacheString(repository.SSHURL, 8<<10, false) ||
95				!validCacheString(repository.Visibility, 128, false) ||
96				!validCacheString(repository.DefaultBranch, 1024, false) ||
97				repository.UpdatedAt.After(now.Add(maxCacheClockSkew)) {
98				return false
99			}
100		}
101		return true
102	}
103	
104	func validForgeKind(kind Kind) bool {
105		return kind == GitHub || kind == GitLab || kind == AzureDevOps
106	}
107	
108	func validCacheString(value string, limit int, required bool) bool {
109		return (!required || strings.TrimSpace(value) != "") && len(value) <= limit && !strings.ContainsRune(value, '\x00')
110	}
111	
112	// FreshFor additionally requires the cache to describe the same configured
113	// provider endpoints/targets. Caches without a source ID remain displayable but
114	// are immediately revalidated.
115	func (c Cache) FreshFor(maxAge time.Duration, sourceID string) bool {
116		return sourceID != "" && c.SourceID == sourceID && c.Fresh(maxAge)
117	}
118	
119	func (c Cache) Fresh(maxAge time.Duration) bool {
120		if c.Version != CacheVersion || !c.Complete {
121			return false
122		}
123		if maxAge <= 0 {
124			return true
125		}
126		if len(c.Providers) == 0 {
127			return time.Since(c.FetchedAt) <= maxAge
128		}
129		for _, provider := range c.Providers {
130			if !provider.Complete || provider.Error != "" || provider.FetchedAt.IsZero() || time.Since(provider.FetchedAt) > maxAge {
131				return false
132			}
133		}
134		return true
135	}
136	
137	// SaveCache atomically replaces the cache. A partial forge response may be
138	// cached — its FetchedAt still says exactly when it was observed.
139	func SaveCache(path string, repos []RemoteRepo) error {
140		now := time.Now().UTC()
141		providers := map[Kind]ProviderStatus{}
142		for _, repo := range repos {
143			providers[repo.Forge] = ProviderStatus{FetchedAt: now, Complete: true}
144		}
145		return SaveCacheState(path, Cache{Version: CacheVersion, FetchedAt: now, Complete: true, Providers: providers, Repos: repos})
146	}
147	
148	// SaveCacheState atomically replaces the versioned inventory cache.
149	func SaveCacheState(path string, cache Cache) error {
150		return SaveCacheStateContext(context.Background(), path, cache)
151	}
152	
153	// SaveCacheStateContext serializes one cache target and checks cancellation
154	// while holding that ordering boundary. A superseded generation therefore
155	// cannot rename after a newer generation has committed.
156	func SaveCacheStateContext(ctx context.Context, path string, cache Cache) error {
157		if path == "" {
158			return errors.New("empty cache path")
159		}
160		if ctx == nil {
161			ctx = context.Background()
162		}
163		lock := cacheWriteLock(path)
164		lock.Lock()
165		defer lock.Unlock()
166		if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
167			return err
168		}
169		if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(path), 0o755); err != nil {
170			return err
171		}
172		if cache.Version == 0 {
173			cache.Version = CacheVersion
174		}
175		if cache.FetchedAt.IsZero() {
176			cache.FetchedAt = time.Now().UTC()
177		}
178		b, err := json.MarshalIndent(cache, "", "  ")
179		if err != nil {
180			return err
181		}
182		b = append(b, '\n')
183		tmp, err := os.CreateTemp(filepath.Dir(path), ".remotes-*.tmp")
184		if err != nil {
185			return err
186		}
187		name := tmp.Name()
188		defer os.Remove(name)
189		if _, err := tmp.Write(b); err != nil {
190			tmp.Close()
191			return err
192		}
193		if err := tmp.Close(); err != nil {
194			return err
195		}
196		if err := os.Chmod(name, 0o600); err != nil {
197			return err
198		}
199		if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
200			return err
201		}
202		return os.Rename(name, path)
203	}
204	
205	func cacheWriteLock(path string) *sync.Mutex {
206		loaded, _ := cacheWriteLocks.LoadOrStore(filepath.Clean(path), &sync.Mutex{})
207		return loaded.(*sync.Mutex)
208	}
209	
210	// CacheExists reports whether any cache file exists, even stale. Used only for
211	// diagnostics.
212	func CacheExists(path string) bool {
213		_, err := os.Stat(path)
214		return err == nil || !errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist)
215	}
```

```text
14	
15	var errPromptCanceled = errors.New("prompt canceled")
16	
17	type prompter struct {
18		input io.Reader
19		in    *bufio.Reader
20		out   io.Writer
21		style cliStyle
22	}
23	
24	func newPrompter(app *App) *prompter {
25		return &prompter{
26			input: app.In,
27			in:    bufio.NewReader(app.In),
28			out:   app.Out,
29			style: app.outStyle(),
30		}
31	}
32	
33	func (p *prompter) line(label, fallback string) (string, error) {
34		return p.lineWithDisplayFallback(label, fallback, fallback)
35	}
36	
37	func (p *prompter) lineWithDisplayFallback(label, fallback, displayFallback string) (string, error) {
38		prefix := fmt.Sprintf("%s %s: ", p.style.prompt("?"), p.style.prompt(label))
39		if displayFallback != "" {
40			prefix = fmt.Sprintf("%s %s %s: ", p.style.prompt("?"), p.style.prompt(label), p.style.dim("["+displayFallback+"]"))
41		}
42		value, err := p.readLine(prefix)
43		if err != nil {
44			return "", err
45		}
46		value = strings.TrimSpace(value)
47		if value == "" {
48			value = fallback
49		}
50		return value, nil
51	}
52	
53	func (p *prompter) dangerLine(label string) (string, error) {
54		prefix := fmt.Sprintf("%s %s: ", p.style.danger("?"), p.style.danger(label))
55		line, err := p.readLine(prefix)
56		if err != nil {
57			return "", err
58		}
59		return strings.TrimSpace(line), nil
60	}
61	
62	func (p *prompter) choice(label, fallback, hint string, choices map[string]string) (string, error) {
63		for {
64			value, err := p.line(label, fallback)
65			if err != nil {
66				return "", err
67			}
68			value = strings.ToLower(value)
69			if resolved, ok := choices[value]; ok {
70				return resolved, nil
71			}
72			fmt.Fprintf(p.out, "  %s\n", p.style.warning("enter one of: "+hint))
73		}
74	}
75	
76	func (p *prompter) confirm(label string, defaultYes bool) (bool, error) {
77		fallback := "y/N"
78		if defaultYes {
79			fallback = "Y/n"
80		}
81		for {
82			prefix := fmt.Sprintf("%s %s %s: ", p.style.prompt("?"), p.style.prompt(label), p.style.dim("["+fallback+"]"))
83			line, err := p.readLine(prefix)
84			if err != nil {
85				return false, err
86			}
87			value := strings.TrimSpace(line)
88			switch strings.ToLower(value) {
89			case "y", "yes":
90				return true, nil
91			case "n", "no":
92				return false, nil
93			case "":
94				return defaultYes, nil
95			default:
96				fmt.Fprintln(p.out, "  "+p.style.warning("enter y or n"))
97			}
98		}
99	}
100	
101	func (p *prompter) readLine(prefix string) (string, error) {
102		if terminalPair(p.input, p.out) {
103			return runLineEditor(p.input, p.out, prefix)
104		}
105	
106		fmt.Fprint(p.out, prefix)
107		line, err := p.in.ReadString('\n')
108		if err != nil {
109			return "", errPromptCanceled
110		}
111		return line, nil
112	}
113	
114	type fileDescriptor interface {
115		Fd() uintptr
116	}
117	
118	func terminalPair(input io.Reader, output io.Writer) bool {
119		in, inputOK := input.(fileDescriptor)
120		out, outputOK := output.(fileDescriptor)
121		return inputOK && outputOK && term.IsTerminal(in.Fd()) && term.IsTerminal(out.Fd())
122	}
123	
124	type lineEditorModel struct {
125		prefix   string
126		input    textinput.Model
127		done     bool
128		canceled bool
129	}
130	
131	func newLineEditorModel(prefix string) lineEditorModel {
132		input := textinput.New()
133		input.Prompt = prefix
134		input.Focus()
135		return lineEditorModel{prefix: prefix, input: input}
136	}
137	
138	func (m lineEditorModel) Init() tea.Cmd {
139		return textinput.Blink
140	}
141	
142	func (m lineEditorModel) Update(message tea.Msg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
143		if key, ok := message.(tea.KeyMsg); ok {
144			switch key.Type {
145			case tea.KeyEnter:
146				m.done = true
147				m.input.Blur()
148				return m, tea.Quit
149			case tea.KeyEsc, tea.KeyCtrlC:
150				m.done = true
151				m.canceled = true
152				m.input.Blur()
153				return m, tea.Quit
154			}
155		}
156	
157		var command tea.Cmd
158		m.input, command = m.input.Update(message)
159		return m, command
160	}
161	
162	func (m lineEditorModel) View() string {
163		if m.done {
164			// Leave the completed prompt in scrollback. Bubble Tea clears the line
165			// containing its cursor when the renderer stops, so the trailing newline
166			// moves that cursor below the submitted value first.
167			return m.prefix + m.input.Value() + "\n"
168		}
169		return m.input.View()
170	}
171	
172	func runLineEditor(input io.Reader, output io.Writer, prefix string) (string, error) {
173		final, err := tea.NewProgram(
174			newLineEditorModel(prefix),
175			tea.WithInput(input),
176			tea.WithOutput(output),
177		).Run()
178		if err != nil {
179			return "", fmt.Errorf("prompt editor: %w", err)
180		}
181		model, ok := final.(lineEditorModel)
182		if !ok {
183			return "", errors.New("prompt editor returned an unexpected model")
184		}
185		if model.canceled {
186			return "", errPromptCanceled
187		}
188		return model.input.Value(), nil
189	}
```

```text
1	# Context
2	
3	`dev` already has robust domain-owned caches (forge remotes, fleet snapshots, disk sizes, note FTS, templates), but it has no generic cache of selectable CLI values and no picker integration. Repository discovery/inventory remains deliberately live. The first useful integration is therefore narrow: reuse the existing forge cache to choose a remote for `dev repo clone`, use fast live discovery to choose a local repository in the `dev start` wizard, and expose the existing `dev repo remote --json` contract to Television/fzf recipes. This removes repetitive path/name typing without making fzf mandatory, changing scripted behavior, or adding a second inventory/cache.
4	
5	The user selected an internal configurable picker plus composable external recipes, with a built-in Bubble Tea fallback. This slice intentionally does not add pickers to `dev done` (which already has task completion) or to every finite-choice command.
6	
7	## 1. Add a reusable, safe selector primitive
8	
9	- Add `internal/textmatch` with an exported term matcher equivalent to the current `internal/tui/rows.go:matches`: trim/lowercase, split whitespace, require every term as a substring. Have the TUI delegate to it so the built-in picker and `/` keep one tested matching contract; do not introduce a fuzzy-scoring dependency.
10	- Add `internal/picker` with small caller-neutral types such as:
11	  - `Item { Value, Label, Description string }`
12	  - `Request { Prompt, InitialQuery string; Items []Item }`
13	  - `Result { Item Item; Selected, Canceled bool }`
14	  - a selector object constructed with input/output/error streams and configured external argv, exposing `Select(context.Context, Request) (Result, error)`.
15	- Keep backend selection internal: use the configured external executable when `exec.LookPath` succeeds, otherwise use the built-in Bubble Tea backend. An explicitly empty argv forces the built-in backend. A configured executable that starts and then fails is an error rather than silently replaying the interaction in a second UI.
16	- Execute external argv directly with `exec.CommandContext`, never via a shell. Feed normalized, uniquely rendered candidate lines on child stdin, capture only the selected line from stdout, and leave stderr attached to the caller terminal for fzf-style UI. Map the exact returned line back to the source `Item`; decorate otherwise-identical rendered lines with a deterministic ordinal so duplicate labels/descriptions cannot select the wrong value. Reject unexpected/multiple output instead of guessing. Treat exit codes 1 and 130 as cancellation, propagate context cancellation, and report other exits.
17	- Support a literal `{prompt}` substitution in argv elements so the per-call label can reach fzf without shell interpolation. Newlines/NULs in item display fields are normalized before rendering; the opaque `Value` is never rendered or trusted back from the child.
18	- Implement the fallback as a compact Bubble Tea list with `bubbles/textinput`: live term filtering, up/down plus Ctrl-N/Ctrl-P, Enter to select, Esc/Ctrl-C to cancel, and a bounded viewport. Test the model directly rather than requiring a real terminal.
19	- Add an `App` adapter/test seam in `internal/cli` that passes `App.In/Out/Err` and `App.Cfg.Picker` into `internal/picker`. It should only open a picker when input and output are a terminal pair; non-TTY readers keep the existing deterministic line prompts.
20	
21	Critical files: `internal/picker/*.go`, `internal/textmatch/*.go`, `internal/tui/rows.go`, `internal/cli/app.go`, and a small `internal/cli/picker.go` adapter.
22	
23	## 2. Add minimal global picker configuration
24	
25	- Extend `internal/config/config.go` with `Config.Picker` and a global-only `[picker]` section containing one `command []string` argv vector. Default it to fzf with conservative presentation args and `{prompt}` (for example `fzf`, reverse layout, bounded height/border, and a prompt). `command = []` is the documented way to force the built-in picker.
26	- Keeping executable and arguments in one replacement-valued slice avoids a partial TOML overlay accidentally retaining fzf arguments when the executable is changed to `tv`, `sk`, or `gum`.
27	- Validation permits an empty vector, but rejects an empty first element and NUL/newline-bearing argv elements. It does not require the binary to be installed: absence is a supported fallback state.
28	- Add the annotated section to `internal/cli/config.go`'s starter config. `dev config show` will include it automatically. Keep picker policy out of repo-owned `.dev-cli/config.toml`.
29	- Extend `dev doctor` to identify the configured external selector as optional and state that the built-in picker will be used when it is unavailable; do not install anything.
30	
31	Critical files: `internal/config/config.go`, `internal/config/config_test.go`, `internal/cli/config.go`, `internal/cli/doctor.go` and focused CLI tests.
32	
33	## 3. Wire only the two approved interactive entry points
34	
35	### `dev repo clone`
36	
37	- In `internal/cli/repo_create_wizard.go:runRepoCloneWizard`, before the existing free-form source prompt, read the raw forge cache through `cachedRemoteRows(app)` / `forge.LoadCacheAny`. This is disk-only and must not trigger provider network calls or the expensive `matchRemoteLocals` repository scan.
38	- Build candidates from cache rows with non-empty `CloneURL`, displaying forge-qualified full name plus visibility/archived/description metadata. Preserve cache ordering (or the existing deterministic updated/name ordering). Use `RemoteRepo.CloneURL` as `Item.Value`, not `FullName`, so GitHub, GitLab (including self-hosted), and Azure DevOps keep the exact provider URL.
39	- Append a synthetic “Enter a URL, path, or owner/name…” item. Selecting it, having no usable cache/candidates, or running through non-TTY input goes through the current `prompter.line` path unchanged. A stale but source-compatible cache remains useful and is visibly warned as stale; a missing/source-mismatched cache simply falls back to manual entry. Never refresh the network merely to open the picker.
40	- Picker cancellation returns `errPromptCanceled`, preserving the command’s existing “Canceled; nothing was cloned” behavior. Explicit positional refs and non-interactive/`--json` behavior bypass the picker exactly as today.
41	- Do not add a costly local scan merely to badge/exclude already-cloned remotes. Existing destination/nested-repository checks remain authoritative and prevent unsafe duplicate acquisition.
42	
43	### `dev start`
44	
45	- Replace `internal/cli/start_wizard.go:promptStartRepository`’s numbered listing with the shared picker.
46	- Obtain candidates with `repo.Discover(..., repo.CompletionOptions())`, filter to non-bare Git repositories, and render `Repo.Display()` plus `config.Contract(Repo.Path)`. Put the current repository first when it resolves, while retaining a synthetic manual/name/path item for values not discovered under configured roots.
47	- Return the selected repo directly; the manual path continues through `repo.Resolve`. Preserve explicit `dev start <repo>`, non-TTY prompts, empty-inventory errors, and cancellation before any mutation.
48	
49	Tests should inject selector results through the `App` seam, so command/wizard tests do not depend on fzf, PTYs, or a developer’s PATH.
50	
51	## 4. Ship composable Television/fzf usage without another command
52	
53	- Do not add `dev pick`: `dev repo remote --cached --json` already supplies the cache-backed, pipe-friendly candidate contract, while `--refresh` explicitly populates it. Reusing this command avoids duplicate filtering, freshness, JSON, and cache semantics.
54	- Add `contrib/television/dev-remote-repos.toml`. Its source invokes `dev repo remote --cached --json` and `jq` to emit TSV containing exact `repo.clone_url`, display/full name, forge, visibility, local path, and description. Enter outputs the exact clone URL; an action can run `dev repo clone` on it. Metadata declares `dev` and `jq` requirements. The repository only ships the file; it does not modify the user’s Television/chezmoi configuration.
55	- Document both compositions near repository bootstrap:
56	  - initialize/refresh once with `dev repo remote --refresh`;
57	  - copy or symlink the channel and use `dev repo clone "$(tv dev-remote-repos)"`;
58	  - provide an fzf shell function that transforms the same JSON with `jq`, displays descriptive columns, extracts the exact clone URL, handles cancellation/empty output, and invokes `dev repo clone`.
59	- Explain that the internal no-argument clone picker needs neither `tv` nor `jq`, uses no network, and falls back to the built-in UI when its configured external command is absent.
60	
61	## 5. Record intentionally deferred picker surfaces
62	
63	Replace the completed `TODO.md` “Television / fzf channel” item with a scoped backlog item for extending the shared selector only where it improves over completion. List:
64	
65	- `tries *`, `graduate`, note show/edit/delete, fleet open/host, artifact discard, and skill update;
66	- interactive disambiguation for structured repo/experiment/catalog ambiguity errors;
67	- branch/base selection after adding one canonical `gitx` branch enumerator;
68	- larger enum sets currently handled by `prompter.choice`.
69	
70	Explicitly note that task lifecycle commands such as `dev done` already expose shell completion and should not automatically gain a picker merely because the primitive exists.
71	
72	## 6. Keep product surfaces synchronized
73	
74	- Add the user-visible feature to `[Unreleased]` in `CHANGELOG.md`.
75	- Update `README.md`, `docs/reference/commands-config.md` and its zh-TW pair for `[picker]`, and `docs/reference/compatibility.md` plus zh-TW for external-missing/built-in fallback and non-TTY behavior.
76	- Update the English/zh-TW repository/TUI workflow guide where clone and external-tool composition are described (principally `docs/guides/tui-repos-bootstrap*.md`).
77	- Update `internal/skill/dev-cli/SKILL.md` and `internal/skill/dev-cli/references/repository-bootstrap.md` with picker/cache/manual-fallback semantics. The Cobra syntax need not change, but run `make skill-sync` and inspect the generated command reference because help text may be clarified.
78	- Regenerate `docs/llms*.txt` only if the source check reports drift, per repository guidance.
79	
80	## 7. Verification
81	
82	1. Unit tests:
83	   - `go test ./internal/textmatch ./internal/picker ./internal/config`
84	   - picker duplicate mapping, filtering/navigation/cancel, unavailable executable fallback, context cancellation, exit 1/130 cancellation, malformed child output, and non-zero failure. Use a Go helper-process invocation of the current test binary rather than platform-specific shell scripts.
85	2. Focused CLI tests:
86	   - cached clone selection returns the exact `CloneURL` without a provider call;
87	   - stale/no/source-mismatched cache and manual-item fallback;
88	   - picker cancellation performs no clone;
89	   - explicit/non-interactive/JSON clone paths remain unchanged;
90	   - start selects current/other/manual repos and fast discovery excludes bare/linked worktrees.
91	3. Repository gates: `make skill-sync`, inspect its diff, `make skill-check`, format-preserving check (`files="$(gofmt -l .)" && test -z "$files"`), `make vet`, `go test -race ./...`, and `make build` (or `make all` plus race test).
92	4. Documentation gates: `uv sync --frozen --extra docs`, source check, `mkdocs build --strict`, and site check; regenerate llms files only when instructed by the checker.
93	5. Manual smoke test with an existing remote cache: run no-arg `dev repo clone`, verify configured fzf and forced built-in modes show the same candidates, select manual entry, and cancel before confirmation; run `dev start`, switch repository, and cancel before creation. 181	Structured filters include `scope:`, `agent:`, and `update:`.
```
182	
183	## External tools
184	
185	```bash
186	dev tui tools
187	```
188	
189	Configured tools run through `$SHELL` in the selected checkout while the alternate screen is suspended. `interactive = true` uses `$SHELL -lic` so local aliases/functions can resolve; use a real executable on `PATH` when the binding must be portable. Availability probes run in a bounded background load after the first view; rendering never starts a login shell, and unresolved bindings fail closed.
190	
191	```toml
192	[[tui.tools]]
193	key = "L"
194	name = "lazygit"
195	run = "lazygit"
196	```
197	
198	Keys are case-sensitive and cannot shadow dashboard-owned bindings. Returning from an editor can reload most config; switching runtime backend requires restarting the TUI.
199	
200	## Inventory an existing machine
201	
202	Start with a report:
203	
204	```bash
205	dev bootstrap ~/code /mnt/work
206	dev bootstrap ~/code --json
207	```
208	
209	The scanner identifies canonical checkouts, linked worktrees, bare repositories, and symlink aliases, then deduplicates them by Git identity.
210	
211	The recommended organization layer is a non-destructive symlink index:
212	
213	```bash
214	dev bootstrap ~/code --index ~/Projects --layout flat
215	dev bootstrap ~/code --index ~/Projects --layout flat --apply
216	```
217	
218	Physical moves are a separate, stricter mode. A move plan blocks dirty repositories, linked worktrees, live sessions/current working directories, aliases that would break, occupied destinations, and cross-filesystem renames. If any row is blocked, apply moves none.
219	
220	## Adopt work already in flight
221	
222	Bootstrap answers **where repositories are**. Adoption answers **which existing branches, worktrees, and sessions are active work**:
223	
224	```bash
225	dev adopt
226	dev adopt --apply
227	```
228	
229	Adopt reports by default and only writes task entries after `--apply` plus confirmation. It does not move, rename, or delete checkouts, and it excludes recognized harness-ephemeral worktrees.
230

110	
111	For a non-Homebrew install, generate completion files wherever your shell loads
112	them:
113	
114	```bash
115	mkdir -p ~/.zfunc ~/.local/share/bash-completion/completions ~/.config/fish/completions
116	dev completion zsh  > ~/.zfunc/_dev
117	dev completion bash > ~/.local/share/bash-completion/completions/dev
118	dev completion fish > ~/.config/fish/completions/dev.fish
119	```
120	
121	Tab completion includes commands and flags plus local tasks, repositories,
122	worktrees, help topics and bundled gitignore templates. Completion never queries
123	a forge or the network.
124	
125	Add the directory-changing wrapper to your shell rc file:
126	
127	```bash
128	eval "$(dev shell-init zsh)"      # zsh
129	eval "$(dev shell-init bash)"     # bash
130	dev shell-init fish | source      # fish
131	```
132	
133	```powershell
134	Invoke-Expression (& dev shell-init powershell | Out-String)   # PowerShell
135	```
136	
137	A child process cannot change its parent's working directory, so the wrapper
138	passes directory changes back through a private, child-only file descriptor
139	while leaving normal stdout/stderr connected to the terminal. That preserves
140	the interactive TUI and normal pipe behavior.
141	
142	The agent skill is an explicit, optional post-install step:
143	
144	```bash
145	dev skill install
146	dev skill list    # project + global skills, agents and sources
147	dev doctor       # what works on this machine, and what degrades
148	```
149	
150	Only **git** is required at runtime. `herdr`, `tmux`, `zellij`, `gh`, `glab` and
151	Azure CLI each enable more and degrade cleanly when absent.
152	
153	## Create, clone, or set up a repository
154	
155	Repository bootstrap works from any directory. Bare `dev repo new` opens an
156	interactive flow that chooses the destination under the configured
157	`project_root`, previews the setup, and confirms before writing anything:
158	
159	```bash
160	dev repo new                                  # interactive new-repository flow
161	dev repo create api --preset agent-ready      # `create` is an alias for `new`
162	dev repo new owner/api                        # clear clone reference: preserve history/origin
163	dev repo new api --template owner/starters --template-subdir go/service
164	dev repo new api --check-in stage -m "chore: initialize api"
165	dev repo clone owner/api                      # owner/name or a Git URL
166	dev repo setup . --preset agent-ready         # add the same setup to an existing repo
167	```
168	
169	`repo new NAME` keeps the small scripted default: `main`, README, and an
170	initial commit. When the argument is clearly a Git URL, local Git path, or
171	owner/name, however, `new`/`create` routes to the clone flow and preserves the
172	source history and configured remote; `repo clone` remains the explicit spelling.
173	Bare `dev repo clone` selects from the existing private forge cache without a
174	network refresh, while still offering manual URL/path/`owner/name` entry. Bare
175	`dev start` similarly selects a local repository with fast live discovery.
176	The external selector defaults to `fzf`; if it is missing (or `[picker] command = []`),
177	dev uses its built-in Bubble Tea picker. Pipes remain line-oriented.
178	Clone can optionally apply a preset after the checkout exists, while `repo setup` repeat-safely merges native
179	initializers and preset files into a repository you already have. Custom hooks
180	and skill setup remain responsible for their own idempotency. Use `--dry-run`
181	to inspect the available plan without mutating the target repository.
182	
183	`repo new` can also start from a content snapshot rather than an empty tree.
184	`--template` accepts a local directory/repository, Git URL, or owner/name;
185	`--template-ref` selects a branch, tag, or commit, and `--template-subdir`
186	selects a confined folder within the source. The snapshot becomes a fresh Git
187	history: source `.git` metadata is never copied, template files win scaffold
188	conflicts, regular-file modes are preserved, and traversal, symlinks, and
189	special files fail before the destination is created. A local Git working tree

```text
10	// openCheckout makes a directory live, asking the backend to treat it as a git
11	// worktree when it knows how — that is what groups the checkout under its
12	// parent repo in a sidebar instead of listing it as an unrelated directory.
13	func openCheckout(ctx context.Context, rt runtime.Runtime, dir, label string) (runtime.OpenResult, error) {
14		if wo, ok := rt.(runtime.WorktreeOpener); ok {
15			return wo.OpenWorktree(ctx, dir, label)
16		}
17		return rt.Open(ctx, dir, label)
18	}
19	
20	// activateRuntime performs the interactive half of navigation. Runtime Open
21	// calls are detached by design; explicit open/resume actions opt into either
22	// switching the current multiplexer client or attaching from a plain shell.
23	func activateRuntime(ctx context.Context, rt runtime.Runtime, handle string) error {
24		if rt == nil || rt.Name() == "none" || handle == "" {
25			return nil
26		}
27		activator, ok := rt.(runtime.Activator)
28		if !ok {
29			return errors.New("runtime " + rt.Name() + " cannot activate sessions")
30		}
31		return activator.Activate(ctx, handle)
32	}
33	
34	func persistedRuntimeHandle(rt runtime.Runtime, opened runtime.OpenResult) string {
35		if rt == nil || rt.Name() == "none" {
36			return ""
37		}
38		return opened.Handle
39	}
40	
41	func worktreeRuntimeLabel(repo, branch string) string { return repo + "/" + branch }
42	
43	// asError is errors.As with a typed target, kept here so call sites read as
44	// one line.
45	func asError[T error](err error, target *T) bool { return errors.As(err, target) }
```

```text
2	// flags, call into the domain packages, and render. All policy lives in

30		Tasks    *task.Store
31		Catalog  *catalog.Store
32		Registry *catalog.Registry
33		Notes    *note.Service
34		Sizes    *diskusage.Manager
35	
36		In  io.Reader
37		Out io.Writer
38		Err io.Writer
39	
40		// configPath is the --config override; empty means the XDG default.
41		configPath string
42		// remotesPath is the --remotes override; empty means dev/remotes.toml.
43		remotesPath string
44		// scaffoldsPath is the --scaffolds override; empty means dev/scaffolds.toml.
45		scaffoldsPath string
46		// runtimeOverride is the --runtime flag; empty means use the config.
47		runtimeOverride string
48		// noRuntime disables all multiplexer interaction for one invocation.
49		noRuntime bool
50		// allowSharedCheckout is an explicit escape hatch for coordinated agents
51		// whose file ownership is known to be disjoint.
52		allowSharedCheckout bool
53		// colorMode controls styling of human-readable output.
54		colorMode string
55		// interactiveCheck is a test seam for commands that prompt only when a real
56		// terminal is attached. Production falls back to interactive().
57		interactiveCheck func() bool
58		// runtimeInstance, runtimesByName and pickerSelect are injection seams used by
59		// focused command tests.
60		runtimeInstance runtime.Runtime
61		runtimesByName  map[string]runtime.Runtime
62		pickerSelect    func(context.Context, picker.Request) (picker.Result, error)
63		// trace is an opt-in, process-local performance recorder. It is deliberately
64		// separate from durable activity stats and ordinary command output.
65		trace                  *perftrace.Recorder
66		tracePath              string
67		traceOnce              *sync.Once
68		traceTUI               bool
69		deferredReleaseRefresh bool
```
