```text
1	// Package repo discovers the repositories a user actually owns by walking the
2	// configured scan roots. It answers "what projects do I have?", which is a
3	// different question from "what am I working on?" — that one belongs to
4	// package task.
5	package repo
6	
7	import (
8		"context"
9		"io/fs"
10		"os"
11		"path/filepath"
12		"sort"
13		"strings"
14	
15		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/gitx"
16	)
17	
18	// Repo is one discovered repository.
19	type Repo struct {
20		// Name is the directory basename, which is how users refer to it.
21		Name string
22		// Path is the absolute path reached through the scan root. It may be a
23		// symlink from a bootstrap index; commands intentionally keep that human
24		// navigation path rather than replacing it with the physical one.
25		Path string
26		// RealPath is the physical checkout path.
27		RealPath string
28		// Symlink reports that Path is an alias to RealPath.
29		Symlink bool
30		// Root is the scan root it was found under.
31		Root string
32		// Category is the path between the scan root and the repo ("Quant",
33		// "Web/Frontend"), empty for a repo sitting directly in the root. It is
34		// human organisation metadata, preserved for `dev graduate` to place new
35		// projects consistently.
36		Category string
37		// GitDir is this checkout's administrative directory; CommonDir is shared
38		// by every linked worktree of the clone.
39		GitDir    string
40		CommonDir string
41		MainRoot  string
42		// Bare reports a bare repository (a worktree hub).
43		Bare bool
44		// HasGit distinguishes a real repo from a plain directory that was found
45		// in a scan root; non-repos are reported so `dev repo list` can offer to
46		// initialise them.
47		HasGit bool
48	}
49	
50	// Display renders "Category/Name" or just "Name".
51	func (r Repo) Display() string {
52		if r.Category == "" {
53			return r.Name
54		}
55		return r.Category + "/" + r.Name
56	}
57	
58	// Options tunes discovery.
59	type Options struct {
60		// MaxDepth limits how deep below a scan root a repo may be found. The
61		// default layout is <root>/<Category>/<Repo>, so 2 suffices; 3 leaves room
62		// for a nested grouping without walking an entire home directory.
63		MaxDepth int
64		// IncludeNonRepos reports plain directories alongside repositories.
65		IncludeNonRepos bool
66		// Fast avoids per-repository git subprocesses. It is intended for shell
67		// completion: direct .git-file checkouts are skipped as linked worktrees and
68		// symlink aliases are deduplicated by their physical path.
69		Fast bool
70	}
71	
72	// DefaultOptions is the discovery configuration used by dev's commands.
73	func DefaultOptions() Options { return Options{MaxDepth: 3} }
74	
75	// CompletionOptions trades full Git metadata for interactive latency.
76	func CompletionOptions() Options { return Options{MaxDepth: 3, Fast: true} }
77	
78	// skipDirs are never descended into. These are large, never contain a project
79	// the user organises by hand, and walking them dominates scan time.
80	var skipDirs = map[string]bool{
81		"node_modules": true, ".venv": true, "venv": true, "target": true,
82		"vendor": true, "__pycache__": true, ".tox": true, "dist": true,
83		"build": true, ".next": true, ".cache": true, ".terraform": true,
84		"Library": true, ".Trash": true,
85	}
86	
87	// Discover walks every root and returns the repositories found, sorted by
88	// display name. Unreadable directories are skipped rather than fatal — a scan
89	// root that has been unmounted must not break `dev ls`.
90	func Discover(ctx context.Context, roots []string, opts Options) ([]Repo, error) {
91		if opts.MaxDepth <= 0 {
92			opts.MaxDepth = DefaultOptions().MaxDepth
93		}
94		seen := map[string]bool{}
95		// clone identities stop a physical path and a symlink index from showing
96		// the same repository twice. The first scan root wins, which lets users
97		// choose whether the curated index or the physical hierarchy is their UI
98		// simply by ordering scan_roots.
99		identities := map[string]bool{}
100		var out []Repo
101	
102		for _, root := range roots {
103			info, err := os.Stat(root)
104			if err != nil || !info.IsDir() {
105				continue // a missing scan root is normal on a fresh machine
106			}
107			rootClean := filepath.Clean(root)
108	
109			err = filepath.WalkDir(rootClean, func(path string, d fs.DirEntry, err error) error {
110				if err != nil {
111					return nil // unreadable entry: skip, keep walking
112				}
113				if ctx.Err() != nil {
114					return ctx.Err()
115				}
116				isRoot := path == rootClean
117				name := d.Name()
118				isLink := d.Type()&os.ModeSymlink != 0
119				isDir := d.IsDir()
120				if isLink {
121					// WalkDir does not follow symlinks. Inspect a direct symlink to
122					// a repository, but do not recurse through arbitrary symlinked
123					// containers — bootstrap does that with cycle detection.
124					if info, err := os.Stat(path); err == nil {
125						isDir = info.IsDir()
126					}
127				}
128				if !isDir {
129					return nil
130				}
131				if !isRoot && (skipDirs[name] || (strings.HasPrefix(name, ".") && name != ".bare")) {
132					return filepath.SkipDir
133				}
134	
135				rel := "."
136				depth := 0
137				if !isRoot {
138					rel, _ = filepath.Rel(rootClean, path)
139					depth = len(strings.Split(rel, string(filepath.Separator)))
140				}
141	
142				if isRepoDir(path) {
143					real, _ := filepath.EvalSymlinks(path)
144					if real == "" {
145						real = path
146					}
147					bare := isBareDir(path)
148					identity, gitDir, commonDir, mainRoot := real, real, real, real
149					if !bare && opts.Fast && gitEntryIsFile(path) {
150						// A direct .git file at a discovered root is a linked
151						// worktree. Submodules are already hidden below their parent
152						// repository because discovery never descends into one.
153						return filepath.SkipDir
154					}
155					if !bare && !opts.Fast {
156						if g, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, path); err == nil {
157							// A linked worktree is execution state, not another
158							// project in the repo inventory.
159							if g.IsLinkedWorktree {
160								return filepath.SkipDir
161							}
162							identity, gitDir, commonDir, mainRoot = g.GitCommonDir, g.GitDir, g.GitCommonDir, g.MainRoot
163							real = g.MainRoot
164						}
165					}
166					if !seen[path] && !identities[identity] {
167						seen[path], identities[identity] = true, true
168						out = append(out, Repo{
169							Name:      name,
170							Path:      path,
171							RealPath:  real,
172							Symlink:   isLink,
173							Root:      rootClean,
174							Category:  filepath.ToSlash(filepath.Dir(rel)),
175							GitDir:    gitDir,
176							CommonDir: commonDir,
177							MainRoot:  mainRoot,
178							Bare:      bare,
179							HasGit:    true,
180						})
181					}
182					// Never descend into a repo: its subdirectories are source
183					// code, and any nested .git is a submodule or a worktree that
184					// belongs to this repo, not a project of its own.
185					return filepath.SkipDir
186				}
187				if depth >= opts.MaxDepth {
188					return filepath.SkipDir
189				}
190				if opts.IncludeNonRepos && depth == 1 {
191					if !seen[path] {
192						seen[path] = true
193						out = append(out, Repo{Name: name, Path: path, Root: rootClean, Category: ""})
194					}
195				}
196				return nil
197			})
198			if err != nil && ctx.Err() != nil {
199				return out, ctx.Err()
200			}
201		}
202	
203		for i := range out {
204			if out[i].Category == "." {
205				out[i].Category = ""
206			}
207		}
208		sort.Slice(out, func(i, j int) bool {
209			if out[i].Name != out[j].Name {
210				return strings.ToLower(out[i].Name) < strings.ToLower(out[j].Name)
211			}
212			return out[i].Path < out[j].Path
213		})
214		return out, nil
215	}
216	
217	// isRepoDir reports whether path is a repository root: it holds a .git entry
218	// (directory for a normal clone, file for a linked worktree or submodule).
219	func isRepoDir(path string) bool {
220		if _, err := os.Lstat(filepath.Join(path, ".git")); err == nil {
221			return true
222		}
223		return isBareDir(path)
224	}
225	
226	func gitEntryIsFile(path string) bool {
227		info, err := os.Lstat(filepath.Join(path, ".git"))
228		return err == nil && info.Mode().IsRegular()
229	}
230	
231	// isBareDir recognises a bare repository by its skeleton, without shelling out.
232	func isBareDir(path string) bool {
233		for _, marker := range []string{"HEAD", "objects", "refs"} {
234			if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(path, marker)); err != nil {
235				return false
236			}
237		}
238		return true
239	}
240	
241	// Resolve finds a repo by name, display name, or path.
242	//
243	// Matching is deliberately layered: an exact name or path wins outright, and
244	// only then does a substring search run — so a repo literally named "web"
245	// is never shadowed by "web-frontend".
246	func Resolve(ctx context.Context, roots []string, ref string) (Repo, []Repo, error) {
247		return resolve(ctx, roots, ref, DefaultOptions())
248	}
249	
250	// ResolveCompletion resolves the same references without launching one Git
251	// process per repository in the scan roots.
252	func ResolveCompletion(ctx context.Context, roots []string, ref string) (Repo, []Repo, error) {
253		return resolve(ctx, roots, ref, CompletionOptions())
254	}
255	
256	func resolve(ctx context.Context, roots []string, ref string, opts Options) (Repo, []Repo, error) {
257		all, err := Discover(ctx, roots, opts)
258		if err != nil {
259			return Repo{}, nil, err
260		}
261		if abs, err := filepath.Abs(ref); err == nil {
262			if g, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, abs); err == nil {
263				real, _ := filepath.EvalSymlinks(abs)
264				if real == "" {
265					real = g.MainRoot
266				}
267				// Preserve an explicit navigation alias. The caller named this
268				// path on purpose; resolving it to the physical checkout would
269				// defeat a bootstrap symlink catalog.
270				return Repo{
271					Name: filepath.Base(abs), Path: abs, RealPath: real,
272					Symlink: real != abs, CommonDir: g.GitCommonDir, HasGit: true, Bare: g.Bare,
273				}, nil, nil
274			}
275		}
276		for _, r := range all {
277			if r.Name == ref || r.Display() == ref || r.Path == ref {
278				return r, nil, nil
279			}
280		}
281		needle := strings.ToLower(ref)
282		var hits []Repo
283		for _, r := range all {
284			if strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(r.Display()), needle) {
285				hits = append(hits, r)
286			}
287		}
288		switch len(hits) {
289		case 1:
290			return hits[0], nil, nil
291		case 0:
292			return Repo{}, nil, &NotFoundError{Ref: ref}
293		default:
294			return Repo{}, hits, &AmbiguousError{Ref: ref, Candidates: hits}
295		}
296	}
297	
298	// NotFoundError reports a repo reference that matched nothing.
299	type NotFoundError struct{ Ref string }
300	
301	func (e *NotFoundError) Error() string { return "no repository matching " + e.Ref }
302	
303	// AmbiguousError reports a repo reference that matched several repos.
304	type AmbiguousError struct {
305		Ref        string
306		Candidates []Repo
307	}
308	
309	func (e *AmbiguousError) Error() string {
310		names := make([]string, len(e.Candidates))
311		for i, c := range e.Candidates {
312			names[i] = c.Display()
313		}
314		return e.Ref + " is ambiguous: " + strings.Join(names, ", ")
315	}
```

```text
153	func promptRepoCloneReference(app *App, p *prompter) (string, error) {
154		manual := func() (string, error) {
155			return p.line("Git URL, path, or owner/name", "")
156		}
157		if !app.canPick() {
158			return manual()
159		}
160	
161		cache, ok := forge.LoadCacheAny(remoteCachePath())
162		sourceID := remoteCacheSourceID(app)
163		if !ok || (cache.SourceID != "" && cache.SourceID != sourceID) {
164			return manual()
165		}
166		items := make([]picker.Item, 0, len(cache.Repos)+1)
167		for _, remote := range cache.Repos {
168			if strings.TrimSpace(remote.CloneURL) == "" {
169				continue
170			}
171			var details []string
172			if remote.Visibility != "" {
173				details = append(details, strings.ToLower(remote.Visibility))
174			}
175			if remote.Archived {
176				details = append(details, "archived")
177			}
178			if remote.Description != "" {
179				details = append(details, truncate(remote.Description, 72))
180			}
181			items = append(items, picker.Item{
182				Value:       remote.CloneURL,
183				Label:       remote.Label(),
184				Description: strings.Join(details, " · "),
185			})
186		}
187		if len(items) == 0 {
188			return manual()
189		}
190		items = append(items, picker.Item{
191			Value:       manualCloneReference,
192			Label:       "Enter a URL, path, or owner/name manually…",
193			Description: "use a source not present in the cached forge inventory",
194		})
195		if !cache.FreshFor(app.Cfg.Forge.CacheTTL.Duration, sourceID) {
196			app.warnf("remote cache is stale or incomplete; run `dev repo remote --refresh` to update picker candidates")
197		}
198		result, used, err := app.pick(ctxOf(), picker.Request{Prompt: "Repository to clone", Items: items})
199		if err != nil {
200			return "", err
201		}
202		if !used || !result.Selected || result.Item.Value == manualCloneReference {
203			if result.Canceled {
204				return "", errPromptCanceled
205			}
206			return manual()
207		}
208		return result.Item.Value, nil
209	}

358	func promptScaffoldOptions(p *prompter, catalog scaffold.Config, presetName string, flags *repoBootstrapFlags) error {
359		preset, err := catalog.ResolvePreset(presetName)
360		if err != nil {
361			return err
362		}
363		for _, input := range preset.Inputs {
364			label := input.Label
365			if label == "" {
366				label = input.ID
367			}
368			fallback := parseInputDefault(input.Default)
369			switch input.Type {
370			case scaffold.InputBool:
371				value, _ := strconvParseBoolDefault(fallback)
372				chosen, err := p.confirm(label, value)
373				if err != nil {
374					return err
375				}
376				flags.set = replaceSetValue(flags.set, input.ID, fmt.Sprint(chosen))
377			case scaffold.InputChoice:
378				choices := map[string]string{}
379				for _, choice := range input.Choices {
380					choices[strings.ToLower(choice)] = choice
381				}
382				if fallback == "" && len(input.Choices) > 0 {
383					fallback = input.Choices[0]
384				}
385				value, err := p.choice(label+" ("+strings.Join(input.Choices, "/")+")", fallback,
386					strings.Join(input.Choices, ", "), choices)
387				if err != nil {
388					return err
389				}
390				flags.set = replaceSetValue(flags.set, input.ID, value)
391			default:
392				for {
393					value, err := p.line(label, fallback)
394					if err != nil {
395						return err
396					}
397					if input.IsRequired() && strings.TrimSpace(value) == "" {
398						fmt.Fprintln(p.out, "  "+p.style.warning(label+" is required"))

401					flags.set = replaceSetValue(flags.set, input.ID, value)
```

```text
17	// Cache is the on-disk forge inventory. It exists for UI latency, not as a
18	// source of truth: the REMOTE tab should open instantly, and r refreshes it.
19	type Cache struct {
20		Version   int                     `json:"version,omitempty"`
21		SourceID  string                  `json:"source_id,omitempty"`
22		FetchedAt time.Time               `json:"fetched_at"`
23		Complete  bool                    `json:"complete,omitempty"`
24		Providers map[Kind]ProviderStatus `json:"providers,omitempty"`
25		Repos     []RemoteRepo            `json:"repos"`
26	}
27	
28	const (
29		CacheVersion      = 2
30		maxCacheBytes     = 32 << 20
31		maxCachedRepos    = 100_000
32		maxCacheClockSkew = 5 * time.Minute
33	)
34	
35	var cacheWriteLocks sync.Map
36	
37	type ProviderStatus struct {
38		FetchedAt time.Time `json:"fetched_at,omitempty"`
39		Complete  bool      `json:"complete"`
40		Error     string    `json:"error,omitempty"`
41	}
42	
43	// LoadCache returns only a fresh, complete cache. TUI callers that can label
44	// stale rows while refreshing use LoadCacheAny instead.
45	func LoadCache(path string, maxAge time.Duration) (Cache, bool) {
46		c, ok := LoadCacheAny(path)
47		if !ok || !c.Fresh(maxAge) {
48			return Cache{}, false
49		}
50		return c, true
51	}
52	
53	// LoadCacheAny returns a cache regardless of age or completeness. This powers
54	// stale-while-revalidate UI behavior; callers must inspect Fresh/Complete.
55	func LoadCacheAny(path string) (Cache, bool) {
56		info, err := os.Stat(path)
57		if err != nil || info.Size() < 0 || info.Size() > maxCacheBytes {
58			return Cache{}, false
59		}
60		b, err := os.ReadFile(path)
61		if err != nil {
62			return Cache{}, false
63		}
64		var c Cache
65		if json.Unmarshal(b, &c) != nil || !validCache(c, time.Now().UTC()) {
66			return Cache{}, false
67		}
68		if c.Version == 0 {
69			// Version 1 caches were valid snapshots but capped per provider, so they
70			// are useful for instant display and must immediately be refreshed.
71			c.Complete = false
72		}
73		return c, true
74	}
75	
76	func validCache(c Cache, now time.Time) bool {
77		if (c.Version != 0 && c.Version != CacheVersion) || c.FetchedAt.IsZero() ||
78			c.FetchedAt.After(now.Add(maxCacheClockSkew)) || len(c.Repos) > maxCachedRepos ||
79			!validCacheString(c.SourceID, 128, false) {
80			return false
81		}
82		for kind, status := range c.Providers {
83			if !validForgeKind(kind) || len(status.Error) > 16<<10 || strings.ContainsRune(status.Error, '\x00') ||
84				status.FetchedAt.After(now.Add(maxCacheClockSkew)) {
85				return false
86			}
87		}
88		for _, repository := range c.Repos {
89			if !validForgeKind(repository.Forge) || pathx.ValidateComponent(repository.Name) != nil ||
90				!validCacheString(repository.FullName, 2048, true) ||
91				!validCacheString(repository.Description, 64<<10, false) ||
92				!validCacheString(repository.URL, 8<<10, false) ||
93				!validCacheString(repository.CloneURL, 8<<10, false) ||
94				!validCacheString(repository.SSHURL, 8<<10, false) ||
95				!validCacheString(repository.Visibility, 128, false) ||
96				!validCacheString(repository.DefaultBranch, 1024, false) ||
97				repository.UpdatedAt.After(now.Add(maxCacheClockSkew)) {
98				return false
99			}
100		}
101		return true
102	}
103	
104	func validForgeKind(kind Kind) bool {
105		return kind == GitHub || kind == GitLab || kind == AzureDevOps
106	}
107	
108	func validCacheString(value string, limit int, required bool) bool {
109		return (!required || strings.TrimSpace(value) != "") && len(value) <= limit && !strings.ContainsRune(value, '\x00')
110	}
111	
112	// FreshFor additionally requires the cache to describe the same configured
113	// provider endpoints/targets. Caches without a source ID remain displayable but
114	// are immediately revalidated.
115	func (c Cache) FreshFor(maxAge time.Duration, sourceID string) bool {
116		return sourceID != "" && c.SourceID == sourceID && c.Fresh(maxAge)
117	}
118	
119	func (c Cache) Fresh(maxAge time.Duration) bool {
120		if c.Version != CacheVersion || !c.Complete {
121			return false
122		}
123		if maxAge <= 0 {
124			return true
125		}
126		if len(c.Providers) == 0 {
127			return time.Since(c.FetchedAt) <= maxAge
128		}
129		for _, provider := range c.Providers {
130			if !provider.Complete || provider.Error != "" || provider.FetchedAt.IsZero() || time.Since(provider.FetchedAt) > maxAge {
131				return false
132			}
133		}
134		return true
135	}
136	
137	// SaveCache atomically replaces the cache. A partial forge response may be
138	// cached — its FetchedAt still says exactly when it was observed.
139	func SaveCache(path string, repos []RemoteRepo) error {
140		now := time.Now().UTC()
141		providers := map[Kind]ProviderStatus{}
142		for _, repo := range repos {
143			providers[repo.Forge] = ProviderStatus{FetchedAt: now, Complete: true}
144		}
145		return SaveCacheState(path, Cache{Version: CacheVersion, FetchedAt: now, Complete: true, Providers: providers, Repos: repos})
146	}
147	
148	// SaveCacheState atomically replaces the versioned inventory cache.
149	func SaveCacheState(path string, cache Cache) error {
150		return SaveCacheStateContext(context.Background(), path, cache)
151	}
152	
153	// SaveCacheStateContext serializes one cache target and checks cancellation
154	// while holding that ordering boundary. A superseded generation therefore
155	// cannot rename after a newer generation has committed.
156	func SaveCacheStateContext(ctx context.Context, path string, cache Cache) error {
157		if path == "" {
158			return errors.New("empty cache path")
159		}
160		if ctx == nil {
161			ctx = context.Background()
162		}
163		lock := cacheWriteLock(path)
164		lock.Lock()
165		defer lock.Unlock()
166		if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
167			return err
168		}
169		if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(path), 0o755); err != nil {
170			return err
171		}
172		if cache.Version == 0 {
173			cache.Version = CacheVersion
174		}
175		if cache.FetchedAt.IsZero() {
176			cache.FetchedAt = time.Now().UTC()
177		}
178		b, err := json.MarshalIndent(cache, "", "  ")
179		if err != nil {
180			return err
181		}
182		b = append(b, '\n')
183		tmp, err := os.CreateTemp(filepath.Dir(path), ".remotes-*.tmp")
184		if err != nil {
185			return err
186		}
187		name := tmp.Name()
188		defer os.Remove(name)
189		if _, err := tmp.Write(b); err != nil {
190			tmp.Close()
191			return err
192		}
193		if err := tmp.Close(); err != nil {
194			return err
195		}
196		if err := os.Chmod(name, 0o600); err != nil {
197			return err
198		}
199		if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
200			return err
201		}
202		return os.Rename(name, path)
203	}
204	
205	func cacheWriteLock(path string) *sync.Mutex {
206		loaded, _ := cacheWriteLocks.LoadOrStore(filepath.Clean(path), &sync.Mutex{})
207		return loaded.(*sync.Mutex)
208	}
209	
210	// CacheExists reports whether any cache file exists, even stale. Used only for
211	// diagnostics.
212	func CacheExists(path string) bool {
213		_, err := os.Stat(path)
214		return err == nil || !errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist)
215	}
```

```text
1164	func matchRemoteRepoRows(remoteRepos []forge.RemoteRepo, locals []tui.RepoRow) []tui.RemoteRow {

1166		ambiguous := map[string]bool{}
1167		for _, r := range locals {
1168			if r.RemoteForge == forge.Unknown || r.RemoteName == "" {
1169				continue
1170			}
1171			key := string(r.RemoteForge) + "/" + strings.ToLower(r.RemoteName)

1173				continue
1174			}
1175			if _, exists := byRemote[key]; exists {
1176				delete(byRemote, key)
1177				ambiguous[key] = true
```

```text
277			if r.Name == ref || r.Display() == ref || r.Path == ref {
278				return r, nil, nil
279			}
280		}
281		needle := strings.ToLower(ref)
282		var hits []Repo
283		for _, r := range all {
284			if strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(r.Display()), needle) {
285				hits = append(hits, r)
286			}
287		}
288		switch len(hits) {
289		case 1:
290			return hits[0], nil, nil
291		case 0:
292			return Repo{}, nil, &NotFoundError{Ref: ref}
293		default:
294			return Repo{}, hits, &AmbiguousError{Ref: ref, Candidates: hits}
295		}
296	}
297	
298	// NotFoundError reports a repo reference that matched nothing.
299	type NotFoundError struct{ Ref string }
300	
301	func (e *NotFoundError) Error() string { return "no repository matching " + e.Ref }
302	
303	// AmbiguousError reports a repo reference that matched several repos.
304	type AmbiguousError struct {
305		Ref        string
306		Candidates []Repo
307	}
308	
309	func (e *AmbiguousError) Error() string {
310		names := make([]string, len(e.Candidates))
311		for i, c := range e.Candidates {
312			names[i] = c.Display()
313		}
314		return e.Ref + " is ambiguous: " + strings.Join(names, ", ")
315	}
```

```text
3	import (
4		"context"
5		"os"

9	
10	// Repo identifies one repository, independent of which worktree you are
11	// standing in. Two linked worktrees of the same clone share a Key.
12	type Repo struct {
13		// Root is the working-tree root of the checkout that was probed.
14		Root string
15		// GitDir is this checkout's administrative directory. A linked worktree has
16		// its own entry below the shared common directory.
17		GitDir string
18		// GitCommonDir is the shared .git directory — the same value for every
19		// worktree of a clone, which makes it the natural identity.
20		GitCommonDir string
21		// Name is the basename users recognise the repo by.
22		Name string
23		// IsLinkedWorktree reports whether Root is a linked worktree rather than
24		// the main checkout.
25		IsLinkedWorktree bool
26		// MainRoot is the main (non-linked) checkout of this clone.
27		MainRoot string
28		// Bare reports whether the main checkout is a bare repository.
29		Bare bool
30	}
31	
32	// Key is the stable identity of the clone, shared by all its worktrees.
33	func (r Repo) Key() string { return r.GitCommonDir }
34	
35	// Discover probes dir and reports the repository containing it.
36	func Discover(ctx context.Context, dir string) (Repo, error) {
37		// A single rev-parse call answers everything: batching avoids four
38		// process spawns per repo, which matters when scanning 39 of them.
39		out, err := run(ctx, dir,
40			"rev-parse",
41			"--path-format=absolute",
42			"--show-toplevel",
43			"--git-dir",
44			"--git-common-dir",
45			"--is-bare-repository",
46		)
47		if err != nil {
48			return Repo{}, err
49		}
50		f := lines(out)
51		r := Repo{}
52		// A bare repo has no toplevel, so git prints one fewer line.
53		switch len(f) {
54		case 4:
55			r.Root = f[0]
56			r.GitDir = f[1]
57			r.GitCommonDir = f[2]
58			r.Bare = f[3] == "true"
59		case 3:
60			r.GitDir = f[0]
61			r.GitCommonDir = f[1]
62			r.Bare = f[2] == "true"
63		default:
64			return Repo{}, ErrNotARepo
65		}
66	
67		// The main checkout is the parent of the common .git dir, except for a
68		// bare repo (where the common dir *is* the repo).
69		if r.Bare {
70			r.MainRoot = strings.TrimSuffix(r.GitCommonDir, string(filepath.Separator))
71		} else if r.GitDir == r.GitCommonDir {
72			// A normal checkout may use --separate-git-dir, so the common directory's
73			// parent is not necessarily the working-tree root.
74			r.MainRoot = r.Root
75		} else {
76			r.MainRoot = filepath.Dir(r.GitCommonDir)
77		}
78		r.IsLinkedWorktree = r.Root != "" && r.GitDir != r.GitCommonDir
79		r.Name = filepath.Base(r.MainRoot)
80		if r.Bare {
81			// ".../foo/.bare" or ".../foo.git" should both read as "foo".
82			r.Name = strings.TrimSuffix(filepath.Base(r.MainRoot), ".git")
83			if strings.HasPrefix(r.Name, ".") {
84				r.Name = filepath.Base(filepath.Dir(r.MainRoot))
85			}
86		}
87		return r, nil
88	}
89	
90	// IsRepo reports whether dir is inside a git working tree, without the cost of
91	// a full Discover.
92	func IsRepo(ctx context.Context, dir string) bool {
93		_, err := run(ctx, dir, "rev-parse", "--git-dir")
94		return err == nil
95	}
96	
97	// DefaultBranch resolves the repository's default branch — origin/HEAD when the
98	// remote advertises it, else the first of main/master that exists locally.
99	// Returns "" when nothing can be determined, which callers must treat as
100	// "ask the user" rather than guessing.
101	func DefaultBranch(ctx context.Context, dir string) string {
102		if out, err := run(ctx, dir, "symbolic-ref", "--short", "refs/remotes/origin/HEAD"); err == nil {
103			if _, b, ok := strings.Cut(out, "/"); ok {
104				return b
105			}
106		}
107		for _, cand := range []string{"main", "master", "trunk", "develop"} {
108			if _, err := run(ctx, dir, "show-ref", "--verify", "--quiet", "refs/heads/"+cand); err == nil {
109				return cand
110			}
111		}
112		return ""
113	}
114	
115	// Remote returns the push URL of the named remote ("origin" when empty).
116	func Remote(ctx context.Context, dir, name string) string {
117		if name == "" {
118			name = "origin"
119		}
120		out, err := run(ctx, dir, "remote", "get-url", name)
121		if err != nil {
122			return ""
123		}
124		return out
125	}
126	
127	// RemoteFromConfig reads one remote URL directly from a Git common directory.
128	// It is the zero-process path used by whole-machine inventory, where spawning
129	// `git remote get-url` once per repo dominated startup. Includes and URL
130	// rewriting are deliberately not evaluated; callers that need Git's complete
131	// semantics should use Remote instead.
132	func RemoteFromConfig(commonDir, name string) string {
133		if commonDir == "" {
134			return ""
135		}
136		if name == "" {
137			name = "origin"
138		}
139		b, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(commonDir, "config"))
140		if err != nil {
141			return ""
142		}
143		want := `remote "` + name + `"`
144		section := ""
145		for _, raw := range strings.Split(string(b), "\n") {
146			line := strings.TrimSpace(raw)
147			if line == "" || strings.HasPrefix(line, "#") || strings.HasPrefix(line, ";") {
148				continue
149			}
150			if strings.HasPrefix(line, "[") && strings.HasSuffix(line, "]") {
151				section = strings.TrimSpace(line[1 : len(line)-1])
152				continue
153			}
154			if section != want {
155				continue
156			}
157			key, value, ok := strings.Cut(line, "=")
158			if ok && strings.TrimSpace(key) == "url" {
159				return strings.Trim(strings.TrimSpace(value), `"`)
160			}
161		}
162		return ""
163	}
```

```text
1	// Package picker selects one value from a caller-provided list. It can hand
2	// the terminal to a line-oriented external picker such as fzf, and otherwise
3	// falls back to dev's built-in Bubble Tea interface.
4	package picker
5	
6	import (
7		"bytes"
8		"context"
9		"errors"
10		"fmt"
11		"io"
12		"os/exec"
13		"strings"
14	)
15	
16	// Item is one selectable value. Value is opaque caller data and is never sent
17	// to an external picker; Label and Description are display-only.
18	type Item struct {
19		Value       string
20		Label       string
21		Description string
22	}
23	
24	// Request describes one selection interaction.
25	type Request struct {
26		Prompt       string
27		InitialQuery string
28		Items        []Item
29	}
30	
31	// Result distinguishes a selection from an explicit cancellation.
32	type Result struct {
33		Item     Item
34		Selected bool
35		Canceled bool
36	}
37	
38	// Selector owns the streams and optional external command for one application.
39	type Selector struct {
40		in       io.Reader
41		out      io.Writer
42		errOut   io.Writer
43		command  []string
44		lookPath func(string) (string, error)
45	}
46	
47	// New constructs a selector. command is an argv vector, not a shell command;
48	// an empty vector always selects the built-in backend.
49	func New(in io.Reader, out, errOut io.Writer, command []string) *Selector {
50		return &Selector{
51			in:       in,
52			out:      out,
53			errOut:   errOut,
54			command:  append([]string(nil), command...),
55			lookPath: exec.LookPath,
56		}
57	}
58	
59	// Select uses the configured external picker when it is installed and the
60	// built-in picker otherwise.
61	func (s *Selector) Select(ctx context.Context, request Request) (Result, error) {
62		if len(request.Items) == 0 {
63			return Result{}, nil
64		}
65		if len(s.command) == 0 {
66			return s.selectBuiltin(ctx, request)
67		}
68		path, err := s.lookPath(s.command[0])
69		if err != nil {
70			return s.selectBuiltin(ctx, request)
71		}
72		return s.selectExternal(ctx, path, request)
73	}
74	
75	func (s *Selector) selectExternal(ctx context.Context, path string, request Request) (Result, error) {
76		lines, items := renderCandidates(request.Items)
77		args := make([]string, len(s.command)-1)
78		for index, arg := range s.command[1:] {
79			args[index] = strings.ReplaceAll(arg, "{prompt}", request.Prompt)
80		}
81		cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, path, args...)
82		cmd.Stdin = strings.NewReader(strings.Join(lines, "\n") + "\n")
83		if s.errOut == nil {
84			cmd.Stderr = io.Discard
85		} else {
86			cmd.Stderr = s.errOut
87		}
88		var stdout bytes.Buffer
89		cmd.Stdout = &stdout
90	
91		err := cmd.Run()
92		if ctxErr := ctx.Err(); ctxErr != nil {
93			return Result{}, ctxErr
94		}
95		if err != nil {
96			var exitErr *exec.ExitError
97			if errors.As(err, &exitErr) && (exitErr.ExitCode() == 1 || exitErr.ExitCode() == 130) {
98				return Result{Canceled: true}, nil
99			}
100			return Result{}, fmt.Errorf("external picker: %w", err)
101		}
102	
103		selected, err := selectedLine(stdout.String())
104		if err != nil {
105			return Result{}, err
106		}
107		item, ok := items[selected]
108		if !ok {
109			return Result{}, fmt.Errorf("external picker returned an unknown selection")
110		}
111		return Result{Item: item, Selected: true}, nil
112	}
113	
114	func selectedLine(output string) (string, error) {
115		output = strings.TrimSuffix(output, "\n")
116		output = strings.TrimSuffix(output, "\r")
117		if output == "" || strings.ContainsAny(output, "\r\n\x00") {
118			return "", errors.New("external picker returned malformed output")
119		}
120		return output, nil
121	}
122	
123	func renderCandidates(items []Item) ([]string, map[string]Item) {
124		lines := make([]string, 0, len(items))
125		byLine := make(map[string]Item, len(items))
126		for _, item := range items {
127			label := cleanDisplay(item.Label)
128			if label == "" {
129				label = "(unnamed)"
130			}
131			base := label
132			if description := cleanDisplay(item.Description); description != "" {
133				base += "\t" + description
134			}
135			line := base
136			for ordinal := 2; ; ordinal++ {
137				if _, exists := byLine[line]; !exists {
138					break
139				}
140				line = fmt.Sprintf("%s\t[%d]", base, ordinal)
141			}
142			lines = append(lines, line)
143			byLine[line] = item
144		}
145		return lines, byLine
146	}
147	
148	func cleanDisplay(value string) string {
149		return strings.Join(strings.FieldsFunc(value, func(r rune) bool {
150			return r == '\r' || r == '\n' || r == '\t' || r == 0
151		}), " ")
152	}
153
```

```text
152	func (r RepoRow) matches(query string) bool {
153		query = strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(query))
154		for _, term := range strings.Fields(query) {
155			key, value, structured := strings.Cut(term, ":")
156			if structured {
157				switch key {
158				case "tag":
159					if r.Asset == nil || !r.Asset.HasTag(value) {
160						return false
161					}
162					continue
163				case "remote":
164					if !strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(r.Topology.Summary()), value) {
165						return false
166					}
167					continue
168				case "size":
169					if !matchesSize(r.Usage, value) {
170						return false
171					}
172					continue
173				case "kind":
174					kind := catalog.KindRepository
175					if r.Asset != nil {
176						kind = r.Asset.Kind
177					}
178					if string(kind) != value {
179						return false
180					}
181					continue
182				}
183			}
184			if !strings.Contains(r.searchText(), term) {
185				return false
186			}
187		}
188		return true
189	}
```

```text
2	// lists. It deliberately matches terms rather than assigning fuzzy scores so
3	// filtering stays predictable across dev's built-in interfaces.
4	package textmatch
5	
6	import "strings"

8	// Terms reports whether every whitespace-separated query term appears in the
9	// haystack, case-insensitively and in any order. An empty query matches all.
10	func Terms(haystack, query string) bool {
11		haystack = strings.ToLower(haystack)
12		query = strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(query))
13		for term := range strings.FieldsSeq(query) {
14			if !strings.Contains(haystack, term) {
15				return false
16			}
17		}

19	}
```

```text
146		if !used || !result.Selected || result.Item.Value == manualStartRepository {
147			return repo.Repo{}, false, nil
148		}
149		selected, ok := byPath[result.Item.Value]
150		if !ok {
151			return repo.Repo{}, false, fmt.Errorf("picker returned an unknown repository")
152		}
153		resolved, err := resolveStartRepository(ctx, app, selected.Path)
154		if err != nil {
155			return repo.Repo{}, false, err
156		}
157		return resolved, true, nil
158	}
```

112	external commands receive candidates on stdin and must return one unchanged

```text
          This flag works identically in both channel mode and ad-hoc mode.
          
          Note that most channels stream entries asynchronously which means that
          knowing if there's only one entry will require waiting for the channel
          to finish loading first.
          
          For most channels and workloads this shouldn't be a problem since the
          loading times are usually very short and will go unnoticed by the user.

      --take-1
          Take the first entry from the list after the channel has finished loading.
          
          This flag works identically in both channel mode and ad-hoc mode.
          
          This will wait for the channel to finish loading all entries and then
          automatically select and output the first entry. Unlike `select_1`, this
          will always take the first entry regardless of how many entries are available.

      --take-1-fast
          Take the first entry from the list as soon as it becomes available.
          
          This flag works identically in both channel mode and ad-hoc mode.
          
          This will immediately select and output the first entry as soon as it
          appears in the results, without waiting for the channel to finish loading.
          This is the fastest option when you just want the first result.

Keybindings:
  -k, --keybindings <STRING>
          Keybindings to override the default keybindings.
          
          This flag works identically in both channel mode and ad-hoc mode.
          
          This can be used to override the default keybindings with a custom subset.
          The keybindings are specified as a semicolon separated list of keybinding
          expressions using the configuration file formalism.
          
          Example: `tv --keybindings='quit="esc";select_next_entry=["down","ctrl-j"]'`

      --expect <STRING>
          Keys that can be used to confirm the current selection in addition to the default ones
          (typically `enter`).
          
          When this is set, confirming the selection will first output an extra line with the key
          that was used to confirm the selection before outputting the selected entry.
          
          Example: `tv --expect='ctrl-q'` will output `ctr-q\n<selected_entry>` when `ctrl-q` is
          pressed to confirm the selection.

Configuration:
      --config-file <PATH>
          Provide a custom configuration file to use.
          
          This flag works identically in both channel mode and ad-hoc mode.

      --cable-dir <PATH>
          Provide a custom cable directory to use.
          
          This flag works identically in both channel mode and ad-hoc mode.

History:
      --global-history
          Use global history instead of channel-specific history.
          
          This flag only works in channel mode.
          
          When enabled, history navigation will show entries from all channels.
          When disabled (default), history navigation is scoped to the current channel.
```

```text
1	// Package picker selects one value from a caller-provided list. It can hand
2	// the terminal to a line-oriented external picker such as fzf, and otherwise
3	// falls back to dev's built-in Bubble Tea interface.
4	package picker
5	
6	import (
7		"bytes"
8		"context"
9		"errors"
10		"fmt"
11		"io"
12		"os/exec"
13		"strings"
14	)
15	
16	// Item is one selectable value. Value is opaque caller data and is never sent
17	// to an external picker; Label and Description are display-only.
18	type Item struct {
19		Value       string
20		Label       string
21		Description string
22	}
23	
24	// Request describes one selection interaction.
25	type Request struct {
26		Prompt       string
27		InitialQuery string
28		Items        []Item
29	}
30	
31	// Result distinguishes a selection from an explicit cancellation.
32	type Result struct {
33		Item     Item
34		Selected bool
35		Canceled bool
36	}
37	
38	// Selector owns the streams and optional external command for one application.
39	type Selector struct {
40		in       io.Reader
41		out      io.Writer
42		errOut   io.Writer
43		command  []string
44		lookPath func(string) (string, error)
45	}
46	
47	// New constructs a selector. command is an argv vector, not a shell command;
48	// an empty vector always selects the built-in backend.
49	func New(in io.Reader, out, errOut io.Writer, command []string) *Selector {
50		return &Selector{
51			in:       in,
52			out:      out,
53			errOut:   errOut,
54			command:  append([]string(nil), command...),
55			lookPath: exec.LookPath,
56		}
57	}
58	
59	// Select uses the configured external picker when it is installed and the
60	// built-in picker otherwise.
61	func (s *Selector) Select(ctx context.Context, request Request) (Result, error) {
62		if len(request.Items) == 0 {
63			return Result{}, nil
64		}
65		if len(s.command) == 0 {
66			return s.selectBuiltin(ctx, request)
67		}
68		path, err := s.lookPath(s.command[0])
69		if err != nil {
70			return s.selectBuiltin(ctx, request)
71		}
72		return s.selectExternal(ctx, path, request)
73	}
74	
75	func (s *Selector) selectExternal(ctx context.Context, path string, request Request) (Result, error) {
76		lines, items := renderCandidates(request.Items)
77		args := make([]string, len(s.command)-1)
78		for index, arg := range s.command[1:] {
79			args[index] = strings.ReplaceAll(arg, "{prompt}", request.Prompt)
80		}
81		cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, path, args...)
82		cmd.Stdin = strings.NewReader(strings.Join(lines, "\n") + "\n")
83		if s.errOut == nil {
84			cmd.Stderr = io.Discard
85		} else {
86			cmd.Stderr = s.errOut
87		}
88		var stdout bytes.Buffer
89		cmd.Stdout = &stdout
90	
91		err := cmd.Run()
92		if ctxErr := ctx.Err(); ctxErr != nil {
93			return Result{}, ctxErr
94		}
95		if err != nil {
96			var exitErr *exec.ExitError
97			if errors.As(err, &exitErr) && (exitErr.ExitCode() == 1 || exitErr.ExitCode() == 130) {
98				return Result{Canceled: true}, nil
99			}
100			return Result{}, fmt.Errorf("external picker: %w", err)
101		}
102	
103		selected, err := selectedLine(stdout.String())
104		if err != nil {
105			return Result{}, err
106		}
107		item, ok := items[selected]
108		if !ok {
109			return Result{}, fmt.Errorf("external picker returned an unknown selection")
110		}
111		return Result{Item: item, Selected: true}, nil
112	}
113	
114	func selectedLine(output string) (string, error) {
115		output = strings.TrimSuffix(output, "\n")
116		output = strings.TrimSuffix(output, "\r")
117		if output == "" || strings.ContainsAny(output, "\r\n\x00") {
118			return "", errors.New("external picker returned malformed output")
119		}
120		return output, nil
121	}
122	
123	func renderCandidates(items []Item) ([]string, map[string]Item) {
124		lines := make([]string, 0, len(items))
125		byLine := make(map[string]Item, len(items))
126		for _, item := range items {
127			label := cleanDisplay(item.Label)
128			if label == "" {
129				label = "(unnamed)"
130			}
131			base := label
132			if description := cleanDisplay(item.Description); description != "" {
133				base += "\t" + description
134			}
135			line := base
136			for ordinal := 2; ; ordinal++ {
137				if _, exists := byLine[line]; !exists {
138					break
139				}
140				line = fmt.Sprintf("%s\t[%d]", base, ordinal)
141			}
142			lines = append(lines, line)
143			byLine[line] = item
144		}
145		return lines, byLine
146	}
147	
148	func cleanDisplay(value string) string {
149		return strings.Join(strings.FieldsFunc(value, func(r rune) bool {
150			return r == '\r' || r == '\n' || r == '\t' || r == 0
151		}), " ")
152	}
153
```

```text
1	package picker
2	
3	import (
4		"context"
5		"fmt"
6		"strings"
7	
8		"github.com/charmbracelet/bubbles/textinput"
9		tea "github.com/charmbracelet/bubbletea"
10		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/textmatch"
11	)
12	
13	const defaultVisibleRows = 10
14	
15	type builtinModel struct {
16		input    textinput.Model
17		items    []Item
18		visible  []int
19		cursor   int
20		offset   int
21		rows     int
22		width    int
23		done     bool
24		canceled bool
25		selected Item
26	}
27	
28	func newBuiltinModel(request Request) builtinModel {
29		input := textinput.New()
30		input.Prompt = fmt.Sprintf("? %s: ", request.Prompt)
31		input.SetValue(request.InitialQuery)
32		input.Focus()
33		model := builtinModel{
34			input: input,
35			items: append([]Item(nil), request.Items...),
36			rows:  defaultVisibleRows,
37		}
38		model.refilter()
39		return model
40	}
41	
42	func (m builtinModel) Init() tea.Cmd {
43		return textinput.Blink
44	}
45	
46	func (m builtinModel) Update(message tea.Msg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
47		switch msg := message.(type) {
48		case tea.WindowSizeMsg:
49			m.width = msg.Width
50			available := msg.Height - 3
51			switch {
52			case available < 1:
53				m.rows = 1
54			case available < defaultVisibleRows:
55				m.rows = available
56			default:
57				m.rows = defaultVisibleRows
58			}
59			m.keepVisible()
60			return m, nil
61		case tea.KeyMsg:
62			switch msg.Type {
63			case tea.KeyEsc, tea.KeyCtrlC:
64				m.done = true
65				m.canceled = true
66				m.input.Blur()
67				return m, tea.Quit
68			case tea.KeyEnter:
69				if len(m.visible) == 0 {
70					return m, nil
71				}
72				m.done = true
73				m.selected = m.items[m.visible[m.cursor]]
74				m.input.Blur()
75				return m, tea.Quit
76			case tea.KeyUp, tea.KeyCtrlP:
77				m.move(-1)
78				return m, nil
79			case tea.KeyDown, tea.KeyCtrlN:
80				m.move(1)
81				return m, nil
82			}
83		}
84	
85		query := m.input.Value()
86		var command tea.Cmd
87		m.input, command = m.input.Update(message)
88		if m.input.Value() != query {
89			m.refilter()
90		}
91		return m, command
92	}
93	
94	func (m builtinModel) View() string {
95		if m.done {
96			return "\n"
97		}
98		var out strings.Builder
99		out.WriteString(m.input.View())
100		out.WriteByte('\n')
101		if len(m.visible) == 0 {
102			out.WriteString("  No matches\n")
103			return out.String()
104		}
105		end := m.offset + m.rows
106		if end > len(m.visible) {
107			end = len(m.visible)
108		}
109		for position := m.offset; position < end; position++ {
110			item := m.items[m.visible[position]]
111			marker := "  "
112			if position == m.cursor {
113				marker = "> "
114			}
115			line := marker + item.Label
116			if item.Description != "" {
117				line += "  " + item.Description
118			}
119			out.WriteString(clipRunes(line, m.width))
120			out.WriteByte('\n')
121		}
122		return out.String()
123	}
124	
125	func (m *builtinModel) refilter() {
126		m.visible = m.visible[:0]
127		for index, item := range m.items {
128			if textmatch.Terms(item.Label+" "+item.Description, m.input.Value()) {
129				m.visible = append(m.visible, index)
130			}
131		}
132		m.cursor = 0
133		m.offset = 0
134	}
135	
136	func (m *builtinModel) move(delta int) {
137		if len(m.visible) == 0 {
138			return
139		}
140		m.cursor += delta
141		if m.cursor < 0 {
142			m.cursor = len(m.visible) - 1
143		}
144		if m.cursor >= len(m.visible) {
145			m.cursor = 0
146		}
147		m.keepVisible()
148	}
149	
150	func (m *builtinModel) keepVisible() {
151		if m.rows <= 0 {
152			m.rows = 1
153		}
154		if m.cursor < m.offset {
155			m.offset = m.cursor
156		}
157		if m.cursor >= m.offset+m.rows {
158			m.offset = m.cursor - m.rows + 1
159		}
160	}
161	
162	func clipRunes(value string, width int) string {
163		if width <= 0 {
164			return value
165		}
166		runes := []rune(value)
167		if len(runes) <= width {
168			return value
169		}
170		if width == 1 {
171			return "…"
172		}
173		return string(runes[:width-1]) + "…"
174	}
175	
176	func (s *Selector) selectBuiltin(ctx context.Context, request Request) (Result, error) {
177		program := tea.NewProgram(
178			newBuiltinModel(request),
179			tea.WithInput(s.in),
180			tea.WithOutput(s.out),
181			tea.WithContext(ctx),
182		)
183		final, err := program.Run()
184		if ctxErr := ctx.Err(); ctxErr != nil {
185			return Result{}, ctxErr
186		}
187		if err != nil {
188			return Result{}, fmt.Errorf("built-in picker: %w", err)
189		}
190		model, ok := final.(builtinModel)
191		if !ok {
192			return Result{}, fmt.Errorf("built-in picker returned an unexpected model")
193		}
194		if model.canceled {
195			return Result{Canceled: true}, nil
196		}
197		if !model.done {
198			return Result{}, nil
199		}
200		return Result{Item: model.selected, Selected: true}, nil
201	}
202
```

```text
13	// pick opens a selector only when both application streams are terminals. The
14	// bool reports whether an interaction was attempted, allowing callers to retain
15	// their deterministic line-oriented fallback for pipes and tests.
16	func (a *App) pick(ctx context.Context, request picker.Request) (picker.Result, bool, error) {
17		if len(request.Items) == 0 {
18			return picker.Result{}, false, nil
19		}

21			result, err := a.pickerSelect(ctx, request)
22			return result, true, err
23		}

25			return picker.Result{}, false, nil
26		}
27		result, err := picker.New(a.In, a.Out, a.Err, a.Cfg.Picker.Command).Select(ctx, request)
28		return result, true, err
```

```text
17	func promptStartRepository(ctx context.Context, app *App, p *prompter, req startRequest) (repo.Repo, error) {
18		if req.RepoExplicit {
19			return resolveStartRepository(ctx, app, req.RepoRef)
20		}
21	
22		var current repo.Repo
23		if r, err := resolveStartRepository(ctx, app, ""); err == nil {
24			current = r
25		}
26		if app.canPick() {
27			selected, ok, err := pickStartRepository(ctx, app, current)
28			if err != nil {
29				return repo.Repo{}, err
30			}
31			if ok {
32				return selected, nil
33			}
34		}
35		if current.Path == "" {
36			all, err := repo.Discover(ctx, app.Cfg.DiscoveryRoots(), repo.DefaultOptions())
37			if err != nil {
38				return repo.Repo{}, err
39			}
40			candidates := all[:0:0]
41			for _, r := range all {
42				if r.HasGit && !r.Bare {
43					candidates = append(candidates, r)
44				}
45			}
46			all = candidates
47			if len(all) == 0 {
48				return repo.Repo{}, errors.New("no non-bare repositories found under paths.scan_roots")
49			}
50			fmt.Fprintln(p.out, p.style.title("Repositories:"))
51			for i, r := range all {
52				fmt.Fprintf(p.out, "  %d) %-24s %s\n", i+1, r.Display(), config.Contract(r.Path))
53			}
54			fallback := ""
55			if len(all) == 1 {
56				fallback = all[0].Display()
57			}
58			for {
59				value, err := p.line("Repository", fallback)
60				if err != nil {
61					return repo.Repo{}, err
62				}
63				if value == "" {
64					fmt.Fprintln(p.out, "  "+p.style.warning("repository is required"))
65					continue
66				}
67				var index int
68				if _, err := fmt.Sscanf(value, "%d", &index); err == nil && index > 0 && index <= len(all) {
69					return all[index-1], nil
70				}
71				r, _, err := repo.Resolve(ctx, app.Cfg.DiscoveryRoots(), value)
72				if err == nil {
73					return r, nil
74				}
75				fmt.Fprintf(p.out, "  %s\n", p.style.warning(err.Error()))
76			}
77		}
78	
79		for {
80			value, err := p.line("Repository", current.Display())
81			if err != nil {
82				return repo.Repo{}, err
83			}
84			if value == current.Display() || value == current.Name || value == current.Path {
85				return current, nil
86			}
87			r, _, err := repo.Resolve(ctx, app.Cfg.DiscoveryRoots(), value)
88			if err == nil {
89				return r, nil
90			}
91			fmt.Fprintf(p.out, "  %s\n", p.style.warning(err.Error()))
92		}
93	}

95	const manualStartRepository = "\x00manual-start-repository"

97	func pickStartRepository(ctx context.Context, app *App, current repo.Repo) (repo.Repo, bool, error) {
98		discovered, err := repo.Discover(ctx, app.Cfg.DiscoveryRoots(), repo.CompletionOptions())
99		if err != nil && current.Path == "" {
100			return repo.Repo{}, false, err
101		}
102	
103		items := make([]picker.Item, 0, len(discovered)+2)
104		byPath := make(map[string]repo.Repo, len(discovered)+1)
105		seen := make(map[string]bool, len(discovered)+1)
106		add := func(repository repo.Repo) {
107			if repository.Path == "" || !repository.HasGit || repository.Bare {
108				return
109			}
110			identity := repository.RealPath
111			if identity == "" {
112				identity = repository.Path
113			}
114			identity = filepath.Clean(identity)
115			if seen[identity] {
116				return
117			}
118			seen[identity] = true
119			byPath[repository.Path] = repository
120			items = append(items, picker.Item{
121				Value:       repository.Path,
122				Label:       repository.Display(),
123				Description: config.Contract(repository.Path),
124			})
125		}
126		add(current)
127		for _, repository := range discovered {
128			add(repository)
129		}
130		if len(items) == 0 {
131			return repo.Repo{}, false, nil
132		}
133		items = append(items, picker.Item{
134			Value:       manualStartRepository,
135			Label:       "Enter a repository name or path manually…",
136			Description: "resolve a repository not present in the discovered list",
137		})
138	
139		result, used, err := app.pick(ctx, picker.Request{Prompt: "Repository", Items: items})
140		if err != nil {
141			return repo.Repo{}, false, err
142		}
143		if result.Canceled {
144			return repo.Repo{}, false, errPromptCanceled
145		}
146		if !used || !result.Selected || result.Item.Value == manualStartRepository {
147			return repo.Repo{}, false, nil
148		}
149		selected, ok := byPath[result.Item.Value]
150		if !ok {
151			return repo.Repo{}, false, fmt.Errorf("picker returned an unknown repository")
152		}
153		resolved, err := resolveStartRepository(ctx, app, selected.Path)
154		if err != nil {
155			return repo.Repo{}, false, err
156		}
157		return resolved, true, nil
158	}

160	func runStartWizard(ctx context.Context, app *App, req startRequest) (*startSpec, bool, error) {
161		p := newPrompter(app)
162		fmt.Fprintln(p.out, p.style.title("Start a tracked change stream"))
163	
164		r, err := promptStartRepository(ctx, app, p, req)
165		if err != nil {
166			return nil, false, err
167		}
168		if r.Bare {
169			return nil, false, fmt.Errorf("%s is a bare repository and cannot host a task checkout", r.Display())
170		}
171		req.RepoRef, req.RepoExplicit = r.Path, true
172	
173		for strings.TrimSpace(req.Name) == "" {
174			req.Name, err = p.line("Task name", "")
175			if err != nil {
176				return nil, false, err
177			}
178			if strings.TrimSpace(req.Name) == "" {
179				fmt.Fprintln(p.out, "  "+p.style.warning("task name is required"))
180			}
181		}
182	
183		for {
184			if !req.ModeExplicit {
185				fallback := "worktree"
186				switch req.Mode {
187				case task.ModeBranch:
188					fallback = "branch-only"
189				case task.ModeDirect:
190					fallback = "direct"
191				}
192				selected, err := p.choice("Mode (w=worktree, b=branch-only, d=direct)", fallback,
193					"worktree (w), branch-only (b), direct (d)", map[string]string{
194						"w": "worktree", "worktree": "worktree",
195						"b": "branch-only", "branch": "branch-only", "branch-only": "branch-only",
196						"d": "direct", "direct": "direct",
197					})
198				if err != nil {
199					return nil, false, err
200				}
201				switch selected {
202				case "direct":
203					req.Mode = task.ModeDirect
204				case "branch-only":
205					req.Mode = task.ModeBranch
206				default:
207					req.Mode = task.ModeWorktree
208				}
209			}
210	
211			if req.Mode == task.ModeDirect {
212				st, statusErr := gitx.StatusOf(ctx, r.Path)
213				if statusErr != nil {
214					return nil, false, statusErr
215				}
216				req.Branch, req.Base = st.Branch, st.Branch
217			} else {
218				if !req.BranchExplicit {
219					fallback := req.Branch
220					if fallback == "" {
221						fallback = "feat/" + config.Slug(req.Name)
222					}
223					req.Branch, err = p.line("Branch", fallback)
224					if err != nil {
225						return nil, false, err
226					}
227				}
228				if !req.BaseExplicit {
229					fallback := req.Base
230					if fallback == "" {
231						fallback = gitx.DefaultBranch(ctx, r.Path)
232					}
233					req.Base, err = p.line("Base", fallback)
234					if err != nil {
235						return nil, false, err
236					}
237				}
238			}
239			if !req.NextExplicit {
240				req.Next, err = p.line("Next action (optional)", req.Next)
241				if err != nil {
242					return nil, false, err
243				}
244			}
245	
246			spec, buildErr := buildStartSpec(ctx, app, req)
247			if buildErr != nil {
248				fmt.Fprintf(p.out, "  %s\n", p.style.warning(buildErr.Error()))
249				if req.BranchExplicit || req.BaseExplicit || req.ModeExplicit {
250					return nil, false, buildErr
251				}
252				req.Branch, req.Base = "", ""
253				continue
254			}
255	
256			rt := app.Runtime()
257			checkout := spec.RepoPath
258			if spec.WorktreePath != "" {
259				checkout = spec.WorktreePath
260			}
261			fmt.Fprintln(p.out, "\n"+p.style.title("Summary"))
262			fmt.Fprintf(p.out, "  %s  %s (%s)\n", p.style.label("repository"), spec.RepoName, config.Contract(spec.RepoPath))
263			fmt.Fprintf(p.out, "  %s        %s\n", p.style.label("task"), spec.Name)
264			fmt.Fprintf(p.out, "  %s        %s\n", p.style.label("mode"), spec.Mode)
265			fmt.Fprintf(p.out, "  %s      %s\n", p.style.label("branch"), spec.Branch)
266			fmt.Fprintf(p.out, "  %s        %s\n", p.style.label("base"), spec.Base)
267			fmt.Fprintf(p.out, "  %s    %s\n", p.style.label("checkout"), config.Contract(checkout))
268			fmt.Fprintf(p.out, "  %s   %s\n", p.style.label("provision"), p.style.success(fmt.Sprint(!spec.NoProvision)))
269			fmt.Fprintf(p.out, "  %s     %s\n", p.style.label("runtime"), p.style.success(rt.Name()))
270			fmt.Fprintf(p.out, "  %s       %s\n", p.style.label("focus"), fmt.Sprint(spec.Focus))
271			if spec.Run != "" {
272				fmt.Fprintf(p.out, "  %s         %s\n", p.style.label("run"), "configured for the new Herdr root pane")
273			}
274			if spec.Next != "" {
275				fmt.Fprintf(p.out, "  %s        %s\n", p.style.label("next"), spec.Next)
276			}
277	
278			confirmed, err := p.confirm("Create this task?", true)
279			if err != nil {
280				return nil, false, err
281			}
282			return spec, confirmed, nil
283		}
284	}
```

```text
153	func promptRepoCloneReference(app *App, p *prompter) (string, error) {
154		manual := func() (string, error) {
155			return p.line("Git URL, path, or owner/name", "")
156		}
157		if !app.canPick() {
158			return manual()
159		}
160	
161		cache, ok := forge.LoadCacheAny(remoteCachePath())
162		sourceID := remoteCacheSourceID(app)
163		if !ok || (cache.SourceID != "" && cache.SourceID != sourceID) {
164			return manual()
165		}
166		items := make([]picker.Item, 0, len(cache.Repos)+1)
167		for _, remote := range cache.Repos {
168			if strings.TrimSpace(remote.CloneURL) == "" {
169				continue
170			}
171			var details []string
172			if remote.Visibility != "" {
173				details = append(details, strings.ToLower(remote.Visibility))
174			}
175			if remote.Archived {
176				details = append(details, "archived")
177			}
178			if remote.Description != "" {
179				details = append(details, truncate(remote.Description, 72))
180			}
181			items = append(items, picker.Item{
182				Value:       remote.CloneURL,
183				Label:       remote.Label(),
184				Description: strings.Join(details, " · "),
185			})
186		}
187		if len(items) == 0 {
188			return manual()
189		}
190		items = append(items, picker.Item{
191			Value:       manualCloneReference,
192			Label:       "Enter a URL, path, or owner/name manually…",
193			Description: "use a source not present in the cached forge inventory",
194		})
195		if !cache.FreshFor(app.Cfg.Forge.CacheTTL.Duration, sourceID) {
196			app.warnf("remote cache is stale or incomplete; run `dev repo remote --refresh` to update picker candidates")
197		}
198		result, used, err := app.pick(ctxOf(), picker.Request{Prompt: "Repository to clone", Items: items})
199		if err != nil {
200			return "", err
201		}
202		if !used || !result.Selected || result.Item.Value == manualCloneReference {
203			if result.Canceled {
204				return "", errPromptCanceled
205			}
206			return manual()
207		}
208		return result.Item.Value, nil
209	}

618	func replaceSetValue(values []string, key, value string) []string {
619		prefix := key + "="
620		result := values[:0]
621		for _, existing := range values {
622			if !strings.HasPrefix(existing, prefix) {
623				result = append(result, existing)
624			}
625		}
626		return append(result, prefix+value)
627	}
628	
629	func removeString(values []string, remove string) []string {
630		result := values[:0]
631		for _, value := range values {
632			if value != remove {
633				result = append(result, value)
634			}
635		}
636		return result
637	}
638	
639	func splitCommaValues(value string) []string {
640		var result []string
641		for _, part := range strings.Split(value, ",") {
642			if trimmed := strings.TrimSpace(part); trimmed != "" {
643				result = append(result, trimmed)
644			}
645		}
646		return result
647	}
648	
649	func defaultString(value, fallback string) string {
650		if value != "" {
651			return value
652		}
653		return fallback
654	}
```

```text
72	// Load reads configuration and prepares the shared stores.
73	func (a *App) Load() error {
74		cfg, err := config.Load(a.configPath)
75		if err != nil {
76			return err
77		}
78		a.Cfg = cfg
79		if a.In == nil {
80			a.In = os.Stdin
81		}
82		if a.Out == nil {
83			a.Out = os.Stdout
84		}
85		if a.Err == nil {
86			a.Err = os.Stderr
87		}
88		a.Tasks = task.NewStore(cfg.TasksDir())
89		a.Catalog = catalog.NewStore(cfg.AssetsDir(), catalog.WithDiagnosticSink(func(diagnostic catalog.Diagnostic) {
90			fmt.Fprintf(a.Err, "%s %s\n", a.errStyle().warning("dev: warning:"), diagnostic.Error())
91		}))
92		a.Registry = catalog.NewRegistry(a.Catalog)
93		noteStore := note.NewStore(cfg.NotesDir(), note.WithDiagnosticSink(func(path string, err error) {
94			fmt.Fprintf(a.Err, "dev: warning: skipping note %s: %v\n", filepath.Base(path), err)
95		}))
96		a.Notes = note.NewService(noteStore, cfg.NotesIndexFile())
97		a.Notes.IndexDiagnostic = func(err error) {
98			fmt.Fprintf(a.Err, "dev: warning: note search index: %v\n", err)
99		}
100		if a.Sizes == nil {
101			cache := diskusage.NewCache(filepath.Join(config.CacheHome(), "dev", "sizes-v1.json"), 10*time.Minute)
102			a.Sizes = diskusage.NewManager(cache, 2)
103		}
104		return nil
105	}

114	// Runtime resolves the multiplexer backend for this invocation, honouring
115	// --runtime and --no-runtime.
116	func (a *App) Runtime() runtime.Runtime {
117		if a.runtimeInstance != nil {
118			return a.runtimeInstance
119		}
120		if a.noRuntime {
121			return runtime.None{}
122		}
123		backend := a.Cfg.Runtime.Backend
124		if a.runtimeOverride != "" {
125			backend = a.runtimeOverride
126		}
127		return a.runtimeNamed(backend)
128	}
129	
130	// runtimeNamed resolves the backend that owns a persisted opaque handle. It
131	// deliberately bypasses the current backend override: feeding a Herdr handle to
132	// tmux after a config change is never valid.
133	func (a *App) runtimeNamed(name string) runtime.Runtime {
134		if rt := a.runtimesByName[name]; rt != nil {
135			return rt
136		}
137		if a.runtimeInstance != nil && (name == "" || a.runtimeInstance.Name() == name) {
138			return a.runtimeInstance
139		}
140		rt := runtime.Select(name)
141		if h, ok := rt.(*runtime.Herdr); ok {
142			return h.WithMetadataSource(a.Cfg.Runtime.MetadataSource)
143		}
144		return rt
145	}

152	// warnf writes a non-fatal notice to stderr, so it never pollutes piped output.
153	func (a *App) warnf(format string, args ...any) {
154		message := fmt.Sprintf(format, args...)
155		fmt.Fprintf(a.Err, "%s %s\n", a.errStyle().warning("dev:"), message)
156	}

158	// cdDirective asks the shell wrapper to move its parent process. The wrapper
159	// gives dev a child-only file descriptor so normal output stays connected to
160	// the terminal and an inherited environment variable can never name a file to
161	// overwrite. NUL terminates the path because filesystem paths may contain
162	// newlines. Without the wrapper, retain the printable directive used by older
163	// integrations.
164	func (a *App) cdDirective(dir string) error {
165		// Windows shells do not inherit an extra descriptor the way the POSIX
166		// wrapper's `3>file` redirection does, so the PowerShell wrapper names a
167		// temp file instead and reads it back after dev exits.
168		if path := os.Getenv("DEV_SHELL_CD_FILE"); path != "" {
169			return os.WriteFile(path, append([]byte(dir), 0), 0o600)
170		}
171		if rawFD := os.Getenv("DEV_SHELL_CD_FD"); rawFD != "" {
172			fd, err := strconv.Atoi(rawFD)
173			if err != nil || fd < 3 {
174				return fmt.Errorf("invalid DEV_SHELL_CD_FD %q", rawFD)
175			}
176			file := os.NewFile(uintptr(fd), "dev-shell-cd")
177			if file == nil {
178				return fmt.Errorf("invalid shell directory descriptor %d", fd)
179			}
180			if _, err := file.Write(append([]byte(dir), 0)); err != nil {
181				return fmt.Errorf("write shell directory directive: %w", err)
182			}
183			if err := file.Close(); err != nil {
184				return fmt.Errorf("close shell directory directive: %w", err)
185			}
186			return nil
187		}
188		_, err := fmt.Fprintf(a.Out, "cd %s\n", shellQuote(dir))
189		return err
190	}
191	
192	// ctx is the cancellable context commands run under.
193	func ctxOf() context.Context { return context.Background() }
```

```text
160	
161		cache, ok := forge.LoadCacheAny(remoteCachePath())
162		sourceID := remoteCacheSourceID(app)
163		if !ok || (cache.SourceID != "" && cache.SourceID != sourceID) {
164			return manual()
165		}
166		items := make([]picker.Item, 0, len(cache.Repos)+1)
167		for _, remote := range cache.Repos {
168			if strings.TrimSpace(remote.CloneURL) == "" {
169				continue
170			}
171			var details []string
172			if remote.Visibility != "" {
173				details = append(details, strings.ToLower(remote.Visibility))
174			}
175			if remote.Archived {
176				details = append(details, "archived")
177			}
178			if remote.Description != "" {
179				details = append(details, truncate(remote.Description, 72))
180			}
```

```text
123	func renderCandidates(items []Item) ([]string, map[string]Item) {
124		lines := make([]string, 0, len(items))
125		byLine := make(map[string]Item, len(items))
126		for _, item := range items {
127			label := cleanDisplay(item.Label)
128			if label == "" {
129				label = "(unnamed)"
130			}
131			base := label
132			if description := cleanDisplay(item.Description); description != "" {
133				base += "\t" + description
134			}

136			for ordinal := 2; ; ordinal++ {

139				}
140				line = fmt.Sprintf("%s\t[%d]", base, ordinal)
141			}

143			byLine[line] = item
144		}
145		return lines, byLine
146	}
```

```text
97	func pickStartRepository(ctx context.Context, app *App, current repo.Repo) (repo.Repo, bool, error) {
98		discovered, err := repo.Discover(ctx, app.Cfg.DiscoveryRoots(), repo.CompletionOptions())
99		if err != nil && current.Path == "" {
100			return repo.Repo{}, false, err
101		}
102	
103		items := make([]picker.Item, 0, len(discovered)+2)
104		byPath := make(map[string]repo.Repo, len(discovered)+1)
105		seen := make(map[string]bool, len(discovered)+1)
106		add := func(repository repo.Repo) {
107			if repository.Path == "" || !repository.HasGit || repository.Bare {
108				return
109			}
110			identity := repository.RealPath
111			if identity == "" {
112				identity = repository.Path
113			}
114			identity = filepath.Clean(identity)
115			if seen[identity] {
116				return
117			}
118			seen[identity] = true
119			byPath[repository.Path] = repository
120			items = append(items, picker.Item{
121				Value:       repository.Path,
122				Label:       repository.Display(),
123				Description: config.Contract(repository.Path),
124			})
125		}
126		add(current)
127		for _, repository := range discovered {
128			add(repository)
129		}
130		if len(items) == 0 {
131			return repo.Repo{}, false, nil
132		}
133		items = append(items, picker.Item{
134			Value:       manualStartRepository,
135			Label:       "Enter a repository name or path manually…",
136			Description: "resolve a repository not present in the discovered list",
137		})
138	
139		result, used, err := app.pick(ctx, picker.Request{Prompt: "Repository", Items: items})

142		}

154		if err != nil {

156		}
157		return resolved, true, nil
158	}
```

```text
1	// Package repo discovers the repositories a user actually owns by walking the
2	// configured scan roots. It answers "what projects do I have?", which is a
3	// different question from "what am I working on?" — that one belongs to
4	// package task.
5	package repo
6	
7	import (
8		"context"
9		"io/fs"
10		"os"
11		"path/filepath"
12		"sort"
13		"strings"
14	
15		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/gitx"
16	)
17	
18	// Repo is one discovered repository.
19	type Repo struct {
20		// Name is the directory basename, which is how users refer to it.
21		Name string
22		// Path is the absolute path reached through the scan root. It may be a
23		// symlink from a bootstrap index; commands intentionally keep that human
24		// navigation path rather than replacing it with the physical one.
25		Path string
26		// RealPath is the physical checkout path.
27		RealPath string
28		// Symlink reports that Path is an alias to RealPath.
29		Symlink bool
30		// Root is the scan root it was found under.
31		Root string
32		// Category is the path between the scan root and the repo ("Quant",
33		// "Web/Frontend"), empty for a repo sitting directly in the root. It is
34		// human organisation metadata, preserved for `dev graduate` to place new
35		// projects consistently.
36		Category string
37		// GitDir is this checkout's administrative directory; CommonDir is shared
38		// by every linked worktree of the clone.
39		GitDir    string
40		CommonDir string
41		MainRoot  string
42		// Bare reports a bare repository (a worktree hub).
43		Bare bool
44		// HasGit distinguishes a real repo from a plain directory that was found
45		// in a scan root; non-repos are reported so `dev repo list` can offer to
46		// initialise them.
47		HasGit bool
48	}
49	
50	// Display renders "Category/Name" or just "Name".
51	func (r Repo) Display() string {
52		if r.Category == "" {
53			return r.Name
54		}
55		return r.Category + "/" + r.Name
56	}
57	
58	// Options tunes discovery.
59	type Options struct {
60		// MaxDepth limits how deep below a scan root a repo may be found. The
61		// default layout is <root>/<Category>/<Repo>, so 2 suffices; 3 leaves room
62		// for a nested grouping without walking an entire home directory.
63		MaxDepth int
64		// IncludeNonRepos reports plain directories alongside repositories.
65		IncludeNonRepos bool
66		// Fast avoids per-repository git subprocesses. It is intended for shell
67		// completion: direct .git-file checkouts are skipped as linked worktrees and
68		// symlink aliases are deduplicated by their physical path.
69		Fast bool
70	}
71	
72	// DefaultOptions is the discovery configuration used by dev's commands.
73	func DefaultOptions() Options { return Options{MaxDepth: 3} }
74	
75	// CompletionOptions trades full Git metadata for interactive latency.
76	func CompletionOptions() Options { return Options{MaxDepth: 3, Fast: true} }
77	
78	// skipDirs are never descended into. These are large, never contain a project
79	// the user organises by hand, and walking them dominates scan time.
80	var skipDirs = map[string]bool{
81		"node_modules": true, ".venv": true, "venv": true, "target": true,
82		"vendor": true, "__pycache__": true, ".tox": true, "dist": true,
83		"build": true, ".next": true, ".cache": true, ".terraform": true,
84		"Library": true, ".Trash": true,
85	}
86	
87	// Discover walks every root and returns the repositories found, sorted by
88	// display name. Unreadable directories are skipped rather than fatal — a scan
89	// root that has been unmounted must not break `dev ls`.
90	func Discover(ctx context.Context, roots []string, opts Options) ([]Repo, error) {
91		if opts.MaxDepth <= 0 {
92			opts.MaxDepth = DefaultOptions().MaxDepth
93		}
94		seen := map[string]bool{}
95		// clone identities stop a physical path and a symlink index from showing
96		// the same repository twice. The first scan root wins, which lets users
97		// choose whether the curated index or the physical hierarchy is their UI
98		// simply by ordering scan_roots.
99		identities := map[string]bool{}
100		var out []Repo
101	
102		for _, root := range roots {
103			info, err := os.Stat(root)
104			if err != nil || !info.IsDir() {
105				continue // a missing scan root is normal on a fresh machine
106			}
107			rootClean := filepath.Clean(root)
108	
109			err = filepath.WalkDir(rootClean, func(path string, d fs.DirEntry, err error) error {
110				if err != nil {
111					return nil // unreadable entry: skip, keep walking
112				}
113				if ctx.Err() != nil {
114					return ctx.Err()
115				}
116				isRoot := path == rootClean
117				name := d.Name()
118				isLink := d.Type()&os.ModeSymlink != 0
119				isDir := d.IsDir()
120				if isLink {
121					// WalkDir does not follow symlinks. Inspect a direct symlink to
122					// a repository, but do not recurse through arbitrary symlinked
123					// containers — bootstrap does that with cycle detection.
124					if info, err := os.Stat(path); err == nil {
125						isDir = info.IsDir()
126					}
127				}
128				if !isDir {
129					return nil
130				}
131				if !isRoot && (skipDirs[name] || (strings.HasPrefix(name, ".") && name != ".bare")) {
132					return filepath.SkipDir
133				}
134	
135				rel := "."
136				depth := 0
137				if !isRoot {
138					rel, _ = filepath.Rel(rootClean, path)
139					depth = len(strings.Split(rel, string(filepath.Separator)))
140				}
141	
142				if isRepoDir(path) {
143					real, _ := filepath.EvalSymlinks(path)
144					if real == "" {
145						real = path
146					}
147					bare := isBareDir(path)
148					identity, gitDir, commonDir, mainRoot := real, real, real, real
149					if !bare && opts.Fast && gitEntryIsFile(path) {
150						// A direct .git file at a discovered root is a linked
151						// worktree. Submodules are already hidden below their parent
152						// repository because discovery never descends into one.
153						return filepath.SkipDir
154					}
155					if !bare && !opts.Fast {
156						if g, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, path); err == nil {
157							// A linked worktree is execution state, not another
158							// project in the repo inventory.
159							if g.IsLinkedWorktree {
160								return filepath.SkipDir
161							}
162							identity, gitDir, commonDir, mainRoot = g.GitCommonDir, g.GitDir, g.GitCommonDir, g.MainRoot
163							real = g.MainRoot
164						}
165					}
166					if !seen[path] && !identities[identity] {
167						seen[path], identities[identity] = true, true
168						out = append(out, Repo{
169							Name:      name,
170							Path:      path,
171							RealPath:  real,
172							Symlink:   isLink,
173							Root:      rootClean,
174							Category:  filepath.ToSlash(filepath.Dir(rel)),
175							GitDir:    gitDir,
176							CommonDir: commonDir,
177							MainRoot:  mainRoot,
178							Bare:      bare,
179							HasGit:    true,
180						})
181					}
182					// Never descend into a repo: its subdirectories are source
183					// code, and any nested .git is a submodule or a worktree that
184					// belongs to this repo, not a project of its own.
185					return filepath.SkipDir
186				}
187				if depth >= opts.MaxDepth {
188					return filepath.SkipDir
189				}
190				if opts.IncludeNonRepos && depth == 1 {
191					if !seen[path] {
192						seen[path] = true
193						out = append(out, Repo{Name: name, Path: path, Root: rootClean, Category: ""})
194					}
195				}
196				return nil
197			})
198			if err != nil && ctx.Err() != nil {
199				return out, ctx.Err()
200			}
201		}
202	
203		for i := range out {
204			if out[i].Category == "." {
205				out[i].Category = ""
206			}
207		}
208		sort.Slice(out, func(i, j int) bool {
209			if out[i].Name != out[j].Name {
210				return strings.ToLower(out[i].Name) < strings.ToLower(out[j].Name)
211			}
212			return out[i].Path < out[j].Path
213		})
214		return out, nil
215	}
216	
217	// isRepoDir reports whether path is a repository root: it holds a .git entry
218	// (directory for a normal clone, file for a linked worktree or submodule).
219	func isRepoDir(path string) bool {
220		if _, err := os.Lstat(filepath.Join(path, ".git")); err == nil {
221			return true
222		}
223		return isBareDir(path)
224	}
225	
226	func gitEntryIsFile(path string) bool {
227		info, err := os.Lstat(filepath.Join(path, ".git"))
228		return err == nil && info.Mode().IsRegular()
229	}
230	
231	// isBareDir recognises a bare repository by its skeleton, without shelling out.
232	func isBareDir(path string) bool {
233		for _, marker := range []string{"HEAD", "objects", "refs"} {
234			if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(path, marker)); err != nil {
235				return false
236			}
237		}
238		return true
239	}
240	
241	// Resolve finds a repo by name, display name, or path.
242	//
243	// Matching is deliberately layered: an exact name or path wins outright, and
244	// only then does a substring search run — so a repo literally named "web"
245	// is never shadowed by "web-frontend".
246	func Resolve(ctx context.Context, roots []string, ref string) (Repo, []Repo, error) {
247		return resolve(ctx, roots, ref, DefaultOptions())
248	}
249	
250	// ResolveCompletion resolves the same references without launching one Git
251	// process per repository in the scan roots.
252	func ResolveCompletion(ctx context.Context, roots []string, ref string) (Repo, []Repo, error) {
253		return resolve(ctx, roots, ref, CompletionOptions())
254	}
255	
256	func resolve(ctx context.Context, roots []string, ref string, opts Options) (Repo, []Repo, error) {
257		all, err := Discover(ctx, roots, opts)
258		if err != nil {
259			return Repo{}, nil, err
260		}
261		if abs, err := filepath.Abs(ref); err == nil {
262			if g, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, abs); err == nil {
263				real, _ := filepath.EvalSymlinks(abs)
264				if real == "" {
265					real = g.MainRoot
266				}
267				// Preserve an explicit navigation alias. The caller named this
268				// path on purpose; resolving it to the physical checkout would
269				// defeat a bootstrap symlink catalog.
270				return Repo{
271					Name: filepath.Base(abs), Path: abs, RealPath: real,
272					Symlink: real != abs, CommonDir: g.GitCommonDir, HasGit: true, Bare: g.Bare,
273				}, nil, nil
274			}
275		}
276		for _, r := range all {
277			if r.Name == ref || r.Display() == ref || r.Path == ref {
278				return r, nil, nil
279			}
280		}
281		needle := strings.ToLower(ref)
282		var hits []Repo
283		for _, r := range all {
284			if strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(r.Display()), needle) {
285				hits = append(hits, r)
286			}
287		}
288		switch len(hits) {
289		case 1:
290			return hits[0], nil, nil
291		case 0:
292			return Repo{}, nil, &NotFoundError{Ref: ref}
293		default:
294			return Repo{}, hits, &AmbiguousError{Ref: ref, Candidates: hits}
295		}
296	}
297	
298	// NotFoundError reports a repo reference that matched nothing.
299	type NotFoundError struct{ Ref string }
300	
301	func (e *NotFoundError) Error() string { return "no repository matching " + e.Ref }
302	
303	// AmbiguousError reports a repo reference that matched several repos.
304	type AmbiguousError struct {
305		Ref        string
306		Candidates []Repo
307	}
308	
309	func (e *AmbiguousError) Error() string {
310		names := make([]string, len(e.Candidates))
311		for i, c := range e.Candidates {
312			names[i] = c.Display()
313		}
314		return e.Ref + " is ambiguous: " + strings.Join(names, ", ")
315	}
```
