```text
153	func promptRepoCloneReference(app *App, p *prompter) (string, error) {
154		manual := func() (string, error) {
155			return p.line("Git URL, path, or owner/name", "")
156		}
157		if !app.canPick() {
158			return manual()
159		}
160	
161		cache, ok := forge.LoadCacheAny(remoteCachePath())
162		sourceID := remoteCacheSourceID(app)
163		if !ok || (cache.SourceID != "" && cache.SourceID != sourceID) {
164			return manual()
165		}
166		items := make([]picker.Item, 0, len(cache.Repos)+1)
167		for _, remote := range cache.Repos {
168			if strings.TrimSpace(remote.CloneURL) == "" {
169				continue
170			}
171			var details []string
172			if remote.Visibility != "" {
173				details = append(details, strings.ToLower(remote.Visibility))
174			}
175			if remote.Archived {
176				details = append(details, "archived")
177			}
178			if remote.Description != "" {
179				details = append(details, truncate(remote.Description, 72))
180			}
181			items = append(items, picker.Item{
182				Value:       remote.CloneURL,
183				Label:       remote.Label(),
184				Description: strings.Join(details, " · "),
185			})
186		}
187		if len(items) == 0 {
188			return manual()
189		}
190		items = append(items, picker.Item{
191			Value:       manualCloneReference,
192			Label:       "Enter a URL, path, or owner/name manually…",
193			Description: "use a source not present in the cached forge inventory",
194		})
195		if !cache.FreshFor(app.Cfg.Forge.CacheTTL.Duration, sourceID) {
196			app.warnf("remote cache is stale or incomplete; run `dev repo remote --refresh` to update picker candidates")
197		}
198		result, used, err := app.pick(ctxOf(), picker.Request{Prompt: "Repository to clone", Items: items})
199		if err != nil {
200			return "", err
201		}
202		if !used || !result.Selected || result.Item.Value == manualCloneReference {
203			if result.Canceled {
204				return "", errPromptCanceled
205			}
206			return manual()
207		}
208		return result.Item.Value, nil
209	}

488	func promptUpstream(app *App, p *prompter, name string, flags *repoBootstrapFlags) error {
489		create, err := p.confirm("Create a GitHub/GitLab upstream?", flags.remote)
490		if err != nil || !create {
491			flags.remote = false
492			return err
493		}
494		ready := forge.ProbeAll(ctxOf())
495		var available []forge.Readiness
496		for _, candidate := range ready {
497			if candidate.Ready() {
498				available = append(available, candidate)
499			} else {
500				fmt.Fprintf(p.out, "  %s: %s (%s)\n", candidate.Forge, candidate.Status, candidate.Action)
501			}
502		}
503		if len(available) == 0 {
504			fmt.Fprintln(p.out, "  "+p.style.warning("no authenticated GitHub or GitLab CLI is ready; creating locally only"))
505			flags.remote = false
506			return nil
507		}
508		selected := available[0].Forge
509		if len(available) > 1 {
510			choices := map[string]string{"github": "github", "gh": "github", "gitlab": "gitlab", "gl": "gitlab"}
511			choice, err := p.choice("Forge (github/gitlab)", string(selected), "github, gitlab", choices)
512			if err != nil {
513				return err
514			}
515			selected = forge.Kind(choice)
516		}
517		flags.remote = true
518		flags.forge = string(selected)
519		flags.namespace, err = p.line("Owner / organization / namespace (optional)", flags.namespace)
520		if err != nil {
521			return err
522		}
523		flags.visibility, err = p.choice("Visibility (private/public/internal)", "private",
524			"private, public, internal", map[string]string{
525				"private": "private", "public": "public", "internal": "internal",
526			})
527		if err != nil {
528			return err
529		}
530		flags.push, err = p.confirm("Push the initial branch?", true)
531		_ = name
532		return err
533	}
```

```text
97	func pickStartRepository(ctx context.Context, app *App, current repo.Repo) (repo.Repo, bool, error) {

109			}
```

```text
48	// an empty vector always selects the built-in backend.
49	func New(in io.Reader, out, errOut io.Writer, command []string) *Selector {
50		return &Selector{
51			in:       in,
52			out:      out,
53			errOut:   errOut,
54			command:  append([]string(nil), command...),
55			lookPath: exec.LookPath,
56		}
57	}

63			return Result{}, nil
64		}
65		if len(s.command) == 0 {
66			return s.selectBuiltin(ctx, request)

69		if err != nil {
```

```text
160		}
161		return IsChild(canonicalRoot, canonicalCandidate)
162	}
163	
164	// ValidateComponent requires a non-empty relative value containing exactly one
165	// path component. Both slash styles are rejected so state synced between Unix
166	// and Windows cannot acquire a different meaning on another host.
167	func ValidateComponent(component string) error {
168		switch {
169		case strings.TrimSpace(component) == "":
170			return fmt.Errorf("empty component: %w", ErrInvalidComponent)
171		case strings.ContainsRune(component, '\x00'):
172			return fmt.Errorf("component contains NUL: %w", ErrInvalidComponent)
173		case component == "." || component == "..":
174			return fmt.Errorf("component %q is reserved: %w", component, ErrInvalidComponent)
175		case filepath.IsAbs(component) || filepath.VolumeName(component) != "" || driveQualified(component):
176			return fmt.Errorf("component %q is absolute or drive-qualified: %w", component, ErrInvalidComponent)
177		case strings.ContainsAny(component, `/\\`):
178			return fmt.Errorf("component %q contains a path separator: %w", component, ErrInvalidComponent)
179		case filepath.Clean(component) != component || filepath.Base(component) != component:
180			return fmt.Errorf("component %q is not a single clean name: %w", component, ErrInvalidComponent)
181		default:
182			return nil
183		}
184	}
185	
186	// PortablePathLimits bounds the encoded path, each encoded component, and path
187	// depth. Zero means unbounded for that field; negative values are invalid.
188	// File-count and byte-size ceilings live in safefile because they describe a
189	// collection of files rather than a path.
```

```text
18	// CreatePR opens a GitHub pull request.
19	func (g *gh) CreatePR(ctx context.Context, dir string, req PRRequest) (string, error) {
20		if !g.Available() {
21			return "", &ErrNoCLI{Kind: GitHub, Bin: "gh"}
22		}
23		args := []string{"pr", "create", "--base", req.Base, "--head", req.Head}
24		switch {
25		case req.Title != "":
26			args = append(args, "--title", req.Title, "--body", req.Body)
27		default:
28			// --fill derives title and body from the branch's commits, which is
29			// the right default for a solo workflow where the commits already say
30			// what happened.
31			args = append(args, "--fill")
32		}
33		if req.Draft {
34			args = append(args, "--draft")
35		}
36		if req.Web {
37			args = append(args, "--web")
38		}
39		out, err := run(ctx, "gh", dir, args...)
40		return lastURL(out), err
41	}

43	// CreateRepo creates a GitHub repository from the local checkout.
44	func (g *gh) CreateRepo(ctx context.Context, dir string, req RepoRequest) (string, error) {
45		if !g.Available() {
46			return "", &ErrNoCLI{Kind: GitHub, Bin: "gh"}
47		}
48		target, err := resolveRepoRequest(req)
49		if err != nil {
50			return "", err
51		}
52		args := []string{"repo", "create", target.fullName, "--source", ".", "--remote", target.remoteName,
53			visibilityFlag(target.visibility)}
54		if req.Description != "" {
55			args = append(args, "--description", req.Description)
56		}
57		if req.Push {
58			args = append(args, "--push")
59		}
60		out, err := run(ctx, "gh", dir, args...)
61		return lastURL(out), err
62	}

65	// not pass --source, --remote or --push, leaving all local Git mutations to the

67	func (g *gh) PublishRepo(ctx context.Context, dir string, req RepoRequest) (CreateRepoResult, error) {

100	// lines before the created resource's address.
101	func lastURL(out string) string {
102		found := lastHTTPURL(out)
103		if found == "" {
104			return strings.TrimSpace(out)
105		}
106		return found
107	}
108	
109	// ListRepos lists GitHub repositories visible to the authenticated user —
110	// owned, collaborated on, and organisation membership — most recently pushed
111	// first. gh api is intentionally used instead of a custom HTTP client:
112	// authentication and token refresh stay owned by the forge CLI.
113	func (g *gh) ListRepos(ctx context.Context) ([]RemoteRepo, error) {
114		if !g.Available() {
115			return nil, &ErrNoCLI{Kind: GitHub, Bin: "gh"}
116		}
117		ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, 60*time.Second)
118		defer cancel()
119		const pageSize = 100
120		var result []RemoteRepo
121		for page := 1; ; page++ {
122			out, err := run(ctx, "gh", "", "api", "user/repos", "--method", "GET",
123				"-f", "per_page=100", "-f", fmt.Sprintf("page=%d", page),
124				"-f", "sort=pushed", "-f", "direction=desc")
125			if err != nil {
126				return result, err
127			}
128			repos, err := parseGitHubRepos(out)
129			if err != nil {
130				return result, err
131			}
132			result = append(result, repos...)
133			if len(repos) < pageSize {
134				break
135			}
136		}
137		return result, nil
138	}
139	
140	func parseGitHubRepos(out string) ([]RemoteRepo, error) {
141		var raw []struct {
142			Name          string `json:"name"`
143			FullName      string `json:"full_name"`
144			Description   string `json:"description"`
145			URL           string `json:"html_url"`
146			CloneURL      string `json:"clone_url"`
147			SSHURL        string `json:"ssh_url"`
148			Visibility    string `json:"visibility"`
149			Fork          bool   `json:"fork"`
150			Archived      bool   `json:"archived"`
151			PushedAt      string `json:"pushed_at"`
152			DefaultBranch string `json:"default_branch"`
153		}
154		if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(out), &raw); err != nil {
155			return nil, fmt.Errorf("decode gh api user/repos: %w", err)
156		}
157		result := make([]RemoteRepo, 0, len(raw))
158		for _, r := range raw {
159			updated, _ := time.Parse(time.RFC3339, r.PushedAt)
160			result = append(result, RemoteRepo{
161				Forge: GitHub, Name: r.Name, FullName: r.FullName,
162				Description: r.Description, URL: r.URL,
163				CloneURL: r.CloneURL, SSHURL: r.SSHURL,
164				Visibility: r.Visibility, DefaultBranch: r.DefaultBranch,
165				Archived: r.Archived, Fork: r.Fork, UpdatedAt: updated,
166			})
167		}
168		return result, nil
169	}
```

```text
256	func resolve(ctx context.Context, roots []string, ref string, opts Options) (Repo, []Repo, error) {
257		all, err := Discover(ctx, roots, opts)
```

```text
// taskSearchText is what a filter query matches a task row against.
func taskSearchText(r inventory.Row) string {
	t := r.Task
	return strings.ToLower(strings.Join([]string{
		t.Title(), t.Repo, t.Branch, t.Next, t.Note, string(t.State),
	}, " "))
}

// matches reports whether every whitespace-separated term of the query appears
// in the haystack.
//
// Term-wise rather than substring so "auth api" finds a task named "api token
// auth" — the order words come to mind in is rarely the order they appear in.
func matches(haystack, query string) bool {
	query = strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(query))
	if query == "" {
		return true
	}
	for _, term := range strings.Fields(query) {
		if !strings.Contains(haystack, term) {
			return false
		}
	}
	return true
}
```

```text
59			case task.Hot:
60				if !r.Live() {
61					return "no live session"
62				}
63			case task.Warm, task.Cold:
64				if r.Live() {
65					return "session is live"
66				}
67			}
68		}
69		if r.Task.State == task.Cold && r.CheckoutExists && r.Task.WorktreePath != "" {
70			return "worktree still on disk"
71		}
72		if r.WorktreeMissing {
73			return "worktree is gone"
74		}
75		return ""
76	}
77	
78	// Age is how long since the task's last commit, falling back to when the entry
79	// was last written for a task with no commits of its own.
80	func (r Row) Age() time.Duration {
81		ref := r.LastCommit
82		if ref.IsZero() || r.Task.Updated.After(ref) {
83			ref = r.Task.Updated
84		}
85		if ref.IsZero() {
86			return 0
87		}
88		return time.Since(ref)
89	}
90	
91	// Options tunes what a Collect call spends time on.
92	type Options struct {
93		// SkipRuntime avoids querying the multiplexer, for callers that only need
94		// git facts (and for tests).
95		SkipRuntime bool
96		// SkipGit avoids running git per task, for a fast listing.
97		SkipGit bool
98		// Sessions lets a coordinating caller share one runtime query across task,
99		// repository, and Try inventories.
100		Sessions        []runtime.Session
101		SessionsSet     bool
102		SessionsTracked bool
103		// Limiter shares one process-heavy enrichment bound across collectors.
104		Limiter *Limiter
105	}
106	
107	// Collect builds the enriched inventory. Git probes run concurrently: each is
108	// a handful of process spawns, and a machine with dozens of tasks would
109	// otherwise make `dev ls` feel slow.
110	func Collect(ctx context.Context, tasks []*task.Task, rt runtime.Runtime, opts Options) []Row {
111		rows := make([]Row, len(tasks))
112	
113		sessions := opts.Sessions
114		tracked := opts.SessionsTracked
115		if !opts.SessionsSet && !opts.SkipRuntime && rt != nil && rt.Name() != "none" {
116			if s, err := rt.List(ctx); err == nil {
117				sessions, tracked = s, true
118			}
119		}
120	
121		var wg sync.WaitGroup
122		// Bound concurrency: git is process-heavy and an unbounded fan-out over a
123		// large inventory would thrash. Coordinated TUI loads share this limiter with
124		// repository enrichment.
125		limiter := opts.Limiter
126		if limiter == nil {
127			limiter = NewLimiter(8)
128		}
129	
130		for i, t := range tasks {
131			rows[i].Task = t
132			rows[i].Checkout = checkoutOf(t)
133	
134			if opts.SkipGit || rows[i].Checkout == "" {
135				continue
136			}
137			wg.Add(1)
138			go func(i int) {
139				defer wg.Done()
140				release, ok := limiter.Acquire(ctx)
141				if !ok {
142					return
143				}
144				defer release()
145				enrich(ctx, &rows[i])
146			}(i)
147		}
148		wg.Wait()
149	
150		for i := range rows {
151			rows[i].Session = matchSession(sessions, rows[i])
152			rows[i].sessionsTracked = tracked
153		}
154		return rows
155	}
156	
157	func checkoutOf(t *task.Task) string {
158		if t.WorktreePath != "" {
159			return t.WorktreePath
160		}
161		return t.RepoPath
162	}
163	
164	func enrich(ctx context.Context, r *Row) {
165		info, err := os.Stat(r.Checkout)
166		r.CheckoutExists = err == nil && info.IsDir()
167		if !r.CheckoutExists {
168			if r.Task.WorktreePath != "" {
169				r.WorktreeMissing = true
170			}
171			return
172		}
173		if st, err := gitx.StatusOf(ctx, r.Checkout); err != nil {
174			r.StatusErr = err
175		} else {
176			r.Status = st
177		}
178		if unix, _, err := gitx.LastCommit(ctx, r.Checkout); err == nil && unix > 0 {
179			r.LastCommit = time.Unix(unix, 0)
180		}
```

```text
26		}
```

The “fast” option only removes per-repository Git subprocesses; it does not cache discovery or cap directory count/time. The walk is depth-limited to three path components and skips known heavy/hidden directories, but synchronously enumerates every eligible directory at those levels (including filesystem probes), so a broad or network-mounted root can still delay picker startup without an item/count/deadline bound.

```go
package devtuimatchbench

import (
	"fmt"
	"strings"
	"testing"
)

var matched bool

func oldMatches(haystack, query string) bool {
	query = strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(query))
	if query == "" {
		return true
	}
	for _, term := range strings.Fields(query) {
		if !strings.Contains(haystack, term) {
			return false
		}
	}
	return true
}

func currentMatches(haystack, query string) bool {
	haystack = strings.ToLower(haystack)
	query = strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(query))
	for term := range strings.FieldsSeq(query) {
		if !strings.Contains(haystack, term) {
			return false
		}
	}
	return true
}

func BenchmarkMatch(b *testing.B) {
	for _, size := range []int{64, 128, 256, 512} {
		haystack := strings.Repeat("repository task branch next note hot ", size/37+1)[:size]
		for _, query := range []string{"", "repository hot"} {
			label := "terms"
			if query == "" { label = "empty" }
			b.Run(fmt.Sprintf("old/%s/%dB", label, size), func(b *testing.B) {
				var result bool
				b.ReportAllocs()
				for b.Loop() { result = oldMatches(haystack, query) }
				matched = result
			})
			b.Run(fmt.Sprintf("current/%s/%dB", label, size), func(b *testing.B) {
				var result bool
				b.ReportAllocs()
				for b.Loop() { result = currentMatches(haystack, query) }
				matched = result
			})
		}
	}
}

func BenchmarkLowerAlreadyLower(b *testing.B) {
	for _, size := range []int{64, 128, 256, 512} {
		haystack := strings.Repeat("repository task branch next note hot ", size/37+1)[:size]
		b.Run(fmt.Sprintf("%dB", size), func(b *testing.B) {
			var result string
			b.ReportAllocs()
			for b.Loop() { result = strings.ToLower(haystack) }
			if len(result) != size { b.Fatal(len(result)) }
		})
	}
}
```

```text
1	// Package picker selects one value from a caller-provided list. It can hand
2	// the terminal to a line-oriented external picker such as fzf, and otherwise
3	// falls back to dev's built-in Bubble Tea interface.
4	package picker
5	
6	import (
7		"bytes"
8		"context"
9		"errors"
10		"fmt"
11		"io"
12		"os/exec"
13		"strings"
14		"unicode"
15	)
16	
17	// Item is one selectable value. Value is opaque caller data and is never sent
18	// to an external picker; Label and Description are display-only.
19	type Item struct {
20		Value       string
21		Label       string
22		Description string
23	}
24	
25	// Request describes one selection interaction.
26	type Request struct {
27		Prompt       string
28		InitialQuery string
29		Items        []Item
30	}
31	
32	// Result distinguishes a selection from an explicit cancellation.
33	type Result struct {
34		Item     Item
35		Selected bool
36		Canceled bool
37	}
38	
39	// Selector owns the streams and optional external command for one application.
40	type Selector struct {
41		in       io.Reader
42		out      io.Writer
43		errOut   io.Writer
44		command  []string
45		lookPath func(string) (string, error)
46	}
47	
48	// New constructs a selector. command is an argv vector, not a shell command;
49	// an empty vector always selects the built-in backend.
50	func New(in io.Reader, out, errOut io.Writer, command []string) *Selector {
51		return &Selector{
52			in:       in,
53			out:      out,
54			errOut:   errOut,
55			command:  append([]string(nil), command...),
56			lookPath: exec.LookPath,
57		}
58	}
59	
60	// Select uses the configured external picker when it is installed and the
61	// built-in picker otherwise.
62	func (s *Selector) Select(ctx context.Context, request Request) (Result, error) {
63		if len(request.Items) == 0 {
64			return Result{}, nil
65		}
66		if len(s.command) == 0 {
67			return s.selectBuiltin(ctx, request)
68		}
69		path, err := s.lookPath(s.command[0])
70		if err != nil {
71			return s.selectBuiltin(ctx, request)
72		}
73		return s.selectExternal(ctx, path, request)
74	}
75	
76	func (s *Selector) selectExternal(ctx context.Context, path string, request Request) (Result, error) {
77		lines, items := renderCandidates(request.Items)
78		args := make([]string, len(s.command)-1)
79		for index, arg := range s.command[1:] {
80			args[index] = strings.ReplaceAll(arg, "{prompt}", request.Prompt)
81		}
82		cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, path, args...)
83		cmd.Stdin = strings.NewReader(strings.Join(lines, "\n") + "\n")
84		if s.errOut == nil {
85			cmd.Stderr = io.Discard
86		} else {
87			cmd.Stderr = s.errOut
88		}
89		var stdout bytes.Buffer
90		cmd.Stdout = &stdout
91	
92		err := cmd.Run()
93		if ctxErr := ctx.Err(); ctxErr != nil {
94			return Result{}, ctxErr
95		}
96		if err != nil {
97			var exitErr *exec.ExitError
98			if errors.As(err, &exitErr) && (exitErr.ExitCode() == 1 || exitErr.ExitCode() == 130) {
99				return Result{Canceled: true}, nil
100			}
101			return Result{}, fmt.Errorf("external picker: %w", err)
102		}
103	
104		selected, err := selectedLine(stdout.String())
105		if err != nil {
106			return Result{}, err
107		}
108		item, ok := items[selected]
109		if !ok {
110			return Result{}, fmt.Errorf("external picker returned an unknown selection")
111		}
112		return Result{Item: item, Selected: true}, nil
113	}
114	
115	func selectedLine(output string) (string, error) {
116		output = strings.TrimSuffix(output, "\n")
117		output = strings.TrimSuffix(output, "\r")
118		if output == "" || strings.ContainsAny(output, "\r\n\x00") {
119			return "", errors.New("external picker returned malformed output")
120		}
121		return output, nil
122	}
123	
124	func renderCandidates(items []Item) ([]string, map[string]Item) {
125		lines := make([]string, 0, len(items))
126		byLine := make(map[string]Item, len(items))
127		for _, item := range items {
128			label := cleanDisplay(item.Label)
129			if label == "" {
130				label = "(unnamed)"
131			}
132			base := label
133			if description := cleanDisplay(item.Description); description != "" {
134				base += "\t" + description
135			}
136			line := base
137			for ordinal := 2; ; ordinal++ {
138				if _, exists := byLine[line]; !exists {
139					break
140				}
141				line = fmt.Sprintf("%s\t[%d]", base, ordinal)
142			}
143			lines = append(lines, line)
144			byLine[line] = item
145		}
146		return lines, byLine
147	}
148	
149	func cleanDisplay(value string) string {
150		return strings.Join(strings.FieldsFunc(value, func(r rune) bool {
151			return r == '\r' || r == '\n' || r == '\t' || r == 0
152		}), " ")
153	}
154
```

```text
13	const defaultVisibleRows = 10
14	
15	type builtinModel struct {
16		input    textinput.Model
17		items    []Item
18		visible  []int
19		cursor   int
20		offset   int
21		rows     int
22		width    int
23		done     bool
24		canceled bool
25		selected Item
26	}
27	
28	func newBuiltinModel(request Request) builtinModel {
29		input := textinput.New()
30		input.Prompt = fmt.Sprintf("? %s: ", request.Prompt)
31		input.SetValue(request.InitialQuery)
32		input.Focus()
33		model := builtinModel{
34			input: input,
35			items: append([]Item(nil), request.Items...),
36			rows:  defaultVisibleRows,
37		}
38		model.refilter()
39		return model
40	}
41	
42	func (m builtinModel) Init() tea.Cmd {
43		return textinput.Blink
44	}
45	
46	func (m builtinModel) Update(message tea.Msg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
47		switch msg := message.(type) {
48		case tea.WindowSizeMsg:
49			m.width = msg.Width
50			available := msg.Height - 3
51			switch {
52			case available < 1:
53				m.rows = 1
54			case available < defaultVisibleRows:
55				m.rows = available
56			default:
57				m.rows = defaultVisibleRows
58			}
59			m.keepVisible()
60			return m, nil
61		case tea.KeyMsg:
62			switch msg.Type {
63			case tea.KeyEsc, tea.KeyCtrlC:
64				m.done = true
65				m.canceled = true
66				m.input.Blur()
67				return m, tea.Quit
68			case tea.KeyEnter:
69				if len(m.visible) == 0 {
70					return m, nil
71				}
72				m.done = true
73				m.selected = m.items[m.visible[m.cursor]]
74				m.input.Blur()
75				return m, tea.Quit
```

_**Agent - sidechain (gpt-5.6-sol 2026-09-03 09:11:47Z)**_

CONFIRMED — Trigger: built-in picker fallback while typing. For N items and K query edits, it performs N×K haystack concatenation/lowercase passes and at least N×K heap allocations from repeated `m.input.Value()` conversion; lowercase copies add allocations when casing changes. The clone picker can receive the full paginated forge cache, validated up to 100,000 repositories. At 1,000 items and 10 keystrokes, that is at least 10,000 query allocations plus 10,000 haystack normalization passes.

Quote: `if textmatch.Terms(item.Label+" "+item.Description, m.input.Value())`, followed by `haystack = strings.ToLower(haystack)` and `query = strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(query))`.

Cost: `CompletionOptions` limits traversal to depth 3 and avoids per-repository Git subprocesses, but `filepath.WalkDir` still enumerates every eligible directory across all configured exact paths and scan roots, with no item limit, deadline, or persisted cache. Broad or network-mounted roots can therefore block before the picker appears. Existing `internal/inventory` inventories tracked tasks, not owned repositories; the appropriate path would be a cached/bounded snapshot owned by the `repo` domain, retaining current/manual resolution as fallback.

```text
+func pickStartRepository(ctx context.Context, app *App, current repo.Repo) (repo.Repo, bool, error) {
+	discovered, err := repo.Discover(ctx, app.Cfg.DiscoveryRoots(), repo.CompletionOptions())
+	if err != nil && current.Path == "" {

+	}

+	seen := make(map[string]bool, len(discovered)+1)
+	add := func(repository repo.Repo) {
+		if repository.Path == "" || !repository.HasGit || repository.Bare {
+			return
+		}
+		identity := repository.RealPath
+		if identity == "" {
+			identity = repository.Path
+		}
+		identity = filepath.Clean(identity)
+		if seen[identity] {
+			return
+		}
+		seen[identity] = true
```

```bash
 out=[]; used=0

  if used+w>n-1:break

 return "".join(out)+"…"
```

```text
72		}
73		return left == right
```

```text
46	func (m builtinModel) Update(message tea.Msg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
47		switch msg := message.(type) {
48		case tea.WindowSizeMsg:
49			m.width = msg.Width
50			available := msg.Height - 3
51			switch {
52			case available < 1:
53				m.rows = 1
54			case available < defaultVisibleRows:
55				m.rows = available
56			default:
57				m.rows = defaultVisibleRows
58			}
59			m.keepVisible()
60			return m, nil
61		case tea.KeyMsg:
62			switch msg.Type {
63			case tea.KeyEsc, tea.KeyCtrlC:
64				m.done = true
65				m.canceled = true
66				m.input.Blur()
67				return m, tea.Quit
68			case tea.KeyEnter:
69				if len(m.visible) == 0 {
70					return m, nil
71				}
72				m.done = true
73				m.selected = m.items[m.visible[m.cursor]]
74				m.input.Blur()
75				return m, tea.Quit
76			case tea.KeyUp, tea.KeyCtrlP:
77				m.move(-1)
78				return m, nil
79			case tea.KeyDown, tea.KeyCtrlN:
80				m.move(1)
81				return m, nil
82			}
83		}
84	
85		query := m.input.Value()
86		var command tea.Cmd
87		m.input, command = m.input.Update(message)
88		if m.input.Value() != query {
89			m.refilter()
90		}
91		return m, command
92	}

94	func (m builtinModel) View() string {
95		if m.done {
96			return "\n"
97		}
98		var out strings.Builder
99		out.WriteString(m.input.View())
100		out.WriteByte('\n')
101		if len(m.visible) == 0 {
102			out.WriteString("  No matches\n")
103			return out.String()
104		}
105		end := m.offset + m.rows
106		if end > len(m.visible) {
107			end = len(m.visible)
108		}
109		for position := m.offset; position < end; position++ {
110			item := m.items[m.visible[position]]
111			marker := "  "
112			if position == m.cursor {
113				marker = "> "
114			}
115			line := marker + cleanDisplay(item.Label)
116			if description := cleanDisplay(item.Description); description != "" {
117				line += "  " + description
118			}

125	func (m *builtinModel) refilter() {
126		m.visible = m.visible[:0]

128			if textmatch.Terms(item.Label+" "+item.Description, m.input.Value()) {
129				m.visible = append(m.visible, index)

131		}
132		m.cursor = 0
133		m.offset = 0
134	}

136	func (m *builtinModel) move(delta int) {
137		if len(m.visible) == 0 {
138			return
139		}
140		m.cursor += delta
141		if m.cursor < 0 {
142			m.cursor = len(m.visible) - 1
143		}
144		if m.cursor >= len(m.visible) {
145			m.cursor = 0
146		}
147		m.keepVisible()
148	}
149	
150	func (m *builtinModel) keepVisible() {
151		if m.rows <= 0 {
152			m.rows = 1
153		}
154		if m.cursor < m.offset {
155			m.offset = m.cursor
156		}
157		if m.cursor >= m.offset+m.rows {
158			m.offset = m.cursor - m.rows + 1
159		}
160	}

162	func clipColumns(value string, width int) string {
163		if width <= 0 || lipgloss.Width(value) <= width {
164			return value
165		}
166		if width == 1 {
167			return "…"
168		}
169		var out strings.Builder
170		used := 0
171		for _, r := range value {
172			cellWidth := lipgloss.Width(string(r))
173			if used+cellWidth > width-1 {
174				break
175			}
176			out.WriteRune(r)
177			used += cellWidth
178		}
179		return out.String() + "…"
180	}
```

```text
60	// Select uses the configured external picker when it is installed and the

62	func (s *Selector) Select(ctx context.Context, request Request) (Result, error) {
63		if len(request.Items) == 0 {
64			return Result{}, nil
65		}
66		if len(s.command) == 0 {
67			return s.selectBuiltin(ctx, request)
68		}
69		path, err := s.lookPath(s.command[0])

71			return s.selectBuiltin(ctx, request)
72		}
73		return s.selectExternal(ctx, path, request)
74	}

76	func (s *Selector) selectExternal(ctx context.Context, path string, request Request) (Result, error) {
77		lines, items := renderCandidates(request.Items)
78		args := make([]string, len(s.command)-1)
79		for index, arg := range s.command[1:] {
80			args[index] = strings.ReplaceAll(arg, "{prompt}", request.Prompt)
81		}
82		cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, path, args...)
83		cmd.Stdin = strings.NewReader(strings.Join(lines, "\n") + "\n")
84		if s.errOut == nil {
85			cmd.Stderr = io.Discard
86		} else {
87			cmd.Stderr = s.errOut
88		}
89		var stdout bytes.Buffer
90		cmd.Stdout = &stdout
91	
92		err := cmd.Run()
93		if ctxErr := ctx.Err(); ctxErr != nil {
94			return Result{}, ctxErr
95		}
96		if err != nil {
97			var exitErr *exec.ExitError
98			if errors.As(err, &exitErr) && (exitErr.ExitCode() == 1 || exitErr.ExitCode() == 130) {
99				return Result{}, ErrCanceled
100			}
101			return Result{}, fmt.Errorf("external picker: %w", err)
102		}
103	
104		selected, err := selectedLine(stdout.String())
105		if err != nil {
106			return Result{}, err
107		}
108		item, ok := items[selected]
109		if !ok {
110			return Result{}, fmt.Errorf("external picker returned an unknown selection")
111		}
112		return Result{Item: item}, nil
113	}
114	
115	func selectedLine(output string) (string, error) {
116		output = strings.TrimSuffix(output, "\n")
117		output = strings.TrimSuffix(output, "\r")
118		if output == "" || strings.ContainsAny(output, "\r\n\x00") {
119			return "", errors.New("external picker returned malformed output")
120		}
121		return output, nil
122	}
123	
124	func renderCandidates(items []Item) ([]string, map[string]Item) {
125		lines := make([]string, 0, len(items))
126		byLine := make(map[string]Item, len(items))
127		for _, item := range items {
128			label := cleanDisplay(item.Label)
129			if label == "" {
130				label = "(unnamed)"
131			}
132			base := label
133			if description := cleanDisplay(item.Description); description != "" {
134				base += "\t" + description
135			}
136			line := base
137			for ordinal := 2; ; ordinal++ {
138				if _, exists := byLine[line]; !exists {
139					break
140				}
141				line = fmt.Sprintf("%s\t[%d]", base, ordinal)
142			}
143			lines = append(lines, line)
144			byLine[line] = item
145		}
146		return lines, byLine
147	}
148	
149	func cleanDisplay(value string) string {
150		return strings.Join(strings.FieldsFunc(value, unicode.IsControl), " ")
151	}
```

```text
101		}

103		items := make([]picker.Item, 0, len(discovered)+2)
104		byPath := make(map[string]repo.Repo, len(discovered)+1)
105		seen := make(map[string]bool, len(discovered)+1)
106		add := func(repository repo.Repo) {
107			if repository.Path == "" || !repository.HasGit || repository.Bare {
108				return
109			}
110			identity := repository.RealPath
111			if identity == "" {
112				identity = repository.Path
113			}
114			identity = filepath.Clean(identity)
115			if seen[identity] {
116				return
117			}
118			seen[identity] = true
119			byPath[repository.Path] = repository
120			items = append(items, picker.Item{
121				Value:       repository.Path,
122				Label:       repository.Display(),
123				Description: config.Contract(repository.Path),
124			})
125		}
126		add(current)
127		for _, repository := range discovered {
128			add(repository)
129		}
130		if len(items) == 0 {
131			return repo.Repo{}, false, nil
132		}
133		items = append(items, picker.Item{
134			Value:       manualStartRepository,
135			Label:       "Enter a repository name or path manually…",
136			Description: "resolve a repository not present in the discovered list",
137		})
138	
139		result, used, err := app.pick(ctx, picker.Request{Prompt: "Repository", Items: items})
140		if errors.Is(err, picker.ErrCanceled) {
141			return repo.Repo{}, false, errPromptCanceled
142		}
143		if err != nil {
144			return repo.Repo{}, false, err
145		}
146		if !used || result.Item.Value == manualStartRepository {
147			return repo.Repo{}, false, nil
148		}
149		selected, ok := byPath[result.Item.Value]
150		if !ok {
151			return repo.Repo{}, false, fmt.Errorf("picker returned an unknown repository")
152		}
153		resolved, err := resolveStartRepository(ctx, app, selected.Path)
154		if err != nil {
155			return repo.Repo{}, false, err
156		}
157		return resolved, true, nil
158	}
```

```text
4	package textmatch

6	import "strings"

8	// Terms reports whether every whitespace-separated query term appears in the
```

```text
76	func (s *Selector) selectExternal(ctx context.Context, path string, request Request) (Result, error) {
77		lines, items := renderCandidates(request.Items)
78		args := make([]string, len(s.command)-1)
79		for index, arg := range s.command[1:] {
80			args[index] = strings.ReplaceAll(arg, "{prompt}", request.Prompt)
81		}
82		cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, path, args...)
83		cmd.Stdin = strings.NewReader(strings.Join(lines, "\n") + "\n")
84		if s.errOut == nil {
85			cmd.Stderr = io.Discard
86		} else {
87			cmd.Stderr = s.errOut
88		}
89		var stdout bytes.Buffer
90		cmd.Stdout = &stdout
91	
92		err := cmd.Run()
93		if ctxErr := ctx.Err(); ctxErr != nil {
94			return Result{}, ctxErr
95		}
96		if err != nil {
97			var exitErr *exec.ExitError
98			if errors.As(err, &exitErr) && (exitErr.ExitCode() == 1 || exitErr.ExitCode() == 130) {
99				return Result{}, ErrCanceled
100			}
101			return Result{}, fmt.Errorf("external picker: %w", err)
102		}
103	
104		selected, err := selectedLine(stdout.String())
105		if err != nil {
106			return Result{}, err
107		}
108		item, ok := items[selected]
109		if !ok {
110			return Result{}, fmt.Errorf("external picker returned an unknown selection")
111		}
112		return Result{Item: item}, nil
113	}
114	
115	func selectedLine(output string) (string, error) {
116		output = strings.TrimSuffix(output, "\n")
117		output = strings.TrimSuffix(output, "\r")
118		if output == "" || strings.ContainsAny(output, "\r\n\x00") {
119			return "", errors.New("external picker returned malformed output")
120		}
121		return output, nil
122	}
123	
124	func renderCandidates(items []Item) ([]string, map[string]Item) {
125		lines := make([]string, 0, len(items))
126		byLine := make(map[string]Item, len(items))
127		for _, item := range items {
128			label := cleanDisplay(item.Label)
129			if label == "" {
130				label = "(unnamed)"
131			}
132			base := label
133			if description := cleanDisplay(item.Description); description != "" {
134				base += "\t" + description
135			}
136			line := base
137			for ordinal := 2; ; ordinal++ {
138				if _, exists := byLine[line]; !exists {
139					break
140				}
141				line = fmt.Sprintf("%s\t[%d]", base, ordinal)
142			}
143			lines = append(lines, line)
144			byLine[line] = item
145		}
146		return lines, byLine
147	}
148	
149	func cleanDisplay(value string) string {
150		return strings.Join(strings.FieldsFunc(value, unicode.IsControl), " ")
151	}
```

```text
145		}
146		return resolveStartRepository(ctx, app, selected.Path)
147	}

149	func runStartWizard(ctx context.Context, app *App, req startRequest) (*startSpec, bool, error) {
150		p := newPrompter(app)
151		fmt.Fprintln(p.out, p.style.title("Start a tracked change stream"))
152	
153		r, err := promptStartRepository(ctx, app, p, req)
154		if err != nil {
155			return nil, false, err
156		}
157		if r.Bare {
158			return nil, false, fmt.Errorf("%s is a bare repository and cannot host a task checkout", r.Display())
159		}
160		req.RepoRef, req.RepoExplicit = r.Path, true
161	
162		for strings.TrimSpace(req.Name) == "" {
163			req.Name, err = p.line("Task name", "")
164			if err != nil {
165				return nil, false, err
166			}
167			if strings.TrimSpace(req.Name) == "" {
168				fmt.Fprintln(p.out, "  "+p.style.warning("task name is required"))
169			}
170		}
171	
172		for {
173			if !req.ModeExplicit {
174				fallback := "worktree"
175				switch req.Mode {
176				case task.ModeBranch:
177					fallback = "branch-only"
178				case task.ModeDirect:
179					fallback = "direct"
180				}
```

_**User (2026-09-03 09:18:47Z)**_

Base directory for this skill: /Users/zhouhanru/Worktrees/dev-cli/feat-combine-fzf/.claude/skills/agent-history-hygiene

# agent-history-hygiene

Keep agent chat transcripts and plan files committed together with the
code they produced, without leaking secrets. Pairs with the
`redact-agent-secrets` + `gitleaks` pre-commit hooks the skill installs.

Three surfaces, separated by purpose:

| Surface                          | Question it answers                                          |
|----------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------|
| `find-session.sh`                | "Which transcript / plan file is *my* current session?"      |
| `stage-agent-artifacts.sh`       | "Which agent files belong in the next commit?"               |
| `bootstrap-project.sh`           | "How do I get pre-commit + gitleaks + redactor into a repo?" |
| `scan-staged.sh`                 | "Is there a leaked secret in what I'm about to commit?"      |
| `probe-specstory-redaction.py`   | "What does SpecStory already redact, so we don't redo it?"   |
| `references/remediation.md`      | "I already pushed a secret — now what?"                      |

## Core invariants

1. **Agent transcripts and plan files are committed alongside the diff
   that produced them.** Never add them to `.gitignore`. An agent that
   drops these from a commit has broken the user's review trail.
2. **Rotate at the provider before any git rewrite.** The only act
   that revokes a leaked credential is rotation. History rewriting
   scrubs bytes on one clone and leaves them on every other.
3. **`git push --force` against a shared branch is never the fix for a
   leak.** At best it's useless; at worst it destroys teammate work and
   silently re-introduces the secret when someone merges their old
   history back.

## When to use this skill

Use it when the user (or you) surface any of:

- "Commit my chat" / "save the specstory session" / "include the plan
  file in this commit" / "把 plan 跟 specstory 一起 commit 進去".
- You see dirty `.specstory/history/*.md`, `.claude/plans/*.md`,
  `.cursor/plans/*.md`, or any other configured agent artifact during
  `git status` and you're about to commit a feature.
- "Scrub this transcript" / "redact my key" / "gitleaks flagged my
  chat history".
- "Set up pre-commit for this repo" / "I'm starting a new project — how
  do I get the hook stack?" / "bootstrap secret scanning here".
- "I pushed a `.env`" / "a secret went to main" / "do I need to force
  push?" — the agent must steer to `references/remediation.md` and
  stop the user from force-pushing reflexively.

## When NOT to use

- The user explicitly wants agent transcripts **excluded** from the
  repo. Respect that; suggest a one-liner `.gitignore` addition and
  skip this skill entirely.
- The leak is already on a shared `main`/release branch. Do **not**
  offer to rewrite history — jump to `references/remediation.md` §5.
- The project genuinely has no agent session (no `.specstory/`, no
  `.claude/plans/`, etc.). Nothing to stage.
- Single-file, single-commit hygiene that the agent handles without any
  script (e.g., adding a missing trailing newline).

## Integration with existing infrastructure

This skill sits **on top of** any chezmoi-managed stack the user
already has. It does not duplicate:

- **chezmoi's global `core.hooksPath`** (`~/.config/git/hooks/pre-commit`)
  — that wrapper runs the repo's `.pre-commit-config.yaml` and then
  optionally `gitleaks git --staged`. The skill bootstraps the repo-level
  config the wrapper expects to find.
- **chezmoi's `.gitleaks.toml`** — the user's config already carries
  curated rules for common API keys (OpenAI, Anthropic, Supabase,
  Linear, WakaTime, Cursor, HuggingFace, Notion, Tailscale, Clash /
  V2Ray tokens). The skill's `assets/gitleaks.toml.template` ships the
  same rule IDs so `.gitleaksignore` / allowlist tweaks stay portable.
- **the pinned `redact-agent-secrets` hook** — the redactor ships as a
  pinned pre-commit hook from this repo
  (`.pre-commit-hooks.yaml`), so every consuming repo gets fixes via
  `pre-commit autoupdate` instead of a vendored copy that drifts. Details
  in [`references/pre-commit-redaction-stack.md`](references/pre-commit-redaction-stack.md).

What this skill **adds**:

- Agent-facing discipline (this `SKILL.md` + `references/remediation.md`).
- A single-command project bootstrap (`bootstrap-project.sh`) for repos
  without chezmoi or where the user wants the stack in one go.
- Session-discovery heuristics (`find-session.sh`) for the "find my
  current transcript among many" problem.
- An exit-code wrapper (`scan-staged.sh`) agents can branch on before
  committing.

## Workflow A: commit-time hygiene

Default flow when the agent is about to commit feature changes plus
chat/plan artifacts.

```bash
# 1. Make sure the agent knows which session is "ours" — mostly
#    relevant when multiple Claude/SpecStory sessions run in the repo.
bash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/scripts/find-session.sh

# 2. Stage code the usual way, then auto-add agent artifacts.
git add path/to/feature/file.ts
bash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/scripts/stage-agent-artifacts.sh
# Use --session-only if you want ONLY the current SpecStory + newest plan;
# default stages every dirty *.md in every configured agent dir.

# 3. Belt-and-suspenders secret scan before commit. Exit 0 = clean.
bash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/scripts/scan-staged.sh || {
  # Exit 10/20: leaks found. Jump to references/remediation.md.
  echo "Leaks detected — see references/remediation.md before committing." >&2
  exit 1
}

# 4. Commit. pre-commit (installed by bootstrap) runs redact-agent-secrets
#    then gitleaks again as a catch-all.
git commit -m "feat: ..."
```

## Workflow B: bootstrap a new project

For repos that don't yet have `.pre-commit-config.yaml` / `.gitleaks.toml`
installed. Runs once per repo.

```bash
cd /path/to/new/project
bash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/scripts/bootstrap-project.sh \
  --install-hook            # optional: auto-stage on every commit

# Verify: shake out any existing issues in the working tree.
pre-commit run --all-files
```

What `bootstrap-project.sh` does:

1. Drops `.pre-commit-config.yaml` + `.gitleaks.toml` into the repo
   (skips if already present unless `--force`). The redactor is a pinned
   remote hook (`repo: …/agent-skills`, `rev: ahh-v1.1.0`), **not** a
   vendored `scripts/redact_secrets.py` — so `pre-commit autoupdate`
   keeps it current everywhere.
2. Runs `pre-commit install` (or `uvx pre-commit@4 install` if
   pre-commit isn't on `PATH`).
3. Audits `.gitignore` / `.git/info/exclude` for patterns that would
   silently hide an agent artifact dir — warns without editing.
4. Checks `~/.claude/settings.json` for `plansDirectory`; prints the
   one-line patch if missing.
5. With `--install-hook`: writes a `prepare-commit-msg` hook that calls
   `stage-agent-artifacts.sh --session-only --allow-empty` so every
   `git commit` auto-attaches the current session file.

Migrating a repo off the **old vendored layout** (a committed
`scripts/redact_secrets.py` + a `- repo: local` redact hook):

```bash
bash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/scripts/bootstrap-project.sh --migrate
```

removes the vendored script and rewrites the local hook into the pinned
remote hook, leaving your other hooks and `.gitleaks.toml` untouched
(idempotent; safe to re-run).

## Workflow C: post-leak remediation

When `scan-staged.sh` reports exit `10`/`20`, or the user says "I
committed / pushed a secret":

1. **STOP** the user from running `git push --force` reflexively.
2. Read `references/remediation.md` end-to-end.
3. Walk the user through **step 1 (rotate)** regardless of blast
   radius. Only after rotation does the question of scrubbing history
   become worth discussing.
4. Use the decision tree in the runbook to pick the right git action.

## Gotchas

- **SpecStory >= 2.4.0 already redacts on write — plan around it, not
  against it.** Since
  [PR #235](https://github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/pull/235) shipped in
  v2.4.0 (2026-07-20), the CLI redacts secrets via the
  [Betterleaks](https://github.com/betterleaks/betterleaks) ruleset **by
  default**, covering both local markdown and cloud sync, writing
  `[REDACTED:<rule-id>]`. Measured coverage is 36 of 54 class/context pairs;
  15 are ours alone (every webhook rule, plus every custom key in prose
  context — betterleaks catches many classes only in `KEY=value` form via its
  entropy-based `generic-api-key` rule). So: **keep this layer, but never
  rewrite what SpecStory already cleaned.** `redact_secrets.py` writes the
  same `[REDACTED:<rule-id>]` sentinel and `.gitleaks.toml` allowlists it, so
  a cleaned transcript is left untouched and pre-commit stops demanding a
  re-`git add`. Full matrix + knobs in
  [`references/specstory-native-redaction.md`](references/specstory-native-redaction.md).
  Only `[redaction] enabled` is configurable upstream — the PR's
  `extra_patterns` did not survive the Betterleaks rewrite, so repo-specific
  rules stay our job. For SpecStory older than 2.4.0 (or with redaction
  disabled), run `redact_secrets.py --fix --legacy`.
- **`plansDirectory` project-level sometimes ignored.** Claude Code
  issue [#19537](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/19537)
  reports project-level `plansDirectory` being ignored in some
  versions. After running a `/plan`, verify the file actually landed
  where you expected before relying on `stage-agent-artifacts.sh`
  picking it up. User-level config (`~/.claude/settings.json` with
  `"plansDirectory": "./.claude/plans"`) is the recommended default.
- **`gitleaks protect` is deprecated.** Since v8.19.0 use
  `gitleaks git --staged --redact` (pre-commit) and
  `gitleaks dir <path>` (working directory). The older commands still
  work but emit a deprecation notice. This skill uses the modern
  syntax everywhere.
- **`pre-commit install` is per-clone.** Each teammate must run
  `pre-commit install` in their own clone for hooks to fire. CI cannot
  be trusted as the single gate — it's second-chance, not last-chance.
- **Transcript files can be huge.** A long SpecStory session can exceed
  2 MB. The template bumps `check-added-large-files` to `--maxkb=2048`
  to avoid false positives, but a very long session can still overflow.
  If you hit the limit, rotate sessions (`specstory run claude`
  creates a fresh file) instead of raising the cap further.
- **Session-UUID divergence between SpecStory CLI and VS Code
  extension.** The extension autosaves into `.specstory/history/`
  continuously; the CLI (`specstory run claude`) creates one file per
  invocation. If both are active you can end up with two transcripts
  for what feels like "one session" — mtime-newest wins in
  `find-session.sh`.
- **Global `core.hooksPath` means bare repos aren't protected.** The
  chezmoi setup's global hook runs `.pre-commit-config.yaml` IF it
  exists — so a repo without `.pre-commit-config.yaml` has no
  protection. Run `bootstrap-project.sh` before the first commit with
  agent artifacts, not after.
- **Active SpecStory writer can defeat the redact loop.** The standard
  `git add → git commit → pre-commit auto-fixes → re-stage → re-commit`
  flow assumes the file is **quiescent** during the commit. SpecStory's
  `specstory_*_watch` daemon tails the agent transcript continuously,
  so if the chat captured `ps -axo args`-style output that contained an
  unrelated daemon's secret in argv (e.g. SpecStory's own
  `--cloud-token …` flag), every diagnostic command (`grep`, `sed -n
  '<line>p'`, `cat | head | tail`) prints the secret again, SpecStory
  appends it to the transcript, and the redact-then-restage cycle
  never converges. Symptom: pre-commit says "Successfully redacted N
  file(s)" but `gitleaks-system` immediately fails on the same line,
  re-running `git add && git commit` doesn't help, and `grep -c
  '<secret-prefix>' file` shows the count *increasing* over commit
  attempts. **Workaround**: a single atomic
  `python3 -c "<in-place re.sub>" && git add <file> && git commit -m
  "..."` pipeline so the index is frozen before any new specstory write
  lands. **Don't** print, grep, or diff the secret line during the
  recovery — every print echoes back into the transcript. Diagnose with
  `lsof <file>` (looking for `specstory_*` writers) instead. See
  `pitfalls/redact-secrets-loop-with-active-specstory-writer.md` in
  upstream chezmoi for the full debugging trail.
  **Fixed sub-case:** the *bare-phrase* variant of this loop — where the
  redactor's own `PRIVATE KEY` substring match kept flagging prose that
  merely *discusses* private keys (this skill's docs, or a chat about
  redaction) with **no real secret present** — no longer happens.
  `redact_secrets.py` now scopes to key *headers* (the
  `detect-private-key` BLACKLIST), so prose mentions are ignored and
  converge immediately. The atomic-commit workaround above is still
  needed for the harder case: a **real** secret an active writer keeps
  re-appending. When only the substring redactor (`redact-agent-secrets`)
  trips while `gitleaks` + `detect-private-key` pass, it's the false
  positive — verify with `gitleaks git --staged` and, if clean, commit
  with `SKIP=redact-agent-secrets` (keeps the real gates active).

## Available scripts

- **`scripts/find-session.sh [--format=specstory|claude|both] [--json]`**
  Discover the current agent session files for `$PWD`. TSV default,
  `--json` for structured callers. Never exits non-zero (always 0,
  empty fields signal absence).

- **`scripts/stage-agent-artifacts.sh [--session-only] [--include-all-plans] [--dry-run] [--allow-empty]`**
  `git add` the right agent artifacts before the next commit.
  `--session-only` stages only the current SpecStory + newest plan;
  default stages every dirty `*.md` in every configured artifact dir.
  Refuses to run if there are no code changes (prevents "commit just
  transcript"); override with `--allow-empty`.

- **`scripts/scan-staged.sh [--redact] [--verbose]`**
  Run `gitleaks git --staged` with agent-friendly exit codes
  (0 clean / 10 redacted / 20 leaks / 30 gitleaks missing). JSON lines
  on stdout, prose diagnostics on stderr.

- **`scripts/probe-specstory-redaction.py [--json] [--keep] [--dry-run]`**
  Measure which secret classes SpecStory's native redaction covers, by
  synthesizing a Claude Code session and rendering it twice (with and without
  `--no-redact-secrets`). Prints a coverage matrix and the residual set our
  layer must still handle. Exit 30 when specstory isn't installed.

- **`scripts/bootstrap-project.sh [--from-chezmoi] [--migrate] [--install-hook] [--force] [--dry-run]`**
  Install `.pre-commit-config.yaml` + `.gitleaks.toml` into the current
  repo, wire the hook to the installed skill's redactor, then run
  `pre-commit install`. Audits
  `.gitignore` and `~/.claude/settings.json` for misconfigurations
  (warns, never silently edits).

## Bundled assets

- `assets/artifact-dirs.txt` — the canonical list of agent artifact
  directories (SpecStory, Claude plans, Cursor plans + rules, OpenCode
  plans, Spec-kit, Codex). Consumed by `stage-agent-artifacts.sh` and
  by `bootstrap-project.sh` when rendering the pre-commit `files:`
  regex.
- `assets/pre-commit-config.yaml.template` — minimal
  `.pre-commit-config.yaml` with `redact-agent-secrets` + gitleaks +
  standard hygiene hooks.
- `assets/gitleaks.toml.template` — portable subset of the chezmoi
  `.gitleaks.toml` with custom rule IDs + a path-scoped allowlist for
  agent artifact dirs.
- `assets/redact_secrets.py` — the redactor, published to consuming repos
  as the pinned `redact-agent-secrets` pre-commit hook (root
  `.pre-commit-hooks.yaml`). Writes `[REDACTED:<rule-id>]`, the sentinel
  SpecStory also writes natively; `--legacy` writes the pre-2.4.0
  placeholders instead. Release procedure in
  `references/pre-commit-redaction-stack.md`.

## Reference files

- [`references/transcript-session-discovery.md`](references/transcript-session-discovery.md)
  — SpecStory / Claude session layouts and the `$PWD → slug` algorithm.
  Read when `find-session.sh` returns empty or ambiguous results.
- [`references/pre-commit-redaction-stack.md`](references/pre-commit-redaction-stack.md)
  — three-layer defense (redact → gitleaks → `scan-staged.sh`),
  allowlist design, sync procedure for the bundled redactor. Read
  when tuning rules or debugging unexpected pre-commit failures.
- [`references/specstory-native-redaction.md`](references/specstory-native-redaction.md)
  — what SpecStory >= 2.4.0 redacts on its own, measured per secret class and
  per context, plus the upstream PRs, config knobs, and why our layer is still
  load-bearing. Read before changing anything about redaction placeholders.
- [`references/remediation.md`](references/remediation.md) —
  rotate-first runbook for "I committed / pushed a secret". Read
  **before** any `git filter-repo` / `git push --force` action.

## Tests

The skill ships with a three-level test suite under
[`tests/`](tests/README.md). Run from repo root:

```bash
make test-skill
```

- `test_redact_secrets.py` — pytest for pure redactor functions.
- `test_gitleaks_corpus.py` — golden-corpus fixtures staged in tmp git
  repos, asserting real-key shapes fire and example shapes are
  allowlisted only inside configured artifact dirs.
- `test_scan_staged.sh` — exit-code contract for
  `scripts/scan-staged.sh` (0 / 20 / 30 / 2).
- `test_specstory_coverage.py` — locks in that SpecStory still redacts by
  default and still writes `[REDACTED:<label>]`; skips without the CLI.

The corpus + shell tests skip gracefully when `gitleaks` isn't on
`PATH`. See [`tests/README.md`](tests/README.md) for what each
regression the suite locks in.

```text
256	func resolve(ctx context.Context, roots []string, ref string, opts Options) (Repo, []Repo, error) {
257		all, err := Discover(ctx, roots, opts)

271					Name: filepath.Base(abs), Path: abs, RealPath: real,
272					Symlink: real != abs, CommonDir: g.GitCommonDir, HasGit: true, Bare: g.Bare,
273				}, nil, nil

279			}

281		needle := strings.ToLower(ref)

283		for _, r := range all {
284			if strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(r.Display()), needle) {
285				hits = append(hits, r)
286			}
287		}
288		switch len(hits) {
289		case 1:
290			return hits[0], nil, nil
291		case 0:
292			return Repo{}, nil, &NotFoundError{Ref: ref}
293		default:
294			return Repo{}, hits, &AmbiguousError{Ref: ref, Candidates: hits}
```

```text
250	// ResolveCompletion resolves the same references without launching one Git
251	// process per repository in the scan roots.
252	func ResolveCompletion(ctx context.Context, roots []string, ref string) (Repo, []Repo, error) {
253		return resolve(ctx, roots, ref, CompletionOptions())
254	}
255	
256	func resolve(ctx context.Context, roots []string, ref string, opts Options) (Repo, []Repo, error) {
257		if abs, err := filepath.Abs(ref); err == nil {
258			if g, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, abs); err == nil {
259				real, _ := filepath.EvalSymlinks(abs)
260				if real == "" {
261					real = g.MainRoot
262				}
263				// Preserve an explicit navigation alias. The caller named this
264				// path on purpose; resolving it to the physical checkout would
265				// defeat a bootstrap symlink catalog.
266				return Repo{
267					Name: filepath.Base(abs), Path: abs, RealPath: real,
268					Symlink: real != abs, CommonDir: g.GitCommonDir, HasGit: true, Bare: g.Bare,
269				}, nil, nil
270			}
271		}
272		for _, r := range all {
273			if r.Name == ref || r.Display() == ref || r.Path == ref {
274				return r, nil, nil
275			}
276		}
277		needle := strings.ToLower(ref)
278		var hits []Repo
279		for _, r := range all {
280			if strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(r.Display()), needle) {
281				hits = append(hits, r)
282			}
283		}
284		switch len(hits) {
285		case 1:
286			return hits[0], nil, nil
287		case 0:
288			return Repo{}, nil, &NotFoundError{Ref: ref}
289		default:
290			return Repo{}, hits, &AmbiguousError{Ref: ref, Candidates: hits}
291		}
```

```text
1	// Package picker selects one value from a caller-provided list. It can hand
2	// the terminal to a line-oriented external picker such as fzf, and otherwise
3	// falls back to dev's built-in Bubble Tea interface.
4	package picker
5	
6	import (
7		"bytes"
8		"context"
9		"errors"
10		"fmt"
11		"io"
12		"os/exec"
13		"strings"
14		"unicode"
15	)
16	
17	// Item is one selectable value. Value is opaque caller data and is never sent
18	// to an external picker; Label and Description are display-only.
19	type Item struct {
20		Value       string
21		Label       string
22		Description string
23	}
24	
25	// ErrCanceled reports that the user left a picker without selecting an item.
26	var ErrCanceled = errors.New("picker canceled")
27	
28	// Request describes one selection interaction.
29	type Request struct {
30		Prompt string
31		Items  []Item
32	}
33	
34	// Result contains the selected original item.
35	type Result struct {
36		Item Item
37	}
38	
39	// Selector owns the streams and optional external command for one application.
40	type Selector struct {
41		in       io.Reader
42		out      io.Writer
43		errOut   io.Writer
44		command  []string
45		lookPath func(string) (string, error)
46	}
47	
48	// New constructs a selector. command is an argv vector, not a shell command;
49	// an empty vector always selects the built-in backend.
50	func New(in io.Reader, out, errOut io.Writer, command []string) *Selector {
51		return &Selector{
52			in:       in,
53			out:      out,
54			errOut:   errOut,
55			command:  append([]string(nil), command...),
56			lookPath: exec.LookPath,
57		}
58	}
59	
60	// Select uses the configured external picker when it is installed and the
61	// built-in picker otherwise.
62	func (s *Selector) Select(ctx context.Context, request Request) (Result, error) {
63		if len(request.Items) == 0 {
64			return Result{}, nil
65		}
66		if len(s.command) == 0 {
67			return s.selectBuiltin(ctx, request)
68		}
69		path, err := s.lookPath(s.command[0])
70		if err != nil {
71			return s.selectBuiltin(ctx, request)
72		}
73		return s.selectExternal(ctx, path, request)
74	}
75	
76	func (s *Selector) selectExternal(ctx context.Context, path string, request Request) (Result, error) {
77		lines, items := renderCandidates(request.Items)
78		args := make([]string, len(s.command)-1)
79		for index, arg := range s.command[1:] {
80			args[index] = strings.ReplaceAll(arg, "{prompt}", request.Prompt)
81		}
82		cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, path, args...)
83		var input strings.Builder
84		inputSize := len(lines)
85		for _, line := range lines {
86			inputSize += len(line)
87		}
88		input.Grow(inputSize)
89		for _, line := range lines {
90			input.WriteString(line)
91			input.WriteByte('\n')
92		}
93		cmd.Stdin = strings.NewReader(input.String())
94		if s.errOut == nil {
95			cmd.Stderr = io.Discard
96		} else {
97			cmd.Stderr = s.errOut
98		}
99		var stdout bytes.Buffer
100		cmd.Stdout = &stdout
101	
102		err := cmd.Run()
103		if ctxErr := ctx.Err(); ctxErr != nil {
104			return Result{}, ctxErr
105		}
106		if err != nil {
107			var exitErr *exec.ExitError
108			if errors.As(err, &exitErr) && (exitErr.ExitCode() == 1 || exitErr.ExitCode() == 130) {
109				return Result{}, ErrCanceled
110			}
111			return Result{}, fmt.Errorf("external picker: %w", err)
112		}
113	
114		selected, err := selectedLine(stdout.String())
115		if err != nil {
116			return Result{}, err
117		}
118		item, ok := items[selected]
119		if !ok {
120			return Result{}, fmt.Errorf("external picker returned an unknown selection")
121		}
122		return Result{Item: item}, nil
123	}
124	
125	func selectedLine(output string) (string, error) {
126		output = strings.TrimSuffix(output, "\n")
127		output = strings.TrimSuffix(output, "\r")
128		if output == "" || strings.ContainsAny(output, "\r\n\x00") {
129			return "", errors.New("external picker returned malformed output")
130		}
131		return output, nil
132	}
133	
134	func renderCandidates(items []Item) ([]string, map[string]Item) {
135		lines := make([]string, 0, len(items))
136		byLine := make(map[string]Item, len(items))
137		nextOrdinal := make(map[string]int, len(items))
138		for _, item := range items {
139			label := cleanDisplay(item.Label)
140			if label == "" {
141				label = "(unnamed)"
142			}
143			base := label
144			if description := cleanDisplay(item.Description); description != "" {
145				base += "\t" + description
146			}
147			ordinal := nextOrdinal[base]
148			if ordinal == 0 {
149				ordinal = 1
150			}
151			line := base
152			for {
153				if ordinal > 1 {
154					line = fmt.Sprintf("%s\t[%d]", base, ordinal)
155				}
156				ordinal++
157				if _, exists := byLine[line]; !exists {
158					nextOrdinal[base] = ordinal
159					break
160				}
161			}
162			lines = append(lines, line)
163			byLine[line] = item
164		}
165		return lines, byLine
166	}
167	
168	func cleanDisplay(value string) string {
169		return strings.Join(strings.FieldsFunc(value, unicode.IsControl), " ")
170	}
171
```

```text
1	package picker
2	
3	import (
4		"context"
5		"fmt"
6		"strings"
7	
8		"github.com/charmbracelet/bubbles/textinput"
9		tea "github.com/charmbracelet/bubbletea"
10		"github.com/charmbracelet/lipgloss"
11		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/textmatch"
12	)
13	
14	const defaultVisibleRows = 10
15	
16	type builtinModel struct {
17		input    textinput.Model
18		items    []Item
19		search   []string
20		visible  []int
21		cursor   int
22		offset   int
23		rows     int
24		width    int
25		done     bool
26		canceled bool
27		selected Item
28	}
29	
30	func newBuiltinModel(request Request) builtinModel {
31		input := textinput.New()
32		input.Prompt = fmt.Sprintf("? %s: ", request.Prompt)
33		input.Focus()
34		items := append([]Item(nil), request.Items...)
35		search := make([]string, len(items))
36		for index, item := range items {
37			search[index] = strings.ToLower(item.Label + " " + item.Description)
38		}
39		model := builtinModel{
40			input:  input,
41			items:  items,
42			search: search,
43			rows:   defaultVisibleRows,
44		}
45		model.refilter()
46		return model
47	}
48	
49	func (m builtinModel) Init() tea.Cmd {
50		return textinput.Blink
51	}
52	
53	func (m builtinModel) Update(message tea.Msg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
54		switch msg := message.(type) {
55		case tea.WindowSizeMsg:
56			m.width = msg.Width
57			available := msg.Height - 3
58			switch {
59			case available < 1:
60				m.rows = 1
61			case available < defaultVisibleRows:
62				m.rows = available
63			default:
64				m.rows = defaultVisibleRows
65			}
66			m.keepVisible()
67			return m, nil
68		case tea.KeyMsg:
69			switch msg.Type {
70			case tea.KeyEsc, tea.KeyCtrlC:
71				m.done = true
72				m.canceled = true
73				m.input.Blur()
74				return m, tea.Quit
75			case tea.KeyEnter:
76				if len(m.visible) == 0 {
77					return m, nil
78				}
79				m.done = true
80				m.selected = m.items[m.visible[m.cursor]]
81				m.input.Blur()
82				return m, tea.Quit
83			case tea.KeyUp, tea.KeyCtrlP:
84				m.move(-1)
85				return m, nil
86			case tea.KeyDown, tea.KeyCtrlN:
87				m.move(1)
88				return m, nil
89			}
90		}
91	
92		query := m.input.Value()
93		var command tea.Cmd
94		m.input, command = m.input.Update(message)
95		if m.input.Value() != query {
96			m.refilter()
97		}
98		return m, command
99	}
100	
101	func (m builtinModel) View() string {
102		if m.done {
103			return "\n"
104		}
105		var out strings.Builder
106		out.WriteString(m.input.View())
107		out.WriteByte('\n')
108		if len(m.visible) == 0 {
109			out.WriteString("  No matches\n")
110			return out.String()
111		}
112		end := m.offset + m.rows
113		if end > len(m.visible) {
114			end = len(m.visible)
115		}
116		for position := m.offset; position < end; position++ {
117			item := m.items[m.visible[position]]
118			marker := "  "
119			if position == m.cursor {
120				marker = "> "
121			}
122			line := marker + cleanDisplay(item.Label)
123			if description := cleanDisplay(item.Description); description != "" {
124				line += "  " + description
125			}
126			out.WriteString(clipColumns(line, m.width))
127			out.WriteByte('\n')
128		}
129		return out.String()
130	}
131	
132	func (m *builtinModel) refilter() {
133		m.visible = m.visible[:0]
134		query := strings.ToLower(m.input.Value())
135		for index, haystack := range m.search {
136			if textmatch.TermsFolded(haystack, query) {
137				m.visible = append(m.visible, index)
138			}
139		}
140		m.cursor = 0
141		m.offset = 0
142	}
143	
144	func (m *builtinModel) move(delta int) {
145		if len(m.visible) == 0 {
146			return
147		}
148		m.cursor += delta
149		if m.cursor < 0 {
150			m.cursor = len(m.visible) - 1
151		}
152		if m.cursor >= len(m.visible) {
153			m.cursor = 0
154		}
155		m.keepVisible()
156	}
157	
158	func (m *builtinModel) keepVisible() {
159		if m.rows <= 0 {
160			m.rows = 1
161		}
162		if m.cursor < m.offset {
163			m.offset = m.cursor
164		}
165		if m.cursor >= m.offset+m.rows {
166			m.offset = m.cursor - m.rows + 1
167		}
168	}
169	
170	func clipColumns(value string, width int) string {
171		if width <= 0 || lipgloss.Width(value) <= width {
172			return value
173		}
174		if width == 1 {
175			return "…"
176		}
177		var out strings.Builder
178		used := 0
179		for _, r := range value {
180			cellWidth := lipgloss.Width(string(r))
181			if used+cellWidth > width-1 {
182				break
183			}
184			out.WriteRune(r)
185			used += cellWidth
186		}
187		return out.String() + "…"
188	}
189	
190	func (s *Selector) selectBuiltin(ctx context.Context, request Request) (Result, error) {
191		program := tea.NewProgram(

194			tea.WithOutput(s.out),

199			return Result{}, ctxErr
200		}
201		if err != nil {
202			return Result{}, fmt.Errorf("built-in picker: %w", err)
203		}
204		model, ok := final.(builtinModel)

207		}
208		if model.canceled {
209			return Result{}, ErrCanceled
210		}
211		if !model.done {
212			return Result{}, nil
213		}
214		return Result{Item: model.selected}, nil
215	}
```

## 已實作

- 新增共用 picker abstraction：
  - external line-selector backend，預設使用 `fzf`
  - executable 不存在或 `[picker] command = []` 時，自動使用 Bubble Tea picker
  - duplicate-safe mapping、控制字元清理、CJK display-width 裁切與明確 cancellation  
  `internal/picker/picker.go:17`  
  `internal/picker/builtin.go:30`

- TUI `/` filter 與 built-in picker 共用 term-wise matching semantics：  
  `internal/textmatch/match.go:1`  
  `internal/tui/rows.go:203`

- 新增全域設定：
  ```toml
  [picker]
  command = ["fzf", "--height=60%", "--layout=reverse", "--border", "--prompt", "{prompt}> "]
  ```
  整個 array 是直接 argv，不經 shell；`dev doctor` 會顯示 external/built-in 狀態。  
  `internal/config/config.go:48`

- Bare `dev repo clone`：
  - 從既有 `remotes.json` raw cache 選 exact `CloneURL`
  - 不做 network refresh，也不為 local badge 額外掃 repositories

  - 保留手動 URL/path/`owner/name`  
  `internal/cli/repo_create_wizard.go:154`

- `dev start`：
  - checkout 外使用 fast live discovery picker
  - 選取後 full-resolve
  - absolute path 會先直接 probe，不再先掃全部 roots
  - checkout 內維持立即採用 current repository 的快速路徑  
  `internal/cli/start_wizard.go:90`  
  `internal/repo/discover.go:256`

- 新增可自行安裝的外部 composition：

```text
1	# Context
2	
3	`dev` already has robust domain-owned caches (forge remotes, fleet snapshots, disk sizes, note FTS, templates), but it has no generic cache of selectable CLI values and no picker integration. Repository discovery/inventory remains deliberately live. The first useful integration is therefore narrow: reuse the existing forge cache to choose a remote for `dev repo clone`, use fast live discovery to choose a local repository in the `dev start` wizard, and expose the existing `dev repo remote --json` contract to Television/fzf recipes. This removes repetitive path/name typing without making fzf mandatory, changing scripted behavior, or adding a second inventory/cache.
4	
5	The user selected an internal configurable picker plus composable external recipes, with a built-in Bubble Tea fallback. This slice intentionally does not add pickers to `dev done` (which already has task completion) or to every finite-choice command.
6	
7	## 1. Add a reusable, safe selector primitive
8	
9	- Add `internal/textmatch` with an exported term matcher equivalent to the current `internal/tui/rows.go:matches`: trim/lowercase, split whitespace, require every term as a substring. Have the TUI delegate to it so the built-in picker and `/` keep one tested matching contract; do not introduce a fuzzy-scoring dependency.
10	- Add `internal/picker` with small caller-neutral types such as:
11	  - `Item { Value, Label, Description string }`
12	  - `Request { Prompt, InitialQuery string; Items []Item }`
13	  - `Result { Item Item; Selected, Canceled bool }`
14	  - a selector object constructed with input/output/error streams and configured external argv, exposing `Select(context.Context, Request) (Result, error)`.
15	- Keep backend selection internal: use the configured external executable when `exec.LookPath` succeeds, otherwise use the built-in Bubble Tea backend. An explicitly empty argv forces the built-in backend. A configured executable that starts and then fails is an error rather than silently replaying the interaction in a second UI.
16	- Execute external argv directly with `exec.CommandContext`, never via a shell. Feed normalized, uniquely rendered candidate lines on child stdin, capture only the selected line from stdout, and leave stderr attached to the caller terminal for fzf-style UI. Map the exact returned line back to the source `Item`; decorate otherwise-identical rendered lines with a deterministic ordinal so duplicate labels/descriptions cannot select the wrong value. Reject unexpected/multiple output instead of guessing. Treat exit codes 1 and 130 as cancellation, propagate context cancellation, and report other exits.
17	- Support a literal `{prompt}` substitution in argv elements so the per-call label can reach fzf without shell interpolation. Newlines/NULs in item display fields are normalized before rendering; the opaque `Value` is never rendered or trusted back from the child.
18	- Implement the fallback as a compact Bubble Tea list with `bubbles/textinput`: live term filtering, up/down plus Ctrl-N/Ctrl-P, Enter to select, Esc/Ctrl-C to cancel, and a bounded viewport. Test the model directly rather than requiring a real terminal.
19	- Add an `App` adapter/test seam in `internal/cli` that passes `App.In/Out/Err` and `App.Cfg.Picker` into `internal/picker`. It should only open a picker when input and output are a terminal pair; non-TTY readers keep the existing deterministic line prompts.
```
